- **Marker:** 2026-06-28-deterministic-env-gated-l4-mode · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-06-28T19:32:43Z
- **Capability:** P-073 (intent F13a) · KEYSTONE

Make the digest→L4→incident chain complete **reproducibly without a GPU/3B model** by adding an env/flag-gated **deterministic L4 mode**: when the gate is set, the L4 interpretation step returns a fixed, schema-valid canned `L4Output` (JSON) instead of invoking the real `llama-cli` subprocess. This unblocks the AI-debug climax for demos, tests, and external (Conductor) verification — decoupling the chain's *completion* from the 3B model's *judgment quality* (explicitly out of scope per intent §5).

Codebase reality (research): the concrete `LlmInferenceRunner` lives at the binary boundary (`LlamaCliInference @ pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs:499`), is constructed + cast to `Arc<dyn LlmInferenceRunner>` as `llm_runner @ pulse-app/src/main.rs:442-448`, and is invoked by `inference_runtime::handle_digest_outcome @ pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:294` which calls `generate_constrained(prompt, L4_OUTPUT_JSON_SCHEMA)` (returns a raw JSON **String**) → parses → drives the incident path. A production deterministic runner does NOT exist — the `StubInferenceRunner` the intent names is a TEST construct (`pulse-app/tests/unit_inference_runtime.rs:99`). So this chunk **productionizes that pattern**: a new binary-boundary impl selected by the gate, returning a canned JSON String that the existing parse→incident path consumes unchanged. The trait is honored unchanged (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] swap-path); the env-gate follows the `feature_gate.rs` truthy-parse pattern (per security extract); obs adds an `inference_mode` field (per obs-plan §3) without logging canned content.

1. **Add the deterministic runner** — new `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs`: `DeterministicInferenceRunner` implementing `interpretation::contract::LlmInferenceRunner` (`Send + Sync`). `current_status` → `Loaded`; `identity` → `Some(ModelIdentity { semantic_name: "deterministic-stub" })`; `tier` → the configured tier; `generate_constrained` → returns a FIXED canned schema-valid L4 JSON `String` (no subprocess, no network). Modeled on `pulse-app/tests/unit_inference_runtime.rs:99-130` `StubInferenceRunner::new_ok`.

2. **Define the canned `L4Output`** — a module-level fixed JSON constant that is schema-valid per `crates/interpretation/src/schema.json`, decodes to `L4Output` (`crates/interpretation/src/schema.rs:158`), and carries a deterministic **non-`info` severity** (so the red-dot / Findings climax fires) + fixed first-party title/symptom/etc. (no PII, no real telemetry — per security extract). Add a unit assertion that it parses via the same path `handle_digest_outcome` uses.

3. **Add the env gate** — `pub const ENV_L4_DETERMINISTIC: &str = "ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC";` + a truthy-parse helper (`Ok("1"|"true"|"yes")` → on), copying `crates/mcp-server/src/feature_gate.rs:3,17`. Name avoids collision with the reserved env set (arch §Occupied Resources).

4. **Branch runner selection at boot** — `pulse-app/src/main.rs` ~442-448: if the gate is truthy, construct `DeterministicInferenceRunner` as the `Arc<dyn LlmInferenceRunner>` `llm_runner` (the `ModelApiImpl` + `inference_runtime` subscriber consume it unchanged); else the existing `LlamaCliInference`. Emit a boot-time `tracing::info!` with an `inference_mode` field (`"deterministic" | "real"`) per obs extract — no canned-output content logged.
5. **Expose for tests** — `pub mod deterministic_inference;` in `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` so the integration + unit tests reach the runner + gate.

6. **Tests** — `pulse-app/tests/unit_deterministic_inference.rs` (runner returns schema-valid JSON + `Loaded` + deterministic severity; gate truthy-parse table) + `pulse-app/tests/integration_deterministic_l4_mode.rs` (env-gated: a seeded `Digest` driven through `inference_runtime::handle_digest_outcome` with the deterministic runner yields a parsed `L4Output` + a created incident, asserted reproducibly across two runs).

7. **Surface the arch registration** — note the new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` var for arch §Occupied Resources Environment-variables registration at wrap (phase is read-only on arch; this is a wrap amendment, per arch extract).
- `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs` — `DeterministicInferenceRunner` impl + canned `L4Output` JSON const + `ENV_L4_DETERMINISTIC` const + truthy-parse helper.
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_deterministic_inference.rs` — unit tests (runner contract + canned-output schema validity + gate parse).
- `pulse-app/tests/integration_deterministic_l4_mode.rs` — env-gated digest→deterministic-L4→incident reproducibility.

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — branch the `llm_runner` selection (~442-448) on the env gate; boot-time `inference_mode` log (preserve the existing `LlamaCliInference` construction + `load_from_env_if_configured` fire-and-forget as the non-deterministic path).
- `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod deterministic_inference;`.

```bash

cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci

# boot-smoke (main.rs touched → per testing.md boot-smoke-coverage); the real smoke is /implement P3
bash scripts/agent-run.sh status    # agent-driven status probe
# npx @tauri-apps/cli dev (60s; watch "ready in"/"Local:") — /implement P3 boot smoke
```

- (arch) The deterministic runner is a third `LlmInferenceRunner` impl behind the unchanged trait (`Send + Sync`, no subprocess/network); selected at the `main.rs` binary boundary by the env gate (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] + §Stack).
- (arch) `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` is registered in arch §Occupied Resources Environment-variables at wrap (phase-deferred amendment).

- (security) The env var is validated via a bounded truthy parse — no unbounded string accepted, no string-interpolation into queries/paths/logs (per security-plan §Input Validation; pattern `feature_gate.rs`).
- (security) The canned `L4Output` contains only first-party constants — no PII, secrets, or real telemetry (asserted by a no-canary unit test) (per security-plan §Threat Model user-content).
- (tests) Contract: the canned `L4Output` JSON is schema-valid + parses via the `handle_digest_outcome` path (per test-plan §8).

- (tests) Integration: with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`, a seeded digest → deterministic L4 → a created incident, **reproducibly** across two runs, with a deterministic non-`info` severity (per test-plan §6; **verification-matrix.json#P-073**).
- (tests) Negative: without the gate, `LlamaCliInference` is selected (no degradation of the real path) (per test-plan §1).

- (obs) Deterministic runner selection is logged at startup with an `inference_mode` field; no canned-output content is logged; p99 latency SLO is neutral (not asserted) on deterministic mode (per obs-plan §3 + §10).
- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` returns 0; `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy …-D warnings` + `cargo xtask capability-drift` clean.

- Spec anchors: arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime — L4 interpretation layer] + §Stack + §Occupied Resources (env vars); security-plan §Input Validation + §Threat Model + §Error Handling; test-plan §1/§6/§8; obs-plan §3/§10.
- Extracts: `arch.md`, `security.md`, `tests.md`, `obs.md` (design/layouts/a11y → No domain coverage).

- Research files inspected: `pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs`, `pulse-app/src/main.rs` §420-490, `crates/interpretation/src/contract.rs`, `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` §270-340; code-graph trace `tree-query-2026-06-28-deterministic-env-gated-l4-mode.json`.

- **`generate_constrained` returns a String, not `L4Output`** — the deterministic runner returns canned JSON TEXT; the existing `handle_digest_outcome @ inference_runtime.rs:294` owns parse→L4Output→incident. Do NOT short-circuit that path (per arch extract anti-pattern: the deterministic output must flow through the real incident-creation chain, chunk #92 producer).

- **Source-level `mod tests` in pulse-app are dead** (`[lib] test=false`) — put ALL tests in `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` (per testing.md 2026-05-20); also keep any source `mod tests` compile-clean for the clippy `--all-targets` gate (2026-06-04).

- **Canned-output severity** — pick a fixed `error`-class severity + a stable title/symptom so Conductor (P-075) + the integration UX test (P-076) can assert a KNOWN incident. Severity is tunable; documented as a const.
- **bindings.ts** — this chunk adds no TauRPC procedure, so capability-drift is unaffected; still run the standard gate. (No `mcp` regen concern beyond the existing wrap discipline.)

**Marker:** `2026-06-28-deterministic-env-gated-l4-mode`
**Capability:** P-073 (intent F13a) · **KEYSTONE**
**Working entry:** "Deterministic env-gated L4 mode — canned `L4Output` via `StubInferenceRunner`, env/flag-selected, so the incident path completes without GPU/3B (P-073 · intent F13a)"

An **env/flag-gated deterministic L4 mode**: when the gate is set, the L4 interpretation step returns a **canned, deterministic `L4Output`** (reusing the existing `StubInferenceRunner` pattern) instead of invoking the real `llama-cli` subprocess — so the **digest → L4 → incident** chain completes **reproducibly**, with no GPU / model / 3B dependency, for demos, tests, and external (Conductor) verification.

OBSERVED (intent F13a): a real retry-storm produced NO incident — the digest→L4→incident chain never completes because the real L4/LLM step is degraded/fragile. The deterministic mode makes the chain's completion reproducible, decoupled from model quality (explicitly out of scope for v0.3.0 per intent §5).
**In scope:**
- A new env/flag gate (an `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` variable) that selects the deterministic L4 runner at the `pulse-app` binary boundary (where the `LlmInferenceRunner` impl is chosen per hardware tier).
- A deterministic canned `L4Output` that is schema-valid and drives the EXISTING incident-creation path to a real incident — including a deterministic severity so the red-dot / Findings climax fires.
- Honoring the existing `LlmInferenceRunner` trait contract unchanged — the deterministic runner is another impl behind it, selected by the gate.
**Out of scope:**
- The real `LlamaCliInference` behavior + the 3B model's judgment quality (deferred per intent §5 — the deterministic mode sidesteps it for verification).
- The incident-creation producer itself (chunk #92, already landed) — this chunk only makes the L4 step deterministic so the EXISTING chain completes.
- Investigate-action wiring (P-072), Conductor verification (P-075), the integration UX test (P-076) — separate chunks that CONSUME this deterministic mode.
- `interpretation` crate — `LlmInferenceRunner` trait + the existing `StubInferenceRunner` pattern (the canned-output source).
- `pulse-app` binary boundary — the runner-selection site (currently picks `LlamaCliInference` per chunk #80 `HardwareProfileSource` tier); add the deterministic-gate branch.
- A new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` env var → arch §Occupied Resources registration (surfaced for a wrap amendment; phase is read-only on arch).
- The `L4Output` contract (the canned value must be valid) + the chunk #81 cadence/digest subscriber that invokes L4.

With the deterministic L4 env/flag set, a seeded digest yields a deterministic `L4Output` and a created incident, **reproducibly**, with no GPU/model. (Verification: integration — `verification-matrix.json#P-073`.)

- **Marker:** 2026-06-28-investigate-actions-functional · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-06-28
- **Capability:** P-072 · intent F12 (Epoch 1 — Foundation: AI-debug spine) · keystone-gated on P-073 (complete)

Make each of the 4 Investigate actions (diagnose latency outlier / find error correlation / trace failed
request / summarize service health) run a **real L4-LLM-backed analysis with visible progress and a surfaced
result or error — never a silent no-op** (per intent F12 / requirements P-072). Today the modal auto-generates
the snapshot correctly, but each action button only copies a prompt template to the clipboard
(`InvestigationModalForm.tsx:127 handlePresetPick`); from the user's POV the product's core AI-debug value is
dead. This chunk wires the buttons to a new backend resolver that builds a curated-telemetry context, runs the
L4 inference, and returns a structured analysis the modal renders.

**Decision locked (P4 user dialogue):** reuse the existing incident `L4Output` schema + parse path rather than
introduce a new free-form analysis contract. The new resolver calls the EXISTING
`LlmInferenceRunner::generate_constrained(prompt, L4_OUTPUT_JSON_SCHEMA)` (the only inference entry point;
`crates/interpretation/src/contract.rs:183`) and `interpretation::schema::parse_bounded`, then maps the parsed
`L4Output` to a transient result DTO — **no `LlmInferenceRunner` trait change, no `interpretation`-crate change,
no change to the just-landed P-073 deterministic runner.** The investigate path is an ADDITIVE second consumer
of `generate_constrained` (today's only production caller is `inference_runtime::handle_digest_outcome @
pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:336` — code-graph confirms zero blast radius). It deliberately does NOT call
`create_incident_from_l4_output` — the result is transient (no incident persisted/broadcast per click).

Backend path is in-process L4 (not MCP): MCP is feature-gated/off-by-default and would not run under the
deterministic-L4 acceptance, so it is considered-and-rejected here (per intent §5 MCP-compliance deferral).
Reproducibility comes from the deterministic-L4 mode (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` truthy, P-073): under
it the runner returns the canned `L4Output` for every action, so the acceptance test is deterministic with no
GPU/model. With a real model the 4 distinct prompt framings yield 4 distinct analyses.

1. **Backend — new `investigate` TauRPC namespace** (`pulse-app/src/investigate_router.rs`, new). Define
   `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "investigate")] trait InvestigateApi { async fn run_action(action_id: String)
   -> Result<InvestigateResultDto, AppError>; }` + `InvestigateApiImpl { conn: Option<Arc<Mutex<Connection>>>,
   data_dir: PathBuf, runner: Arc<dyn LlmInferenceRunner> }` mirroring `model_router.rs` (resolver-injection)
   and `snapshot_runtime.rs` (conn+data_dir). `InvestigateResultDto` is a `serde + specta::Type` payload of the
   L4Output analysis fields the modal renders (e.g. `title`, `symptom`, `timeline`, `hypotheses: Vec<{statement,
   justification}>`, `investigation_steps: Vec<{step, expected_yield}>`); String/Vec fields only (the
   model_router String-payload convention sidesteps cross-crate specta plumbing).

2. **Resolver body** — (a) validate `action_id` against the 4 known ids (the `snapshot_runtime.rs:46`
   `PRESET_PROMPT_DEFINITIONS` set) → unknown ⇒ `AppError::Validation { field: "action_id", … }`; (b) build the
   curated-telemetry context by reusing the snapshot primitives (`load_recent_spans` → `snapshot::contract::
   curate` → `format_markdown`) — factor a shared `curated_context()` helper out of `snapshot_runtime.rs` so

research falsified the intent's "elastic queue / TIER1_QUEUE_CAP=3 drops 75%" mechanism (the `LwwQueue` is a
dead side-channel — `drain_all` has zero production callers; the L4 feed is the broadcast). The real defect is

`assemble(mode, None, …)` (`pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs:125`), so a storm's Tier1 digest carries
`attention_cues == []`, and `create_incident_from_l4_output` (`inference_runtime.rs:648-654`) returns early —

completes, confirms the existing coalescing (storm one-shot, `pattern/storm.rs`) + incident dedup

A hard constraint shapes the mechanism: `CadenceEvent` IS the `pulse://stream/cadence-events` L6-visibility
topic and is deliberately **PII-free** (chunk #80 carries a negative-canary test asserting `scope_id` never
appears in its JSON; per security-plan §Logging + the triage aggregate-only cardinality discipline). The cue
identity includes `scope_id`, so it MUST reach the assembler **off** that topic — never by adding `scope_id`
to `CadenceEvent`.

1. **Deliver the triggering cue to the assembler off the L6 topic.** The cadence coordinator already holds the
   full `AttentionCue` (`run_one_coordinator_cycle(… , triggering_cue: Option<&AttentionCue>)`). Add a
   dedicated, non-L6 in-process carrier from the coordinator to the digest-assembly adapter that conveys the
   full cue for cue-triggered cycles (Tier1/Tier2), while the existing `pulse://stream/cadence-events`
   broadcast continues to emit **labels-only** for L6 visibility unchanged. Recommended shape (HOW is
   /implement's call): a `triage`-side trigger channel `{ mode, window-relevant timing, Option<AttentionCue> }`
   consumed by the digest adapter — keeping the cue (with `scope_id`) off the PII-free topic. Alternative: the
   digest adapter subscribes to the existing `pulse://stream/attention-cues` broadcast (which already carries
   full cues incl. `scope_id` as the product surface) and pairs it with the cadence trigger. Choose the path
   with the least correlation fragility; default to the dedicated carrier.

2. **Pass `Some(&cue)` into `assemble`.** `spawn_cadence_subscriber` (`pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs`)

title: The storm → incident pipeline (as it exists today)

data.head: ## The storm → incident pipeline (as it exists today)

body: 1. **Storm detection** — `crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs::record_occurrence`: per-fingerprint occurrence tracking. **Already coalesces at the cue level**: 5-in-30s → ONE `Suggested` `RetryStorm` cue; 10-in-30s → ONE `Autonomous` cue; then **one-shot dedup** (`last_emitted`) suppresses further cues until the 60s window fully empties. A 426-identical-fingerprint storm emits only ~2 cues, NOT 426. Cue → `pulse://stream/attention-cues` broadcast.

2. **Cadence coordinator** — `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs::start_cadence_coordinator`: subscribes to the cue broadcast; an **Autonomous** cue fires `run_one_coordinator_cycle(Tier1, …, Some(&cue))` → runs Q1-Q7 → emits a `CadenceEvent` on `CadenceEventBroadcast`.
3. **Digest assembler adapter** — `pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs::spawn_cadence_subscriber`: subscribes to `CadenceEventBroadcast`; per event calls `assembler.assemble(mode, **None**, …)`.

4. **Assembler** — `crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs::assemble`: builds the `Digest`, `push`es to the shared `Arc<Mutex<LwwQueue>>` (Tier1 → `push_tier1`, cap 3), and **unconditionally broadcasts** on `DigestBroadcast` (line 543).
5. **L4 subscriber** — `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs::spawn_l4_inference_subscriber`: subscribes to **`DigestBroadcast`** (NOT the queue); per digest runs L4 → `create_incident_from_l4_output`.

title: Two root-cause findings (the intent's mechanical diagnosis is incomplete)

data.head: ## Two root-cause findings (the intent's mechanical diagnosis is incomplete)

title: FINDING 1 (KEYSTONE) — the cue is never threaded cadence→digest, so a storm yields ZERO incidents

data.head: ### FINDING 1 (KEYSTONE) — the cue is never threaded cadence→digest, so a storm yields ZERO incidents

body: `spawn_cadence_subscriber` calls `assemble(mode, None, …)` (`digest_runtime.rs:125`) — the triggering cue is dropped (comment line 7-8: *"triggering cue passthrough deferred к future chunk"*). So a Tier1 cadence digest has `attention_cues == []`. Then `create_incident_from_l4_output` (`inference_runtime.rs:626-654`) derives incident identity from `digest.attention_cues.first()`, and with no cue (and kind ≠ Reflection) hits `else { return; }` — **no incident is ever created from a cadence storm digest.** This is the dominant reason "a real storm produced no incident": even a clean L4 success cannot create the incident. **This must be fixed or the acceptance is unreachable regardless of any queue change.** (This is the 2026-05-30 "data producer assumed-but-inert" pattern: the cue-carrying storm digest is constructed only in `#[cfg(test)]`; the production cadence path passes `None`.)

title: FINDING 2 — the `LwwQueue` is NOT the L4 feed; the intent's "TIER1_QUEUE_CAP=3 drops 75%" describes a drop-METRIC, not L4 delivery

data.head: ### FINDING 2 — the `LwwQueue` is NOT the L4 feed; the intent's "TIER1_QUEUE_CAP=3 drops 75%" describes a drop-METRIC, not L4 delivery

body: Code-graph: `drain_all` has **zero production callers** (refs only at `queue.rs:393,408`, both `#[cfg(test)]`). The `LwwQueue` is push-only in production — `push_tier1` tracks depth + emits `digest.lww.drop` warnings + `metric.pipeline.l3.lww_drop_count_total`, but its contents are never consumed. The real L4 feed is `DigestBroadcast` (bounded `BROADCAST_CAPACITY`). The actual storm-loss path under sustained load + ~4s L4 is **broadcast lag** (`RecvError::Lagged` → skipped digests), not the Tier1 cap. Because the storm detector already coalesces to ~1-2 cues/digests per storm, for a SINGLE-fingerprint storm there is little volume to drop — the dominant defect is FINDING 1, not queue overflow. → "make the queue elastic" needs reinterpretation (see Open question 1).

title: Already-present coalescing/dedup (reduces what this chunk must build)

data.head: ### Already-present coalescing/dedup (reduces what this chunk must build)

body: - Cue-level coalescing: storm detector one-shot per fingerprint/window (above).

- Incident-level dedup: `create_incident_from_l4_output` re-emission dedup on `(kind, scope, scope_id)` (`inference_runtime.rs:661-682`) → bumps an existing active incident instead of creating a duplicate. So "exactly ONE incident" is largely **already handled** once the cue threads through.

- **`LwwQueue`** — refs only within `crates/triage` (`contract.rs` re-export, `assembler.rs` construction/use). Leaf-internal; changing its policy has zero cross-crate blast beyond the assembler + the binary adapters.
- **`drain_all`** — zero production callers (test-only) → safe to repurpose/remove/wire-in.
- **`DigestAssembler::assemble`** — production caller is `digest_runtime.rs:124`; threading a real cue is a one-call-site change (plus the `CadenceEvent` carrier).

- `CadenceEvent` (`cadence/broadcast.rs:22`) carries only `cue_kind_label`/`cue_priority_label` (`Option<&'static str>`) — **not** the full cue. Threading the cue needs the carrier to hold cue identity (kind + scope + scope_id + priority_tier) or a parallel channel.
- `AttentionCue` (`contract.rs:284`): kind, scope, scope_id, magnitude, absolute_value, persistence_seconds, confidence, priority_tier, suppression_bypassed.

- `DigestCueRef` (`contract.rs:448`): kind, priority_tier, summary, scope, scope_id — exactly what `create_incident_from_l4_output` consumes. `Digest.attention_cues: Vec<DigestCueRef>` built from `triggering_cue` in `assemble` (empty when `None`).
- `DigestLwwMode::Tier1NeverLww` (`contract.rs:411`) + `TIER1_QUEUE_CAP=3` (`queue.rs:28`).

- **Cross-crate state delivery** (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16/05-23): traits/state in `triage`; binary adapters in `pulse-app`. The cue carrier extension stays in `triage` (`CadenceEvent`), the reconstruction-and-pass stays in `pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs`.

- **Aggregate-only obs** (`storm.rs`, `assembler.rs`): bounded counts + enum tags; never `scope_id`/`service_name` in self-observation events. New coalesce/queue metrics reuse the `metric.pipeline.l3.*` family.

- **Heartbeat tick shape** (`storm.rs::start_storm_detector`, `coordinator.rs` 15s interval, `inference_runtime.rs::spawn_l4_queue_depth_heartbeat`): `tokio::time::interval`, skip first tick, `MissedTickBehavior::Skip`, aggregate `value` field.
- **PII negative-canary tests** (`storm.rs` tests, `coordinator.rs::…does_not_leak_pii_canary…`): assert no canary in serialized payloads — required for any new cue-carrying `CadenceEvent` field.
- **pulse-app tests live in `pulse-app/tests/*.rs`** (`[lib] test = false`; CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20).

- `crates/triage/src/cadence/broadcast.rs` — extend `CadenceEvent` to carry the triggering cue identity (full `AttentionCue` or a bounded subset) so the digest adapter can rebuild it. (serde + Clone + PII test.)
- `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs` — populate the cue into the emitted `CadenceEvent`.
- `pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs` — `spawn_cadence_subscriber`: rebuild the cue from the event and call `assemble(mode, Some(&cue), …)`.
- `crates/triage/src/digest/queue.rs` — elastic Tier1 policy + (if chosen) a heartbeat-drain consumer; coalesce-in-place option.
- `crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs` — coalesce-count observability; (cue→attention_cues already works when `Some`).
- `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` — if the queue becomes the load-bearing feed, wire the heartbeat-drain → L4; else ensure broadcast delivery reliability.
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — allowlist any new `metric.pipeline.l3.*` / `*.tick` target.

- `pulse-app/tests/integration_tier1_storm_one_incident.rs` — acceptance: ≥100 identical-fingerprint hard signals (via storm detector → cue → cadence → digest → deterministic-L4 P-073) yield exactly ONE incident with no dropped-by-cap loss. (deterministic-L4 makes it reproducible without GPU/model.)

title: Open questions (resolve at P4 / surface at P5)

data.head: ## Open questions (resolve at P4 / surface at P5)

body: 1. **"Elastic queue" interpretation** — the `LwwQueue` is not the L4 feed (`drain_all` dead). Three shapes: **(A)** fix cue-passthrough + rely on existing coalescing/dedup + ensure broadcast delivery (minimal, hits the root cause; the queue stays a metrics side-channel); **(B)** make the Tier1 queue the load-bearing heartbeat-drained L4 feed per the literal intent (largest change; wires `drain_all`→L4); **(C)** cue-passthrough + elastic Tier1 cap + heartbeat-drain alongside the broadcast (middle). All three REQUIRE FINDING 1's cue-passthrough. → AskUserQuestion at P4.
2. **Cue carrier mechanism** — extend `CadenceEvent` with the cue (simplest; one carrier) vs a parallel cue channel into the assembler. Lean: extend `CadenceEvent`.
3. **Acceptance harness** — run under deterministic-L4 (P-073) so "exactly one incident" is reproducible with no GPU/model. (Assumed yes.)

**Capability:** P-074 · intent F13b

**Status at promotion:** pending

Make a sustained identical-fingerprint hard-signal storm yield **exactly ONE incident, reproducibly**,

digest→L4→incident chain returns early and no incident is ever created.

title: Premise correction (research-corrects-intent — recorded as a conscious amendment)

data.head: ## Premise correction (research-corrects-intent — recorded as a conscious amendment)

body:
The intent (F13b) and the original matrix P-074 framed the fix as *"coalesce identical hard-signals
into one digest + an elastic queue with heartbeat ticks; the TIER1_QUEUE_CAP=3 + ~4s L4 latency drops
~75% of storm digests."* Phase-3 research **falsified that mechanism**:

1. **The real bug is an un-threaded cue.** `pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs::spawn_cadence_subscriber`
   calls `assemble(mode, None, …)` — the triggering cue is dropped (a chunk #81 "deferred к future
   chunk" TODO). So a Tier1 cadence storm digest has `attention_cues == []`, and
   `create_incident_from_l4_output` (`inference_runtime.rs:648-654`) hits `else { return }` → **zero
   incidents from a storm**, regardless of any queue behavior. This is THE defect.

2. **The `LwwQueue` is dead on the L4 path.** `drain_all` has zero production callers (code-graph:
   refs only in `#[cfg(test)]`); the real L4 feed is `DigestBroadcast`. `TIER1_QUEUE_CAP=3` only
   gates a drop-*metric*, not L4 delivery. There is no elastic queue to make elastic.

3. **Coalescing to exactly-one already exists** (to be CONFIRMED, not rebuilt): the storm detector
   one-shots ~2 cues per fingerprint/window (`pattern/storm.rs`), and `create_incident_from_l4_output`
   dedups on `(kind, scope, scope_id)` (`inference_runtime.rs:661-682`), processed serially by the
   single-consumer L4 recv loop.

The OUTCOME the intent wanted (one reliable incident under a storm) is unchanged; only the falsified
*mechanism* (elastic queue / TIER1_QUEUE_CAP / "drop 75%") is dropped. This scope + the matrix P-074
entry are corrected to reality (per the user dialogue at /phase P4; the working-route line + intent.md
are left as the human-authored historical source).

1. **Thread the triggering cue cadence→digest (the fix).** Carry the cue identity (kind + scope +
   scope_id + priority_tier) from the cadence trigger through to the assembled digest's
   `attention_cues`, so `create_incident_from_l4_output` derives a real `(kind, scope, scope_id)`
   identity and actually creates the incident. Lean mechanism: extend `CadenceEvent` to carry the cue;
   `spawn_cadence_subscriber` rebuilds it and calls `assemble(mode, Some(&cue), …)`.

2. **Confirm — and only-if-needed complete — dedup to exactly ONE.** Verify a sustained storm
   coalesces to exactly one incident through the existing storm one-shot + incident dedup; if the
   acceptance test reveals a gap (e.g. Suggested-Tier2 + Autonomous-Tier1 producing two incidents, or
   any ordering edge), close THAT gap — still far cheaper than a queue.

3. **Aggregate-only observability** for the threaded-cue path as warranted (no per-service identifiers;
   reuse the `metric.pipeline.l3.*` family). Minimal — only what the behavior change needs.

data.head: # Plan — 2026-06-29-predictable-close-self-verify: "Predictable close + honest tray + agent self-verify"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-06-29-predictable-close-self-verify · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-06-29
- **Capabilities:** P-063 (Predictable close + honest tray) · P-078 (NEW — Agent-headful self-verify harness, authored this chunk)
- **Epoch:** 2 (Window & shell hygiene)

Two coupled deliverables. **(A) P-063 — Predictable close + honest tray.** A live-dogfood premise correction grounds the
scope: close is NOT broken — `pulse-app/src/window.rs::on_window_event` (l.100-124) already does `api.prevent_close()` +
`handle_close_to_tray` → `window.hide()` (chunk #24's hide-to-tray, the arch §Tray-icon-policy default), wired globally at
`main.rs:1021`. Intent F3's "X doesn't quit / the dashboard cannot be closed" is the *symptom* of an **unsignposted**
hide-to-tray: the window vanishes with zero indication the app is still alive. The fix is the missing signpost, not a new
close mechanism — a one-time OS-native notification on the FIRST close ("andromeda-pulse is still running in the tray —
right-click to quit"), gated on the existing `Settings.notifications_enabled` (`crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs:119`),
emitted Rust-side via the already-initialized `tauri_plugin_notification` (`main.rs:1020`). The tray (icon + `Quit` →
`app.exit(0)`, `tray.rs:258-263`) stays the single honest "still running" surface; the static summary-line live-refresh is
explicitly out of F3 scope. Per arch §Tray-icon-policy + §OS-notification-policy + design-system §Surface desktop-native.

**(B) P-078 — Agent-headful self-verify harness (NEW).** A minimal, agent-runnable `cargo xtask self-verify` that boots the
REAL release binary (isolated data dir), asserts shell health from the structured log + window state, runs the existing
a11y/contrast harness, and **quits cleanly with zero orphan** — a deterministic pass/fail an agent can run unattended. This
is the chunk's larger deliverable and the strategic reason it is sequenced first: the close-fix (A) is the enabling
prerequisite for a clean-quitting headful gate, so every later Epoch-2/3 UI chunk can be autonomously boot→verify→quit
verified instead of shipped visually unseen (v0.2.0 passed 1676 tests yet shipped illegible). It COMPOSES existing pieces —
the agent-run boot/cleanup discipline (`scripts/agent-run.sh`), the `npm run test:a11y` suite (`pulse-app/ui/package.json`),
and the `agent-latest.jsonl` boot spans (obs-plan §3) — adding NO heavy deps. The FULL integration-UX e2e + headful
tauri-driver DOM/drag-delta is explicitly P-076 (Epoch 4), which already CARRIES the P-061 drag-delta residual.
**A — Close signpost (P-063)**

1. Add a session-scoped "first close shown" flag (e.g. `Arc<AtomicBool>`) and thread it (plus the means to read
   `notifications_enabled`) into the `.on_window_event` closure at `main.rs:1021` alongside the existing
   `window_geometry_for_event` / `data_dir_for_event` captures.

2. Extract a pure decision seam `should_show_close_signpost(notifications_enabled: bool, already_shown: bool) -> bool`
   (returns true only when enabled AND not-yet-shown) so the policy is unit-testable without a window.

3. In the close path (`window.rs::handle_close_to_tray` or a sibling called from `on_window_event`'s `CloseRequested` arm),
   when the decision is true: emit ONE OS notification via the notification plugin (Rust-side `NotificationExt`), set the
   flag, and emit a bounded aggregate-only obs span (extend the existing `ui.layout.transition` close span with a
   `signpost_shown: bool`, OR a new `tray.signpost.shown` target — NO notification body, NO per-service ids; obs §5 +
   2026-05-17 aggregate-only). Notification copy is contemplative/observational per design-system §Brand voice.

4. Confirm the signpost emits at MOST once per process run and is suppressed when `notifications_enabled = false`. Keep
   hide-to-tray + `prevent_close` exactly as-is; tray→Quit (`app.exit(0)`) stays the terminate path.
**B — xtask self-verify (P-078)**

5. Add a `SelfVerify` subcommand to `xtask` (new `xtask/src/self_verify.rs` + `Cmd` variant + dispatch in `xtask/src/main.rs`),
   mirroring the existing `capability-drift` / `harness:status` subcommand shape. No new workspace deps.

6. Orchestration (deterministic, machine-parseable, single exit code): (a) boot the real release binary with an isolated
   `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` tempdir via `tokio::process::Command` with `kill_on_drop(true)` (reuse the `scripts/agent-run.sh`
   boot pattern); (b) **assert shell health** by tailing `<data_dir>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` for `app.boot` + child boot
   spans (`app.boot.webview.init` / `app.boot.tray.init` / the `ui.layout.transition` window-shown span) within a timeout,
   asserting ZERO `ERROR`/`app.panic.fatal` lines and at least one heartbeat tick — NO pixel-scrape (verification-harness.md
   "IPC/log is the test surface"); (c) run the a11y/contrast harness (`npm run test:a11y --prefix pulse-app/ui` or delegate to
   the existing `xtask test:a11y`), capturing its exit code; (d) **clean quit + zero-orphan**: terminate the booted app

7. Headless tolerance: on a display-less environment where the GUI app cannot boot, detect and **skip-clean** (deterministic

   green on display-less CI.

title: Why these two are ONE chunk

data.head: ## Why these two are ONE chunk

body: The close bug is the *cause* of the missing self-verify: the running app does not quit cleanly (X / taskbar-close do not terminate; only Tray→Quit or a kill stops it), so a headful boot→verify→quit harness would orphan the process on Windows. That is exactly why **boot-smoke is skipped every UI chunk** today (the Windows GUI-orphan hazard). Fixing the close behavior (P-063) is the prerequisite that *unblocks* a clean-quitting self-verify harness (~P-078). Landing both together, FIRST in the UI run, means every later Epoch-2/3 UI chunk can be autonomously boot→assert→quit verified instead of shipped visually unseen (v0.2.0 passed 1676 tests yet shipped illegible).

title: Deliverable A — Predictable close + honest tray (P-063)

data.head: ## Deliverable A — Predictable close + honest tray (P-063)

body: **What it builds:** a predictable, signposted window-close. Window-close (the titlebar close button, the OS taskbar close, Alt-F4) performs ONE configured, honest action; the dashboard window is genuinely closable; the tray is the single honest "still running" surface; tray→Quit is the one true terminate path.

- The architecture already mandates the default: arch §Tray icon policy — "closing the main window minimizes to tray rather than terminating the process (process termination requires the explicit Quit menu item or OS-level kill)." So the **expected default = minimize/hide-to-tray on close**, NOT terminate.

- F3's gap is that this is currently broken AND unsignposted: the window does not hide and there is **no clear indication it is still running**. The fix makes close actually hide-to-tray AND adds a clear "still running in the tray" signpost.

- The **prior chunk (P-061) granted the `allow-close` capability** (window close button fires) but explicitly deferred the close *behavior* to P-063 (per the P-061 matrix note + the 2026-06-29 capability learning). This chunk owns the behavior + the signpost, not the capability grant.

**Boundaries (A):** does not redesign the tray menu surface (arch §Tray policy already fixes its actions: open/focus, ingest summary, snapshot, quit); only ensures the tray honestly reflects running state and is reachable after close. No new tray *actions* beyond what arch already reserves.

title: Deliverable B — Agent-headful self-verify harness (~P-078, NEW cap)

data.head: ## Deliverable B — Agent-headful self-verify harness (~P-078, NEW cap)

body: **What it builds:** a MINIMAL, agent-runnable, headful self-verification path: **boot the real app headful → assert the window is up + correctly placed/rendered + key interactions respond → run the existing a11y/contrast assertion harness → clean quit (zero orphan process)**. Machine-parseable pass/fail, deterministic exit code (agent-driven Development Style per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns). It composes the existing pieces rather than inventing a new test framework:
- the existing **5-command agent harness** `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` (boot/run/status/cleanup/logs) per arch §xtask + verification-harness rules;
- the existing **a11y/contrast harness** (a11y-plan §3 — axe-core / Lighthouse / pa11y / Playwright / colorjs.io; SC 2.3.3 reduced-motion);
- the existing IPC introspection envelope (`app_info` / `health` / `ready`) + window geometry (P-061's `window-geometry.json` + the centered/remembered logic) as the assert surface.
**Boundaries (B) — this is the MINIMAL self-verify, deliberately not the full e2e:**

data.head: ## Open questions (resolve at P4 via AskUserQuestion)

body: 1. **Close behavior** — minimize/hide-to-tray (arch default) with a first-close "still running" signpost · vs quit-on-close · vs a `Settings.close_to_tray` toggle (default hide-to-tray). Arch §Tray policy leans hide-to-tray; F3 permits either.
2. **"Still running" signpost form** — OS-notification toast on first close (pulse:notification, respects `notifications_enabled`) · vs a persistent tray tooltip/title · vs both.

3. **Self-verify harness mechanism + extent** — extend the `agent-run` script harness asserting via IPC/geometry · vs an `xtask self-verify` verb · vs a tauri-driver headful WebDriver spec; and how minimal (shell-health + clean-quit only, vs +basic render/key-interaction assertions). The a11y/contrast reuse is fixed; the driver is the open choice.

- Window-close performs the configured action (hide-to-tray with a visible/clear running indication, OR quit per the P4 decision); the dashboard window genuinely closes; tray→Quit terminates the process with no orphan.

- The agent-headful self-verify harness boots the real app, asserts shell health (window present + placed + rendered + a key interaction responds) + runs the a11y/contrast harness, and quits cleanly with a deterministic pass/fail exit — runnable by an agent unattended.
- No regression: `xtask capability-widening-check` + `xtask capability-drift` stay green; the 3 NEVER-widen caps unwidened.

Make Pulse open as a properly-placed, movable shell. The live dogfood (intent F1) reported the window
"opens tiny, pinned to the top-left corner, cannot be moved." Research **corrects the intent's stated
mechanism**: the custom frameless titlebar's `data-tauri-drag-region` markup has existed since chunk #24
(`Titlebar.tsx`, rendered by `CompactWidget.tsx:55`) — so we are NOT building a drag region. The real defect is
that `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` grants only `["core:default","updater:default"]`, and Tauri 2's
`core:window:default` (inside `core:default`) is **read-only getters + `allow-internal-toggle-maximize` only** —
it omits `core:window:allow-start-dragging`. So the existing drag region's `startDragging()` IPC is **silently
rejected** (this project's negative-default model, CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings; Tauri's "Window Customization"
guide names exactly this permission). The same root cause silently breaks the titlebar's minimize / maximize
buttons (`use-window-controls.ts:17-18` call `allow-minimize` / `allow-toggle-maximize`, also absent).

This chunk (a) grants the window permissions a frameless custom-titlebar app needs — `allow-start-dragging`
(F1 movability) plus `allow-minimize` + `allow-toggle-maximize` (the orphaned, same-root-cause titlebar
controls; user-chosen in-chunk fix; `close` is left to P-063); (b) gives the dashboard a sane default via
`"center": true` and hardens the compact-widget's existing TopRight corner-snap so a monitor-unavailable snap
no longer silently lands at the OS top-left; and (c) adds **remembered free position** — capture each window's
post-drag position and restore it at boot, falling back to center/snap when none is stored. Per arch
§Cross-cutting "Webview IPC capability policy" the capability addition carries a stated rationale; per
layout-templates §Custom titlebar + design-system §Custom titlebar the titlebar stays a drag region with
interactive controls clickable; per a11y-plan §6 the window-control buttons keep their ≥24px target + names.

1. **Grant window permissions (the keystone F1 fix).** In `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` add to
   `permissions`: `core:window:allow-start-dragging`, `core:window:allow-minimize`,
   `core:window:allow-toggle-maximize`. Append a P-061 provenance sentence to the file's `description`
   (the file already keeps a per-chunk provenance log) stating the rationale: frameless custom-titlebar
   window ops — movable shell (F1) + functional minimize/maximize; `close` deferred to P-063. These are
   **core** permissions, not TauRPC procedures → `xtask capability-drift` is unaffected (2026-05-03), and not
   one of the 3 NEVER-widen caps → `xtask capability-widening-check` is unaffected.

2. **Center the dashboard default.** In `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` add `"center": true` to the `main`
   window object (its no-remembered-position default). The compact-widget keeps its corner-snap default
   (`WidgetPosition::TopRight`); leave the existing 480×270 / 1280×800 sizes (deliberate per design — not
   "tiny"). Centering via static config needs no JS capability.

3. **Harden the compact-widget snap fallback.** In `pulse-app/src/window.rs::apply_widget_settings`, the
   `current_monitor()`/`outer_size()`-unavailable arm currently warns and SKIPS positioning — leaving the
   window at the OS top-left default (the "pinned top-left" path). Change the fallback to center the window

title: Headline finding — the capability ALREADY exists; the *permission grant* does not

data.head: ## Headline finding — the capability ALREADY exists; the *permission grant* does not

body: This is the 2026-06-01 "capability already exists" inverse + a partial **premise-correction** (2026-06-28). The intent's stated mechanism — "the custom titlebar IS a drag region so the window is movable" implying we must *build* a drag region — is **falsified**: the drag-region markup has existed since chunk #24. The REAL defect is a missing Tauri-2 capability permission.

- **`Titlebar.tsx`** (chunk #24): the `<header>` already carries `data-tauri-drag-region` (plus app-icon / title / grow spans); interactive buttons correctly excluded. **CompactWidget.tsx:55 renders `<Titlebar>`** — so the boot window (compact-widget) HAS the drag region on screen.

- **Why dragging "does nothing":** Tauri 2's `data-tauri-drag-region` invokes `getCurrentWindow().startDragging()` over IPC, which requires the `core:window:allow-start-dragging` permission. **`pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` grants only `["core:default", "updater:default"]`** (default.json:7-10). Tauri 2's `core:window:default` (bundled in `core:default`) is **read-only getters + `allow-internal-toggle-maximize` only** — it does NOT include `allow-start-dragging`. → the drag IPC is **silently rejected** (this project's negative-default model, CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings). The official Tauri "Window Customization" guide requires exactly `core:window:allow-start-dragging` for `data-tauri-drag-region`.

- **Sibling discovery (same root cause):** the titlebar's three window-control buttons also call permission-gated APIs absent from `core:default`: `minimize()`→`allow-minimize`, `toggleMaximize()`→`allow-toggle-maximize`, `close()`→`allow-close` (use-window-controls.ts:17-19). So minimize / maximize / close-to-tray buttons are ALSO currently silent no-ops. (`close` overlaps P-063's "predictable close + honest tray"; minimize/maximize are orphaned — owned by no other chunk.)

- `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` (full) — two windows: `compact-widget` (480×270, `alwaysOnTop:true`, `decorations:false`, `visible:false`) + `main` (1280×800, `decorations:false`, `visible:false`). **Neither has `center` or an explicit position** → OS-default placement (top-left / cascade). Default sizes are deliberate, not "tiny" (480×270 is the design-spec quarter-screen glance widget).

- `pulse-app/src/window.rs` (full) — `apply_widget_settings()` snaps the compact-widget to `settings.widget_position` via `compute_snap_position` + sets `always_on_top`; on `current_monitor()`/`outer_size()` unavailable it **warns and SKIPS the snap**, leaving the window at the tauri.conf OS-default (top-left) — the likely "pinned top-left" path. `on_window_event` intercepts `CloseRequested`→`prevent_close()`+`handle_close_to_tray` (hides, not quits — the existing F3 close-to-tray plumbing). `show_compact_widget` shows the widget at boot. NO positioning applied to the `main` window anywhere.

- `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` Settings (70-244) — `widget_position: WidgetPosition` (**default `TopRight`**, contract.rs:78-79) + `always_on_top` (default `true`). **No free-form geometry fields** (no x/y/width/height) → "remembered" *free* position does not exist today; only the 4-corner snap enum. `Settings` derives `PartialEq + Eq` (the f32-blocks-Eq constraint per 2026-05-19 — any persisted geometry must be integer-typed).

- `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/CompactWidget.tsx` (full) — renders `<Titlebar onInvestigateClick=…/>` at top + `<main>` (constellation canvas + findings band). Confirms the drag region is present in the boot window.
- `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` (full) — `windows:["compact-widget","main"]`, `permissions:["core:default","updater:default"]`. The single edit point for any window permission.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/components/{Titlebar,WindowControls}.tsx` + `hooks/use-window-controls.ts` — confirm the drag markup + the three window-op buttons and their permission-gated calls.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/components/Titlebar.test.tsx` — existing vitest asserts `data-tauri-drag-region` present + no tabindex + button ARIA. Extend here for any titlebar test.

- **`apply_widget_settings` / `show_compact_widget` / `on_window_event`** — each called from exactly ONE site: `pulse-app::main()` at main.rs:1012 / 1022 / 1024. Single caller, leaf wiring → hardening the snap fallback or centering is a low-blast-radius additive change. (DB regenerated: 6508 nodes / 32080 edges.)
- **Frameless custom titlebar** (`decorations:false` + `data-tauri-drag-region`) — frontend.md §Custom titlebar documents exactly this; the missing piece is the capability grant, not markup.

- **Boot-time window config via the setup closure** (window.rs `apply_widget_settings`, main.rs:1024) — the established place to apply geometry, not a new TauRPC procedure (arch §Cross-cutting; 2026-05-09 Settings-extension learning).

- **Corner-snap glance widget** (`compute_snap_position` + `WidgetPosition`, default TopRight) — the compact-widget is BY DESIGN a corner-snapped `alwaysOnTop` quarter-screen widget (chunk #30 + layout-templates §Compact widget), not a centered window.

- **Capability JSON is the single negative-default gate** — adding a `core:window:*` permission is a one-file edit to default.json; it is NOT a TauRPC procedure so `xtask capability-drift` is unaffected (2026-05-03), and not one of the 3 NEVER-widen capabilities so `capability-widening-check` is unaffected.

- **Centering via static config** — `"center": true` on a window in tauri.conf.json centers natively at creation with NO JS permission required (vs computing a centered `set_position`, which would need `allow-set-position`). Prefer config-centering to keep the capability surface minimal.

- **Window permission rationale** — arch §Webview IPC capability policy: core APIs beyond enumerated TauRPC require "an explicit per-feature capability addition with a stated rationale." Adding `core:window:allow-start-dragging` (movability) is the stated F1 rationale; document it in default.json's `description` (the file already carries a per-chunk provenance log).

- **Boot smoke gate is mandatory** — this chunk touches `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` + `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` (+ maybe main.rs/window.rs), so per testing.md `boot-smoke-coverage` the plan MUST include `npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` (60s) — and the actual F1 fix (drag works) can only be confirmed by a runtime drag test, classified as the e2e/manual residual.
- **Settings integer-only if persisting geometry** — any "remembered" x/y must be integer (`i32`), never f32 (Settings `Eq` derive; 2026-05-19).

data.head: ## Open questions (→ resolve at P4 via AskUserQuestion)

body: 1. **Position behavior** — center the `main` dashboard + keep/harden the compact-widget's TopRight corner-snap (rely on now-working drag to reposition) vs add "remembered" free-position persistence vs center both windows. The corner-snap is established design; "remembered" needs new Settings fields + `allow-set-position`.

2. **Capability breadth** — grant only `allow-start-dragging` (strict F1) vs also `allow-minimize` + `allow-toggle-maximize` (fix the orphaned, same-root-cause titlebar controls in-chunk; `close` left to P-063). The user's standing preference favors in-chunk fixes.

**Marker:** `2026-06-29-window-geometry-movable-shell`
**Capability:** P-061 (intent F1 · Epoch 2 — Window & shell hygiene)
**Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0
**Carried annotations:** none (the working entry had no `PREREQ:` / `CARRY:` suffix)
- **Working entry:** "Window geometry + movable shell — sane default size/position (centered or remembered) and a working custom-titlebar drag region (P-061 · intent F1 · layout-templates)"

- **Intent F1 · Geometry/position.** OBSERVED: opens tiny, pinned to the top-left corner, cannot be moved (dragging the titlebar does nothing). EXPECT: opens at a sane default size + position (centered or remembered); the custom frameless titlebar is a drag region so the window is movable.

- **P-061 acceptance (matrix):** "Launched window opens at the configured default size and centered/remembered position and is movable by dragging the titlebar (window position delta > 0)." (method: e2e)
Make the Pulse window a *proper, movable shell*. Two concrete defects from the live dogfood, both closed here:

1. **Sane default geometry** — the window opens at a deliberate default **size** (not tiny) and a deliberate **position** (centered on the active monitor, or a remembered prior position). No more top-left pin at a degenerate size.

2. **Working titlebar drag region** — because the shell is frameless (custom titlebar, `decorations: false`), the OS gives no native move affordance. The custom titlebar must declare a Tauri **drag region** so click-drag on the titlebar moves the window. Today dragging does nothing.

"Remembered" position is acceptable but **centered-on-launch is the floor**; if a remembered-geometry path is added it persists through the existing Settings surface rather than a new IPC namespace (keeps the capability surface flat). The recommendation between *centered-only* vs *centered + remembered* is a P4 scope-ambiguity to resolve with the user.

- **`pulse-app/tauri.conf.json`** — window definition(s): default `width`/`height`, `center: true` (or explicit position), confirm `decorations: false` is the reason a drag region is needed. (Per-platform window config is here.)

- **Webview titlebar component** (`pulse-app/ui/src/…`) — the custom frameless titlebar element gains the Tauri drag-region affordance (`data-tauri-drag-region` / equivalent) so the header is a move handle; interactive controls inside the titlebar must remain clickable (drag region must not swallow button clicks).

- **Boot-time geometry application** (`pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure) — IF a remembered/default position is applied at boot, it rides the existing `apply_widget_settings()`-style path (the established Settings → boot-apply pattern), not a new TauRPC procedure.

- **Settings** (`crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs::Settings`) — ONLY if "remembered geometry" is chosen; would extend the existing `Settings` struct (flows through `get_settings`/`update_settings`, no new namespace) per the 2026-05-09 Settings-extension learning. Centered-only needs no Settings change.

- `prefers-reduced-motion` / a11y: no new animated chrome introduced; if any, it degrades per the universal SC 2.3.3 invariant (likely N/A for a static drag region).

body: Planning (research.md) surfaced the scope was incomplete in one place and the two open questions were resolved with the user. Recorded here so this anchor matches `plan.md`:

- **Premise correction (intent-incomplete):** the intent F1 mechanism "the custom titlebar IS a drag region so the window is movable" implied *building* a drag region. Reality: `Titlebar.tsx` has carried `data-tauri-drag-region` since chunk #24 (rendered by the boot window, `CompactWidget.tsx:55`). The REAL defect is a missing Tauri-2 capability: `default.json` grants only `core:default`, whose `core:window:default` omits `core:window:allow-start-dragging` → the existing drag region's `startDragging()` IPC is silently rejected. The chunk fixes the **permission grant**, not the markup. (Outcome — a movable shell — unchanged; mechanism corrected. The same missing-permission root cause also silently breaks the titlebar minimize/maximize buttons.)

- **Q1 — position behavior → "Add remembered free position":** center the `main` dashboard (`center:true`) + keep/harden the compact-widget TopRight corner-snap, AND persist each window's post-drag position + restore it at boot (fall back to center/snap when none). Capture + restore are Rust-side (`on_window_event` Moved + boot `set_position`), so **no `allow-set-position` capability** is needed (capabilities gate only webview JS). Remembered geometry is kept decoupled from the webview `Settings` form-save path to avoid a clobber bug (see plan.md Implementation notes).

- **Q2 — capability breadth → "Drag + minimize + maximize":** grant `core:window:allow-start-dragging` + `allow-minimize` + `allow-toggle-maximize` in one `default.json` edit (the minimize/maximize buttons share the F1 root cause and are owned by no other chunk — in-chunk fix per the user's standing preference). `close` is left to **P-063** (predictable close + honest tray). Still no `capability-drift` / `capability-widening-check` impact (core perms, not TauRPC; not one of the 3 NEVER-widen caps).

- **Boundaries unchanged:** P-062 (size/aspect), P-063 (close/tray), P-064/065 (chrome suppression), P-066 (widget→dashboard nav) remain out of scope. Full headful tauri-driver drag-delta e2e is a CARRY to the Epoch-4 e2e/Conductor suite (P-075/P-076).

- **Marker:** 2026-06-29-window-size-constraints · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-06-29

Stop the glance widget from being stretched into absurd proportions, and stop both windows from collapsing to
unusably small sizes — the F2 polish for Epoch 2 (Window & shell hygiene). Today the `compact-widget`
(480×270 = 16:9) and `main` (1280×800) windows are `resizable: true` with **no `minWidth`/`minHeight` and no
aspect constraint** (`pulse-app/tauri.conf.json`), so the widget free-resizes to any dimensions and "looks
absurd when stretched" (intent F2 · verification-matrix.json#P-062 observed_gap).

Two constraint classes, split by how the platform enforces them (research.md §API-availability findings —
**Tauri 2.11 / tao 0.35 has `set_min_size` + static `minWidth`/`minHeight` but NO native aspect-ratio API**):

1. **Min-size** is OS-enforced — declared statically in `tauri.conf.json`, the window manager refuses to drag
   below it. Robust, no event loop needed. Applied to **both** windows (Q2 → widget + main): the widget gets a
   16:9-consistent floor; the `main` dashboard gets a sane minimum (no aspect — a dashboard legitimately holds
   varying proportions).

2. **Aspect-ratio** has no native API, so it is enforced (compact-widget only) by a **`WindowEvent::Resized`
   clamp** in `window::on_window_event` — a pure helper recomputes the size to keep `w/h` inside a configured
   aspect *band* and calls `window.set_size(..)`, guarded by a re-entrancy `AtomicBool` (the `set_size` itself
   re-emits `Resized`). The pure helper + its unit tests land in-chunk (mirroring `compute_snap_position`); the
   **live drag-resize-delta** assertion needs headful tauri-driver and **CARRIES to P-076** — the exact P-061
   precedent (verification-matrix.json#P-061 proved via capability/config/unit in-chunk, live drag-delta carried
   to the Epoch-4 e2e suite).

Per arch §Established Decisions [Tauri 2.x] + research §Conventions: **no new TauRPC procedure, capability JSON,
broadcast topic, env var, or workspace dep** — window ops are Rust/config-side; per P-061's finding, Rust-side
window mutation needs no `core:window:*` grant (capabilities gate webview JS only). `capability-drift` +
`capability-widening-check` are expected no-ops.

1. **Static min-size in `tauri.conf.json`** (research §Files to modify). Add `minWidth`/`minHeight` (Tauri 2
   camelCase, matching the existing `alwaysOnTop`) to BOTH window definitions:
   - `compact-widget` — a 16:9-consistent floor (≈ half the 480×270 default, e.g. ~320×180) so the
     titlebar + Halo canvas + footer stack stays readable (layouts extract: layout-templates §Custom titlebar
     space-lg + §Halo State Pulse + §Footer space-sm bound the floor; "readable on a 13-inch laptop").
   - `main` — a sane dashboard minimum (e.g. ~800×600), no aspect. Exact values are /implement's call within
     these bounds.
   - If the static keys are not honored at runtime for any reason, the documented fallback is a boot-time
     `window.set_min_size(Some(..))` in `window::apply_widget_settings` (runtime API confirmed at
     `tauri-2.11.0/src/webview/webview_window.rs:2225`).

2. **Pure aspect-band clamp helper** in `pulse-app/src/window.rs` (research §Patterns — the `compute_snap_position`
   template). A pure fn — e.g. `clamp_to_aspect_bounds(size: (u32,u32), min_aspect: f32, max_aspect: f32) -> Option<(u32,u32)>`
   — returning `Some(corrected)` only when the incoming `w/h` is outside `[min_aspect, max_aspect]` (centered on
   16:9 ≈ 1.778; e.g. ~1.4–2.1), else `None` (in-band → no clamp). Operates on physical-pixel tuples (consistent
   with `compute_snap_position`). Decide which dimension to adjust toward the nearer band edge. Bounds live as
   named `const`s beside the existing window-label consts; sanity-bound them via a module-level `const _: () = {
   assert!(..) }` block (testing.md 2026-05-11 — clippy `assertions_on_constants`).

3. **`WindowEvent::Resized` arm** in `window::on_window_event` (`window.rs:140`, the `_ => {}` slot). Only act
   when `sanitize_window_label(window.label()) == COMPACT_WIDGET_LABEL` (Q2 → aspect on the widget only). Read a
   re-entrancy guard `AtomicBool`: if set, this `Resized` is our own `set_size` echo → clear it + return; else
   call the pure helper, and on `Some(corrected)` set the guard + `window.set_size(corrected)` (best-effort; a
   failed `set_size` logs a `warn` and never aborts, like the existing arms). Emit NO raw w/h (security extract:
   no coordinate/dimension values logged — reuse the existing `ui.layout.transition` aggregate span shape if any
   obs is wanted, label-only).

4. **Thread the guard atomic** through the `main.rs` setup closure (research §Files to modify): capture an
   `Arc<AtomicBool>` into the `.on_window_event(..)` closure exactly as `signpost_shown` is captured today
   (`main.rs` ~1025), passing it as a new `&AtomicBool` param on `on_window_event`.

5. **Unit tests** for the pure helper, colocated in `window.rs` `mod tests` (the helper takes primitives, so it
   runs there like `compute_snap_position` — NOT subject to the `[lib] test = false` dead-test trap per
   testing.md 2026-05-20, since these are pure-fn tests with no lib-surface needs; if any test needs the lib
   surface, it moves to `pulse-app/tests/unit_window_constraints.rs`). Cover: in-band → `None`; too-wide →
   clamped into band; too-tall → clamped into band; exactly-at-edge → `None`; the min-size floor values are
   16:9-consistent (a `const` assertion).

6. **Boot-smoke** (tests extract, test-plan §3 boot-smoke — chunk touches `tauri.conf.json` + `main.rs`/`window.rs`):
   run `npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` (60s) at /implement P3; the app must boot without panic and both windows show.

- **Band, not pin** — the matrix acceptance says the ratio "stays within the configured BOUND"; a tolerance band

1. **Tests in `pulse-app/tests/unit_window_constraints.rs`, not `window.rs mod tests`** — plan Step 5's explicitly-anticipated fallback. Confirmed `[lib] test = false` (Cargo.toml:12) makes src-level `mod tests` compile-but-never-run under nextest (2026-05-20 trap). Verified the 6 tests run (1713→1719). Helper + 2 consts exposed `pub #[doc(hidden)]`.

2. **Min-size value 320×180 → 400×225** (compact-widget). The plan left exact values to implement; the initial 320×180 was tuned UP after the user's live screenshot showed the titlebar wrapping (title + 5 buttons can't fit on one row at ~320px → overflow). In-scope value refinement.

3. **Aspect clamp: debounced (settle-then-clamp), not per-event** — the plan specified a re-entrancy-guarded per-`Resized` `set_size`. Live testing surfaced that per-frame `set_size` during a Windows modal resize fights the cursor and flickers badly. Re-implemented as a generation-counter debounce (clamp once after ~150ms of no new Resized). Better UX + eliminates the fighting; the re-entrancy guard became the generation counter.

4. **`core:window:allow-close` grant — OUT of P-062's plan scope (folded in).** The frameless custom-titlebar ✕ (`use-window-controls.ts` `getCurrentWindow().close()`) was silently rejected (negative-default ACL) → "nothing happens on click". **P-063 residual:** P-061 granted drag/minimize/maximize but deferred close to P-063; P-063 added the close *signpost* on the Rust `CloseRequested` handler but never granted the webview permission to *reach* it. P-063 is marked `verified`, yet its primary close affordance was dead — the self-verify boot-quit never clicked the real button. Folded in per the user's standing in-chunk-fix preference. **wrap should record this corrects P-063.**

5. **Widget scrollbar fix (`CompactWidget.tsx` `minHeight`→`height`) — OUT of P-062's plan scope (folded in).** Pre-existing widget-shell CSS overflow: `<main minHeight: calc(100vh - 32px)>` let the element GROW past the viewport → vertical scrollbar (design-banned on the glance widget). Fixed to `height` (locks to viewport; could not use `overflow:hidden` — the findings dropdown pops downward and would be clipped). Frontend/CSS, separate from window-sizing. Folded in per user preference.

- **P4 scope decisions (user-selected, recorded in scope.md):** Q1 → min-size + aspect *band* (not hard 16:9 pin), both delivered in-chunk; Q2 → constrain the widget AND give the `main` dashboard a min-size.

- **Min-size values must be validated against the real titlebar/content layout, not just aspect math** — 320×180 satisfied the aspect band but broke the titlebar (wrap → overflow). Needed live visual feedback to set 400×225.

- **A per-event `set_size` aspect clamp during an interactive (modal) window resize fights the cursor → flicker;** debounce-on-settle (clamp once the resize stops) is the fix. The `tauri::async_runtime::spawn` + `tokio::time::sleep` debounce ran cleanly at runtime (no "no timer" panic — Tauri's runtime has timers).

- **A frameless custom-titlebar window's ✕/minimize/maximize each need their own `core:window:allow-*` grant** (extends the P-061 lesson to `allow-close`). A capability marked "verified" can still hide a DEAD affordance when the verification (boot-quit self-verify) never exercises the real user-facing button — manual click-testing caught what 1719 tests + the boot smoke did not.

- **`minHeight` on a viewport-fill flex container lets it grow → scrollbar; use a fixed `height`.** And `overflow:hidden` is unusable as the scrollbar cure when a descendant popover (findings dropdown, `top: calc(100% + …)`) must render outside the container.
- **User preference reconfirmed:** fix adjacent bugs in-chunk rather than deferring (multiple folded-in fixes accepted this session) — consistent with the saved `fix-in-chunk-preference` memory.

- **Acceptance MET:** resize below the min-size is clamped (OS-enforced via `tauri.conf.json`); aspect stays within the configured band (pure-helper unit tests + live-verified). Live headful resize-delta e2e CARRIED to P-076 (P-061 precedent).

- **Event-handler dispatch with threaded state** (`window.rs:140`): `on_window_event` already fans `WindowEvent` arms with `&Mutex<GeometryStore>` + `&AtomicBool` state; a `Resized` arm + a re-entrancy-guard atomic slot in beside `signpost_shown`.

title: API-availability findings (the scope's open question — RESOLVED)

data.head: ## API-availability findings (the scope's open question — RESOLVED)

body: - **Min-size: SUPPORTED, OS-enforced.** `tauri::WebviewWindow::set_min_size(Option<Size>)` exists (`tauri-2.11.0/src/webview/webview_window.rs:2225`); tao `set_min_inner_size` backs it (`tao-0.35.0/src/window.rs:790`). Static `minWidth`/`minHeight` in `tauri.conf.json` is the declarative equivalent. **Min-size is enforced by the window manager** — the user cannot drag below it — so it needs **no event-loop clamp** and is robustly verifiable (config assertion + the OS refuses smaller).

- **Aspect-ratio: NO native API.** tao 0.35 has **no** window aspect-ratio lock (the only `aspect` hits are `DVASPECT_CONTENT` OLE constants in the Windows drag-drop handler — unrelated); winit/tao have never shipped one. → aspect must be enforced by a **`WindowEvent::Resized(size)` clamp** in `on_window_event`: recompute the size to keep `w/h` within a configured aspect band and call `window.set_size(..)` (`webview_window.rs:2220`), guarded by a re-entrancy `AtomicBool` (the `set_size` itself emits a `Resized`). The **live** "aspect stays within bound during a real drag-resize" assertion needs headful tauri-driver → **CARRY to P-076** (exactly the P-061 headful-drag-delta precedent: pure-helper + config proof land in-chunk; the live delta carries to the Epoch-4 e2e suite).

- (none expected) — all logic lands in the existing `pulse-app/src/window.rs` + `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json`; tests colocate in `window.rs` `mod tests` IF pure-helper-only, OR move to `pulse-app/tests/unit_window_constraints.rs` per the 2026-05-20 `[lib] test = false` discipline if they need the lib surface (the pure helper is testable in `mod tests` since it takes primitives, like `compute_snap_position`).
- `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` — add `minWidth`/`minHeight` to `compact-widget` (and to `main` if Q2 → both-windows).

- `pulse-app/src/window.rs` — add a pure `clamp_to_aspect_bounds()` helper + unit tests; add a `WindowEvent::Resized` arm to `on_window_event` invoking it with a re-entrancy guard (IF Q1 → aspect-in-chunk).

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — capture the re-entrancy-guard `Arc<AtomicBool>` into the `on_window_event` closure (mirrors `signpost_shown`); optionally call `set_min_size` at boot if the runtime path is chosen over static config.

2. **Aspect-ratio constraint** — the widget holds *fixed-ish proportions* (it is a glance surface, not a free-form panel). Today there is no aspect lock, so the constellation/halo content distorts when stretched.

This chunk does geometry + movability only."* Geometry + movability + close are already done (P-061 + P-063); this chunk adds only the size *constraints*.

Per-window config lives here; P-061 confirmed there are two windows (`main` dashboard + the compact widget).

Window size constraints are Rust/config-side; per P-061's finding, Rust-side window operations need no Tauri capability grant (capabilities gate webview JS only). A native aspect-ratio API called from Rust likewise needs no `core:window:*` grant; only if enforcement were driven from webview JS would a grant be in play (not the expected path).

data.head: ## P4 resolutions (val-1 reconciliation — appended at /phase P5)

body: Research (research.md) resolved the scope's central open question and the two ambiguities were resolved with the user. Recorded here so this anchor matches `plan.md`:

- **API-availability finding (research):** Tauri 2.11 / tao 0.35 has `set_min_size` + static `minWidth`/`minHeight` (min-size is **OS-enforced**, no event loop needed) but **NO native aspect-ratio API** (the only `aspect` hits in tao are unrelated `DVASPECT_CONTENT` OLE constants). So aspect must be enforced by a `WindowEvent::Resized` clamp in the existing `window::on_window_event` (`window.rs:140`, the `_ => {}` arm), reusing the `compute_snap_position` pure-helper-+-unit-test pattern.

- **Q1 — aspect mechanism / in-chunk depth → "Min-size + aspect band":** deliver BOTH P-062 constraints in-chunk — static min-size (OS-enforced) + a pure `clamp_to_aspect_bounds` helper (unit-tested) wired into the `Resized` event with a re-entrancy `AtomicBool` guard. The aspect is a tolerance *band* centered on 16:9 (matches the matrix wording "stays within the configured BOUND"), not a hard pin. The **live headful resize-delta** assertion CARRIES to P-076 (the exact P-061 headful-drag-delta precedent — unit/config proof lands in-chunk).

- **Q2 — constraint scope → "Widget + main min-size":** aspect-band + min-size on `compact-widget`; a sane min-size (no aspect) on the `main` dashboard too (today 1280×800 with no floor → can collapse). Cheap adjacent fix per the user's standing in-chunk-fix preference.

- **Boundaries unchanged:** P-061 (geometry/movability — DONE), P-063 (close/tray — DONE), P-064/065 (chrome suppression), P-066 (widget→dashboard nav) remain out of scope. No new TauRPC namespace / capability JSON / broadcast topic / env var / workspace dep (default outcome holds; window ops are Rust/config-side).

- **Marker:** 2026-06-30-browser-chrome-suppression · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-06-30

Suppress the two browser-grade affordances that leak into the desktop app and carry zero meaning in a telemetry
tool: the default WebView2 right-click context menu (Back / Refresh / Save-as / Print / Inspect — **P-064**) and
the canvas "save/drag image" interaction (**P-065**). Both are webview-only frontend hygiene (intent F4/F5;
"Quick wins" per intent §5) on top of the working v0.2.0 shell — no Rust, no IPC, no new capability.

The mechanism is a single app-wide suppression hook plus one global CSS rule. Per research, **both windows
render through the single `App.tsx` root** (it routes `compact-widget` → `<CompactWidget>` else `<Dashboard>`
via `useWindowLabel`), so a `document`-level effect mounted in `App` is app-wide by construction — no per-window
wiring. The context-menu handler is **production-gated** (`import.meta.env.PROD`) so the dev inner loop keeps
right-click → Inspect/devtools (per design-system §Anti-Patterns "dev preserve" + the intent/matrix wording "in
a production build"), and **exempts editable elements** (inputs / textareas / contenteditable) so native
copy/paste/spellcheck survives in the Settings form (a11y SC 3.3.2 / 4.1.2 — **user-confirmed at /phase P4**:
"Exempt text fields"). The canvas affordance is killed two ways for defense-in-depth: a global
`canvas { -webkit-user-drag: none; user-select: none }` CSS rule (covers all 5 existing canvases + any future
one) and a PROD-gated `dragstart` handler in the same hook; the context-menu handler additionally removes the
canvas "Save image as" entry.

Provenance: design-system §Anti-Patterns (desktop-webview) + a11y-plan §1 P7 / §5 (keyboard / editable
exemption) + test-plan §4 (vitest) / §3 (gate set) + arch §Webview IPC capability policy (DOM handler needs no
capability) + obs §8 / §10 (no event logging, no per-event telemetry). **Net-new** — research confirms zero
existing `contextmenu` / `import.meta.env` / `draggable` / `user-select` usage (the P2 extracts' "mirror the
existing PROD-gate pattern" was inaccurate; this is the first use of `import.meta.env.PROD`, standard Vite).

1. **New hook `use-suppress-browser-chrome.ts`** (`pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/`). On mount, when `import.meta.env.PROD` is true, attach two `document` listeners and remove them on cleanup: - `contextmenu` → if `event.target.closest('input, textarea, [contenteditable="true"]')` is null (target is **non-editable**), call `event.preventDefault()` (suppresses the WebView2 menu incl. canvas "Save image as"); editable targets keep the native menu. - `dragstart` → if the target is a `` or ``, call `event.preventDefault()` (kills drag-to-save). - When `PROD` is false (dev / test), install nothing (dev keeps right-click → Inspect). - Handlers call `preventDefault()` only — NEVER read/log target, coordinates, or event content (obs §8); no telemetry emission (obs §10 frame-budget).

2. **Mount the hook in `App.tsx`** — call `useSuppressBrowserChrome()` once at the top of `App()` (alongside the
   existing `document.title` effect). Single mount point = app-wide (both windows route through `App`).

3. **Global canvas CSS** — append to `pulse-app/ui/src/styles/tokens.css` (after the `@theme` block) a rule
   `canvas { -webkit-user-drag: none; user-select: none; }`. Always-on (harmless in dev; a canvas is never a
   saveable image) and covers all 5 canvas hosts + future ones in one place. Use CSS, not an inline React style,
   because `-webkit-user-drag` is not in React's `CSSProperties` typing.

4. **Colocated test `use-suppress-browser-chrome.test.tsx`** — vitest jsdom:
   - PROD path (`vi.stubEnv('PROD', true)`): `fireEvent.contextMenu(div)` on a non-editable node →
     `event.defaultPrevented === true`; `fireEvent.contextMenu(input)` on an `<input>` → NOT prevented
     (editable-exempt); `fireEvent.dragStart(canvas)` on a `<canvas>` → prevented.
   - DEV path (default, no stub): `fireEvent.contextMenu(div)` → NOT prevented (handler not installed).
   - `afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllEnvs())` (per the 2026-05-08 unstub discipline). Mount the hook via a tiny test
     host component or `renderHook`.

5. **Run the full gate set** (Test Commands below), including the standing UI gate `cargo xtask self-verify` (boots
   the real app + a11y/contrast harness + clean quit) so the suppression is proven not to regress boot, focus, or
   a11y; webview vitest is the owning affordance proof for P-064/P-065.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-suppress-browser-chrome.ts` — the app-wide suppression hook (PROD-gated contextmenu
  [editable-exempt] + dragstart [canvas/img], document listeners with cleanup).
- `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-suppress-browser-chrome.test.tsx` — vitest PROD-path + DEV-path assertions.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/App.tsx` — add `useSuppressBrowserChrome()` call (preserve the existing `document.title`
  effect + window-label routing).

- `pulse-app/ui/src/styles/tokens.css` — append the global `canvas { -webkit-user-drag: none; user-select: none; }`
  rule after the `@theme` block (preserve all existing tokens).
