body: - **Depth:** moderate–deep · **Reads:** 11 files (full) · **Globs/Greps:** 8 · **Code-graph:** 1 query (refs to ConnectionStatePayload / ServiceListPayload)

- `pulse-app/ui/src/components/ConnectionDot.tsx` (full) — the **CARRY target**. `formatLastSpanAgo(ms)` returns `"just now"` for `ms < 1000` (l.67-77); `lastSpan` + `ariaLabel` render `last span {lastSpan}` whenever `payload` exists (l.83-90). On fresh boot with zero telemetry the payload is `{state: Listening, last_span_ago_ms: 0}` → the dot's accessible name reads **"Connection: Listening — last span just now"** — dishonest (no span ever arrived).

- `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs` (full) — `ConnectionStatePayload { state, last_span_ago_ms, severity, message, reason }` (l.106-112). **`compute_state` returns `Listening` IFF `last_ingest_at_nanos == 0`** (l.194-195) and **`last_span_ago_ms` returns 0 IFF no ingest** (l.209-215). So `state === "Listening"` is the exact "no span ever received" sentinel — the clean discriminator for the CARRY fix. Payload carries connection state + lag ONLY — **no source count, no spans/sec, no buffer fill.**

- `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-connection-state.ts` (full) — 1s-poll PULL hook over `connection.current_state()` (l.22-54): `poll()` on mount + `setInterval(1000)` + `window` focus + cleanup, `.catch(()=>{})` keep-last. The status-line's connection word reuses this.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/constellation-types.ts` (full) — **`isServiceLive(item, nowUnixNano)`** (l.29-31) gated by `LIVE_RECENCY_WINDOW_NANOS = 60s` (l.27), the P-067 recency selector. `ServiceListItem` carries `last_seen_unix_nano` / `state` / `service` / `priority_tier`. **The connected-source count reuses `isServiceLive` verbatim** so the worded count and the constellation dots agree by construction (scope Q3 → yes).

- `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-service-constellation.ts` (full) — 1s-poll PULL hook over `services.list_with_states()` → `ServiceListItem[]` (l.26-57). Same shape as use-connection-state. **The connected-count data source already exists frontend-side, no backend delta.**

- `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` (full) — `HealthEnvelope` (subsystems + pid + uptime) and `ReadyEnvelope { ready, checked_at, checks }` where **`ReadyChecks = { duckdb_connection, ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct, broadcast_subscribers, plugins_loaded, mcp_server_enabled }`** (l.403-411). **NO `rows_ingested`, NO buffer fill, NO spans/sec anywhere on the IPC surface.** `IntrospectionApi` is the top-level envelope (`app_info`/`health`/`ready`/`get_settings`/`update_settings`, l.292-298); `IntrospectionApiImpl` already holds `broadcast_senders: Option<Arc<buffer::BroadcastSenders>>` (l.310) — the constructor is the extension point for a `BufferState` handle if the backend path is chosen.

- `crates/buffer/src/state.rs` (full) — `BufferState { rows_ingested, eviction_count, memory_bytes, retention_window_active }` + `snapshot() -> BufferStateSnapshot` (l.27-34). **The rate + fill raw data EXISTS here but is consumed only by heartbeat-tick logging — never exposed via any TauRPC.** `retention_window_active` latches true after the first retention sweep (a coarse "buffer warmed to full window" flag).

- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/FooterStatusBar.tsx` (full) — **the designated read-only footer status band, currently an EMPTY `<footer>`** (population "lands in chunks #34/#35" per its docstring — never happened). Already styled per layout-templates (flex row, `--color-base` bg, subtle Earth-Blue top border, `--color-text-secondary`, `--font-body` 12px). **This is the reuse-first placement** (layouts extract → footer status region).

- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/StatusLiveRegion.tsx` (full) — `StatusLiveRegionProvider` + **`useStatusAnnouncer()`** polite `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region (l.24-72). The exact SC 4.1.3 announce mechanism P-081 reused (a11y.md 2026-07-07) — the connected↔no-telemetry transition announce goes through this, once, on the edge.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/router.tsx` (grep l.170) — **`<FooterStatusBar />` is mounted in the dashboard shell root layout** (inside the StatusLiveRegion provider tree). Placement confirmed.

- **ConnectionStatePayload** — all refs are inside `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs` (definition, field access, `from_parts`, tests). No cross-crate consumers of the struct itself; the webview consumes it via generated bindings. The CARRY touches ONLY `ConnectionDot.tsx` render logic (no payload change) → **zero cross-crate blast.**
- **ServiceListPayload / ServiceListItem** — consumed frontend-side via `use-service-constellation.ts`; the connected count is a pure frontend filter over existing data → **zero backend blast.**

- **1s-poll PULL hook** (`use-connection-state.ts:22-54`, `use-service-constellation.ts:26-57`): `poll()` + `setInterval(poll,1000)` + `window` focus listener + cleanup + `.catch(()=>{})` keep-last. A new status/ready hook (if backend delta) follows this exact shape (+ the 2026-07-07 SILENT-BACKGROUND-REFRESH keep-last-on-repoll-error discipline).
- **Shared recency gate** (`constellation-types.ts:29-31`): `isServiceLive` is THE selector both the dots and the worded count must share so they never disagree (P-067 live-only truth).

- **Polite once-on-edge announce** (`StatusLiveRegion.tsx` + `useStatusAnnouncer`): `useRef(prev)` + `useEffect` firing `announce` only on the connected↔disconnected transition, never per rate-tick (a11y extract; P-081 precedent).
- **Empty footer status slot** (`FooterStatusBar.tsx`, mounted `router.tsx:170`): populate-in-place, the layouts-sanctioned home.

- **ready/health sync command as the live-stat surface** (`health.rs:376-419`): obs-sanctioned ("use the sync command, not log-tailing"). Extending `ReadyChecks` FIELDS adds no procedure → `xtask capability-drift` / `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` / capability JSON all unaffected (2026-05-09 Settings-extension precedent, applied to the ready envelope).

- **Reuse-first / extend-not-add** (arch extract C1; 2026-06-01 "capability already exists"): populate the existing empty `FooterStatusBar`; reuse `services.list_with_states` + `connection.current_state`; if rate/fill need exposure, ADD FIELDS to `ReadyChecks` (top-level envelope, already in Occupied Resources) rather than mint a namespace.

- **Design tokens** (design extract): numerics (count · spans/s · buffer min) in JetBrains Mono Data role `tabular-nums`; words in IBM Plex Sans; `--color-text-primary`/`secondary`, NEVER `--color-text-tertiary` at 12–14px; state color from the semantic palette, never color-alone.

- **a11y** (a11y extract): the worded line IS the not-color-alone complement; polite once-on-edge announce via `useStatusAnnouncer`; text passes SC 1.4.3 on the full-dashboard axe sweep (NOT contrast-exempt — supersedes scope's tentative note); ConnectionDot honest recency lives in the **accessible name** (aria-label), which the dot already uses.

**Marker:** `2026-07-07-plain-language-connection-status`
**Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · Epoch 3 — State honesty & legibility
**Capability:** P-070 (intent F10) → `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json#P-070`

**Working-route source (verbatim):**
> Plain-language connection status — a human-readable services-connected, spans-per-second, and
> buffer-state line using design-system typography (P-070 · intent F10) · CARRY: make the
> ConnectionDot recency honest — its "Listening · last span · just now" tooltip (chunk #89) can read
> "just now" on zero telemetry; deferred from P-067 (RESEARCH-CORRECTS-INTENT — that phrasing was the
> intent's F7 evidence but belongs to the connection-status surface, not the constellation, which
> P-067 fixed).

**Observed gap (P-070):** Nowhere does the UI state, *in words*, how many sources are connected, whether
telemetry is arriving, or the buffer state. The app has a minimal `ConnectionDot` (chunk #89) — a colored
dot + tooltip — and a live constellation, but no plain-language sentence a developer can read at a glance to
answer "is my telemetry actually flowing, and from how many services?"

**Requirement (P-070):** A human-readable status line states sources-connected / telemetry-arriving /
buffer-state — e.g. *"Receiving from 5 services · ~540 spans/s · buffer 2 min / 10 min"* — rendered with
design-system typography.

**Why now:** Epoch 3 is "State honesty & legibility." P-067 made the constellation live-only; P-068/P-069
made Traces + dots legible; P-081 made the table live. The one remaining honesty gap is the *worded* status —
the plain-language complement to the visual dot/constellation, so a user never has to infer connection health
from color alone.

1. **A plain-language connection-status line** on the dashboard (design-system typography), reporting in words:
   - **connected-source count** — how many services are *currently live* (recency-gated, consistent with the
     P-067 live-only truth model — never counting stale/persisted registry entries as connected);
   - **ingest rate** — spans-per-second (a human-rounded rate, e.g. "~540 spans/s");
   - **buffer state** — fill vs. the configured retention window (e.g. "buffer 2 min / 10 min").
   - Honest zero/empty phrasing: with zero live telemetry the line says so plainly (e.g. "No telemetry yet —
     listening on :4317/:4318") rather than implying flow that is not there.

2. **Folded CARRY — ConnectionDot recency honesty.** Fix the chunk-#89 `ConnectionDot` tooltip so its recency
   phrasing (currently "Listening · last span · just now") cannot read "just now" when there has been **zero**
   telemetry / no span has ever arrived. On a fresh boot with no spans, the tooltip must state an honest
   "listening, no spans yet" rather than a recency ("just now") that implies a span just landed. This is the
   P-067 dual for the connection surface (P-067 fixed the constellation; the intent's F7 "just now" evidence
   actually belonged here, per the RESEARCH-CORRECTS-INTENT note carried from P-067).

- **Primarily webview** (matrix `method: webview`). The status line is a rendered UI surface consuming existing
  telemetry/state contracts. A backend delta is IN scope **only if** research (P3) shows the three data points
  (live-source count · spans/s · buffer fill) are not already retrievable from an existing TauRPC/stream — in
  which case the minimal-cost path (extend an existing payload / reuse `services.list_with_states` +
  `connection.current_state` + a buffer/rate source) is preferred over a new TauRPC namespace, per the
  Settings-extension / reuse-first discipline in the session-learnings.

- **Placement:** the dashboard is the primary home for the worded line (the compact widget stays aggregate-glance
  per the P-069 layout boundary); whether a condensed form also belongs in the widget is a P4 plan question, not
  assumed here.

- **Consistency with live-only truth (P-067):** the "connected sources" count MUST use the same recency gate as
  the constellation's live-only visibility — the worded count and the dot count must not disagree.

- **Marker:** 2026-07-07-traces-table-auto-refresh · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-07-07
- **Surface:** webview-only (`pulse-app/ui/**`); zero `.rs` delta (CARRY deferred — see below).

The Traces table queries `viz.query.traces` exactly once at mount and never re-polls (`use-traces.ts:48-82`, one `useEffect` keyed `[timeWindowSeconds, limit]`, `cursor: null`, `cancelled`-guard). On a fresh boot the query resolves before spans land (`row_count 0`), the table renders "No traces yet", and then freezes there while telemetry flows — the constellation on the *same* Traces route (`useServiceConstellation`, a 1s poll) shows live data, so the frozen table reads as broken for an observability app (operator-hit live at the P-079 wrap). This chunk adds a periodic re-poll to `use-traces.ts` — mirroring the `use-service-constellation.ts` precedent (mount-poll + `setInterval(1000)` + focus listener + cleanup) — so the table transitions out of the empty state once data lands and keeps its rows current, as a **silent background refresh** that preserves the P-068 anomaly-first ordering, the "Errors only" filter, and the active sort across every tick.

Because `TraceTable.tsx` already re-derives its view via `useMemo([rows, sortState, errorsOnly])` (`:34-37`) and `TracesRoute.tsx` renders `<TraceTable rows={rows} …>` with no `key` (`:67`), a `rows`-prop update re-renders in place — filter/sort state and keyboard focus are preserved **by construction** (no remount). The chunk actualizes the a11y-plan "P4 Live trace list" surface (the list becomes live), so it also adds the SC 4.1.3 obligation: a **one-shot polite announcement** on the empty→populated transition via the existing `useStatusAnnouncer` region — never per-tick, never assertive (per a11y-plan §1 P4 + §7; design/layouts §Motion "confirm state, not arrive" ⇒ instant swap, no entrance animation).

Reuse-only at the boundary: the re-poll re-invokes the existing `traces.query` under `pulse:default` — **no new TauRPC procedure, no capability JSON, no capability-drift, no Rust change** (arch §Webview IPC capability policy + security §API). The working-route **CARRY** (viz `next_cursor` keyed on start-time vs P-068's `ORDER BY end_time`) **re-defers**: `crates/viz/src/query.rs:17-18` already documents it as a latent caveat, and the re-poll keeps `cursor: null` (page 1), so pagination is never exercised — it stays a documented latent caveat handed to a future pagination-touching chunk.

1. **Add the re-poll to `use-traces.ts`** (mirror `use-service-constellation.ts:29-54`). Introduce a `POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 1000` const. Inside the existing `useEffect`, factor the fetch into a `poll()` closure over the current `args` (keep `cursor: null` — do NOT touch pagination). On mount: call `poll()` once; then `window.setInterval(poll, 1000)`; add a `window` `"focus"` listener calling `poll()` (mirrors the constellation; catches focus-return). Cleanup returns: set `cancelled = true`, `clearInterval`, `removeEventListener("focus")` — no leaked timer. Effect dep array stays `[options.timeWindowSeconds, options.limit]` (an args change tears down + re-establishes the interval, correct).

2. **Silent background-refresh semantics** in the same `poll()`. Success (guard `!cancelled`): `setState({ rows: res.items, total: res.total, isLoading: false, error: null })`. Error (guard `!cancelled`): branch on whether the first load has completed — if `prev.isLoading` is still `true` (the INITIAL fetch failed, nothing to preserve) keep today's behavior (`{ rows: [], total: 0, isLoading: false, error }`); else (already loaded, a transient re-poll hiccup) **return `prev` unchanged** (keep last-good rows, mirroring the constellation `.catch(() => {})` — no mid-poll blank/flicker). Do NOT re-flip `isLoading` to `true` on re-polls (would flash "Loading…" is guarded by `rows.length === 0`, but re-flipping is semantically wrong for a background refresh).

3. **One-shot empty→populated announcement in `TraceTable.tsx`** (SC 4.1.3). Track the previous `rows.length` in a `useRef`; in a `useEffect` keyed on `rows.length`, when prev was `0` and current `> 0`, call the existing `announce(...)` (from `useStatusAnnouncer`, `:31`) ONCE with a short polite phrase (e.g. "Traces loaded"), then update the ref. Fire only on the `0 → >0` edge — not on subsequent count changes, not on `>0 → >0`. Reuse the existing polite region — add NO new live element, NO `role="alert"`/assertive. Leave the `useMemo` (`:34-37`) untouched (filter/sort preservation already correct). Introduce no transition/animation on the row swap (design §Motion Hard limits — instant).

4. **Extend `use-traces.test.ts`** with fake-timer re-poll coverage (per `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-07-02): fake ONLY timers (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["setInterval","clearInterval"] })` or Date-scoped as needed), advance with `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1000)`, restore in `try/finally`. Assert: `queryFn` re-invoked (`toHaveBeenCalled()` / `≥ 2`, not exact — React 19 double-invoke, 2026-05-08); a second resolved value updates `result.current.rows`; after `unmount()`, advancing the timer yields no further `queryFn` calls (interval cleared); a re-poll rejection AFTER a successful first load keeps the prior `rows` (not blanked). Never real time.

5. **Extend `TraceTable.test.tsx`**: (a) empty→populated announces once — render with `rows: []`, rerender with `rows: [row]`, assert the polite announcer fired once; a further rerender with more rows does NOT re-announce. (b) Focus preserved — focus the `trace-errors-only-filter` button, rerender with new `rows`, assert `document.activeElement` is still that button. (c) Filter/sort survive a refresh — toggle Errors-only (`aria-pressed=true`) + apply a sort, rerender with a new `rows` array, assert `aria-pressed` + `aria-sort` unchanged and the filtered/sorted view holds (no blank). Wire the `useStatusAnnouncer` dependency as the existing TraceTable tests already do (provider wrap or announce mock — per the 2026-05-10 context-provider-wrap discipline).

6. **Verify no CARRY activation** — confirm `use-traces.ts` still sends `cursor: null` (page 1); leave `crates/viz/src/query.rs` untouched. Record the CARRY as still-deferred in the wrap handoff (hand to a future pagination chunk).
- none.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/traces/TraceTable.tsx` — one-shot polite empty→populated announcement (step 3); `useMemo` filter/sort logic unchanged.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/traces/use-traces.test.ts` — fake-timer re-poll tests (step 4).
- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/traces/TraceTable.test.tsx` — announcement + focus-preserved + filter/sort-survive tests (step 5).

title: D3 — Constellation per-dot label collision-avoidance (CARRY, folded)

data.head: ### D3 — Constellation per-dot label collision-avoidance (CARRY, folded)

body: The P-069 always-on per-dot service-name labels on the **Traces constellation hero** can **overlap** when dots cluster (no avoidance yet). Add a layout refinement so labels do not overlap / occlude neighbouring dots when the constellation is dense. Scope is the **dashboard Traces constellation hero** only (the compact widget stays aggregate-glance per the P-069 layout boundary). Must preserve the P-069 verified contract: each dot keeps an always-on accessible name + a non-color severity token (SC 1.4.1 / 4.1.2).

In `TraceTable.tsx`, the **pre-existing** `handleSort` / `handleToggleErrorsOnly` handlers call `announce(...)` (a `StatusLiveRegion` setState) from **inside** a `setSortState` / `setState` updater callback — which runs during render, triggering a React "Cannot update a component while rendering a different component" warning. Move each `announce(...)` **out of** the state-updater and **into** the event-handler body (compute the announcement from current state, call `announce` directly). This is a correctness fix for a pre-existing warning (NOT introduced by the P-081 auto-refresh chunk, whose empty→populated announce is correctly in a `useEffect`). Must preserve the existing announce semantics (sort-direction / Errors-only-toggle announcements still fire once per user action, politely).

> **Research amendment (2026-07-09 /phase P5 val-1 — intent-incomplete):** the CARRY named BOTH `handleSort` and `handleToggleErrorsOnly`, but the codebase (`TraceTable.tsx:47-63`) shows only `handleSort` calls `announce(...)` *inside* the `setSortState` updater; `handleToggleErrorsOnly` ALREADY announces *outside* its setter (announce → `setErrorsOnly(next)`). So D4 fixes `handleSort` only; `handleToggleErrorsOnly` is confirmed correct (no-op). Outcome (no render-phase announce warning) unchanged.

**Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Epoch 3 — State honesty & legibility**
**Origin:** operator-directed at the `2026-07-06-incidents-panel-dropdown-layout-bug` (P-080) wrap — the
operator chose "separate floating panel below the widget" over the upward-popover / grow-the-window options.
No dedicated capability id (P-061..P-082 are all claimed/verified); this is a disclosure-surface refinement
beyond the numbered v0.3.0 plan. **Matrix link: none** (addresses no unverified cap).

Surface unread incidents (Findings) in a **SEPARATE borderless, always-on-top window docked directly BELOW
the compact widget** — replacing the in-widget upward popover that `2026-07-06-incidents-panel-dropdown-layout-bug`
landed as the interim bounded-popover bug-fix. The new window **reuses that chunk's bounded / scrollable /
opaque `FindingsDropdown` content verbatim** — this chunk changes the *container* (in-widget popover → its own
window), not the incident-list rendering.
Concretely, the chunk delivers:

1. **A second app window (label-scoped)** — a borderless, always-on-top, non-taskbar, focus-on-demand window
   whose webview renders ONLY the Findings disclosure content, selected by a **window-label render branch**
   (the same mechanism as the existing widget/dashboard split — the frontend keys its root render on the
   current window label).

2. **Below-the-widget positioning** — the Findings window positions itself directly below the compact widget,
   derived from the **widget's live position + size** at open time. Must handle **off-screen / multi-monitor
   clamping** (if the widget sits near a screen's bottom edge, the panel must not open off-screen — clamp into
   the work area, or flip above the widget).

3. **Cross-window focus + the disclosure a11y contract** — honour the chunk #87 disclosure a11y contract
   ACROSS windows: opening the panel moves focus into it; **Esc returns focus to the triggering unread badge**
   in the widget window (cross-window focus restoration).

4. **Dismiss lifecycle** — the panel hides on: blur (focus leaves the panel window) · Esc · row-select
   (opening an incident) · mark-all-read. "Hide" (not destroy) so re-open is cheap and focus/scroll are
   predictable.

5. **`core:window` capability grants** — the second window's create / position / show / hide operations are
   **negative-default gated** (per the 2026-06-29 `core:window` family lesson: `core:default` grants only
   read-only getters + internal-toggle-maximize; every mutation needs an explicit `core:window:allow-*` or
   `core:webview:allow-*` grant in `pulse-app/capabilities/`, or the IPC is silently rejected). Grant exactly
   the operations this window needs, each with a stated rationale; do NOT widen the 3 never-widen caps
   (`pulse:notification` / `pulse:tray` / `pulse:plugin-fs`).

- **Findings-badge fetch-once-no-repoll bug** — `use-findings.ts` currently fetches incidents only at mount +
  on window-focus, so the unread badge stays hidden until a resize forces a focus refetch. Fix so the badge
  reflects incidents as they arrive: add a periodic re-poll (the constellation's ~1 s cadence is the
  precedent) OR wire the existing `pulse://stream/incidents` push subscription. Folds here because the new
  Findings window reuses `use-findings.ts`; same bug-class as the Traces auto-refresh follow-up (P-081).

  + its trigger/badge in the widget; `use-findings.ts` (CARRY re-poll/subscription); cross-window focus +

  `core:webview` grants are required.

  `core:webview:allow-create-webview-window`) grants for the second window; label-scoped where possible.

  work-area / multi-monitor clamp.

- Esc / blur / row-select / mark-all-read each dismiss the panel; Esc returns focus to the unread badge.
- The unread badge updates as incidents arrive **without** requiring a manual resize/focus (CARRY fixed).

- **Marker:** 2026-08-14-fingerprint-feed-capture-repair · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-14T21:05Z

Make the retry-storm detector's feed actually reachable by a storm of identical exception span-events delivered over OTLP, and prove it with the detector's own latched counters. An outside party measured thirty-one storm-tick lines across three launch arms with every fingerprint field zero, while Pulse's ingest counter showed all nine spans arriving and holding — spans arrive, nothing reaches the fingerprint observer. The region between OTLP receipt and the per-span-event fingerprint hook is where that stops, and no artifact records what happens inside it, because the corpus holds no span table.

Research narrowed that region substantially without settling it. The wiring premise the hand-off could only assert from source is confirmed at HEAD — `main.rs:600-604` constructs `Some(StormObserverAdapter)` and `main.rs:1110` passes it into `run_consumer`, which threads it unconditionally to the per-event fan-out at `appender.rs:394-400`. The security extract's hypothesis that the mandated PII scrub might starve the fingerprint is falsified: `appender.rs:358` computes it from the raw type and stacktrace *before* the scrub, and `exception_type` is never scrubbed. And the buffer-crate path is exercised end-to-end by an existing e2e (`e2e_storm_detection.rs`) that drives a real export request through to the Suggested/Autonomous thresholds. What research newly surfaced is a boot-time branch — `match buffer_conn` at `main.rs:1102`, whose `None` arm spawns a receiver-drain that discards every batch while leaving ingest's counter incrementing — a mechanism that reproduces the measured signature exactly. That is a candidate, not a verdict.

So the chunk runs in that order: close the deferred Rust gate to learn whether the guarding e2e is even green at HEAD, make the feed positively observable rather than inferable from silence, capture it live under a canary storm, localize, repair, and guard. The instrumentation ships permanently (operator-directed at P4): three atomic counters on `BufferState` surfaced on the existing 15s `buffer.tick`, plus a one-time degraded-boot warn — so the next regression of this class announces itself instead of presenting as absence. Self-observation stays `tracing`-only and aggregate-only per obs-plan §3/§5/§8; nothing added here carries an OTLP attribute value.

1. **Close the absorbed Rust gate deferral first — it is a diagnostic, not just hygiene.** Run the workspace suite (memory-throttled per `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-06-28 + 2026-07-25: `cargo build --workspace --tests --jobs 4` under `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, then `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`). Record whether `e2e_storm_detection::chunk_66_storm_detector_emits_suggested_at_5th_autonomous_at_10th` passes. A green result establishes the in-process path works and points the defect at boot/runtime configuration; a red result relocates the whole investigation and is itself the finding. The last full workspace run was 2026-06-28, and commits `6fbbd30` + `de00fbc` touched Rust source with no wrap gate over them.

2. **Add the three feed counters to `BufferState`.** Mirror the existing `rows_ingested` / `eviction_count` shape (`AtomicU64` field + `record_*` method + `BufferStateSnapshot` field): `span_events_seen`, `fingerprints_computed`, `observer_invocations`. Counting happens inside `build_span_events_record_batch`, which is where all three quantities are already known — events pushed to the row vectors, `Some` fingerprints, and observer calls in the fan-out loop.

3. **Thread `BufferState` into the span-events builder.** `build_span_events_record_batch` currently takes `(&[ResourceSpans], Option<&dyn FingerprintObserver>)`; it needs the state handle to record into. Per the code-graph impact query the signature change reaches **7 call sites**: the production caller `consumer.rs:118` (plus its import at `:12`), the `#[cfg(test)]` wrapper at `appender.rs:561`, and four in-test callers at `appender.rs:1560`, `:1756`, `:1803`, `:1834`. Thread all seven in one pass. Keep the increments outside any per-event `tracing` emission — atomics only; the loop is a named hot path per obs-plan §11.

4. **Surface the counters on the existing `buffer.tick`.** Add the three snapshot fields to the emission at `heartbeat.rs:201`. No new tick target, no new cadence — the 15s buffer tick already carries `rows_ingested` and is the module's declared liveness surface (obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks).

5. **Make the degraded-boot branch self-announcing.** The `None` arm at `main.rs:1102` currently spawns a silent drain (`main.rs:1130-1135`). Emit one `warn` naming the reason and the consequence — that DuckDB appends and the fingerprint feed are both inert for this boot — so the condition is a positive reading rather than an inference from the absence of `duckdb.append`. Fires once at boot, not per batch.

6. **Extend the `AllowList`.** The default-deny formatter redacts silently, so the three new tick fields and the new boot target must be registered in `observability.rs` (the `"buffer"` entry at `:171` for the tick fields; a new entry for the boot target). Aggregate-only: counts and bounded reason/consequence strings — never `service_name`, `scope_id`, or any span identity, per the 2026-05-17 + 2026-06-28 triage-cardinality entries in `.claude/rules/observability.md`. Probe each new target with the `allowlist_for_target_resolves_*` pattern before trusting the emission.

7. **Run the live capture.** Fresh data dir, deterministic L4, boot the built binary, drive `inject_demo` (it emits a fixed `exception.type = "PaymentGatewayTimeoutError"` with a fixed stacktrace per error span — an identical-fingerprint storm by construction), then read the obs-log family. Walk the five ranked branch points in `research.md`: (1) `buffer.schema.init.error` present or `duckdb.append` absent → the boot branch; (2) `duckdb.append` at ERROR with `reject_reason` → appends failing; (3) `duckdb.append` for `spans` but never `span_events` → the builder returned `Ok(None)`; (4) `span_events` rows with `fingerprint IS NULL` → `exception_type` did not survive ingest; (5) counters move but the detector's do not → detector-side. Branches 1-3 are answerable from `agent-latest.jsonl` alone.

8. **Repair at the localized cause.** The site is the capture's output, so it is not predictable here. Two boundaries hold regardless: the repair fixes the cause rather than compensating downstream, and it does not weaken ingest's post-`prost` invariant checks or the decode/body-size caps (security-plan §Input Validation). If the cause lands outside this chunk's named region — branch 5, detector-side — that is a scope-boundary event to surface to the operator at /implement, not to absorb silently.

9. **Guard the repair at the tier the defect occupies.** Buffer-crate logic → colocated `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in the owning crate. `ingest → buffer` boundary → an integration test driving a real `tonic` client against loopback `:4317` and asserting through the buffer (test-plan §5). pulse-app boot wiring → `pulse-app/tests/*.rs`, **never** `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `pulse-app/src/` (`[lib] test = false` means those compile under clippy but never run). Self-bootstrapping data only; no sleeps; paused clock for anything touching the 60s retention window.

10. **Assert the negative-canary.** Under the canary storm, no raw `exception.type` / `.message` / `.stacktrace` value appears anywhere in `agent-latest.jsonl` — the storm's own literal values are the canary strings (per the 2026-05-04 "match secret formats, not vocabulary" obs amendment, key on the known literals rather than the word "exception").

- `pulse-app/tests/integration_fingerprint_feed.rs` — the guard test, IF the defect is boot/runtime-shaped (the leading hypothesis): drives the canary storm through the assembled path and asserts the feed counters and the detector's latched totals move off zero. If instead the capture localizes to buffer-crate logic, the guard lands as a colocated `#[cfg(test)]` test inside `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` (already in the modify set) and **no new file is created**. Step 9 decides; exactly one of the two homes is used.
- `crates/buffer/src/state.rs` — three `AtomicU64` counters + `record_*` methods + `BufferStateSnapshot` fields, mirroring `rows_ingested`.

- `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` — `build_span_events_record_batch` gains the state handle; increments at the event push, the `Some(fingerprint)` computation, and the fan-out loop (l.394-400). Preserve the fingerprint-before-scrub ordering at l.352-367 exactly — it is load-bearing for cross-occurrence dedupe.
- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` — thread `state` into the `build_span_events_record_batch` call at l.118 (`dispatch_batch` already holds `&BufferState` at l.98).
- `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` (test call sites) — the five test callers at l.561, 1560, 1756, 1803, 1834 per the impact query.
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — the degraded-boot warn on the `None` arm at l.1102/1130-1135.
- `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs` — three new fields on the `buffer.tick` emission at l.201; its existing tick assertions at l.423/578/660/683 may need updating.
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — `AllowList` extension: the `"buffer"` entry at l.171 plus a new entry for the boot target, with resolver probes.

- **The repair site** — not predictable before step 7. For branch points 1-3 it is one of the files already listed above. Branch 4 (attributes did not survive ingest) additionally brings in `crates/ingest/src/`; branch 5 (detector-side) brings in `crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs` and is the one outcome that exceeds this chunk's named region — surface it to the operator rather than absorbing it.

body: - **Depth:** moderate · **Reads:** 6 · **Globs/Greps:** 5 · **Graph queries:** 1 (77 rows)

The wiring premise the hand-off could only assert from source is **confirmed at HEAD**, and the region it named is **narrower than stated**. The buffer-crate path from `run_consumer` to `on_fingerprint` is intact AND is exercised end-to-end by an existing e2e test, so the algorithm is not the suspect. What research newly surfaced is a **boot-time branch whose `None` arm silently discards every ingest batch while leaving ingest's own counter incrementing** — a mechanism that reproduces the measured signature (`span_count` 1→2→3→9 stable, every fingerprint field zero) exactly.

This does **not** settle the cause. It converts an unbounded region into a small set of discriminable branch points, each of which the live capture can separate by reading one already-emitted log target.

- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` (full) — `run_consumer` takes `fingerprint_observer: Option<Arc<dyn FingerprintObserver>>` (l.40), clones it per batch (l.59), hands it to `dispatch_batch` (l.68), which passes it into `build_span_events_record_batch(&s, fingerprint_observer)` (l.119) for every `Batch::Spans`. No filter, no early return on the observer path.

- `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` (l.340-406) — the per-span-event loop reads all three `exception.*` keys from `event.attributes` (l.346-350), computes the fingerprint from the RAW type + stacktrace (l.358) **before** the PII scrub (l.366-367), and fans out to the observer at l.394-400 for every row whose fingerprint is `Some`.

- `crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs` (l.60-85) — `compute_exception_fingerprint` returns `None` only when `exception_type` is `None` or empty. `NoopFingerprintObserver` exists but is not on the production path.
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (l.590-604, l.1102-1135, l.1471-1500) — observer construction, the consumer-spawn branch, and `init_buffer`.

- `pulse-app/tests/e2e_storm_detection.rs` (structure) — `chunk_66_storm_detector_emits_suggested_at_5th_autonomous_at_10th` drives a real `ExportTraceServiceRequest` through `run_consumer` with a real `StormObserverAdapter` and asserts the Suggested/Autonomous thresholds.

data.head: ## Graph impact (77 rows, `refs` over the four fingerprint symbols)

body: - **`FingerprintObserver#on_fingerprint`** — exactly two implementors: `NoopFingerprintObserver` (`fingerprint.rs:392`) and `StormObserverAdapter` (`storm_observer.rs:72`). One production call site: `appender.rs:396`.
- **`StormObserverAdapter`** — constructed at `main.rs:600` (production) and `e2e_storm_detection.rs:144` (test). No other production construction.
- **`compute_exception_fingerprint`** — one production call site (`appender.rs:358`); the remaining 20 refs are all inside `fingerprint.rs`'s own test module.
- **Zero production references outside `crates/buffer` and `pulse-app`** — the feed has no other consumer, so the blast radius of a repair here is confined to those two crates.

- **Observer-as-`Option`, injected at the binary boundary** (`main.rs:600` → `consumer.rs:40`): the trait lives in the lower crate, the concrete adapter at the root — the project's standing cross-crate state-delivery shape.

- **Fingerprint-before-scrub ordering is deliberate and commented** (`appender.rs:352-357`): content-stable fingerprints preserve cross-occurrence dedupe; scrubbing first would collide unrelated exceptions on the redaction marker. **This closes the security extract's P3 hypothesis — the mandated scrub cannot starve the fingerprint.**

- **Silent-drain fallback on a failed subsystem** (`main.rs:1130-1135`): when the buffer connection is absent the receiver is drained to keep the ingest channel from saturating. Deliberate backpressure hygiene — but it is indistinguishable, from ingest's counters alone, from a healthy path.

- **Boot outcomes are already observable** (`main.rs:1471-1500`): `init_buffer` emits `buffer.schema.init` (info, on success) or `buffer.schema.init.error` (error, with `error_type` = `open_in_memory_failed` | `schema_create`) and records `BufferConnectionStatus` on the heartbeat. No new instrumentation is needed to discriminate this branch.
- **Test-time telemetry injection over the wire** — synthetic spans enter through the real receiver on `:4317`/`:4318`; no in-process bypass (`e2e_storm_detection.rs` is the worked example).

- **Aggregate-only self-observation on triage targets** — counts, enum tags, and numeric values; never `service_name` / `scope_id` / per-span identity in `agent-latest.jsonl` (`.claude/rules/observability.md`, 2026-05-17 + 2026-06-28 entries).
- **No per-span-event emission at `info` in the appender loop** — it is a named hot path; level-gate anything expensive.
- **pulse-app tests belong in `pulse-app/tests/*.rs`**, never `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `pulse-app/src/` — `[lib] test = false` means source-level tests compile under clippy but never run.

title: Candidate branch points for the live capture (ranked, each discriminated by an existing log target)

data.head: ## Candidate branch points for the live capture (ranked, each discriminated by an existing log target)

body: 1. **`buffer_conn == None`** → consumer never spawns; batches drained at `main.rs:1133`. Discriminator: `buffer.schema.init.error` present, or `buffer.schema.init` absent, or `duckdb.append` absent entirely.
2. **`buffer_conn == Some` but appends failing** → `duckdb.append` present at ERROR with `reject_reason` (`consumer.rs:79-91`).

3. **Spans append but events do not** → `duckdb.append` present with `table_name="spans"` but never `"span_events"`; means `build_span_events_record_batch` returned `Ok(None)` (l.386-388: no event rows survived the loop).

4. **Events append but carry no fingerprint** → `span_events` rows present with `fingerprint IS NULL`; means `exception_type` arrived `None`/empty — i.e. the attributes did not survive ingest, the one premise research could not close.
5. **Fingerprints fan out but the detector's counters do not move** → the defect is detector-side, downstream of this chunk's named region.
Branches 1-3 are answerable from `agent-latest.jsonl` alone; 4 needs a `span_events` query; 5 needs the storm-tick series.
Provisional — the repair's site is the live capture's output, not a prediction. Instrumentation-side (deliverable 1) is knowable now:

At minimum it warrants a one-time `warn` naming the consequence (the fingerprint feed and DuckDB appends are both inert this boot), so the condition is self-announcing rather than inferable only by absence.

**Working entry:** _Fingerprint-feed capture and repair — the storm detector's feed observed live, then the dead region between ingest receipt and the fingerprint hook repaired (operator-directed 2026-08-14; evidence: Conductor fingerprint-feed-verdict.md)_

A storm of identical exception span-events, delivered over OTLP the way any instrumented app delivers them, reaches the retry-storm detector's feed. The dead region between OTLP ingest receipt and the per-span-event fingerprint hook is **first localized by live observation, then repaired**, and the repair is proven by the detector's own latched counters under a canary-shaped storm.

This is a diagnose-then-fix chunk: **the cause is unknown by the evidence's nature.** No prior run has seen into the region, because the artifact that would show it (a span table) does not exist in the corpus. Localization is therefore in scope as work, not as a foregone conclusion, and the repair's shape cannot be fixed in advance.

1. **Live observation of the feed.** A run in which the path from OTLP receipt to the fingerprint hook is observable at its intermediate boundaries — enough to say *where* the events stop, not merely *that* they stop. Whatever instrumentation this requires is part of the chunk. **The instrumentation SHIPS PERMANENTLY** (operator-directed at P4): three atomic counters on `BufferState` surfaced on the existing 15s `buffer.tick` — no new tick, no per-event emission — plus a one-time warn when the degraded-boot branch fires. Rationale: this defect survived because "nothing reached the observer" could only be inferred from silence; permanence makes it a positive reading and puts the regression class under the existing obs gates. Rejected at the same gate: diagnostic-only scaffolding (removes the very thing that made the diagnosis possible) and boot-warn-only (leaves branches 3-5 silence-inferred).
2. **The repair.** The localized defect is fixed at its cause.

3. **Proof under a canary-shaped storm.** Identical-fingerprint exception span-events over OTLP move the detector's latched counters off zero, and the repair is guarded by a test at the tier the defect occupies.

title: Acceptance signal — the counters, not the gauge

data.head: ## Acceptance signal — the counters, not the gauge

body: `tracked_fingerprints_count` is a **windowed gauge of DISTINCT fingerprints, sampled after eviction**. A fully healthy six-occurrence storm of *identical* fingerprints reads `1`, never `6`, and legitimately reads `0` once the 60s retention window closes. It cannot serve as the acceptance signal.

The latched, window-immune discriminators are **`storms_detected_total`** and **`fingerprints_evicted_total`** (both cumulative, both reset per process). `fingerprints_evicted_total ≥ 1` proves a fingerprint was tracked and later aged out, whatever the gauge reads. Detection is inline, not tick-driven — a Suggested-threshold cue fires on the occurrence that crosses it, so tick cadence is not a confound.

- **The per-service baseline bootstrap gate** (next markerless entry). No incident is required here: the storm tick fires on its own cadence and occurrences record inline, so a `ready:false` preflight is an expected, non-blocking outcome for this chunk's evidence.
- **Workspace-key alignment** app↔sidecar (third markerless entry). No corpus read-back is needed to prove this chunk.

- **Conductor-side emission.** Proven good at the wire against a real collector stub: non-empty `trace_id`+`span_id`, an `exception` event carrying non-empty `exception.type`/`.message`/`.stacktrace`, distinct span identity with one shared fingerprint, resource `service.name` present.
- **The DuckDB append-path stall** under ~10 min of sustained 10k/s storm (pre-existing chunk-#99 connection-contention class).
- **Any redesign of the storm detector's thresholds, window, or cue semantics.** This chunk restores a feed; it does not retune what consumes it.
- `crates/ingest` — OTLP receipt, post-`prost` invariant checks, mpsc hand-off. Arrival here is already **proven** by measurement (`span_count` 1→2→3→9, stable, in all three arms).

- `crates/buffer` — `consumer.rs` (holds `Option<Arc<dyn FingerprintObserver>>`), `appender.rs` (the per-span-event extraction of the three `exception.*` keys and the observer call), `fingerprint.rs` (`compute_exception_fingerprint`, which returns `None` only on a `None`/empty `exception_type`).
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — construction and wiring of `StormObserverAdapter` over `RetryStormDetector`.
- Self-observation (`tracing` only — never the product's own OTLP ports).

- No new TauRPC procedure, no new capability grant, and no new corpus table. **VERIFIED for the instrumentation half** — the counters, tick fields, and allowlist entries are entirely `tracing`-side and cross no IPC or storage boundary. The repair half remains contingent on the capture; the plan carries an arch acceptance criterion requiring any such resource to be registered in §Occupied Resources at wrap if the repair forces one.

**`PREREQ: close Rust gate deferral (deferred since 2026-07-06-incidents-panel-dropdown-layout-bug).`** This chunk is Rust-touching, so the deferral closes here. It has ridden five consecutive chunks as prose, never as a route annotation, so its age trigger never fired. Two commits (`6fbbd30`, `de00fbc`) additionally touched Rust source outside the chunk loop with no wrap gate ever run over them. Memory, not disk, is the live constraint (D: has 124.7 GB): build first at bounded parallelism under `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, then run the workspace suite. Closure means the full Rust gate set green at this chunk's wrap.

- The production observer is a real `StormObserverAdapter`, not the `NoopFingerprintObserver`, and is constructed as `Some(...)` and passed into the consumer. **VERIFIED** — `pulse-app/src/main.rs:600-604` constructs `Some(Arc::new(StormObserverAdapter::new(...)))`; `main.rs:1110` passes `fingerprint_observer.clone()` into `run_consumer`.

- ~~The dead region lies in the `buffer` crate's consumer→appender path rather than in `ingest`'s decode or hand-off.~~ **[premise-corrected: the buffer-crate path is exercised end-to-end by the existing `pulse-app/tests/e2e_storm_detection.rs` e2e (OTLP export → `run_consumer` → appender → observer → detector, asserting Suggested at the 5th and Autonomous at the 10th occurrence), so the algorithm is not the suspect; the newly-surfaced candidate is the BOOT-TIME branch `match buffer_conn` at `main.rs:1102`, whose `None` arm spawns a receiver-drain task that discards every batch]**

- ~~Nothing upstream of the per-span-event loop drops or empties span events.~~ **[premise-corrected: `main.rs:1130-1135` — the `buffer_conn == None` arm spawns `while rx.recv().await.is_some() {}`, which drains and discards every ingest batch while leaving ingest's own counter incrementing; this reproduces the measured signature exactly]**

- The three `exception.*` attributes are read from the **event's** attribute list. **VERIFIED** — `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:346-350` reads all three via `extract_string_attribute(&event.attributes, …)`.

- The mandated PII scrub does not starve the fingerprint. **VERIFIED** (closes the security extract's P3 hypothesis) — `appender.rs:358` computes the fingerprint from RAW `exception_type` + `exception_stacktrace` BEFORE the scrub at 366-367, and `exception_type` is never scrubbed at all ("class identifier, not user content").
- The canary's exception events survive ingest's post-`prost` invariant checks intact. **STILL OPEN** — not answerable by reading; it is one of the discriminations the live capture must make.

- **Marker:** 2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-14T22:35:07Z

The MCP sidecar filters incidents by a workspace key it derives as `data_dir.to_string_lossy()`
(`crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:74`), while the app stamps and filters by the
**detected project root** since P-079 (`pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs:109`). The sidecar's own comment
still asserts parity with the app — a claim that was true before P-079 and is stale now. Consequence:
`query_incident_list` returns zero rows against a corpus that holds active incidents, which is the
false-pass-as-empty condition Conductor's arm reports.

Research corrected the obvious fix. Both processes' `resolve_data_dir()` are byte-identical raw
`PathBuf::from(env)` copies, so the **fallback** branch already agrees cross-process; only the
detected-root branch diverges, where the sidecar never calls `detect` at all. And simply calling
`detect(current_dir())` in the sidecar does **not** fix Conductor's arm: Conductor spawns the sidecar
with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` propagated but **not** cwd, so the sidecar's cwd is Conductor's own repo
root — a different wrong key. The one value both sides already agree on is the data dir, which
Conductor's contract mandates propagating. So the app **publishes** its resolved key under the data dir
at boot and the sidecar **reads** it, falling back to `data_dir` when absent (operator-selected at P4).
The derivation itself still moves down into `workspace-detector` — a leaf crate with zero outbound
workspace edges and no edge either way with `mcp-server` today, so the new `mcp-server →
workspace-detector` edge cannot form a cycle (`pulse-app` depends on `mcp-server`, which is what closes
the naive import direction).

Per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns (Module dependency direction) + §Established Decisions
[Module Boundaries] for the crate home, security-plan §Input Validation (CLI / env var inputs) for the
published-file boundary, obs-plan §8 (default-deny allowlist) + the chunk-#43 `workspace.detect`
basename-only precedent for any emission, and test-plan §3 (per-chunk gate discipline + boot-smoke) for
the gates.

1. **Host the shared derivation in `workspace-detector`.** Add the workspace-key derivation to that
   crate's contract surface: given `Option<&WorkspaceContext>` and the data dir, return the key string
   and the canonical-path value the producer stamps — preserving the P-079 single-call shape so filter
   and stamp cannot drift. Do **not** re-canonicalize: `detect` already canonicalizes exactly once and
   the key is that output verbatim (see §Constraints).

2. **Add the normalization unit.** Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `workspace-detector` (a
   library crate, so co-located tests do run). Assert that two *entry forms* of the same directory —
   a raw path and its `\\?\` verbatim-prefixed form — reach **one** key through the single
   `canonicalize()` inside `detect`, and that the fallback branch yields `data_dir` on both halves.
   This closes the Windows verbatim-prefix question by construction rather than by observation on one
   host.

3. **Delegate the app side.** `pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs::resolve_workspace_for_incidents`
   delegates to the shared derivation (keeping its name and signature so the 7 existing callers and the
   P-079 contract are untouched in meaning).

4. **Publish the resolved key.** At boot, after the key is resolved (`pulse-app/src/main.rs` ~line 691),
   write it to a small file under the data dir using the atomic `.tmp`-then-rename discipline already
   used for `window-geometry.json`. Write failure is non-fatal — log a warn and continue; the sidecar's
   fallback covers it. Follow the existing `write_pid_file` shape (`pulse-app/src/main.rs:204`), which
   already creates `{data_dir}/run/`.

5. **Read it in the sidecar.** `init_incident_context` reads the published key and uses it as
   `workspace_root`, falling back to `data_dir.to_string_lossy()` when the file is absent or unreadable
   — which preserves today's behaviour exactly for a sidecar running without a live app. Delete the
   stale parity comment at lines 70–73 and replace it with one that states the real contract. Add the
   `workspace-detector` path dependency to `crates/mcp-server/Cargo.toml` if the read helper lives
   there; if the helper is a plain file read, the dependency is still needed for step 1's shared
   derivation to be callable from this crate.

6. **Observe before the fix lands.** Produce the before-evidence: seed a data dir with incidents
   (`cargo run -p ingest --example inject_demo` against a running app — ~10s warmup, then the storm
   crosses the Autonomous threshold in ~1s), then drive `query_incident_list` over the sidecar's stdio
   (both gates set — see the firing form on the `(evidence)` criteria) and record **two** numbers
   together in `evidence/before-query-incident-list.json`: the tool's `total` (expected `0`) and an
   independent read of the same corpus's incident count (expected non-zero). Both numbers are needed —
   `total: 0` alone is indistinguishable from "no incidents were created". Record **counts only**, never
   response bodies (obs-plan §11 Project-specific, Vector 4). This capture cannot survive the fix, so
   the permanent guard is step 7.

6b. **Re-run the same query after the fix.** With steps 3–5 landed, re-issue the **identical**
   invocation against the **identical** data dir and record `evidence/after-query-incident-list.json`.
   The `0 → N` pair across one unchanged command is the chunk's outcome evidence. Keep the capture data
   dir for this — recreating it changes the workspace key and voids the comparison.

7. **Add the permanent parity regression.** A test that asserts the app-published key and the
   sidecar-read key are byte-equal for a detected workspace — the assertion that survives the fix and
   fails if either side drifts again. Place it per the test-home rule: `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` if it
   reaches pulse-app internals, co-located in the library crate otherwise.

8. **Run the Conductor arm-zero leg (operator-scheduled).** With the new `buffer.tick` feed counters,
   one Conductor arm re-run names the second open mystery on sight: `span_events_seen=0` → nothing
   reached the appender; `fingerprints_computed=0` with `span_events_seen>0` → attributes lost in
   ingest; `observer_invocations=0` with `fingerprints_computed>0` → wiring. Conductor is the
   instrument: run its preflight from its own repo root, launch `pulse-app` outside that repo, and land
   **all** evidence in this chunk's folder as `evidence/arm-zero-classification.md`. Never write into
   Conductor's tree. If the arm no longer reproduces (this chunk's fix being the plausible cause),
   record that verbatim as the classification — a non-reproducing arm is a result, not a skip.

title: Order — why this chunk, not the first markerless one

data.head: ## Order — why this chunk, not the first markerless one

body:
The first markerless entry is **Baseline-family reachability**. The operator took this piece up out of
order after the `2026-08-14-fingerprint-feed-capture-repair` capture: that chunk's discovery (the storm
path is healthy at HEAD; storm→cue→incident flows in seconds on a fresh dir) flipped the value order.
Workspace-key alignment now directly unblocks Conductor's preflight-green path and owns **both** open
mysteries; Baseline-family reachability serves Epoch-3 family proofs and waits. The route line for
Baseline-family reachability stays markerless and mutable.

Two processes derive the incident workspace key differently, so the sidecar filters on a key no
incident was ever stamped with.

- **App side** — `pulse-app/src/main.rs:688-693` calls
  `pulse_app::digest_runtime::resolve_workspace_for_incidents(detected.as_ref(), &data_dir)`
  (`pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs:109`). With detection succeeding it returns
  `ctx.root.to_string_lossy()` — the **detected project root**, canonicalized by
  `workspace_detector::detect::detect` (`crates/workspace-detector/src/detect.rs:31` calls
  `candidate_root.canonicalize()`). Only on detection failure does it fall back to `data_dir`. This
  single-sourcing landed at `2026-07-05-constellation-severity-live-wiring` (P-079) so the FILTER key
  equals the STAMPED `digest.workspace`.

- **Sidecar side** — `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:74` sets
  `workspace_root = data_dir.to_string_lossy().to_string()` **unconditionally**. Its comment
  (lines 70-73) claims it "matches the main process's workspace key derivation
  (`incident_workspace_key = data_dir.to_string_lossy()` at pulse-app/src/main.rs)" — a claim that was
  true **before** P-079 and is stale now. The key flows into `IncidentToolContext.workspace_root`
  (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:73`) and is consumed by
  `.load_active_incidents(&ctx.workspace_root)` (`tools.rs:340`).
Consequence: `query_incident_list` returns zero rows against a corpus that holds active incidents.

title: The structural constraint (verified — closes the naive path)

data.head: ## The structural constraint (verified — closes the naive path)

body:
`pulse-app/Cargo.toml` declares `[dependencies.mcp-server-crate] package = "mcp-server" … optional = true`
— **pulse-app depends on mcp-server**. The sidecar importing
`pulse_app::digest_runtime::resolve_workspace_for_incidents` would therefore be a dependency **cycle**.
Single-sourcing must move the derivation DOWN to a crate both ends reach.

- `crates/mcp-server/Cargo.toml` depends on: `buffer`, `viz`, `snapshot`, `corpus`, `triage`,
  `interpretation` (+ optional `rmcp`) — **not** `workspace-detector`, **not** `pulse-app`.

- `crates/workspace-detector/Cargo.toml` depends on no sibling workspace crate (`thiserror`, `serde`,
  `strict-path`, `tracing` only) — it is already the shared detection home, so it is the natural
  candidate and adding an edge to it from `mcp-server` introduces no cycle.

**The exact home is research's design call, not pre-decided here.** P3 recorded the seam facts and they
clear the candidate: the code-graph shows `workspace-detector` has **zero outbound** workspace edges (a
leaf; inbound only from `pulse-app` and `ui-bridge`) and `mcp-server` has **no edge either way** with it
today, so `mcp-server → workspace-detector` cannot form a cycle. `WorkspaceContext` is already `pub`
through that crate's contract module and the dependency would be normal (not dev-only), so it can back a
shipped signature. P4 picks the home on those facts.

1. **OBSERVE before fixing.** Drive incidents into a data dir locally (they are creatable now — the
   storm path is healthy at HEAD per the prior chunk's capture), then read `query_incident_list`
   against that dir and record the zero-vs-nonzero result. This is the **before-evidence** the fix's
   acceptance compares against: the mismatch has only ever been DERIVED from code reading (intent F10),
   never observed. `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` exists at that path and its own header
   documents the timing: ~10s healthy warmup, then ~10 error spans/s sharing one fixed
   `exception.type`/`.stacktrace` fingerprint crosses the Autonomous storm threshold "within ~1s" →
   cue → digest → L4 → incident. The prior chunk's live capture measured 10 incidents created, so the
   ~30s order holds.

2. **One derivation, one runner, both ends agree.**
   **[premise-corrected at P5 val-1: "both processes call it" cannot work under the target topology]** —
   the derivation does move down into a crate both `pulse-app` and `mcp-server` reach, but only the app
   RUNS it. Conductor spawns the sidecar with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` propagated and **cwd NOT set**,
   so a sidecar calling `detect(current_dir())` would derive *Conductor's* repo root — a different wrong
   key, leaving the arm blocked. Instead the app publishes its resolved key under the data dir (the one
   value both sides already agree on, because Conductor's contract mandates propagating it) and the
   sidecar reads it, falling back to `data_dir` when absent. Operator-selected at P4. The sidecar's
   stale parity comment goes either way.

3. **Normalization proven, not assumed.** The app's key passes through `canonicalize()` (Windows
   returns a `\\?\` verbatim-prefixed path); the sidecar's `data_dir` is a raw env-derived string. A
   unit MUST prove the two entry forms (canonicalized vs raw) resolve to the **same** key — or the
   derivation normalizes explicitly. This closes the probe's open question **by construction** rather
   than by observation on one host.

4. **Arm-zero named.** One Conductor arm re-run under the `buffer.tick` feed counters added by
   `2026-08-14-fingerprint-feed-capture-repair` classifies the second open mystery on sight:
   `span_events_seen=0` → nothing reached the appender; `fingerprints_computed=0` with
   `span_events_seen>0` → attributes lost in ingest; `observer_invocations=0` with
   `fingerprints_computed>0` → wiring. This leg needs the operator's headful half — schedule it with
   them rather than assuming it can run unattended. (Conductor is locally reachable at
   `D:\dev\projects\conductor`; the recipe is read-only reference material there.)

- **Conductor is an INSTRUMENT here, not a session.** Run its preflight binary from its own repo root
  (`D:\dev\projects\conductor` — reachable locally); launch `pulse-app` from OUTSIDE that repo; land
  **all** evidence in THIS chunk's folder. **Never write into Conductor's tree** — its own wraps would
  meet unattributable dirt. The six-item live-leg recipe on Conductor's capture-entry CARRY is a
  **read-only** reference.

- Scope is the workspace-key derivation and its two consumers. Not in scope: the baseline-family
  reachability gate (its own markerless entry), the P-075 Conductor e2e closure (a later entry), or
  any change to how incidents are stamped by the producer.

- No new TauRPC procedure is anticipated — verified: `IncidentToolContext.workspace_root` has exactly
  ONE production consumer (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:340`), and the app side threads the key
  through existing constructors only. No IPC surface is involved.

- **[premise-corrected: the app's key is `canonicalize()`'s output kept verbatim, locked by
  `resolver_preserves_windows_extended_length_prefix`]** — the §What this chunk delivers item 3 framing
  "or the derivation normalizes explicitly" must NOT become a downstream re-canonicalization: `detect()`
  canonicalizes exactly once and the key is that output verbatim; re-canonicalizing on either side is
  the documented divergence trap the P-079 test guards. The normalization the acceptance proves is that
  two *entry forms* of the same directory (raw `C:\dev\x` and verbatim `\\?\C:\dev\x`) reach one key
  through that single `canonicalize()`.

- **[premise-corrected: the fallback branch already agrees; only the detected branch diverges]** — both
  `resolve_data_dir()` copies (`pulse-app/src/main.rs:181` and
  `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:27`) are byte-identical raw `PathBuf::from(env)`, so
  on detection failure the two processes already produce the same key. The defect is confined to the
  detected-root branch, where the sidecar never calls `detect` at all.
| Surface | Site |
| App key resolution | `pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs::resolve_workspace_for_incidents` · `pulse-app/src/main.rs:688` |
| Sidecar key resolution | `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs::init_incident_context` |
| Sidecar consumer | `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs::IncidentToolContext.workspace_root` · `tools.rs:340` |
| Detection primitive | `crates/workspace-detector/src/detect.rs` · `contract.rs::WorkspaceContext.root` |
| Corpus filter | `CorpusWriter::load_active_incidents(workspace_key)` |
| Existing regression guard | `pulse-app/tests/integration_constellation_severity_workspace_key.rs` (P-079) |

- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-10-workspace-key-divergence-probe/two-launch-verdict.md` §Re-run
  (read-only, external).

- The prior chunk's capture: `span_events_seen=936 / fingerprints_computed=936 /
  observer_invocations=936`, `storms_detected_total` 0→2, 10 incidents created — the reason incidents
  are locally creatable and the observation leg is possible at all.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-15

Make the corpus AES-256-GCM cell key survive a process boundary, and retire the content that the
per-process-ephemeral-key window orphaned.

The defect is one line of dependency configuration with a large blast radius. The workspace manifest
declares `keyring = "3"` under a comment asserting *"Default features auto-select per target"* — that
belief is false for keyring 3.x, so `Cargo.lock` resolves the crate with `[log, zeroize]` only, no
platform credential-store backend is linked, and the crate's non-persisting store hands out a **fresh
random key per process**. Measured at `2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment`: the second app process emitted
13 `decryption_failed` warnings against rows its own predecessor wrote, and `cmdkey /list` lists zero
entries. The fix restores the posture security-plan.md §Secret Management → Storage → Runtime already
mandates (keychain-primary with `PassphraseFallback`-with-warning, chunk #73 P-049) and that
architecture.md §Occupied Resources → Corpus SQLite → At-rest posture records as INTENDED-but-UNIMPLEMENTED.

Research established that **neither** intended branch executes today: the primary is served by keyring's
mock store, and `BackendKind::PassphraseFallback` is a label with no producer — `OsKeychainBackend::
backend_kind()` returns only Macos/Windows/Linux by `cfg!`, and `Corpus::open` collapses every keychain
error to `Error::KeyringUnavailable`, failing the whole open. So this chunk must make the primary real
**and** give the fallback an execution path, per directive 2.

Research also found that fixing the key alone does **not** restore the read path. `cell_decrypt(...)?`
propagates inside the row loops (`contract.rs:650, :697, :741, :775`), so a single undecryptable row makes
the **entire** query return `Err` — which is why P-075 and P-076 sit behind this whole chunk, not just its
key fix. Two operator decisions were taken at P4 on that basis: orphaned content is **inventoried then
purged** (the keyless audit artifact is written before deletion, so the record of what the ephemeral-key
window destroyed survives even though the content cannot), and the read loops are **hardened to
skip-and-count** so any future undecryptable row degrades the corpus rather than taking it dark.
Recovery of pre-fix content is cryptographically closed and is not attempted — the mock store is
process-local, so every earlier key died with its process; the 13-failure measurement IS that fact.

Provenance: security-plan.md §Secret Management + §Dependency Security · architecture.md §Occupied
Resources → Corpus SQLite → At-rest posture · obs-plan.md §6 + §8 · test-plan.md §3 + §5.

title: Step 0 — FIRST STEP: arm-zero classification (operator-gated, PRE-FIX)

data.head: ### Step 0 — FIRST STEP: arm-zero classification (operator-gated, PRE-FIX)

body:
Runs **before** any code change. The counter read is log-side and needs no decryption, so it does not
depend on this chunk's fix. Schedule the headful half **with the operator** — the agent cannot schedule it
alone.

1. Follow the recipe verbatim at
   `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/chunks/2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment/evidence/arm-zero-classification.md`.

2. Conductor is the **INSTRUMENT, not a session**: run its preflight from its own repo root
   (`D:\dev\projects\conductor`), launch `pulse-app` from **outside** that repo, propagate

3. Read the `buffer.tick` counters landed by `2026-08-14-fingerprint-feed-capture-repair` and classify on
