**Marker:** `2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage`
**Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · Epoch 4 — Polish & ship: verification
**Promoted:** 2026-08-23
> Ingestion scrub coverage — the five client-controlled columns that never reach `scrub_attribute`

CONTEXT (from the entry): measured 2026-08-22 at the `2026-08-22-pii-scrubber-recall` chunk. A **COVERAGE**
gap, distinct from the RECALL gap that chunk closed — these columns never reach the scrubber at all, and the
DuckDB ring buffer is unencrypted, so PII placed in them by an instrumented host app is stored and read in
plaintext.

SCOPE (from the entry): `security-plan.md` §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging was amended AS MEASURED at that
wrap and **NAMES THIS ENTRY as the owner of the impl half**, so this entry is load-bearing for that amendment,
not optional cleanup. `span_events.exception_type` is a separate DELIBERATE exclusion (class identifier, not
user content) and is **NOT in scope**.

NOTE (from the entry): operator-decided 2026-08-22 as a standalone entry rather than a CARRY on the
diagnostics sweep — a security-grade coverage hole should not inherit a housekeeping entry's priority.

PII scrubbing reaches the client-controlled DuckDB ring-buffer columns that currently bypass it — with the
**treatment decided per column class and justified**, not applied uniformly by default.
The deliverable is threefold:
1. **Coverage** — the columns a host app can fill with arbitrary text stop being stored verbatim.

2. **A stated per-class treatment rule** — identifier/key columns and free-text columns are handled by a rule
   the plan argues for, because the naive treatment has a measured failure mode (below).

3. **A measured RED→GREEN proof on the real OTLP path** — matching the precedent both immediately preceding
   chunks set (`pii-scrubber-recall`, `log-records-identity`): assert the leak before the fix, assert its
   absence after, at the wire rather than in a unit fixture alone.
The entry says "five columns". **Measured at HEAD the live target set is FOUR**; the fifth is vacuous.
| # | Column | Class | Write site (verified) | Consumer significance (verified) |

| 1 | `spans.service_name` | **identifier / key** | `appender.rs` — `extract_service_name(rs.resource…)` → `service_names.push` → `StringArray::from` → `Field::new("service_name")`; no `scrub_otlp_field` on the path. **[premise-corrected 2026-08-23: this is ONE of THREE consumers of a single extractor, not a single write path. `extract_service_name` (`appender.rs:107`) is called at `appender.rs:44` (→ this column), `appender.rs:359` (→ NOT a column — `span_events` has no `service_name` field; it feeds `FingerprintObserver::on_fingerprint` at `:425`) and `consumer.rs:232` (→ `SpanObserver::observe_span`, the baseline tap). Scrubbing the column alone leaves two raw paths into `triage` AND makes DuckDB disagree with the baseline/registry identity — see research.md F2]** | `GROUP BY` in Q1, Q2, Q5; `GROUP BY` **and** a JOIN-side comparison predicate (`caller.service_name != callee.service_name`) in Q4 — `crates/triage/src/baseline/sql.rs`. Also reconstructed from a composite key by `BaselineState::iter_operations` (`key.split('/').next()`, `baseline/mod.rs`). Reaches the webview via `viz::query::SELECT_TRACES` → constellation dot labels + table Service column |

| 2 | `span_events.name` | **predicate column** (not pure free text) | `appender.rs::build_span_events_record_batch` — `names.push(event.name.clone())`; `Field::new("name", …)` | `WHERE name = 'exception'` gates Q3_EXCEPTION_FINGERPRINTS (`baseline/sql.rs`) — the storm/fingerprint feed |

| 3 | `metrics_points.metric_name` | **identifier / key** | `appender.rs` — `metric_names.push(name.to_string())` → `StringArray::from` → `Field::new("metric_name")` | Corpus lookup key: `SELECT payload FROM pipeline_metrics WHERE metric_name = ?1 AND layer = ?2`, and `GROUP BY metric_name, layer` in the purge query (`crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`) |

| 4 | `log_records.severity_text` | **bounded-vocabulary text** | `appender.rs` — `severity_texts.push(log.severity_text.clone())`; `Field::new("severity_text", …)` | **VERIFIED 2026-08-23**: SELECTed by `viz::query::SELECT_LOGS` into `LogItem.severity_text` and rendered in the Logs view. Not in any PK. (The a11y not-color-alone precedent from 2026-06-10 is on the incident `ReportRenderer` path, which reads the `triage` severity enum — a different source than this column.) |
| 5 | ~~`instrumentation_scopes.scope_name` / `.scope_version`~~ | **VACUOUS at HEAD** | **none — the table has no producer** | — |

**Finding 5 (proven, not inferred):** `append_record_batch_to_table` is the only DuckDB write path in
`crates/buffer`, and it is called for exactly four tables — `spans`, `metrics_points`, `log_records`,
`span_events`. `instrumentation_scopes` appears only in DDL (`schema.rs`, both representations) and in a
retention `DELETE` (`retention.rs`). Nothing writes it, so nothing can leak through it, and a scrub attached
there would be an emitter that never fires (the producer-never-ran vacuous class — CLAUDE.md session-learning
2026-08-21). Its **disposition is a scope question for the plan**, not silent inclusion or silent omission.
`resources` is in the same never-written state (noted, out of scope).

title: The design tension this chunk must resolve (not assume)

data.head: ## The design tension this chunk must resolve (not assume)

body:
`scrub_attribute`'s stated posture is **recall over precision** — "false positives are acceptable
(over-redaction); false negatives leak secrets" (`crates/security/src/scrubber.rs`, verified). That stance was
written for **values**. Three of the four live targets are **keys or predicates**:

- A false positive on `spans.service_name` does not merely over-redact one cell — it **forks one service into
  two identities** across every `GROUP BY service_name` aggregate, the Q4 self-join, and the composite-key
  parse in `iter_operations`.

- A false positive on `metrics_points.metric_name` breaks the corpus `WHERE metric_name = ?1` lookup for that
  series.

- A false positive on `span_events.name` could disturb the `WHERE name = 'exception'` predicate that feeds the
  storm/fingerprint path.

So **"apply the same scrub everywhere" is a choice this chunk must argue for, not a default**. The plan must
state the treatment per column class and why. The candidate treatments (uniform scrub / key-safe
reject-not-rewrite / bounded-vocabulary validation / drop-and-count) are P4's decision; this scope fixes only
that the decision must be made explicitly and recorded.
**Research sharpened the tension into two decisive facts (research.md F1/F2):**

- **Only `metrics_points.metric_name` sits in a PRIMARY KEY** — `(metric_name, ts_unix_nano, resource_hash)`.
  The other three targets are outside their tables' keys. Two distinct metric names redacting to the same
  `[REDACTED:{category}]` string at the same ts + resource_hash therefore COLLIDE, and the preceding chunk
  measured that a colliding pair fails the **ENTIRE batch** at `flush()`. This is the chunk's sharpest
  constraint and the one genuine fork.

- **`service_name` has a single choke point** — scrubbing inside `extract_service_name` covers all three
  consumers consistently; scrubbing at the column alone splits identity between DuckDB and `triage`.

edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-23T14:47Z

Turn the one-press headful leg into a **scripted five-stage assembled-path e2e** that drives the real
product under deterministic-L4 and asserts, at each stage, against an observable the driver can read.
This claims **P-076** (`verification-matrix.json#P-076`) — the capability two prior chunks advanced and
explicitly declined.

The gap P-076 exists to close is intent F15's: 1886 nextest + 801 vitest + a11y all green while the
*integrated* UX was broken. Every existing gate tests a component in isolation; nothing drives
launch → telemetry → Traces → storm → incident → Investigate as one path. The predecessor
(`2026-08-23-webview-self-verify`) built the harness that can — tauri-driver + WebdriverIO under
`cargo xtask webview-drive` — but pressed exactly one control and asserted one record.

The design rests on three things research established, not assumed. **(1) Every observable already
exists.** All three acceptance assertions bind to obs records emitted at HEAD, and none needs a new
allowlist leaf — verified field-by-field (research.md §The three acceptance observables). **(2) The
storm stage needs no new fixture:** `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` is purpose-built for this
exact chain and speaks real OTLP gRPC, satisfying arch §Test-time telemetry injection's no-back-door
rule. **(3) The selector convention is mixed** — accessible names ship on the Investigate controls and
`ConnectionDot`, `data-testid` on Traces/EmptyState/footer — so the leg binds per surface to what
actually ships, per the operator decision at P5-preview (a11y-plan §1 P1's `region[aria-label=
"Telemetry traces chart"]` does not exist at HEAD and stays owned by the "A11y verification" entry).

Two disciplines from `rules/verification-harness.md` §2026-08-23 are load-bearing and shape every
stage: **match the effect record, never the target alone** (boot itself emits `ui.layout.transition`,
so a target-only match passes on a record the press did not cause), and **a green-on-arrival
regression guard MUST be mutation-checked or it guards nothing**. Every surface this leg drives works
today, so without a discriminating RED arm the whole leg is decorative.

1. **Model the leg as an ordered list of named stages** in `xtask/src/webview_drive.rs`. Each stage
   carries an id, the driver action it expects, and a **predicate over obs records** that is
   discriminating — it must match on a FIELD VALUE the stage causes, never on the target alone.
   Replace the single `is_widget_hidden_transition` boolean with a per-stage predicate set and a
   staged verdict that reports which stages passed and which did not.

2. **Extend the driver script** `pulse-app/ui/tests-e2e/webview-drive.mjs` from one press into the
   stage sequence below, reusing its existing substrate unchanged: `pollUntil` bounded polling (never
   `sleep(N)`, per test-plan §11), `findWidgetHandle`-style per-stage handle resolution (four windows
   exist and the session lands on an arbitrary one), and the `finally`-guarded `deleteSession`.
   Preserve the split: **the script drives the scenario and presses; it asserts nothing.**

3. **Stage sequence** (the operator-selected set — 3 acceptance stages + the two absorbed CARRYs that
   cost no extra driver mechanic):

   | # | Stage | Driver action | Discriminating assertion (xtask side) |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | `launch` | boot under det-L4, resolve the dashboard handle | telemetry arrival — `buffer` rows advancing, not merely a booted window |
   | 2 | `traces-empty` | navigate to Traces before injection | `[data-testid="trace-table-empty"]` present — the pre-state stage 3 needs |
   | 3 | `traces-populate` | spawn the injector; do NOT reload or re-navigate | `viz.query.traces` with **`row_count` > 0** (assertion 1 + CARRY #5: empty→populated on its own) |
   | 4 | `storm-incident` | let the injector reach its storm threshold | `interpretation.incident.created` with **`created` == true** (assertion 2) |
   | 5 | `investigate` | press `button[aria-label="Investigate"]` | `investigate.run_action.request` with **`status` == "success"** AND `deterministic_mode` == true (assertion 3) |
   | + | `empty-states` | navigate to `/metrics` and `/logs` | `metrics-empty-state` + its `-hint` present AND `metrics-error-state` absent (CARRY #7; the hint is what the error variant cannot satisfy) |

4. **The injector is spawned by the script, not by xtask.** Ordering is the reason: stage 2 must
   observe the empty table *before* any telemetry exists, and stage 3's honesty depends on the table
   populating with no driver-initiated reload. That ordering lives in the stage sequence. Spawning a
   scenario process is scenario-driving, not asserting, so the press/assert split holds. The script
   already spawns `tauri-driver` the same way; reuse that shape, including child-process cleanup on
   the `finally` path.

5. **Rework the RED arm into a stage-targeting mutation check.** The current `--expect-absent` inverts
   the whole leg. Give the mutation arm a way to name what must be absent, and add the cheap
   discriminating arm this leg's shape makes available: **an injector-suppressed run**. With no
   telemetry, stages 1–4 must ALL go red while stage 5 stays GREEN — and stage 5 staying green is not
   a guess, it is pinned by the existing
   `empty_buffer_still_yields_a_result()` (`pulse-app/tests/integration_investigate_actions.rs:104`).
   One run discriminates four stages at once and proves the telemetry-dependent stages actually
   depend on telemetry.

6. **Colocated unit tests** for every new stage predicate in `xtask/src/webview_drive.rs`'s existing
   `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (9 today), per test-plan §4. Each predicate needs both a positive case and
   a **near-miss negative** in the shape of the existing `boot_geometry_transition_is_not_a_close` /
   `dashboard_hide_is_not_the_widget_close` pair — a record with the right target but the wrong field
   value must NOT satisfy the predicate. This is where the "match the effect, not the target" rule
   becomes mechanically enforced rather than remembered.

7. **Bound every stage independently.** Per-stage timeouts inside the existing 240s
   `DRIVE_TIMEOUT`; a stage that never observes its record fails that stage and reports which, rather
   than collapsing into one opaque leg failure. Keep the GREEN-only clean-log check
   (`unhealthy_records`) scoped as it is today — test-plan §3 binds the 0-ERROR clause to the GREEN
   leg only, and the injector-suppressed RED arm is by construction an unhealthy run.
- None. The registered harness is extended, not replaced (arch §Stack — GUI verification harness).

- `xtask/src/webview_drive.rs` — stage model + per-stage discriminating predicates + staged verdict +
  stage-targeting RED arm + colocated tests. Consumes four helpers re-exported from
  `self_verify.rs` (`headless_skip_reason` / `locate_pulse_binary` / `read_log_lines` /
  `workspace_root`, `webview_drive.rs:24-26`) — prefer **additive** helpers over re-shaping those,
  since `self_verify.rs` shares them.

- `pulse-app/ui/tests-e2e/webview-drive.mjs` — stage sequence, per-stage handle resolution, injector
  spawn + cleanup. Keep it assertion-free.

- `xtask/src/main.rs` — `Cmd::WebviewDrive` (:114) + its dispatch (:177) if the CLI surface gains a
  stage/arm selector.
- `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` — no new procedure; `core:window:allow-close` already granted.
- `xtask/src/main.rs::EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` — no TauRPC procedure added.
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — **no new allowlist leaf**; all three observables already resolve.
- `pulse-app/ui/package.json` — no new dependency (WebdriverIO + tauri-driver are already devDeps).
- `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` — consumed as-is; formalizing it stays P-077's job.

- Any `pulse-app/ui/src/**` product component — the operator chose the measured-per-surface selector
  binding, so no UI code changes.

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo xtask capability-drift
cargo xtask capability-widening-check
cargo deny check bans licenses sources
cargo deny check advisories
npm run lint --prefix pulse-app/ui
npm run typecheck --prefix pulse-app/ui

cargo xtask self-verify
ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH="$ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH" cargo xtask webview-drive
```

**LIVE-LEG note (test-plan §6 + the harness rules file):** the last line is the chunk's own
acceptance and MUST FIRE, not skip. `resolve_msedgedriver` (`xtask/src/webview_drive.rs:213`) returns
`None` when the var is unset or not a file and the leg then exits 0 cleanly — so **a green exit code
alone is not evidence**. /implement records the run's own artifacts (per-stage observations, clean
shutdown, ports released) as the evidence of record. `cargo deny check advisories` is listed
separately and is **designed-red** at the 8 owned IDs — never fold it into the `bans licenses sources`
invocation (that gate is pass/fail).

**The RED mutation arm is part of this chunk's evidence, not optional:** the injector-suppressed run
(step 5) must be executed and its per-stage outcome recorded — stages 1–4 red, stage 5 green.

- **(P-076 · `verification-matrix.json#P-076`)** A tauri-driver e2e leg drives the assembled path
  under deterministic-L4 and asserts, each against a named obs record with a discriminating field
  value: **Traces render** (`viz.query.traces` `row_count` > 0), **incident creation**
  (`interpretation.incident.created` `created` == true), and **an Investigate result**
  (`investigate.run_action.request` `status` == "success"). Any stage whose record is absent fails
  the leg.

- **(Affordance criterion)** The Investigate stage presses the REAL control
  `button[aria-label="Investigate"]` (`Titlebar.tsx:128`) through the headful driver — never a
  programmatic resolver call or process proxy (per `verification-matrix-contract.md` §Affordance
  honesty).

- (tests) Every stage fails the run when its observable is absent, and the verdict is owned by the
  Rust caller, not by the press returning (per test-plan.md §6 Drivers per surface + §2 Agent-runnable
  invariants).

- (tests) The leg's evidence comes from a run that actually drove the window — recorded as the run's
  own artifacts, not the exit code, because an unset msedgedriver path yields a clean SKIP at exit 0
  (per test-plan.md §6 + §3 Direct-binary smoke variant).

- (tests) All waits are bounded polls on explicit signals with stated timeouts — zero `sleep(N)` — and
  each new stage predicate carries colocated `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests including a wrong-field-value
  near-miss (per test-plan.md §11 E2E + §4 Conventions).

- (tests) The green-on-arrival guard is mutation-checked: the injector-suppressed arm reddens stages
  1–4 while stage 5 stays green (per `rules/verification-harness.md` §2026-08-23 corollary).

- (arch) All stage telemetry enters via OTLP on `:4317`/`:4318` through `inject_demo`, with no
  in-process bypass, feature flag or mock channel (per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns →
  Test-time telemetry injection).

- (arch) The incident stage asserts coalesce-per-cue-identity `(kind, scope, scope_id)` — not
  one-incident-per-fingerprint — and binds to no `Incident.fingerprint` rendered value nor to the
  always-empty `EvidenceRefs.trace_id` / `span_ids` / `timestamps_unix_nano` (per architecture.md
  §Established Decisions → [Fault Identity]).

- (obs) Every asserted field resolves under the shipped allowlist via its target's own leaf or a
  fallback that admits it; **no new leaf is introduced**, and no bare
  `triage`/`incidents`/`corpus`/`interpretation` prefix key is added (per obs-plan.md §8).

- (obs) The GREEN leg's run-window log carries zero `app.panic.fatal` and no >45s heartbeat gap (per
  obs-plan.md §10).

title: Findings not owed to this chunk (surfaced, with owners)

data.head: ## Findings not owed to this chunk (surfaced, with owners)

body: - **`MockMetricPoint` / `MockArrowBatch` do not exist.** test-plan §3 Bootstrap item 6 mandates a `MockMetricPoint` builder in `viz`; a workspace grep for either name returns nothing. Spec-vs-reality gap → wrap amendment candidate. The chunk's OTLP producer is the sanctioned self-bootstrapping form regardless, so nothing here is blocked.

- **The `viz` fixture DDL has no drift guard** (see Conventions). This is the same class the sibling chunk found for `log_records`; it is a structural gap, not a defect this chunk introduces. Named here so a future guard chunk can act on evidence.

**Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Polish & ship: verification
**Working entry:** "metrics_points identity — two data points of one metric differing only by label set both survive ingestion, with their labels"

The `metrics_points` primary key is `(metric_name, ts_unix_nano, resource_hash)`. The table stores no
attributes column at all, so two data points of ONE metric that differ only by their label set — the
ordinary shape of any dimensioned metric (`http.server.duration{route=/a}` vs `{route=/b}`) — are
identical on all three key columns. The claim is that the pair **collides by construction**, and that the
label set is **lost outright even when a point does land**.

Unlike its sibling, this chunk starts from a **measured** failure mode rather than a theorised one.
`2026-08-22-log-records-identity` established on the real OTLP path that the Arrow `Appender` enforces the
primary key at `flush()`, that the resulting loss is **whole-batch** (not a silent per-record drop), and
that it surfaces as `tracing::error!(target: "duckdb.append", …)` with `record_rows_appended` skipped and
the broadcast emit suppressed. That mechanism is inherited as established, not re-litigated. What is NOT
inherited is whether it reproduces on the metrics builder — a different builder, a different key.

**This chunk is MEASURE-FIRST.** The qualifying measurement is end-to-end over the real OTLP path: emit
colliding metric points, then read back what the buffer holds. A schema reading demonstrates the
mechanism; it does not prove the loss.

**A premise correction remains a first-class good outcome.** If the metrics write path does not actually
collide, the finding dies and the chunk records that. Do not reshape the chunk to preserve the finding.

title: The collision has TWO sources — both in scope

data.head: ## The collision has TWO sources — both in scope

body:
**(1) Label-set collision — structural, present since the table was minted.** `collect_metric_points`
(`crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:658`) walks all five OTLP data shapes (Gauge / Sum / Histogram /
ExponentialHistogram / Summary) and calls `push_metric_row` (`:764`) with exactly
`name, p.time_unix_nano, resource_hash, value, kind`. **`p.attributes` is never read** — verified by
sweeping every `.attributes` access in the file: `:133` and `:786`/`:800` are RESOURCE attributes (hashing),
`:403-407` are span-event exception attributes. There is no metric-point attribute read anywhere. So the
label set is discarded at the push site, and two label-differing points arrive at the appender as
byte-identical key tuples.

**(2) Redacted-name collision — added 2026-08-23 by `2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage`.**
`build_metrics_record_batch` now scrubs the metric name once per metric
(`crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:163`, `scrub_otlp_field(&m.name, …)`, deliberately hoisted above the point
loop since every point of one metric shares the name). Two DISTINCT credential-shaped metric names redact
to the same placeholder, so they collide at the same `ts_unix_nano` + `resource_hash`. That chunk stated
this as an accepted, LOUD failure.

The RED measurement must exhibit **both** pairs. Source (2) is the newer and less obvious of the two, and
nothing in the codebase demonstrates it today.

`scope.md` listed "the report's statement on whether the fix generalizes to `metrics_points`" as in-scope,
and its `report.md` does not contain that statement (the sole `metric` occurrence, `report.md:44`, is the
quoted arch PK-convention text about `log_records`). The promised hand-off was not delivered, so the
generalization is established here first-hand rather than inherited. Recorded as a fact, not a grievance.

title: Premise closure (P3 — each bullet VERIFIED or premise-corrected; see `research.md`)

data.head: ## Premise closure (P3 — each bullet VERIFIED or premise-corrected; see `research.md`)

body:
- **The write path** — **VERIFIED**: production metrics writes go through `consumer::dispatch_batch`'s
  `Batch::Metrics` arm → `build_metrics_record_batch` → `append_table_traced(&guard, "metrics_points", rb)`
  (`crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:126`) → `append_record_batch_to_table` (`appender.rs:535-556`), which is
  the SAME `conn.appender()` → `append_record_batch` → `flush()` helper every other table uses. The
  sibling's flush-time enforcement therefore transfers by construction. Note `append_metrics_batch`
  (`appender.rs:585`) is `#[cfg(test)]` only and is NOT the production path.

- **The failure mode reproduces on metrics** — **VERIFIED STRUCTURALLY; the behavioural leg is still
  owed.** The rejection path is identical and constant-valued: `dispatch_batch`'s `?` propagates to the
  consumer loop's `Ok(Err(e))` arm → `tracing::error!(target: "duckdb.append", reject_reason =
  %describe_error(&e), …)` (`consumer.rs:78-83`), with `record_rows_appended` (`consumer.rs:161`) skipped
  because it sits after the append. Nothing metric-specific short-circuits it. The RED measurement still
  runs — a shared code path is not a substitute for observing the behaviour — but it is no longer the
  premise most worth being wrong about.

- **Blast radius of a key change** — **VERIFIED, and NARROWER than stated on readers, WIDER on fixtures.**
  Every production reader names its columns or keys on `ts_unix_nano` alone (`SELECT_METRICS`
  `viz/query.rs:25`; `COUNT_METRICS` `:37`; retention `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:26`), so an added
  ordinal is invisible to all of them. What the bullet under-counted: `push_metric_row` is called from
  **five** sites inside `collect_metric_points` (`appender.rs:671, 688, 705, 722, 739` — one per OTLP data
  shape), so threading the ordinal touches all five; and BOTH `viz` fixture `INSERT`s (`:526`, `:608`) name
  their columns, so a `NOT NULL` ordinal with no DEFAULT breaks both.

- **`crates/viz`'s DDL copy is structurally unguarded** — **NEWLY MEASURED, not anticipated in this
  scope.** `viz` does not depend on `buffer` (`crates/viz/Cargo.toml:9-17`), so it cannot import the DDL,
  and no test cross-checks the two. Of the three sites, only the `schema.rs` pair is pinned (by
  `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema`, `schema.rs:420`). The third must be edited by hand and nothing
  will catch a miss.

- **A duplicate-`INSERT` PK probe is NOT an available measurement** — VERIFIED: `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs`
  (~`:311`) documents that path as "observed to hang in libduckdb-sys 1.10502 on this build". The
  measurement must run through the Appender path, under an explicit timeout.

title: The design tension — named here, DECIDED in the plan

data.head: ## The design tension — named here, DECIDED in the plan

body:
**Identity half — the ordinal.** The `seq` shape generalizes mechanically and is the entry's own stated
expectation. It closes BOTH collision sources at once, and it satisfies the scrub-coverage chunk's
hand-off constraint ("whatever key shape this entry lands must keep it loud rather than reintroducing
silent loss") **by eliminating the loss rather than by keeping it loud** — with an ordinal in the key,
neither colliding pair is rejected, so there is no dropped row for a signal to be silent about. That
reading is stated explicitly here so it is not re-argued downstream.

**Label half — the entry itself calls this "the larger half".** The working entry's own title demands the
points survive *"with their labels"*, so the label question is inside the entry's remit by its own wording,
not an outside addition. It is nonetheless a materially different piece of work — it requires choosing a
representation (a JSON/`MAP` column vs a side table), and it touches the OTLP data-model coverage, the
`viz` response shape, and arch §Conventions.

**RESOLVED at P4 (operator-selected 2026-08-23): the label half CARRIES.** This chunk ships identity only.
Three options were presented — CARRY, storage-only-this-chunk (an `attributes` column written and scrubbed
but never SELECTed), and the full half through the `viz` response shape — and CARRY was selected. The
deciding evidence: P3 measured the identity half **fully separable** (the ordinal closes both collisions
without `p.attributes` ever being read), while the label half needs a representation decision spanning arch
§Occupied Resources, security's scrub remit and the `viz`/MCP response shape, with the arch extract warning
that a producer-less side table reproduces an already-named defect class. Consequence carried honestly: the
entry's stated outcome is **under-delivered until the follow-up lands**, and the CARRY must be minted at
wrap with this chunk's evidence attached (see the silent-loss paragraph below).

**A second decision, taken at the same gate: the `redactions_applied` fold moves IN-CHUNK.** This was not
in the entry and not in this scope as first written — P3 measured it. `state.record_redactions(…)` fires
*inside* all four builders (`crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:73`, `:184`, `:273`, `:468`), i.e. before
`append_table_traced` can fail, so a rejected batch counts cells that never persisted and obs-plan §5's
persisted-cells-only rule does not hold. Pre-existing and common to all four builders, so not this chunk's
defect — but this chunk discovers it and owns the harness that proves it, and the operator selected fixing
it here over CARRYing it to the Diagnostics sweep. The fold moves to each table's own post-append site.
**Sequencing consequence:** the RED measurement must run at HEAD *before* this fix, or the over-count can
no longer be witnessed.

The decision carries one consequence that must be stated wherever it lands: **the ordinal makes the label
loss SILENT — but only in the log, because it is already silent to the user.** P3 measured the
user-facing half and it corrects this scope's first framing. Today a label-differing pair fails the whole
batch loudly at ERROR *in the log sink*; the Metrics view sees nothing of it, because a rejected batch is
not a query error — `viz.query.metrics` succeeds and returns zero rows, so `MetricsRoute.tsx` falls to its
empty branch and renders "No metrics received yet" plus an exporter hint naming the very ports the user is
already exporting to successfully. The error-before-empty rule is correctly implemented and structurally
cannot help, since no rejection signal reaches the frontend.

So the fix does not convert a loud symptom into a silent one at the surface the user actually looks at —
that surface is misleading *today*, and the fix makes it correct (both rows land and render). What the fix
removes is the LOG-side ERROR. After it, both rows land carrying no labels and indistinguishable from one
another, with nothing anywhere announcing that a dimension was dropped. Nothing is newly lost — the labels
were never stored — but the last remaining signal goes quiet. If the label half becomes a CARRY, that CARRY
must be minted with this evidence attached.

**Expect to claim NOTHING in the 0.3.0 matrix, and that is the correct outcome** (operator directive,
verified above by sweeping all 22). The coverage gate no-ops; proof lives in the tests and the report, as
at both preceding chunks. **Do not hunt for a capability to attach this to.** If P3 concludes a 0.3.0 entry
is genuinely warranted, surface it to the operator — never mint one silently.

- **PREREQ — `cargo audit` standing deferral (pin #7).** Ratified 2026-08-16, origin
  `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence`, every-3rd-wrap re-run INTERVAL. Probe points ran at sessions 25, 28,
  31, and **DISCHARGED at 34** (2026-08-23: probe RAN, exit read DIRECTLY as `1`, first diagnostic line
  reproduced byte-identical). **Next point is 37; this chunk's wrap is session 35 — BETWEEN points**, so
  the ratified form applies: record `probe skipped per ratified interval (next: 37)`, never a silent skip,
  and still re-verify basis + overlap. Basis is UNCHANGED and upstream (`parse error: duplicate advisory
  ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244` — no repo change can clear it). Overlap `cargo deny check advisories` stands at
  **eight** owned upgradeable IDs — 0189/0190/0194/0195/0204/0222/0253 plus RUSTSEC-2026-0258 (`h2` 0.4.14,
  safe upgrade `>=0.4.16`) — owned by the Advisory-backlog entry and **never ignore-listed**. A
  probe-auto-satisfy SIGNATURE was recorded at 34 (exit 1 + that exact diagnostic line + overlap green at
  the eight).

- **NOTE (from the working entry) — do not conflate with the scrub chunk.** `metrics_points.metric_name`
  was named in "Ingestion scrub coverage" as an un-scrubbed column; that is a related table and an
  **unrelated defect**, and it COMPLETED 2026-08-23. What this entry inherits from it is one constraint,
  addressed under "The design tension" above.

**In scope:** the `metrics_points` primary key and the `seq` ordinal the fix requires, in all three DDL
representations (`schema.rs` const + live concat, and the unguarded `viz/query.rs` fixture copy); the
end-to-end measurement that BOTH colliding pairs (label-set and redacted-name) survive — including the
small OTLP **producer** that measurement requires, modelled on the sibling's
`crates/ingest/examples/inject_colliding_logs.rs`; confirmation that the whole-batch failure mode
reproduces on the metrics builder before any fix; **the `redactions_applied` fold moving to each table's
post-append site across all four builders** (P4 decision above); regression coverage in `buffer`, including
a DIRECT unit assertion for both ordinal allocators so open trigger
`buffer-log-seq-allocator-unit-coverage` is closed rather than re-minted; a mutation check proving the new
pins discriminate; the generalization statement the sibling promised and did not deliver; the label-half
decision with its silent-loss consequence recorded.

**Out of scope:** **the label half's IMPLEMENTATION** — no attributes/labels column, no `viz` response-shape
change, no UI (P4 decision: CARRY, to be minted at wrap with this chunk's evidence); the `log_records` and
`spans` identity work (both settled); the span-side drop-observability CARRY (owned by the "Diagnostics
un-muting + harness-truth sweep" entry); the three producer-less tables (`resources`,
`instrumentation_scopes`, `span_links`) and their dead retention DELETEs (same sweep entry); a drift guard
for the `viz` fixture DDL (recorded for a future guard chunk — closing it would add a `viz → buffer`
dependency edge for a test fixture); the missing `MockMetricPoint` factory that test-plan §3 mandates
(surfaced for wrap to disposition); the Advisory-backlog upgrades (own entry); a 0.3.0 matrix mint
(operator-surfaced only); any corpus-side change — the corpus `pipeline_metrics` table is a
product-internal namespace in a DIFFERENT database and is explicitly not this table.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-23T10:35Z

A metric data point's label set survives ingestion and reads back, so two data points of one metric that
differ only by their labels stop arriving indistinguishable. This is the declared other half of
`2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`: that chunk gave the pair a `seq` ordinal so both rows persist, but
`metrics_points` stores no attributes column and `push_metric_row` takes no attributes parameter, so both
rows land label-less. Identity closed; information loss open — and *made silent*, because the whole-batch
`duckdb.append` ERROR was the only signal the dimension was being dropped.

The representation is the decision, and it is settled by operator ruling at the P4 gate: **a scrubbed
`labels` column on `metrics_points`**, keys stored verbatim and values passed through
`security::scrubber::scrub_attribute`. Both alternatives were weighed and declined (see §Constraints &
rejected approaches). The deciding fact is measured, not assumed: read-back is the **only witness of any
kind** this project has — `MetricsChart` aggregates only `ts_unix_nano` and `value` into time buckets and
there is no metrics table, legend, or per-row surface anywhere in the webview — so a representation whose
read-back is opaque could not be shown to work at all. The proof therefore lives entirely Pulse-side;
verified first-hand at Conductor HEAD `fb8a8a5`, no external witness exists (`conductor-emit` has no metrics
module and a grep for the metrics symbols across all 9 conductor crates returns zero files).

The work rides infrastructure that already exists. `build_metrics_record_batch` already returns
`Result<Option<(RecordBatch, u64)>, Error>` and `dispatch_batch` already folds that tally at the
`metrics_points` post-append site, so the new scrub joins the persisted-cells-only path with no
restructuring (per obs-plan §5). Ingest already bounds data-point attributes at 128 per point, 256 B per key
and 4096 B per value (`crates/ingest/src/invariants.rs`), so the bound half is inherited rather than built
(per security-plan §Input Validation). Per architecture.md §Conventions → Primary key convention the key
stays the settled four columns — `labels` is **not** part of it — and per §Cross-cutting Patterns →
Test-time telemetry injection the RED and GREEN legs both run over the real OTLP receiver.

1. **Add the `labels` column to all THREE DDL representations.** `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:70` (the
   per-table `CREATE_METRICS_POINTS` const) and `:168` (the concatenated `SCHEMA_DDL`) are forced to agree by
   `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema`; `crates/viz/src/query.rs:481` is a third, structurally
   unguarded copy (`viz` has no `buffer` dep). Column is `labels VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, `snake_case`,
   `NOT NULL` with an empty-string default because a data point with no attributes is the ordinary case and
   the OTLP-spec-optional rule reserves nullability for genuinely absent spec fields (per architecture.md
   §Conventions → Nullable patterns / Database entity naming). **The PRIMARY KEY is unchanged.**

2. **Centralise the label encoding, and scrub the JOINED form.** One crate-internal helper in
   `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` turns a `&[KeyValue]` into the stored string: stable ordering so two points
   with the same label set encode identically, each pair rendered `key=value`, pairs joined by a separator,
   empty attribute set ⇒ empty string. Non-string `AnyValue` variants need a defined rendering — take the
   shape `extract_string_attribute` (`appender.rs:364`) implies and define the rest explicitly rather than by
   accident.

   **The scrub input is the joined `"{key}={value}"` string, NOT the bare value** — this is load-bearing and
   was corrected at the P5 review. `scrub_attribute` (`crates/security/src/scrubber.rs:41`) takes
   `value: &str` and matches the catalog against that one string, but **two of the eight arms require the key
   name to be inside it**: `secret_kv` is `(?i)(password|passwd|secret|token)[\s=:]+\S+` (`:83`) and `api_key`
   is `(?i)(api[_\-]?key|access[_\-]?token|secret[_\-]?key|auth[_\-]?token)[\s=:]+[\w\-]{12,}` (`:77`). A
   label `{password: "hunter2"}` presents only `hunter2` to a value-only scrub and matches **nothing** — the
   whole keyed class would leak while only bare-shape values (the eighth arm) were caught.

   **Evaluate the union — joined form first, then the bare value; redact if EITHER matches.** No arm in the
   catalog uses `^` or `$` (verified), so joining with `=` is a superset in practice for the `\b`-anchored arms
   (`provider_key`, `credit_card`, `ssn`) as well; the union is cheap insurance that stays correct if an
   anchored arm is ever added. On a `Redacted { category }` verdict the pair is reconstructed as
   `{key}=[REDACTED:{category}]` — **the key stays verbatim**, preserving the operator ruling, because
   `ScrubbedValue::Redacted` carries a category and no content, so the key comes from the `KeyValue` we already
   hold. Over-redaction when the KEY alone trips the match (`password=1`) is accepted per the catalog's stated
   recall-over-precision posture (`scrubber.rs:56-58`).

3. **Thread `p.attributes` through the collector.** `collect_metric_points` (`appender.rs:667`) holds `p` in
   scope in all five OTLP arms — Gauge(0) / Sum(1) / Histogram(2) / ExponentialHistogram(3) / Summary(4) —
   and passes it nowhere today. Each arm forwards `&p.attributes`; `push_metric_row` (`appender.rs:768`)
   takes the encoded label string and pushes it onto a new parallel `Vec<String>`. Note the **cardinality
   difference from the metric name**: `metric_name` is scrubbed once per metric (`appender.rs:158-160`, "every
   point of one metric shares the name"), whereas labels are scrubbed **per data point**.

4. **Extend the record batch.** In `build_metrics_record_batch` (`appender.rs:141`) add the 7th `Vec`, build a
   `StringArray`, add `Field::new("labels", DataType::Utf8, false)` as the 8th schema field, and add the array
   to the `RecordBatch::try_new` column list in the same position. The existing `redactions_applied`
   accumulator and its `Ok(Some((record_batch, redactions_applied)))` return need no structural change — the
   label scrub simply adds to it. **`crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` is expected to need no edit**: the fold at
   `consumer.rs:131-137` is already per-table and already post-append.

5. **Widen the read path.** Add `labels` to `SELECT_METRICS` (`crates/viz/src/query.rs:24`), to the
   `query_map` row extraction (`:232-237`), and as a field on `MetricRow` (`:81`). `MetricRow` already derives
   `Serialize + Deserialize + specta::Type`, so the field crosses the TauRPC bridge and widens the MCP
   `query_metrics` response with no edit to `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` (its `dispatch_query_metrics`
   serialises the whole `viz` response at `:256`). The same `RecordBatch` is encoded onto
   `pulse://stream/metrics` by `broadcast::encode_metrics` (`consumer.rs:133`), so the column reaches the live
   stream automatically — no opt-out, worth confirming it does not break the stream decoder.

6. **Reconcile the crate-local companions the change lands on.**
   - `redaction_counter_folds_once_per_batch_across_all_four_builders` (`appender.rs:1177`) — its NAME states
     "four builders"; a fifth scrub site inside an existing builder means its scope claim must be reconciled
     (the builder count is still four; the scrub-site count is not).
   - `metrics_points_primary_key_includes_seq_ordinal` (`schema.rs:402`) — asserts the PK is exactly 4
     columns; adding a non-key column must leave it green.
   - `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema` (`schema.rs:462`), `build_metrics_record_batch_extracts_value_and_kind`
     (`appender.rs:1592`), `query_metrics_returns_seeded_rows` / `query_metrics_populates_value_and_kind`
     (`query.rs:934,955`), and the `consumer.rs` pair `dispatch_folds_redactions_after_a_successful_append` /
     `dispatch_folds_no_redactions_when_the_append_is_rejected` (`:614,:645`), which test-plan §4 records as
     discriminating only as a pair.

7. **Add the in-crate `buffer` pins** (test-plan §4 requires the new boundary pinned in-crate, not only
   cross-crate — a new public `buffer` boundary shipping unpinned mints a tracked gap, the
   `2026-08-22-log-records-identity` precedent):
   - a label-differing data-point pair persists **and reads back distinguishably**;
   - **both credential classes redact, and the KEY survives in both** (the operator ruling made visible as a
     pin): the **keyed class** `{password: "hunter2"}` → `password=[REDACTED:secret_kv]`, which is the case a
     value-only scrub misses entirely; and the **bare class** `{route: "sk_live_…"}` →
     `route=[REDACTED:provider_key]`;
   - a **negative control**: a benign pair such as `{route: "checkout"}` survives byte-identical, so the pin
     proves selectivity rather than blanket redaction — and an ordinary high-entropy identifier (a hex digest
     or UUID, drawn from the scrubber's own false-positive corpus per test-plan §4 → security crate) stays
     `Allowed`;
   - an empty attribute set stores the empty string and does not regress the existing pins.
   Fixtures self-bootstrap via OTLP ingest or per-test in-memory DuckDB — **do not** reach for
   `MockMetricPoint::builder()`, which test-plan §7 records as specified-but-unimplemented (0 workspace hits,
   measured 2026-08-23).

8. **Extend the live-leg producer with a credential-shaped label VALUE.**
   `crates/ingest/examples/inject_colliding_metrics.rs` is the predecessor's witness and **already emits the
   label-differing pair** (its case (a): one metric, two points differing only by attribute set, with a clean
   metric name deliberately chosen "or the redaction count stops being readable"). Its
   `point(ts, value, label: Option<(&str, &str)>)` helper makes the addition small. Add **two** label canaries,
   not one — a RED leg carrying only a bare `sk_live_` value would pass while the keyed class leaks:
   - **keyed class** — `{password: "hunter2"}` (or another `secret_kv` / `api_key` key name). Value-only
     scrubbing misses this; joined-form scrubbing catches it. This is the case that discriminates the two
     designs.
   - **bare class** — `{route: "sk_live_…"}`, caught by the eighth arm either way.
   Keep the existing cases — case (b) still guards the name-collision fix, and the control metric still proves
   selectivity. Follow the file's own stated discipline: **build outside any timed section and invoke the
   binary by path**, because a `cargo run` inside a timeout spends the budget compiling and sends nothing.

9. **Measure RED before GREEN on the real OTLP path**, Direct-binary smoke variant, each leg on its OWN fresh
   `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`. RED at HEAD: the label-differing pair reads back **indistinguishable** (both
   rows present since the identity chunk, both label-less). GREEN after: the pair reads back with distinct
   labels, `redactions_applied` advances for the credential-shaped label value, and the canary literal is
   absent from the log. The 0-`ERROR` / 0-`app.panic.fatal` clean-log assertion binds the **GREEN leg only**.
   Note the contrast with the predecessor: **this RED leg is expected to be ERROR-free as well**, because the
   defect is information loss, not a rejected batch — so the RED evidence here is the *read-back content*
   (two rows, no labels), not a `duckdb.append` ERROR.

10. **Mutation-check the new pins.** Neutralise the label scrub → the redaction pin must redden; drop the
    `labels` column from the SELECT → the distinguishability pin must redden. A pin that stays green under its
    own mutation is not a guard.

11. **Regenerate the TauRPC bindings LAST** and verify the STAGED copy. The `MetricRow` change alters
    `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`; the clobber has now recurred seven times, and any default-features
    cargo op after the regen silently reverts it. Regenerate after every cargo gate, then gate the commit on
    `git show :pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` carrying the mcp shape, per `.claude/rules/security.md`
    2026-06-12.

- None. (The operator ruling on the representation means no new table and therefore no new DDL file, no new
  producer, and no `retention.rs` change.)
- `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` — `labels` column in DDL sites 1 (`:70`) and 2 (`:168`); PK untouched.

- `crates/viz/src/query.rs` — DDL fixture copy (`:481`), `SELECT_METRICS` (`:24`), row mapping (`:232-237`),
  `MetricRow` (`:81`).

- `crates/ingest/examples/inject_colliding_metrics.rs` — the live-leg witness; add the credential-shaped
  label-VALUE case via its existing `point(ts, value, label)` helper, keeping cases (a), (b) and the control.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` — regenerated (not hand-edited).

- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` — **expected NO change**; listed because its test pair pins the fold this
  change feeds.

- `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` — **expected NO change**; listed because the MCP response shape widens
  through it.

**Graph impact** (rust plane, `db_state: fresh`, 10 rows): the write-side caller set is one closed in-crate
chain — `consumer/dispatch_batch() @ consumer.rs:131` → `appender/append_metrics_batch()` →
`appender/build_metrics_record_batch()` → `appender/collect_metric_points() @ appender.rs:681-748` (5 sites) →
`push_metric_row`, plus the test caller
`appender/tests/redaction_counter_folds_once_per_batch_across_all_four_builders() @ appender.rs:1229`. Zero
cross-crate blast radius on the write side; the read side is reached by DTO shape, not by call edge.

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'package(buffer) or package(viz)'
cargo xtask capability-drift
cargo xtask capability-widening-check
npm run lint --prefix pulse-app/ui
npm run typecheck --prefix pulse-app/ui
npm run test --prefix pulse-app/ui
cargo deny check bans licenses sources
cargo deny check advisories

# --- LIVE LEG (run TWICE: once at HEAD = RED, once after the fix = GREEN) ---
# Build the producer OUTSIDE the timed section and invoke it BY PATH — a `cargo run`
# inside a timeout spends the budget compiling and sends nothing (the example's own rule).
cargo build -p ingest --example inject_colliding_metrics

# ONE exported data dir per leg, shared by boot/logs/cleanup within that leg.
# A second `$(mktemp -d)` would put boot and the log read in DIFFERENT dirs.
export ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot
./target/debug/examples/inject_colliding_metrics
# Read the DATE-SUFFIXED family, never the bare name: the sink is a daily roller, and
# `agent-run.sh logs` is a known bare-name reader that silently finds nothing
# (.claude/rules/verification-harness.md 2026-06-29).
cat "$ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR"/logs/agent-latest.jsonl*
bash scripts/agent-run.sh cleanup
```

`cargo deny check advisories` is listed SEPARATELY from `bans licenses sources` and is **designed-RED** at the
eight owned IDs — never fold the two into one invocation (`.claude/rules/security.md` 2026-08-17).
`agent-run.sh status` is deliberately **not** a gate — it exits 0 against a dead system (test-plan §3).

**`cargo xtask self-verify` OMITTED — recorded skip, not a silent pass.** The modify-set contains one frontend
path (`pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`), so the UI-gate heuristic fires. It is skipped with cause: that
file is a GENERATED type declaration, not a rendered surface — this chunk builds no UI (see §Constraints), so
the self-verify's frontend-meaningful half (a11y / contrast / render against the built UI) has no subject that
changed. The substantive frontend coverage is the three `--prefix pulse-app/ui` gates above, which
test-plan §3 requires whenever a `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched and which include `tsc --noEmit` over the
regenerated bindings. No boot-path in the modify-set either (test-plan §3's trigger list is

body: - **Coverage set** is now **FIVE** persisted client-controlled cells (the four above + `metrics_points.labels`). Still NOT covered, by construction and unchanged: `instrumentation_scopes.*` (no producer), `span_events.exception_type` (deliberate exclusion — class identifier).

Labels use neither: they scrub the **JOINED `key=value` form, unioned with the bare value**, because `secret_kv` (`scrubber.rs:83`) and `api_key` (`:77`) are key-name-anchored and are **structurally unreachable on a split value**. Keys are stored verbatim; only the value becomes `[REDACTED:{category}]`.

- **Stated failure mode of the treatment:** over-redaction when the KEY alone trips a match (`password=1` redacts a benign value), accepted per the catalog's own recall-over-precision posture (`scrubber.rs:56-58`). Two distinct keys never collapse into one placeholder — the key survives — so the collision class the predecessor chunk closed is **not** reintroduced.
- **Ring buffer remains UNENCRYPTED** — write-boundary redaction is the control, unchanged.

1. **Step order inverted deliberately.** Producer extension (Step 8) and the RED leg (Step 9) ran BEFORE Steps 1–7, because Step 9 requires the measurement at HEAD. Stated at the time, not silently reordered. Justification: the plan's own text mandates "RED at HEAD".

My Q2 dialogue card had asserted the opposite. The ruling survived unchanged; the MECHANISM changed. Consequence beyond the encoder: the live-leg producer needed **two** canary classes (keyed + bare), since a RED leg carrying only a bare `sk_live_` value would have passed while the keyed class leaked.

Nothing else on the read side inspects labels: `MetricsChart` aggregates only `ts_unix_nano` and `value` into time buckets (`MetricsChart.tsx:180-195`), and `MetricsRoute` renders the chart or an `EmptyState`. **There is no metrics table, legend, or per-row surface in the webview.**

body: - **Depth:** moderate · **Reads:** 14 · **Globs/Greps:** 11 · **Graph queries:** 1 (rust plane, `db_state: fresh`, 10 rows)
- `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` (`:141-231` builder, `:354-362` scrub helper, `:667-787` collect/push, `:789-802` `hash_resource`) — the whole metrics write path.
- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` (`:105-160`) — `dispatch_batch`, the per-table post-append fold site.

- `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` (`:70-79` per-table const, `:168-177` concatenated, `:96-115` `resources`/`instrumentation_scopes`, `:399-430` PK pin, `:462` DDL sync test) — DDL sites 1 and 2 + their guards.
- `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs` (`:22-36` `DELETE_BY_CUTOFF`, `:369-372` drift guard) — the sweep and the guard a new table would trip.
- `crates/viz/src/query.rs` (`:24-27` `SELECT_METRICS`, `:81-88` `MetricRow`, `:199` `query_metrics`, `:223-240` row mapping, `:481-490` fixture DDL) — DDL site 3 + the read surface.
- `crates/ingest/src/invariants.rs` (`:9-11` bounds, `:107-135` metric arms, `:169-190` `validate_attributes`) — the pre-buffer attribute bound.
- `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` (`:240-260`) — `dispatch_query_metrics`.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/metrics/MetricsChart.tsx` + `use-metrics.ts` + `routes/MetricsRoute.tsx` — the webview read path.
- `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/` (`pa11y/pa11y-ci-config.json`, `helpers/mock-tauri.ts`, `helpers/v02-fixtures.ts`) — the audited-route set.
- `xtask/src/main.rs` (`:1001-1078`) — what `capability-drift` actually diffs.

- **`push_metric_row` / `collect_metric_points` / `build_metrics_record_batch`** — the caller set is a single closed chain inside one crate: `consumer/dispatch_batch()` (`consumer.rs:131`) → `appender/append_metrics_batch()` → `appender/build_metrics_record_batch()` → `appender/collect_metric_points()` (5 call sites, `appender.rs:681-748`, one per OTLP data kind) → `push_metric_row`. The only other caller is the test `appender/tests/redaction_counter_folds_once_per_batch_across_all_four_builders()` (`appender.rs:1229`).

- **Meaning for the change:** zero cross-crate blast radius on the WRITE side — the threading is entirely `crates/buffer`. The read side is reached by DTO shape, not by call edge, so it does not appear in this query (see Caller threading below).

- **Return-and-fold, already in place for metrics** (`appender.rs:144`, `consumer.rs:131-137`): `build_metrics_record_batch` returns `Result<Option<(RecordBatch, u64)>, Error>` and `dispatch_batch` calls `state.record_redactions(redactions)` *after* `append_table_traced(&guard, "metrics_points", rb)?`. **This answers the obs extract's research question: the metrics builder already routes its tally the required way.** A label scrub adds to the existing `redactions_applied` accumulator inside the same builder; no restructuring is needed and `consumer.rs` likely needs no edit at all.

- **Scrub cardinality differs between name and label** (`appender.rs:158-160`): the metric name is scrubbed **once per metric** with the explicit comment "every point of one metric shares the name". Label sets are **per data point**, so a label scrub fires inside the point loop — a different call rate and a different contribution to the tally.

- **Six parallel `Vec` columns + a `seq` block** (`appender.rs:146-195`): the builder accumulates six `Vec`s, then reserves one `seq` block per batch (`state.reserve_metric_seq_block(len)`) and zips them into a 7-field Arrow schema. A label column is a 7th `Vec` and an 8th `Field`.

- **The Arrow batch is also the broadcast payload** (`consumer.rs:133`): `broadcast::encode_metrics(&rb)` encodes the *same* `RecordBatch` onto `pulse://stream/metrics`. A new column therefore reaches the live stream automatically — no separate wiring, but also no opt-out.

- **`scrub_otlp_field(value, &mut redactions) -> String`** (`appender.rs:354-362`) is the reusable push-site scrub: `Allowed` passes through, `Redacted { category }` increments and yields `[REDACTED:{category}]`.

- **`hash_resource` is keys-only and toolchain-unstable** (`appender.rs:789-802`): it hashes `kv.key` for each resource attribute plus `dropped_attributes_count` through `DefaultHasher` — never a value. Confirms the scope's cautionary reading of the precedent.

- **Three DDL representations must move together** — `schema.rs:70` (per-table const) and `schema.rs:168` (concatenated `SCHEMA_DDL`) are forced to agree by `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema` (`schema.rs:462`); `crates/viz/src/query.rs:481` is a third, **structurally unguarded** copy (`viz` has no `buffer` dep). Same three-site shape the identity chunk handled.

- **PK/column assertions go through `information_schema`** — `metrics_points_primary_key_includes_seq_ordinal` (`schema.rs:402-430`) reads `key_column_usage` rather than probing with a duplicate INSERT (a documented hang on this build).

- **Ingest already bounds attributes** (`invariants.rs`): `MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_SPAN = 128` is enforced per metric data point in every arm, and `validate_attributes` bounds `MAX_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_BYTES = 256` and `MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES = 4096`. **This answers the security extract's research question: data-point attribute count and per-key/value size are already bounded before `buffer::Appender`.** The chunk inherits the bound rather than adding one — but 128 labels × 4096 B is the per-point worst case a storage shape must tolerate.

- **`capability-drift` keys on procedure NAMES only** (`xtask/src/main.rs:1070-1078`): `parse_bindings` extracts the `ARGS_MAP` keys from `bindings.ts` and set-diffs them against `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` (a list of name strings). **This answers the arch extract's research question and verifies the scope premise** — a DTO field change cannot move that set. (The gate still runs unconditionally per test-plan §3; it simply will not fire on this.)
- None required by the carriage/persistence/read-back path. (A new reserved table, if P4 chooses the side-table shape, lands as DDL inside the existing `schema.rs` — not a new file.)
- `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` — DDL sites 1 + 2; **companions:** `metrics_points_primary_key_includes_seq_ordinal` and `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema` pin this artifact's data/shape.

- `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` — `build_metrics_record_batch` (7th `Vec`, 8th `Field`, label scrub inside the point loop), `collect_metric_points` (all 5 arms must forward `p.attributes`), `push_metric_row` (new parameter); **companions:** `redaction_counter_folds_once_per_batch_across_all_four_builders` (`:1177` — its NAME states "four builders" and its scope claim is reconciled by adding a fifth scrub site inside an existing builder), `build_metrics_record_batch_extracts_value_and_kind` (`:1592`).

- `crates/viz/src/query.rs` — DDL fixture copy (`:481`), `SELECT_METRICS` (`:24`), `MetricRow` (`:81`), the `query_map` row mapping (`:232-237`); **companions:** `query_metrics_returns_seeded_rows` (`:934`), `query_metrics_populates_value_and_kind` (`:955`).

- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` — **expected NO change** (the fold already exists per table); **companions:** `dispatch_folds_redactions_after_a_successful_append` (`:614`) + `dispatch_folds_no_redactions_when_the_append_is_rejected` (`:645`), which test-plan §4 records as discriminating only as a pair.

- `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs` — **only if P4 picks a side table**: `DELETE_BY_CUTOFF` is a fixed `[&str; 7]` and the drift guard at `:369-372` iterates `RESERVED_TABLES`, so a new table must be added to the sweep or to `RETENTION_EXCLUDED_TABLES` or the guard trips.

- `crates/ingest/examples/inject_colliding_metrics.rs` — **added at P4 after this list was first written.** The live-leg witness the predecessor chunk built; it ALREADY emits the label-differing pair (its case (a): one metric, two points differing only by attribute set, deliberately given a clean metric name "or the redaction count stops being readable"), plus case (b) two credential-shaped NAMES and a control metric. This chunk extends it with a credential-shaped label VALUE via its existing `point(ts, value, label: Option<(&str, &str)>)` helper. Its doc comment carries the invocation discipline: build outside any timed section, invoke the binary by path, because a `cargo run` inside a timeout spends the budget compiling and sends nothing. **The live leg is NOT `agent-run.sh run`** — that verb is `cargo nextest run --workspace` per `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` §5-command discipline.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` — regenerated by the `MetricRow` change (the 7×-recurring clobber applies; regenerate last, verify the staged copy).
- `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` — **expected NO change**: `dispatch_query_metrics` (`:256`) serializes the whole `viz` response, so a new `MetricRow` field widens the MCP response with no edit.

**Seam facts:** the type crossing the package boundary is `MetricRow` (`crates/viz`, `serde::Serialize + Deserialize + specta::Type`), consumed by `crates/mcp-server` (normal dep, shipped code) and by the webview through generated bindings. `viz` has **no `buffer` dependency** — that is why its DDL copy is structurally unguarded, and closing that by adding a dep is an arch-DAG contract question, not a convenience (arch extract, §Constraints).

**The load-bearing equality:** the design needs *"two data points of one metric that differ only by label set read back distinguishably"*. Verified this is decided at exactly one place — `SELECT_METRICS`'s column list (`query.rs:24`) and the `MetricRow` it fills. Nothing else on the read side inspects labels: `MetricsChart` aggregates only `ts_unix_nano` and `value` into time buckets (`MetricsChart.tsx:180-195`), and `MetricsRoute` renders the chart or an `EmptyState`. **There is no metrics table, legend, or per-row surface in the webview.**

- **Representation — a scrubbed label column on `metrics_points` vs a side table.** → blocks: **plan-decision**. Research supplies the evidence but not the verdict: the side-table shape's only in-schema instance (`resources`) is producer-less and dead, and a new table trips the retention drift guard; a hashed key over label content is barred by security-plan's content-independent-discriminator rule unless computed over already-scrubbed values, and would be **opaque at the only witness surface that exists** (see below). P4 resolves with the operator.

- **Label KEY disposition — scrubbed like values, or allowed as bounded identifiers?** → blocks: **plan-decision**. Keys are client-controlled and already bounded at 256 B, but the scrub mandate is written for VALUES. obs bars keys from telemetry either way, so this is purely a storage question.

- **Does anything render labels in the webview?** → blocks: **implementation-scope**. Measured: no. `MetricsChart` uses two fields; the a11y mock returns `"metrics.query": { items: [], … }` (`mock-tauri.ts:79`), so the `/metrics` route — which **is** in the audited set (`pa11y-ci-config.json:15`, `axe/p13-empty-states.spec.ts`) — renders only its empty state during audits and has no populated metrics fixture at all. So a label field changes nothing the a11y chain can see, and the design/layouts/a11y constraints stay dormant unless P4 elects to build a UI surface — which the directive does not ask for (it names the e2e read-back as the proof).

title: Intent (from the working entry, verbatim outcome)

data.head: ## Intent (from the working entry, verbatim outcome)

body:
> A metric point's label set survives ingestion and reads back, so dimensioned metrics stop
> arriving indistinguishable.

This is the declared other half of `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`. That chunk's own working
entry asked for survival *"with their labels"* and delivered survival ONLY, by operator decision at
its phase P4 gate. Identity is closed; **information loss is open**, and closing identity made the
loss SILENT — pre-fix the colliding pair failed the whole batch with a `duckdb.append` ERROR, which
was the only signal the dimension was being dropped.

A metric data point's attribute set (its label set) is carried from the OTLP payload through the
appender into the ring buffer, scrubbed at the write boundary, and is readable back out — so two
data points of one metric differing only by label set are distinguishable in the stored row and in
what a reader gets back.

**The representation is the decision, and it is deferred to P4** (the operator directive asks for
the schema's own precedent to be reused or explicitly declined). Two shapes are on the table:
a hashed label-set key (cheap identity, opaque read-back) vs stored label pairs (real read-back,
scrub surface grows). See §Representation precedent below — the evidence is already gathered.

- **In scope:** the label half only — carriage, persistence, scrub, and read-back of a data point's
  attribute set.

- **Out of scope:** identity/PK work (landed at `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`; the `seq`
  ordinal and the 4-column PK are not revisited). Resource-level attributes (`resource_hash`) are a
  *different* attribute set and are not being changed — but they ARE the precedent (below).

- **Out of scope:** the three producer-less tables (`resources`, `instrumentation_scopes`,
  `span_links`) — owned by the "Diagnostics un-muting + harness-truth sweep" entry. This chunk must
  only avoid *adding a fourth* one.

title: Representation precedent (the directive's item 2 — evidence gathered, decision at P4)

data.head: ## Representation precedent (the directive's item 2 — evidence gathered, decision at P4)

body: The schema **does** carry a precedent for "attribute set → identity", and it is a **cautionary** one:

- **The hash shape is live:** `resource_hash` is produced by `hash_resource`
  (`crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:789`). It hashes **only `kv.key`**, never the value, with
  `DefaultHasher` (std SipHash — documented as *not stable across Rust releases*). So the existing
  precedent for a hashed attribute set (a) discards values, (b) is not a stable identity across
  toolchain bumps, and (c) is opaque at read-back.

- **The side-table shape is declared and DEAD:** `resources` exists with `PRIMARY KEY (resource_hash)`
  (`schema.rs:100`) — the "hash → full record" companion — and has **no producer**. It is one of the
  three producer-less tables measured 2026-08-23, and one of the three retention DELETEs that sweep
  permanently-empty tables.

- **A new table has a mechanical guard:** `DELETE_BY_CUTOFF: [&str; 7]`
  (`crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:22`) plus the drift-guard test at `retention.rs:369-372` that
  iterates `RESERVED_TABLES` — so a new reserved table MUST be added to the sweep or to
  `RETENTION_EXCLUDED_TABLES`, or the guard trips.

**VERIFIED at P3, and sharper than stated** — the read-back proof surface is not merely the only
*external* witness, it is the only witness of any kind. `SELECT_METRICS` + `MetricRow`
(`crates/viz/src/query.rs:24,81`) is the sole place label content could be observed:
`MetricsChart` aggregates only `ts_unix_nano` and `value` into time buckets, and there is no
metrics table, legend, or per-row surface anywhere in the webview. A representation whose
read-back is opaque therefore cannot be shown to work by any surface this project has.

- **Storage:** `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` — all THREE DDL representations must stay in sync
  (the shipped `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema` test forces the first two to agree; `viz`'s
  fixture copy is structurally unguarded — `viz` has no `buffer` dep).

- **Ingestion:** `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` — `collect_metric_points` (5 arms) ·
  `push_metric_row` · the metrics record-batch builder (which, since
  `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`, RETURNS its redaction tally rather than folding it, with the
  fold at the table's own post-append site).

- **Security:** every persisted label value is a client-controlled OTLP attribute value and MUST pass
  `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute` at the write boundary — the ring buffer is unencrypted, so
  redaction at write is the control, not confidentiality at rest. Label KEYS are also
  client-controlled and still need a stated disposition (scrub / bound / allow) — **P3 narrowed it
  to a STORAGE question only**: `crates/ingest/src/invariants.rs` already bounds keys at 256 B,
  values at 4096 B and count at 128 per data point (so the bound half is inherited, not built), and
  obs-plan bars keys from telemetry under either answer. P4 decides the storage disposition.

- **Read side:** `SELECT_METRICS` + `MetricRow` (`crates/viz/src/query.rs:24,81` — 5 fields,
  `specta::Type`, crosses the TauRPC bridge) · the `metrics.*` IPC response · MCP `query_metrics`
  (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs`) · `MetricsRoute.tsx` / `MetricsChart`.

- **Specs:** arch §Occupied Resources (a new column, or a new reserved table that must get a producer
  AND a retention sweep) · security-plan §Anti-Patterns → Logging (the scrub-coverage claim currently
  enumerates four columns) · obs-plan §5 (`redactions_applied` persisted-cells-only counting rule).

- **Bindings:** a new `MetricRow` field regenerates `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`.
  **VERIFIED at P3** — no new TauRPC procedure, and `capability-drift` cannot fire on a DTO field:
  `xtask/src/main.rs:1070-1078` parses the `ARGS_MAP` procedure-name keys out of `bindings.ts` and
  set-diffs them against `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`, which is a list of name strings. The gate still runs
  unconditionally per test-plan §3; it simply has nothing to catch here.

- **PREREQ (from the working entry) — `cargo audit` re-check, pin #8.** Standing deferral since
  `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence`, ratified at the 2026-08-16 adaptation wrap with an
  every-3rd-wrap INTERVAL. Probe points ran at sessions 25/28/31/34, **DISCHARGED at 34**; the next
  point is **37**. This chunk wraps as **session 36**, so the probe is **skipped in the ratified
  form** — but the basis and overlap must be re-verified (not echoed) and the PREREQ re-pinned
  forward to the next markerless entry at wrap. Signature for probe-auto-satisfy: exit `1` +
  `error: error loading advisory database: parse error: duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`,
  with `cargo deny check advisories` overlap green at the eight owned IDs
  (0189/0190/0194/0195/0204/0222/0253 + RUSTSEC-2026-0258).
- **No CARRY, no BLOCKED-ON** on this entry.

The working entry's **NOTE** claims: *"the user-facing surface is ALREADY misleading and this entry is what
fixes it — a rejected batch is not a query error, so `MetricsRoute.tsx` falls to its empty branch and shows
'No metrics received yet' plus an exporter hint naming ports the user is exporting to successfully."*

**That claim is FALSIFIED for this chunk, while the entry's OUTCOME stands unchanged.** The misleading empty
state is caused by a REJECTED BATCH — zero rows persist, the query succeeds returning nothing, and
`MetricsRoute` takes its empty branch. Batch rejection was the *collision* defect, and
`2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity` closed it: rows now persist, so the chart populates. Measured at HEAD:
`MetricsChart` consumes only `ts_unix_nano` and `value`, and there is no metrics table, legend, or per-row
surface anywhere in the webview — so labels reach **no rendered surface at all**.

Consequence: this chunk fixes information loss in storage and read-back; it does **not** change the
user-facing surface, and no acceptance criterion should claim it does. The NOTE appears to have been carried
into the entry at the predecessor's wrap without re-checking against the state that wrap had just created.

Per the RESEARCH-CORRECTS-INTENT discipline the working-route line and its NOTE are left as the historical
source; this scope carries the correction, and a user-visible Metrics label surface is a candidate for its own
future entry rather than a silent extension here.

title: Acceptance shape (outcome level — concretized at P4)

data.head: ## Acceptance shape (outcome level — concretized at P4)

body:
1. A metric batch carrying two data points of one metric that differ **only** by label set is
   ingested on the real OTLP path, and both rows persist **distinguishably** — the read-back shows
   which is which.

2. A label value of credential shape is **redacted** at the write boundary, and the redaction is
   counted under the persisted-cells-only rule.

3. RED-before-GREEN on the real OTLP path, per the three preceding chunks' standard: the
   indistinguishability is measured at HEAD first, then measured closed.
4. No new producer-less table and no unswept table is introduced.

title: Plan — 2026-08-23-webview-self-verify: "Webview self-verify on the Windows host"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-08-23-webview-self-verify: "Webview self-verify on the Windows host"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-08-23-webview-self-verify · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-23T12:37Z

Stand up a driver that lets an agent **press a real control in the live Tauri window on this Windows host**,
and prove it with one canonical leg. Today nothing in either repo can do that: `cargo xtask self-verify` is
boot-quit by construction and "NEVER CLICKS a user-facing control" (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md:110`),
while the Playwright a11y suite drives a static `dist` in Chromium via `http-server` (`playwright-a11y.config.ts`)
— never the app. The gap is the driver, not the intent.

The canonical leg is the **custom-titlebar ✕ on the compact widget**. That control is the exact one
`verification-harness.md:110` records as matrix-`verified` under P-063 while doing NOTHING — `getCurrentWindow().close()`
silently dropped by the negative-default ACL. **It works today** (`pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` grants
`core:window:allow-close`), so the leg is a **regression guard, not a bug reproduction** — which is precisely why
it must be mutation-checked: a green-on-arrival leg that cannot go RED is the failure class this chunk exists to
end (the discipline `2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage` established, per test-plan amendments).

Research made the assertion cheap and exact: the effect is **already observable and already allowlisted**.
`handle_close_to_tray` (`pulse-app/src/window.rs:119-129`) emits `ui.layout.transition` with `layout_mode_from`
(the sanitized window label), `layout_mode_to = "hidden"`, `tray_visible`, and the leaf at
`observability.rs:975` permits exactly those fields. **No new tracing target, no new allowlist leaf, no new
production code** — per obs-plan §8 and §4 Scenario P5, whose must-trace span this already is. The chunk claims
**no capability**: P-076 is the consumer and claims at its own chunk (the matrix link step is a deliberate no-op).

1. **Probe both driver shapes before building on either** (the directive's explicit order; both are unmeasured
   on this host). Each probe is minimal and disposable: launch the app, attach, press one control, observe.
   - **(a) tauri-driver + WebdriverIO** — the lean (see §Constraints). Needs `tauri-driver` and an
     **msedgedriver matching WebView2 151.0.4129.101** (both absent from PATH; record the install recipe as a
     HOST fact — Conductor's Epoch-5 head reuses it). Copy the working shape from
     `conductor/crates/conductor-tauri/ui/` (`@crabnebula/tauri-driver ^2.0.9`, `webdriverio ^9.29.1`,
     `wdio.conf.ts`).
   - **(b) WebView2 remote debugging + Playwright `connectOverCDP`** — `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=N`.
     Reuses the installed Playwright stack; zero CDP path exists at HEAD.
   - Record BOTH outcomes (which attached, which pressed, what failed) — a negative result is a finding, and
     Conductor inherits it.

2. **Land the surviving driver on the existing harness spine.** `xtask/src/self_verify.rs` already launches the
   real dev binary under a fresh `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, polls `:4317`/`:4318` for readiness, globs the
   date-suffixed log family, and cleans up with a zero-orphan check. Extend it (or add a sibling module + a
   `Cmd` variant) rather than standing up a second launcher — arch §Occupied Resources registers this lifecycle.
   Note `headless_skip_reason` skips only on display-less **Linux**, so a Windows host never skips.
