data.head: ## Measurements (the first-scan reality the plan dispositions)

body: - **`npm audit --json` (2026-08-30, exit 1)** — **39 vulnerabilities: 1 critical / 20 high / 16 moderate / 2 low** (raw JSON archived at `.andromeda/runs/2026-08-30T00-20-00Z-phase/npm-audit-first-scan.json`). Direct-dep findings: **vitest** (CRITICAL, UI-server arbitrary file read, fix < ^3 boundary — non-major), **vite** (high, fix within ^7), **lighthouse** (high, vulnerable range tops at 13.4.0 — ALL of ^12 vulnerable; `fixAvailable: true` is ambiguous against the ^12 pin — re-measure with `npm audit fix --dry-run` at implement), **pa11y** (high, only fix = 10.0.0 `isSemVerMajor: true` — crosses the a11y-plan §3 pinned major), **pa11y-ci** (high, `fixAvailable: true`), **webdriverio** (high — the whole wdio cluster's suggested "fix" is 8.14.6, a major DOWNGRADE `isSemVerMajor: true` → no forward fix at HEAD → exception-class). Transitive fix-true findings: brace-expansion (10 ids), js-yaml, lodash, nanoid, postcss, ws, esbuild, ip-address, @babel/core, an @opentelemetry/* + @sentry/node cluster (rides lighthouse's tail), @puppeteer/browsers, puppeteer/-core, extract-zip, deepmerge-ts.

- **Licenses (823 installed packages)** — MIT 612 · Apache-2.0 96 · ISC 45 · BSD-2/3 40 · BlueOak-1.0.0 6 · MPL-2.0 4 · CC-BY-4.0 2 (`@promptbook/utils`, `caniuse-lite` — data files) · **LGPL-3.0-only 2 = `pa11y` 9.1.1 + `pa11y-ci` 4.1.0 THEMSELVES** (dev-only tools, not distributed — a per-CLASS license policy handles this: runtime class strict, dev class broader) · Python-2.0 1 (`argparse`) · misc dual/single permissive · **2 genuinely license-less: `css-value` 0.0.1, `union` 0.5.0** (old wdio-chain transitives — exception-class with closing condition).

- **Multi-version packages: 43 of 830** (brace-expansion ×4, minimatch ×4, lru-cache ×3, …) — npm nests by design; **cargo-deny's `multiple-versions = "deny"` does NOT port**. The npm "bans" half = package-NAME denylist (first real entries: the alternate ARIA component libraries per a11y-plan §11) — NOT duplicate-version deny, which would be permanently red.

- **web-vitals: ABSENT** from package.json, lockfile, and ui/src — obs-plan §1/§3 name `web-vitals` 5.x as the frontend bridge mechanism; at HEAD the bridge is the hand-rolled TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.*` surface without it. TARGET-state mandate not yet implemented; NOT this chunk's to fix and no disposition here can break it (nothing to break). Noted for the wrap report's spec-observation channel.

- **Second ARIA library: NOT present** — `node_modules/react-aria` is `react-aria-components`' own dependency (same family); radix/headlessui/ariakit/reach all 0 hits. The a11y §11 ban is satisfied at HEAD; the bans denylist keeps it that way.

- **CI note (context, not this chunk's scope):** the `supply-chain` job's rustsec/audit-check step is subject to the same upstream RustSec-DB decay the pin-#22 standing deferral records (`cargo audit` exit 1 locally, byte-identical basis) — the branch is 44 commits unpushed, so current CI state is unmeasured here.
- **xtask supply-chain verbs** (main.rs:237-238): `Cmd::Audit` → `run_cargo("audit")`, `Cmd::DenyBans` → `run_cargo("deny", check bans licenses sources)` — the new npm verb is their npm-side sibling.
- **npm spawn** (main.rs:1093): `npm.cmd` on Windows, cwd `pulse-app/ui`, `tokio::process::Command`, `status_to_code` exit mapping.
- **Plain `run:` supply-chain CI step** (ci.yml:249-250): the Cranelift assertion — grep + `exit 1`, no third-party action, no SHA-pin obligation.

- **Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`** in all 7 xtask modules (bundle_format:95 … webview_drive:855) — xtask is a bin crate (no `[lib] test = false` trap); new-module pins follow suit, with the wrap-time "each test collected by name" check per the 2026-08-29 precedent.
- **Pinned-expectation gate** (EXPECTED_PROCEDURES + capability-drift): the reviewable-expectation-list shape the policy file mirrors.
- **Verb naming**: kebab + namespace-colon (`check:ingest-progress`, `smoke:gap-resume`, `test:a11y`, `verify:capability-matrix`) — a gate verb belongs in the `check:` namespace.

- **Exception entries as structured fields** (id, package, reason, owner, closing_condition, added-date) per security-plan carve-out discipline — JSON fields, since serde_json is the available parser and JSON carries no comments.
- **Two-invocation lesson applied**: the npm gate is its OWN CI step whose red is legible — never folded into an existing invocation.

- `xtask/src/npm_gate.rs` — the gate module: spawn `npm audit --json`, parse; read `package-lock.json` for the package enumeration + dev-class flags; read each lockfile-listed package's `package.json` license field; evaluate all three checks against the policy file; machine-parseable verdict + exit code; co-located `mod tests` over fixture JSON.

- `pulse-app/ui/npm-policy.json` (name final at plan) — project-owned policy: license allowlists per class (runtime strict / dev broader), package-name denylist, ID-scoped advisory exceptions with provenance fields.
- CI: one step block in the existing `supply-chain` job (setup-node + `npm ci` + `cargo xtask <verb>`) — a modify, listed below.
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — Cmd variant + dispatch arm (the graph-enumerated threading; nothing else).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `supply-chain` job gains setup-node (SHA-pinned action already used in lint-test-build) + `npm ci` + the gate step.
- `pulse-app/ui/package.json` + `package-lock.json` — the disposition upgrades (vitest critical + the fix-true set; majors per the P4 decision).
- (conditional on the majors decision) `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/baselines/*` — a11y re-baseline if pa11y/lighthouse cross majors; plus the full a11y chain re-run evidence.

- **How to disposition advisory fixes that CROSS a11y-plan §3 pinned majors** (pa11y → 10.0.0 measured; lighthouse → 13.x candidate pending dry-run) → blocks: **plan-decision** (P4 resolves via operator question — the a11y extract's "joint decision" clause; options: upgrade + full-chain re-baseline in-chunk / ID-scoped exception with the pin as reason + re-pin closing condition / leave red).

- **Exact remediation set `npm audit fix --dry-run` will apply** (which transitives move, whether lighthouse's `fixAvailable: true` is real within ^12) → blocks: **implementation-scope** (the modify-list's package.json/lockfile delta is provisional until measured at implement; the plan prescribes disposition RULES, not exact versions).

version-bumped. Owner-named by the security-plan §Dependency Security amendment applied at the
`2026-08-23-webview-self-verify` wrap; the gap PRE-EXISTS that chunk and was widened by it.

- **Advisory / license / ban scanning for the npm channel** at `pulse-app/ui` (the workspace's only

- **First-scan findings get dispositions in-chunk** — the gate lands meaningful, not

- `.github/dependabot.yml` — npm ecosystem at `/pulse-app/ui`, weekly: present. Bumps only.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `npm ci` :92 · `npm run build` :114 · no audit/license/ban step.

- `pulse-app/ui/package.json` — **29 direct devDependencies + 9 runtime dependencies**; no

- **Marker:** 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-30T11:44:00Z

The generated TauRPC bindings and the capability grants a commit ACTUALLY CARRIES match their pins, checked by
a gate that runs unconditionally and cannot be skipped — replacing a discipline that failed six times in prose
form. The defect class: any default-features workspace test run rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`
to the no-mcp shape via `taurpc`'s `export_types()` (running the gates is what rewrites the file — trigger (b)
is every chunk), and every shipped check reads the WORKTREE (`capability_drift()` at `xtask/src/main.rs:1173`,
verified P3), which can be correct while the git INDEX carries the clobbered copy — how commit `70344d5`
shipped no-mcp bindings under a clean-reading handoff. The staged copy (`git show :<path>`) is the proven
right subject (the sixth occurrence: index correct, worktree clobbered — a worktree check false-REDs, the
staged read reports truth). The same staged-read mechanism, paid for once, extends to
`pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` — the identical class where a left-revoked `core:window:*` grant is silently
rejected at runtime and no shipped gate reads grants at all (per security-plan §API Security + §Security
Anti-Patterns → API; test-plan §1 trigger `webview-drive-mutation-arm-not-gated`; playbook.md:74–76, whose
interim ordering rule this gate retires).

The gate lands GREEN against the real repo (both copies measured healthy at HEAD: worktree + staged `"mcp":`
count 1 each) and proves its discrimination in runtime-built fixture repos, code-driven and repeatable.

1. **Author `xtask/src/staged_gate.rs`** (gate-module-per-verb shape per `npm_gate.rs` / `harness_status.rs`):
   - **`EXPECTED_GRANTS` pin** — a const table over the SIX capability files (default, clipboard,
     notification, tray, plugin-fs, updater), each entry `{file, identifier, windows: [...], permissions:
     [...]}` transcribed from the inventories in research.md. `description` fields are deliberately OUTSIDE
     the pin (semantic surface only — prose edits must not red a security gate).
   - **Pure classifier** (harness_status `classify()` precedent — test-plan §3): a fn taking the staged
     bindings content (as `Option<&str>` or its `parse_bindings` result), the six staged capability JSON
     parses (`Option<serde_json::Value>` each), and the two pins (`crate::EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` +
     `EXPECTED_GRANTS`), returning a typed verdict. Findings: bindings procedure diff (missing/extra vs
     EXPECTED_PROCEDURES — mcp-absence surfaces as 3 named missing), grant-set inequality per file in BOTH
     directions (revoked AND added permissions; windows-list delta), and a staged-DELETED subject (findings,
     not neutral). Crate-root items (`parse_bindings`, `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`) are visible to the child module
     via `crate::` — no signature or visibility changes.
   - **Thin git IO**: two-step probe from the workspace root — (a) `git -C <root> ls-files --stage`
     (spawn/exec failure or non-zero on a non-repo ⇒ `cannot-evaluate`, exit 2; success ⇒ index membership
     decides the deleted-subject arm), then (b) `git -C <root> show :<repo-relative-path>` per present
     subject (forward slashes, literal paths). First `git` subprocess in xtask — `tokio::process::Command`
     per the existing cargo/npm spawn precedent; no new dependencies (no git2/libgit2).
   - **Verdict surface** (arch xtask-CLI-contract shape; npm_gate `print_verdict` precedent): one JSON
     verdict object on stdout — `{gate: "staged-artifacts", arm, verdict, ...counts + named
     missing/extra/mismatched-file-and-permission lists}` — arms `staged-clean` (exit 0) / `staged-drift`
     (exit 1) / `cannot-evaluate` (exit 2); report twin at `target/staged-artifacts/report.json` mirroring
     `capability-drift/report.json`. All paths in output repo-relative (never full canonicalized host paths).

2. **Wire `xtask/src/main.rs`**: `mod staged_gate;` · `Cmd` variant `#[command(name = "check:staged-artifacts")]`
   · dispatch arm calling `staged_gate::run()`.

3. **Extend `capability_drift()`** (callers: `main()` dispatch only — graph-proven, zero threading): after its
   existing worktree diff, invoke the staged check's inner fn; ANY non-clean staged outcome (drift OR
   cannot-evaluate) → capability-drift's existing `ExitCode::FAILURE`, with the inner verdict printed first.
   capability-drift's 0/1 exit contract is preserved for its existing consumers; the worktree diff is NOT
   re-pointed (see Constraints). This is the unskippable half: every surface that already runs
   capability-drift LAST — every test-plan §3 gate list, the wrap's P7 slot, ci.yml :103 — now transitively
   runs the staged assertion.

4. **Tests** (co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `staged_gate.rs` — xtask is a `[[bin]]` target whose
   tests genuinely run, `capability_drift_tests` precedent):
   - Per-branch unit pins on the pure classifier: clean · bindings missing the mcp set (asserts the 3 names
     appear in the finding) · bindings extra procedure · revoked grant (named file + permission in the
     verdict) · added grant · windows-list delta · deleted subject ⇒ findings · absent inputs ⇒
     cannot-evaluate.
   - Fixture-repo integration pins: runtime-built TempDir repos (`git init` + write + `git add` — no commit,
     so no user.name/email config; never the real tree, never process-global env/CWD mutation per test-plan
     §7/§11) driving the real git IO path for: clean repo · staged-clobbered bindings · staged-revoked grant ·
     non-repo dir ⇒ cannot-evaluate.
   - Verify collection BY NAME (`cargo nextest list -E 'test(staged_gate)'` non-empty) — a matching total can
     hide dead tests (test-plan §1 `[[example]]` lesson).

5. **Wire `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: one plain named `run:` step `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts`
   beside the capability-drift step (:103 region; npm-gate plain-`run:` precedent). No third-party action
   added (SHA-pin rule not triggered); workflow-level `permissions:` untouched. Step placement must not
   precede/preempt existing artifact-upload steps.
6. **Run the gates** (standard set, capability-drift LAST) + confirm the real-repo verdict is `staged-clean`.

- `xtask/src/staged_gate.rs` — the staged-artifacts gate: EXPECTED_GRANTS pin, pure classifier + typed
  verdict, thin git IO, verdict JSON + report twin, co-located per-branch + fixture-repo tests.

- `xtask/src/main.rs` — `mod staged_gate;` + `Cmd::CheckStagedArtifacts` variant + dispatch arm +
  `capability_drift()` extension (staged check after worktree diff; non-clean ⇒ FAILURE with inner verdict
  printed). Preserve the existing report/event-line patterns.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the new named plain `run:` step beside `cargo xtask capability-drift` (:103).

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo nextest list -E 'test(staged_gate)'   # collected-BY-NAME check — non-empty or the pins are dead
cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts          # direct invocation — real repo must land staged-clean, exit 0
cargo xtask capability-widening-check
cargo xtask check:ingest-progress
cargo xtask capability-drift                # LAST — now transitively runs the staged assertion
```

(No webview gates owed — no `pulse-app/ui/**` path in the touchpoints; the bindings file is READ, never
modified. No boot smoke owed — no boot-path file modified; fixture-repo mutations never touch the real
`pulse-app/capabilities/*.json`. Not a UI chunk — no headful self-verify gate.)

- (arch) The gate lives in the `xtask` workspace member with zero new dependency edges and a stated CLI
  contract in the registered shape — named arms `staged-clean`/`staged-drift`/`cannot-evaluate`, exits 0/1/2,
  one machine-parseable JSON verdict on stdout (per arch §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces; §Cross-cutting
  Patterns → Module dependency direction).

  trigger (b) = ANY chunk whose gate set includes a default-features workspace test run — which is
  every chunk, because the plan-mandated `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` is itself a
  default-features run and running the gates is what rewrites the file via `taurpc`'s
  `export_types()`. The assertion therefore runs unconditionally, never on a TauRPC-touched
  predicate.

- **Unskippable wiring** — the entry demands "wired so it cannot be skipped". VERIFIED (P3):
  `capability-drift` runs as its own ci.yml step (:103) AND last in every test-plan §3 gate list AND
  in the wrap's P7 slot — so the staged assertion folds INTO `capability_drift()` (any non-clean
  staged outcome fails it), making every existing invocation transitively run the check, plus an own
  verb + own ci.yml step for direct invocation and a named failure surface. The two consumers see
  different subjects by construction: locally the index is the about-to-be-committed copy; on a
  fresh CI checkout the index equals HEAD, so the same read validates the commit itself.

- **Extension to `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json`** (CARRY folded): the same staged-copy mechanism
  asserts the committed capability grants — identical class (a committed file a gate can silently
  alter). Origin `2026-08-23-webview-self-verify`: its RED mutation arm revokes
  `core:window:allow-close`, rebuilds, then restores BY HAND — only `--expect-absent` is code, so
  "byte-identical after restore" is a DISCIPLINE today and **no shipped gate catches a left-revoked
  grant** (`capability-drift` parses procedures from bindings.ts and never reads grants;
  `capability-widening-check` covers only the 3 NEVER-widen caps and only in the widening
  direction). Tracked test-plan-side as pending trigger `webview-drive-mutation-arm-not-gated`.
  VERIFIED (P3): the baseline is an xtask-side `EXPECTED_GRANTS` pin (sibling of
  `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`, xtask/src/main.rs:1116; name measured free in the graph) over the 6
  capability files' `{identifier, windows, permissions}` — `description` fields deliberately
  excluded (default.json carries ~9.5 KB of prose whose edits must not red a security gate) — with
  set equality asserted in BOTH directions, so a revoked AND an added grant each red.

- **Interim ordering-rule retirement**: `.andromeda/playbook.md` carries the interim ORDERING rule
  codified at the 2026-08-22 wrap that "holds until this lands". VERIFIED (P3): playbook.md:74–76
  states verbatim "until it lands, this rule is the interim" — the wrap re-points the rule at the
  shipped gate (playbook is operational, not a spec master).

- **RED/GREEN proof discipline** (VERIFIED-concretized at P3): the assertion's discrimination is
  proven by mutation — a staged no-mcp copy (and a staged revoked-grant capability file) reds the
  gate; the restored copies green it — in runtime-built TempDir FIXTURE repos (`git init` + write +
  `git add`, per test-plan §7), never by mutating the real tree. Both real copies measured healthy
  at HEAD (worktree + staged `"mcp":` count 1 each), so the gate lands GREEN and the §3 boot-smoke
  conditional trigger does not attach.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-29T16:45Z

A CI round stops being the bottleneck of the build loop, and Linux-only failures surface on the dev host before a
push. P3 moved where the lever is. The "~2 h round" was a cold-cache round (ci#36574279289, `No cache found`); the
first warm round (ci#36593334009) took **44.8 min**, and its ubuntu leg is a serial chain of separate compiles (test
7.1 · perf 6.1 · mcp nextest 7.2 · boot 7.7 · release 3.2 + 3.2 min warm) around a ~30 s test execution. The
macOS/Windows legs follow at 33.4 / 37.1 min. So this chunk:
- **(A)** splits the workflow into parallel jobs whose longest leg, not their sum, is the round;

- **(B)** keeps the dependency cache when a job fails, and re-allocates cache keys under the measured 10 GB repo cap
  (9.27 GB used today) so that no job rides a cache built for a different purpose;
- **(C)** removes the two measured true-duplicate compiles on Linux;
- **(D)** adds a local WSL Ubuntu pre-push verb that runs the Linux-reachable gates in a synced clone.
The CARRY (E) needs no code: the two scenario verbs already exist, so their arch registration is a wrap amendment.

Provenance: arch §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach + §Established Decisions [CI Task Runner] + §Occupied
Resources → xtask CLI surfaces; security-plan §Dependency Security → CI integration + §Bootstrap phases →
dep-security-ci-gate; test-plan §9 Pipeline structure / Build failure conditions + §3 5-command implementation;
obs-plan §9 Telemetry artifact handling + §10 CI gates; a11y-plan §3 CI integration + §9 Per-pipeline-stage a11y
artifacts. P3 closed the scope premises (scope.md `[premise-corrected: …]` bullets). Where an extract leaned on the
falsified "mcp build vs bindings regen" pair, research overrides it: no CI step regenerates bindings.

1. **Workflow job layout** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Replace the three-job layout (`lint-test-build` matrix ·
   `supply-chain` · `coverage`) with these jobs. Each keeps `Harden runner` first and `Export ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`
   second; `checkout → toolchain → rust-cache → tool install → (Linux) apt libraries → Node → npm ci → npm run build`
   is the per-job prelude, each job carrying only the prelude steps its gates need.
   - **`lint-test`** (matrix `ubuntu-22.04` · `macos-latest` · `windows-latest`, `fail-fast: false`). The steps of
     today's `lint-test-build` minus the a11y block and the Linux-only boot/mcp-release block, in today's order:
     - fmt, No-Cyrillic, clippy, typecheck, quarantine-tracking, capability-drift, check:staged-artifacts,
       capability-widening-check, verify:capability-matrix;
     - `cargo xtask test`;
     - Linux only: `cargo xtask perf:slo-load` (Step 3), then `cargo nextest run --workspace --features mcp-server
       --profile ci --no-tests=pass`;
     - macOS/Windows only: `cargo build --workspace --release`;
     - the criterion upload/download/regression, nextest-junit, logs (`logs-${{ runner.os }}`) and capability-drift
       uploads.
   - **`a11y`** (matrix, the same three OSes). Its prelude, then:
     - `npm run build --prefix pulse-app/ui` → Playwright chromium install;
     - the PR-only `a11y-violations-base` download → `cargo xtask test:a11y`;
     - its `if: always()` uploads (`a11y-violations-${{ runner.os }}`, `playwright-a11y-report-${{ runner.os }}`).

     Moved whole: one verb, still blocking, on every OS it runs on today.
   - **`boot`** (`ubuntu-22.04` only). Its prelude, then `cargo build --workspace --release --features mcp-server` (the
     feature-gated binary's build smoke), then the `Boot pulse-app smoke` step unchanged: one `xvfb-run` spanning
     `boot` → `status` → `cleanup`, gating, no `continue-on-error`. Then `cargo xtask ci-gates`, which reads the log
     that boot wrote in this job, then an `if: always()` logs upload named `logs-boot-${{ runner.os }}`.
   - **`supply-chain`** — steps unchanged. Its `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` is now the Linux
     workspace release smoke (Step 4).
   - **`coverage`** — steps unchanged; cache per Step 2.

   The gate roster after the change must equal today's roster. The only removals are Step 3's `-p` compile form (the
   step stays, re-pointed) and Step 4's Linux-only `cargo build --workspace --release` step.

2. **Cache allocation** (`ci.yml`, every `Swatinem/rust-cache@23869a5…` step; the same pinned SHA, no new action).
   - Every job that saves sets `cache-on-failure: true`.
   - Keys, by `shared-key`:
     - `lint-test-${{ runner.os }}` — saved by `lint-test`; restored with `save-if: false` by `a11y`, which needs only
       the xtask build.
     - `boot-Linux` — saved by `boot`; restored with `save-if: false` by `supply-chain`, whose release deps largely
       coincide.
     - `coverage` with `cache-targets: false` — registry only. The instrumented build stays uncached; research
       measured 16–17 min for it, under the predicted critical path.
   - Rationale, derived from `gh api repos/Turbolet85/andromeds-pulse/actions/cache/usage` (9 267 495 585 B across 5
     keys at P3): three `lint-test-*` + one `boot-Linux` target cache + registry-only coverage stays under the 10 GB
     cap. A per-job target cache for every job would not (see Constraints).
   - The renamed keys make the first post-change round cold by construction. The old keys (`${{ runner.os }}-cargo`,
     `ubuntu-22.04-cargo`) go unused and age out LRU.

3. **`perf:slo-load` reuses the workspace test build** (`xtask/src/main.rs` `run_perf_slo_load`, :647). Replace
   `-p pulse-app --test perf_slo_10k_spans` with `--workspace -E 'binary(perf_slo_10k_spans)'`, keeping `--profile
   ci --no-tests=pass --message-format libtest-json` and the `NEXTEST_EXPERIMENTAL_LIBTEST_JSON` env. test-plan §3
   already sanctions this narrowing form ("narrow … with `--filter-expr` / `-E` under `--workspace`, not with `-p`").
   Its only caller is `main()` dispatch (`run_perf_slo_load @ xtask/src/main.rs:273`, the graph's one row). In the
   `lint-test` Linux job it runs AFTER `cargo xtask test`, so it links nothing new. The named step and its
   `a11y_perf_workflow.rs` pin survive.

4. **Remove the Linux duplicate release build** (`ci.yml`): the `cargo build --workspace --release` step no longer
   runs on Linux. `supply-chain`'s `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` builds the same scope under the same
   profile and features, and also embeds the dependency tree. macOS/Windows keep their own release build in
   `lint-test` (Step 1).

5. **Workflow pinning tests follow the layout**:
   - `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` `data_dir_export_precedes_every_consumer`: update the
     `("ci.yml", 3)` job-count pin to the new count, keeping the per-job Harden-runner-first / DATA_DIR-export-second
     assertions.
   - `ci_workflow_uploads_logs_artifact_unchanged` keeps asserting `name: logs-${{ runner.os }}` (still uploaded by
     `lint-test`), and gains an assertion that `logs-boot-` exists.
   - `ci_workflow_test_gates_no_continue_on_error` stays as is; it walks every step block, so the new jobs are
     covered.
   - `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` `ci_workflow_builds_ui_before_a11y_run`: the order assertion must hold
     inside the `a11y` job's block. Scope the `find` to that job's text rather than the whole file, so a build step in
     another job cannot satisfy it.

6. **The WSL Linux pre-push verb** (new `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`; `Cmd::PrePushLinux` registered as `#[command(name =
   "pre-push:linux")]` with its dispatch arm in `xtask/src/main.rs`). Modelled on the Viola precedent (research.md
   §Files inspected); an xtask verb because the 5-command `agent-run` discipline forbids a 6th verb.
   - **Host + distro**: runs only on a Windows host with `wsl.exe` and the `Ubuntu` distro. A constant, not an env
     var, so no new env var is introduced. Every distro call is `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --exec /usr/bin/env -i HOME=…
     PATH=…`, so nothing of the host environment crosses (the `wsl-exec.sh` shape). Absent host or distro →
     `cannot-evaluate`.
   - **Tool pins, read from the repo, never restated**:
     - the Rust channel from `rust-toolchain.toml`, present in the distro's rustup;
     - Node major = `ci.yml`'s `node-version`;
     - `jq`, `git` and `xvfb-run` on PATH;
     - every package in `ci.yml`'s `Install Linux system libraries` apt list installed (`dpkg-query`).

     Any missing → `cannot-evaluate`, naming each missing item and printing the single remediation command built from
     the same list (the operator runs it once with sudo; the verb never escalates).
   - **Sync**: a distro-side clone at `~/andromeda-pulse-pre-push`, brought to the host HEAD plus the working tree as
     ONE binary patch through a temporary index (the real index untouched). Verified by tree-id equality → otherwise
     `red` with `sync-mismatch`. The clone's `target/` is capped (40 GiB, the precedent's cap), and cleared above it.
   - **Stages, inside the clone, in order; each records `{name, ok, ms}`**:
     - `script-modes` — `scripts/agent-run.sh` is git mode 100755.
     - `npm` — `npm ci` + `npm run build` in `pulse-app/ui`.
     - `clippy` — `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
     - `test` — `cargo xtask test`.
     - `ci-gates` — `cargo xtask ci-gates` against a fresh `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` seeded with a few non-metric JSON
       records. This drives `perf-slo-check.sh` / `heartbeat-gap-check.sh` over an empty metric stream on Linux bash.

     The first failing stage stops the run.
   - **Verdict**: one pretty-JSON document on stdout — `verdict` (`green` | `red` | `cannot-evaluate`), `reason`,
     `head`, `tree`, `stages[]`, `missing[]` — plus a report twin `target/pre-push/report.json`. Exits 0 green · 1 red
     · 2 cannot-evaluate.
   - **No boot arm this chunk** (Constraints). The verb never binds a port.
   - **Unit tests** in the module (`#[cfg(test)]`), for the pure parts: the apt-list and `node-version` readers over a
     `ci.yml` string, the toolchain reader over `rust-toolchain.toml` text, the verdict/exit mapping, and the
     `ls-files -s` mode parse. Each has a known-positive and a known-negative case.

7. **CARRY E — no code change.** `smoke:gap-resume` / `smoke:external-resolve` / `smoke:hue-shift` are registered at
   `xtask/src/main.rs:65,81,91` (verified at P3), so only the arch registry lags. The chunk's report cites the three
   registrations as by-construction evidence for the wrap amendment below.

- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` — the `pre-push:linux` verb: host/distro probe, pin reads, binary-patch sync with tree-id
  check, the staged Linux gate run, the JSON verdict + report twin, and unit tests for its pure readers.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the job split (Step 1), cache allocation (Step 2), the Linux duplicate release build
  removed (Step 4), and per-job artifact names.

- `xtask/src/main.rs` — `run_perf_slo_load` re-pointed (Step 3); the `PrePushLinux` variant + dispatch arm + `mod
  pre_push;` (Step 6).
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the job-count and logs-artifact pins follow the layout (Step 5).
- `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` — the build-before-a11y order is scoped to the `a11y` job (Step 5).

The standard gate set runs unconditionally, with `capability-drift` LAST among the cargo gates (test-plan §3
Per-chunk gate discipline). `pulse-app/ui/**` is untouched, so the npm webview gates are not listed.
**Host constraint (operator directive at take-up, standing until released):**
- No release-profile build, no `pulse-app` start, no bind on 4317/4318.
- Every entry below is debug-profile or WSL-side.

- The test suite binds only ephemeral loopback ports: every `try_bind` call site in `pulse-app/tests` +
  `crates/*/tests` passes port 0 (`grep -rn -E "TcpListener|try_bind" …`, e.g. `perf_slo_10k_spans.rs:137`), and the
  literal 4317/4318 appear only as parse values (`grep -rn -E "\b431[78]\b" …`).

- The real boot smoke is out of reach this chunk, for three reasons: /implement P3's boot would start `pulse-app`;
  CI's `boot` job exercises it on the runner; no product code changes.

- `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` needs the one-time operator provisioning it names (apt list + `jq` + Node 24, with
  sudo) before its first green.

The CI half is operator-driven: the hygiene read, the commit+push, and the CI read of the pushed head (a first
post-change round is cold by construction, Step 2, so the wait covers a cold round).

- Leaned (decisive, no question asked):

  what it names: the `wsl.exe` crossing is a NEW dev-harness subprocess that passes only `HOME` + `PATH`, not a
  widening of an already-hardened product boundary, and no product surface gains a crossing.

- `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` on PR pushes — rejected: phase Setup 5a reads the CI verdict of EVERY sha since the
  last wrap, and a cancelled superseded run reads `not green`, which halts the next take-up.

- A per-job target cache for every job — rejected: 9.27 GB of the 10 GB cap is already in use (research.md), so six or
  more target caches evict one another and bring back the cold rounds this chunk removes. Registry-only coverage and

- Dropping the Linux default-features `cargo xtask test` as a "duplicate" of the mcp-feature nextest — rejected: the
  two runs use different feature sets (2398 vs 2433 tests), and default features are the shipping configuration.

- Dropping `test:a11y` on macOS/Windows — rejected: the saving is runner minutes only, with no wall-time gain in the
  new layout; a11y-plan §11 CI "NEVER skip a11y".

- A WSL boot arm (on overridden ports) — deferred, not built: the operator's standing directive forbids starting
  `pulse-app`, and none of the four target classes needs it. A later chunk adds it once the directive is released.

- A new env var for the distro name or clone path — rejected: constants inside the verb keep the production binary's
  env surface untouched (arch §Occupied Resources → Environment variables).

- Making `mcp-server` a default feature to merge the two Linux compiles — forbidden (arch §Conventions → Feature
  flags: default features are minimal; security.md MCP double-gate).

- Lowering a threshold, adding `continue-on-error`, a retry, or `--test-threads=1` to reach green — forbidden
  (test-plan §11 CI; a11y-plan §11; obs-plan §11).

- **Order sensitivity**:
  - In `lint-test`, `capability-drift` / `check:staged-artifacts` stay after typecheck and before `cargo xtask test`,
    as today: the default-features test run rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (ci.yml comment above the
    test step).
  - Step 3's `perf:slo-load` runs after `cargo xtask test` in the same job.
  - `ci-gates` runs after the boot smoke in `boot`.

- **The `a11y` job's needs**: `test:a11y` compiles the xtask binary, and xtask's only workspace edge is `ingest`
  (research.md §Graph impact). Whether the job needs the Linux apt libraries is decided by a green run, not by
  assumption. Keep the apt step on Linux unless the first round proves it unneeded.

- **`gh` artifact names** must be unique across all jobs of a run (upload-artifact v4 refuses a duplicate name). Seven
  upload steps exist today (`grep -c "uses: actions/upload-artifact" .github/workflows/ci.yml` = 7: 6 in
  `lint-test-build` + 1 in `coverage`). Every name that now uploads from two jobs of one OS carries a job token.

- **Pre-push sync is the precedent's shape** (`linux.rs` `sync`): a temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `read-tree HEAD` →
  `add -A` → `write-tree`, `diff --cached --binary HEAD`, applied in the clone after `fetch` + `reset --hard HEAD` +
  `clean -fdq`, then `write-tree` equality. The distro path of the Windows repo is `/mnt/d/…`, converted by the verb.
  `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL` does not apply, because the verb spawns `wsl.exe` directly from Rust.

- **Distro facts measured at P3** (research.md): Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (CI is 22.04, so the apt names match but versions

title: CI runs read (the measurements this plan rests on)

data.head: ## CI runs read (the measurements this plan rests on)

body:
Both are runs of this PR's ci.yml at HEAD shape. Timings are from `gh run view {id} --json jobs` (step
`startedAt`/`completedAt`), and cache lines are from `gh run view {id} --job {job} --log`.
| run | sha | cache state (ubuntu leg) | round wall | ubuntu | windows | macOS | coverage | supply-chain |

Ubuntu leg per step, cold → warm (steps ≥ 30 s). Cold compile/run split read from the
`Finished … in` and `Summary [` lines:
| step | cold | warm | what it compiles |
| clippy `--workspace --all-targets --all-features` | 13.0 | 0.4 | check profile, all features |
| `cargo xtask typecheck` | 11.4 | 0.2 | the xtask binary (dev); tsc itself is seconds |
| `cargo xtask test` (nextest `--workspace --profile ci`, default features) | 14.4 (compile 13m53s, run ~30 s, 2398 tests) | 7.1 | test profile, default features |
| `cargo xtask test:a11y` | 10.0 | 5.9 | the xtask binary only (npm / Playwright / Lighthouse run) |
| `cargo xtask perf:slo-load` (`nextest -p pulse-app --test perf_slo_10k_spans`) | 10.1 (compile 9m52s, run 12.9 s, 1 test) | 6.1 | test profile, `-p pulse-app` feature set |
| `cargo build --workspace --release` | 25.6 | 3.2 | release, default features |
| `cargo build --workspace --release --features mcp-server` | 5.2 | 3.2 | release, mcp feature |
| `cargo nextest run --workspace --features mcp-server --profile ci` | 12.4 (compile 11m54s, run ~30 s, 2433 tests) | 7.2 | test profile, mcp feature |
| Boot smoke (`boot` → `status` → `cleanup` in one xvfb-run) | 12.8 | 7.7 | `--bin pulse-app --release` + xtask, then the ~2 s boot |

- **Premise corrected: the entry's "~2 h per round" is a cold-cache round.** That number came from ci#36574279289, and its
  ubuntu leg logged `No cache found`. The first warm round, ci#36593334009, took 44.8 min. Each of P-025's 8 red rounds
  paid the cold price, because a failed job saves no cache (see B below). So the steady-state bottleneck is ~45 min, and
  it sits on the ubuntu leg, which is **compile-dominated**: every heavy step is a separate compile of a separate
  profile/feature set, and the whole suite's execution is ~30 s.

- The un-split macOS/Windows legs (33.4 / 37.1 min warm) sit just under ubuntu. Splitting ubuntu alone can bring the round
  down no further than those legs.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (full, 431 lines) — the three jobs are at `:19`, `:255` and `:329`:
  - `lint-test-build`: an OS matrix with `fail-fast: false`, holding the serial chain above.
  - `supply-chain`: audit-check, deny-action, the Cranelift assertion, `check:npm-supply-chain`, then
    `cargo auditable build --workspace --release`.
  - `coverage`: `cargo xtask test:coverage`, a threshold `run:` block, then coverage-regression.

  Every job has harden-runner first and the `Export ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` step second. Three rust-cache keys are in
  use: `${{ runner.os }}-cargo` (`:42-45`), and `ubuntu-22.04-cargo`, which `supply-chain` (`:273-276`) and `coverage`
  (`:347-350`) share.

- `xtask/src/main.rs:303-332` `run_cargo_nextest` — `nextest run --workspace --profile ci --no-tests=pass --message-format
  libtest-json` (the `cargo xtask test` body).
- `xtask/src/main.rs:647-670` `run_perf_slo_load` — `nextest run -p pulse-app --test perf_slo_10k_spans --profile ci`.

- `xtask/src/main.rs:334-355` `run_cargo_llvm_cov` — `llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov … --ignore-filename-regex
  COVERAGE_IGNORE_FILENAME_REGEX` (the TEMPORARY xtask exclusion, `:332`).

- `xtask/src/main.rs:357-…` `run_ci_gates` — reads the resolved log dir's `agent-latest.jsonl*`, so it must run in the job
  whose boot wrote those logs.

- `xtask/src/main.rs:65,81,91` — `smoke:gap-resume`, `smoke:external-resolve` and `smoke:hue-shift` are all registered
  `Cmd` names (dispatch `:223`, `:244`, `:256`). **CARRY E's premise holds:** the verbs exist, and only the arch
  registry lags (`architecture.md:241` names `smoke:hue-shift` alone).

- `.config/nextest.toml` — `[profile.default] default-filter = "not binary(perf_load_profiles)"`, so
  `perf_slo_10k_spans` IS collected by the workspace `ci` run. The cold log confirms it: `2398 tests across 115 binaries
  (1 binary skipped via profile.default.default-filter)`.

- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` (393 lines) — pins these parts of the workflow shape:
  - `data_dir_export_precedes_every_consumer` (`:348`) asserts `("ci.yml", 3)` jobs, with Harden runner first and the
    DATA_DIR export second in each.
  - `ci_workflow_test_gates_no_continue_on_error` (`:147`) scans every step block against 12 gate substrings.
  - `ci_workflow_uploads_logs_artifact_unchanged` (`:260`) pins `name: logs-${{ runner.os }}`.
  - Coverage-baseline and criterion steps are pinned by name (`:108-135`, `:221-259`).

- `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` (outline) — pins `cargo xtask test:a11y`, `cargo xtask perf:slo-load`,
  `verify:capability-matrix` and `capability-widening-check` by `contains`. It pins `npm run build --prefix pulse-app/ui`
  appearing BEFORE `cargo xtask test:a11y` by string position (`:44-58`), the `a11y-violations-` and
  `playwright-a11y-report-` artifact prefixes, SHA-pin discipline, and workflow-level `contents: read`.

- `scripts/agent-run.sh:32-56` — port defaults `${ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT:-4317}` / `_HTTP_PORT:-4318`; boot
  exports `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` / `_LOG_LEVEL` / `RUST_LOG`, then pre-builds. `git ls-files -s` → mode `100755`.

- `crates/triage/build.rs:51-53` — the workspace's only `rerun-if-env-changed` pair (`ANDROMEDA_LLAMA3_TOKENIZER_SHA256` /
  `_PATH`). Boot exports neither, so boot's release relink is not an env re-fingerprint of a build script. The feature
  unification of `--bin pulse-app` vs `--workspace` is the unmeasured hypothesis (open question 3).

- `Cargo.toml:252-255` `[profile.release] lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true` — every release link is slow.
  `pulse-app/Cargo.toml:71-74` `[features] default = []`, `mcp-server`, `otap-ingest`.

- `Swatinem/rust-cache` `action.yml` + `README.md` at the pinned SHA `23869a5…` (`gh api …/contents?ref=`) — caches
  `~/.cargo` and `./target` **dependency** artifacts. Workspace crates are not cached (`cache-workspace-crates` default
  false). `cache-on-failure`: "Cache even if the build fails. Defaults to false." `save-if` defaults true.
  `add-job-id-key` defaults true (overridden by `shared-key`).

- Repo cache state (`gh cache list` + `gh api …/actions/cache/usage`) — **5 caches, 9 267 495 585 B active, against the
  10 GB repository cap.** Windows 2 552 MB (created 10:06), macOS 2 067 MB (10:21), `ubuntu-22.04` 1 580 MB (09:00),
  Linux 2 632 MB (15:19), gitleaks 5 MB. All sit on `refs/pull/39/merge`.

- Warm-run cache lines (ci#36593334009): all four rust-cache jobs log `Restored from cache key … full match: true`, then at
  post `Cache up-to-date`. **A full-match restore never re-saves**, so a key saved once stays frozen until its lockfile
  or toolchain hash changes. Two consequences:
  - `coverage` restores `supply-chain`'s release-shaped cache (saved 09:00), so its instrumented build is never cached:
    16–17 min every round.
  - The macOS/Windows caches date from ~10:00. Warm macOS clippy still logs `Compiling libduckdb-sys v1.10505.0` (the
    bundled C++ build), where ubuntu logs `Checking libduckdb-sys`.

- Viola precedent (read-only, another repo):
  - `D:/dev/projects/viola/scripts/wsl-exec.sh` — `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --exec /usr/bin/env -i HOME=… PATH=…`, with
    `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'` and a `--probe` mode proving that only HOME and PATH cross.
  - `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push/linux.rs` — named Stop reasons (`tool-missing`, `tool-pin-mismatch`,
    `sync-failed`, `sync-mismatch`, `linux-document-unreadable`). It keeps a distro-side clone synced from the working
    tree as ONE binary patch through a temporary index, at the same HEAD, verified by tree-id equality. Tool pins are
    read from ci.yml, the clone's `target/` is capped at 40 GiB (`pre_push.rs:28`), and the verdict is one JSON document.
  - `scripts/wsl-provision.sh` — installs ci.yml's pinned Node under the distro home.

- WSL host probes (this session):
  - Distros: `Ubuntu` (WSL2, `Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS`, kernel 6.6.87.2) and `docker-desktop`. No `~/.wslconfig`, so NAT
    networking is the default.
  - The distro has 32 cores and 31 GiB RAM, and its disk image lives on `C:` (151 GB free, so it does not draw on D:'s
    103 GB).
  - Tools present: rustup with `1.98.1` default plus `1.95.0` (auto-installed by this research's `rustup toolchain list`
    probe, run from a cwd carrying `rust-toolchain.toml`), cargo-nextest, cargo-llvm-cov, gcc, xvfb-run, Node `v24.21.0`
    under `~/.local/viola-node/bin`.
  - **Absent:** every Tauri/dbus apt package ci.yml installs (`dpkg -l` finds none of the 9). `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` is
    available (candidate `2.52.6-0ubuntu0.26.04.1`). **`sudo -n true` → interactive authentication required**, so
    installing the libraries is a one-time operator step.
  - CI's image is `ubuntu-22.04`; the distro is 26.04.

title: A. Parallel jobs (the ubuntu leg stops being one ~2 h serial job)

data.head: ### A. Parallel jobs (the ubuntu leg stops being one ~2 h serial job)

body:
- Today `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (431 lines) holds three jobs: `lint-test-build` (`:19`, a matrix over
  `ubuntu-22.04` · `macos-latest` · `windows-latest`, `fail-fast: false`), `supply-chain` (`:255`, ubuntu) and
  `coverage` (`:329`, ubuntu). Verified at P1.

- The ubuntu leg of `lint-test-build` runs its gates in series. Measured 2026-09-29 (entry CONTEXT): ~2 h per round —
  clippy 13 · typecheck 11 · test 14 · a11y 10 · perf 10 · release 26 · mcp build 5 · nextest 12 · boot 12 min.
  `[premise-corrected: those are the COLD-cache round ci#36574279289 (ubuntu log "No cache found"), 119.7 min. The first
  warm round, ci#36593334009 on e98d838, took 44.8 min: ubuntu 44.8 · windows 37.1 · macOS 33.4 · coverage 16.0 ·
  supply-chain 7.8. Warm ubuntu: test 7.1 · a11y 5.9 · perf 6.1 · release 3.2 · mcp release 3.2 · mcp nextest 7.2 ·
  boot 7.7 min. Every heavy step is compile-dominated; the 2398-test suite runs in ~30 s. research.md §CI runs read]`

- Build: split that serial chain into independent jobs that run at the same time, so the round's wall time is the
  longest job (plus shared setup), not the sum of all of them.

- `[premise-corrected: macOS/Windows measured at 33.0 / 42.4 min cold and 33.4 / 37.1 min warm. After an ubuntu-only
  split they set the critical path (33–37 min), so the split or a trim has to reach them too, or the round stays ≥ ~33
  min. research.md §CI runs read]`

- Keep the dependency cache when a job fails (the entry: "keep the dependency cache on failure"). Today every job
  uses `Swatinem/rust-cache@23869a5…` (v2.9.1) with `shared-key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo` (`ci.yml:42-45`, verified).

- The mechanism, verified: rust-cache saves only on job success by default (`cache-on-failure` "Defaults to false",
  action.yml at the pinned SHA). A red round's compiled dependencies are lost, and the next round rebuilds them cold:
  all 8 red P-025 rounds were cold, and the Linux key's first save came at 15:18 on the first green ubuntu leg.

- `[premise-corrected: the measured defect is FREEZING, not racing. A full-match restore never re-saves ("Cache
  up-to-date"), so a key saved once is frozen until its lockfile/toolchain hash changes. coverage shares
  "ubuntu-22.04-cargo" with supply-chain, restores a release-shaped cache and is never warm (16–17 min every round); the
  macOS/Windows keys have been frozen since ~10:00, and warm macOS clippy still compiles libduckdb-sys from source.
  The repo cache is 9.27 GB of the 10 GB cap across 5 keys, so a naive per-job key set evicts and brings cold rounds
  back. Workspace crates are never cached (cache-workspace-crates default false). research.md §Files inspected]`

- Drop the duplicate full rebuilds. The measured list names `release 26`, `mcp build 5`, `test 14` and `nextest 12`
  as separate steps.

- `[premise-corrected: the true duplicates are measured, and they are not the pairs guessed at P1.
  (i) perf:slo-load runs nextest -p pulse-app --test perf_slo_10k_spans, a separate compile (9m52s cold / 6.1 min warm)
  for ONE test the workspace ci run already executes: default-filter excludes only perf_load_profiles.
  (ii) Linux cargo build --workspace --release duplicates supply-chain's cargo auditable build --workspace --release
  (same profile, scope and features).
  Not duplicates: test (default features, 2398 tests) vs nextest --features mcp-server (2433) have different feature
  sets, and default features are the shipping configuration. mcp build vs a "bindings regen": no CI step regenerates
  bindings, and the mcp release build is the only CI smoke of the feature-gated binary.
  Unmeasured: boot's --bin pulse-app --release recompile after --workspace --release (7.7 min warm); feature unification
  is the hypothesis. research.md §Scope premise closure]`

- Boundary: a rebuild goes only when it duplicates another gate's coverage. No gate is dropped for being slow; a gate
  that must survive moves into its own parallel job (A) instead.

title: D. A local Linux pre-push check (WSL Ubuntu)

data.head: ### D. A local Linux pre-push check (WSL Ubuntu)

body:
- Add a local check that runs the Linux-reachable gates in WSL Ubuntu before a push, so Linux-only failures surface
  locally instead of as a red CI round.

- Precedent (read-only, another repo): `D:/dev/projects/viola/scripts/wsl-exec.sh` (2 672 B, verified present) and
  `D:/dev/projects/viola/crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push/linux.rs` (27 876 B, verified present).

- (P3: kept as the target list, not re-derived — it is a recount of past rounds, not a claim about HEAD.) The entry's
  claim, verbatim: «of P-025's 8 red CI rounds, a local Linux (WSL) run would have caught 4
  (apt/libdbus deps and their order, npm 10 vs 11, the perf-slo-check abort, the boot-script mode); gitleaks, cargo
  deny and the coverage threshold are caught by any local run of the same gates; 3 were macOS-only (icons,
  quarantine, salt race) and no local Linux check catches them (the overseer's recount)». This is a recount, not a
  measurement at HEAD. P3 does not re-litigate it but uses it as the target list: the check has to be able to catch
  those four classes.

- `[premise-corrected: the distro exists but is only partly provisioned. Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS on WSL2 (32 cores, 31 GiB,
  disk image on C: with 151 GB free); rustup with 1.95.0 (auto-installed by a P3 probe) + cargo-nextest +
  cargo-llvm-cov; Node v24.21.0 (Viola's, ~/.local/viola-node); gcc; xvfb-run. None of ci.yml's 9 Tauri/dbus apt
  packages are installed, and sudo needs a password, so installing them is a one-time operator step. CI runs
  ubuntu-22.04, so the distro is a newer Ubuntu than the runner. research.md §Files inspected]`

- Its surface belongs with the existing harness verbs, not in a new ad-hoc script. The 5-command `agent-run`
  discipline forbids a 6th verb, so it is an xtask verb (arch §Established Decisions [CI Task Runner]). Its name is a
  P4 decision.

title: Host constraint (operator directive at take-up, 2026-09-29; stands until the operator releases it)

data.head: ## Host constraint (operator directive at take-up, 2026-09-29; stands until the operator releases it)

body:
- Conductor is driving real-model legs against `target/release/pulse-app.exe` on `127.0.0.1:4317`. Until released:
  **no release-profile rebuild, no starting `pulse-app`, no binding `4317`/`4318`**. Debug-profile cargo and WSL work
  are fine.

- Disk: 103 GB free, `target/` 79 GB. Check disk before any heavy step (a cold WSL build populates its own target dir
  inside the distro's filesystem).

- The WSL pre-push check (D) builds in the distro's own clone and target dir, never in the Windows `target/release/`.
  Verified: there is no `~/.wslconfig`, so networking is NAT by default and WSL's loopback is not Windows' loopback.
  `agent-run.sh` honours `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_{GRPC,HTTP}_PORT` (`scripts/agent-run.sh:32-33`), so a WSL boot need
  not use 4317/4318. Whether a WSL boot counts as "starting pulse-app" under the directive is the operator's call
  (research.md open question 2).

- No gate is weakened or removed as a cost cut; every gate that runs today still runs after the change (A/C), or its
  removal is argued as a true duplicate.

- The CI perf-budget gate's vacuousness (it reads the boot log with 0 frame/memory/snapshot samples) belongs to the
  later entry "Perf-budget gate reads real samples". It stays out of scope here, even if the perf step moves.

- The CI security posture stays: third-party actions SHA-pinned, `step-security/harden-runner` as every job's first
  step, workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`. Every new job inherits these (security.md §Supply chain + CI).

- macOS-only failure classes (icons, quarantine, salt race) are out of reach of a Linux pre-push check by
  construction. Nothing here claims them.
- The draft PR #39 is never merged or closed by the builder (handoff note).

- **Marker:** 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-29T05:40:00Z

Make the P-025 hue-shift observable measure the interval its ≤2 000 ms budget bounds, per Conductor's measurement
contract (`D:/dev/projects/conductor/contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` §What a complete implementation
looks like, items 1–4). Today `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms` carries the STALENESS of the service's
`last_seen_unix_nano` at render time, as a slowest-wins maximum across one render pass
(`pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ConstellationCanvas.tsx:112-155`). After this chunk the backend exposes a per-service
`tier_effective_at_unix_nano` on `ServiceListItem`: the instant the service's maximum active-incident tier last
changed value. The rise is the opening incident's `opened_at_unix_nano`; the fall is the `resolved_at_unix_nano`
of the last max-tier holder to resolve. The widget emits ONE sample per service whose tier changed, with
`duration_ms = paint instant − tier_effective_at` at millisecond resolution. The leaf, its field names and its
allowlist entry stay exactly as they are, which is the contract's preferred option (§The observable); only the
value's meaning changes. The operator's rulings shape two edges. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the canvas now
REPAINTS on a data change, so the paint instant exists in that mode (a11y-plan §6). A sample is emitted only for a
change this canvas WITNESSED (`tier_effective_at` ≥ its mount instant), so a tier restored at boot never reports
hours.

Second, per the operator directive (`D:/dev/projects/additional/pc-overseer/relays/pulse-phase-p025-2026-09-29.md`,
founder-delegated): Pulse CI has started no job since at least 2026-07-25. The cause is the workflow-level `env:` in
`ci.yml:12`, `release.yml:35` and `update-channels.yml:53`, which uses `${{ runner.temp }}`. The `runner` context
exists only at STEP level; job-level `env:` does not have it either, per GitHub's context-availability table
fetched at P3. The fix exports `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` from a step into `$GITHUB_ENV`. A committed workflow
self-lint guards it. Because `ci.yml` triggers only on `pull_request` and `push: main`, the operator pass opens ONE
draft PR `chore/migrate-pulse-to-v3 → main` (operator ruling). That PR gives this chunk's commit a real CI run to
read, and every later push re-fires CI. Genuine failures that first run surfaces are this chunk's findings,
triaged under the plan's own rules, not reasons to widen it (directive item 2).

The chunk also discharges two route PREREQs. It is Rust-touching, so it closes the rust gate deferral carried from
`2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth` (workspace clippy + nextest). It records pin #22 at a between-point.
It claims NO capability: P-025 rides P-075, which stays with the Conductor-return entry.

1. **CI parse fix: the three workflow files.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml` and
   `update-channels.yml`:
   - Delete the workflow-level `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/…` line. Leave every other key of those
     workflow-level `env:` blocks untouched.
   - In EVERY job of the three files, insert one step directly AFTER the `Harden runner` step, named
     `Export ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, with `shell: bash`. Its `run` appends
     `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$RUNNER_TEMP/andromeda-pulse-ci-data` (ci.yml), `…-release-data` (release.yml) or
     `…-update-channels-data` (update-channels.yml) to `"$GITHUB_ENV"`, keeping each file's existing suffix. The jobs are `ci.yml`: lint-test-build, supply-chain, coverage;
     `release.yml`: publish-bundle; `update-channels.yml`: update-homebrew, update-scoop.
   - `Harden runner` stays the first step everywhere. No action is added or re-pinned, and `permissions:` is
     untouched.
   - The existing `${{ env.ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR }}` uses (`ci.yml:160,208`, `release.yml:181`) keep resolving,
     because `env` is available in `steps.with`. The boot smoke's three `agent-run.sh` verbs still share one
     exported dir.

2. **Workflow self-lint guard** in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, with two new tests:
   - `workflow_env_references_no_step_only_context`: across `ci.yml`, `release.yml`, `update-channels.yml` and
     `secret-scan.yml`, no value in a workflow-level `env:` block (column-0 `env:` up to the next column-0 key) or a
     job-level `env:` block (a 4-space `env:` directly under a job) contains a `${{ … }}` expression naming `runner.`,
     `job.`, `steps.` or `env.`. Read line-wise and CRLF-safe via `.lines()` (testing.md 2026-05-14).
   - `data_dir_export_precedes_every_consumer`: in each of the six jobs, the `Export ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` step
     sits immediately after `Harden runner`.
   - Mutation-check the first test: re-inserting `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/x` into ci.yml's
     workflow-level env must turn it RED. Restore afterwards.

3. **The `smoke:hue-shift` scenario leg, built BEFORE the fix, run RED at HEAD.**
   - New `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs`, registered as `smoke:hue-shift` in `xtask/src/main.rs`.
   - In `xtask/src/external_resolve.rs`, widen the reused helpers (`spawn_app`, `wait_for_receiver`, `shutdown`,
     `wait_ports_released`, `binary_age`, `tempdir`, `log_family`, `locate_app_binary`, `build_injector`) to
     `pub(crate)`. No behaviour change.
   - Sequence:
     1. Locate the binary and print it with its age.
     2. Build the injector outside the timed section.
     3. Create a fresh data dir and use it as cwd (dev-mode bindings export writes relative to cwd).
     4. Spawn the app with deterministic L4 plus the bootstrap override, then wait for the receiver.
     5. Run the arg-less FINITE storm and poll the app's log family for a `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms`
        record with `severity_tier != "none"` (bounded).
     6. Start `inject_demo --sustained --error-pct=0` in the background, which keeps the services live and healthy
        so the dots stay visible. Poll for a later record with `severity_tier == "none"`, i.e. the fall once the
        120 s auto-resolve fires (bounded).
     7. Stop the injector and the app.
     8. Copy the log family into a per-run directory under `target/hue-shift/`, named by a UTC stamp taken at
        invocation.
   - The PURE verdict `judge_hue_shift(records)` is unit-tested in the same file:
     - **Precondition:** ≥ 1 `interpretation.incident.created` record with `created == true`. Otherwise
       INCONCLUSIVE ("no incident formed — the storm did not trip, or …"; wording per the 2026-08-29 harness rule).
     - **Rise:** the first non-`none` hue record R has anchor error
       `|(R.timestamp_ms − R.duration_ms) − created.timestamp_ms| ≤ 1000`.
     - **Fall:** the first later `none` record F has
       `|(F.timestamp_ms − F.duration_ms) − T.timestamp_ms| ≤ 1000`, where T is the first
       `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick` with `resolved_count ≥ 1` after the rise. If no fall record appeared
       in its window, the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE for the fall, never PASS.
   - Printed lines:
     - `smoke:hue-shift: rise duration_ms=… anchor_error_ms=…`
     - `smoke:hue-shift: fall duration_ms=… anchor_error_ms=…`
     - `smoke:hue-shift: within the 2000 ms budget: yes|no (context only — Conductor grades)`
     - exactly one verdict line, `smoke:hue-shift: PASS`, or `smoke:hue-shift: FAIL — ` / `smoke:hue-shift: INCONCLUSIVE — ` followed by the reason, in the
       sibling's form (`external_resolve.rs:339-343`).
   - Exit codes: 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 INCONCLUSIVE.
   - **Measure first:** build the HEAD release product (`npm run build --prefix pulse-app/ui` →
     `cargo build -p pulse-app --release`) and run `cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift` BEFORE steps 4–8. Record the RED
     reading (the anchor errors) in this chunk's `evidence/` directory. The expected RED is `FAIL` on the rise anchor,
     because at HEAD the anchor is the preceding lifecycle tick (uniform over 15 s). About 7% of RED runs can land
     within 1 000 ms by coincidence; a coincident RED PASS is recorded and the leg re-run, never read as "no defect".

4. **Registry: an all-statuses workspace listing.** Add `list_for_workspace(&self, workspace: &str) -> Vec<Incident>`
   to the `IncidentRegistry` trait (`crates/triage/src/incident/registry.rs`) and implement it on
   `InMemoryIncidentRegistry`. It returns every incident of the workspace, Resolved included; resolved rows are
   retained in the map for the process lifetime. Add a co-located test that it returns Active, Acknowledged and
   Resolved rows and filters by workspace.

6. **Payload field.** `ServiceListItem` (`crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs:54`) gains
   `#[serde(default)] pub tier_effective_at_unix_nano: Option<i64>`, with a single-line doc comment stating the
   rise/fall rule and that it is enriched by the resolver.
   - `list_all` (`:189`) emits `None`.
   - The two test literals at `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/persistence.rs:312,319` gain `None`.

7. **Resolver.** In `pulse-app/src/services_router.rs::list_with_states`:
   - Read `incident_registry.list_for_workspace(&workspace_root)` ONCE.
   - Derive `priority_tier` from its non-Resolved subset (same semantics as today) and `tier_effective_at_unix_nano`
     via `triage::contract::tier_effective_at`, both from that one snapshot, so the two fields can never disagree
     across two reads.
   - Update the module doc (`:16-22`).
   - Extend `pulse-app/tests/unit_services_router.rs` with four cases: a rise, a fall, an acknowledged incident
     (no fall), and an unaffected service (`None`). The existing `priority_tier` tests stay green unchanged.

9. **Webview: fire site + reduced-motion repaint** (`pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ConstellationCanvas.tsx`):
   - Capture `mountedAtMs` once, via a lazily-initialised ref.
   - Replace the P-025 effect body (`:116-156`) with `hueShiftSamples(...)`, where the paint instant is `Date.now()`
     read in the effect. That is the instant contract §The window names: "the instant the canvas effect already
     observes". Call `recordConstellationHueLatency` ONCE PER SAMPLE and drop the slowest-wins loop.
   - Rewrite the effect's comment. It must not describe a rendered halo (design-system §Self-Validation #3).
   - Leave the P-027 effect (`:88-110`) byte-untouched.
   - Hold the frame-loop handle in a ref. Add an effect on `[dots, reducedMotion]` that re-calls the handle's
     `start()` when `reducedMotion` is true. Under reduced motion `start()` paints one static frame from
     `dotsRef.current` and schedules no rAF (`frame-loop.ts:3-9,21-24`), so a tier change now repaints once. It adds
     no transition, animation or literal (design-system §Motion → Accessibility).
   - Update `ConstellationCanvas.test.tsx`:
     - Re-point the existing "emits the delegated timing observables on a live render" hue half. It pinned the old
       first-render emission, which the witnessed rule now correctly suppresses. It becomes a
       rerender-after-mount in which `svc-a` flips to `autonomous` with `tier_effective_at` after mount, asserting
       ONE emission whose `duration_ms` equals the fake-clock delta. Strengthen, never relax (testing.md 2026-08-17
       pinned-defect entry). Use fake `Date` only (testing.md 2026-07-02).
     - Add: two services flipping in one rerender → two calls.
     - Add: a restored tier on first render → zero calls, with discovery asserted as having fired so the absence
       is not vacuous.
     - Add: under a mocked `useReducedMotion() === true`, with the adapter and pipeline mocked available, a
       rerender with a changed tier calls the loop's `start` again, with `frame-loop` mocked to a spy.
   - The P-027 assertions stay.

10. **Bindings + dist + release**, strictly after every default-features cargo op (testing.md 2026-08-30 ARGS_MAP
    entry; security.md 2026-06-12):
    1. Regenerate with `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server --bin pulse-app -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'`.
       `ServiceListItem` gains `tier_effective_at_unix_nano?: number | null`.
    2. `npm run build --prefix pulse-app/ui`.
    3. `cargo build -p pulse-app --release`. The leg and self-verify resolve the release binary first
       (testing.md 2026-07-05 ext. 2026-08-27).
    4. Run `cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift` GREEN and record it in `evidence/`.
    5. Run the full `## Test Commands`.

11. **Wrap-owed records (not /implement edits).**
    - The PREREQ discharge: workspace clippy and nextest ran in this chunk's gates.
    - Pin #22 between-point, recorded in the report at wrap:
      - basis re-verified (`cargo audit` still `duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`);
      - overlap re-enumerated as DISTINCT ids (`cargo deny check advisories`), with `bans licenses sources` exit 0;
      - `probe skipped per ratified interval (next: 67)`, confirming the session count at the wrap and writing no
        ordinal.
- `crates/triage/src/incident/tier_effective.rs` — the pure rise/fall derivation + co-located tests
- `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs` — the `smoke:hue-shift` scenario leg + its pure verdict + tests
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — drop the workflow-level `runner.temp` line; one `$GITHUB_ENV` export step per job (3 jobs)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — same (1 job)
- `.github/workflows/update-channels.yml` — same (2 jobs)
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the two workflow guards
- `crates/triage/src/incident/registry.rs` — `list_for_workspace` on the trait (1 implementor, `InMemoryIncidentRegistry`) + test
- `crates/triage/src/incident/mod.rs` — declare `tier_effective`
- `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` — re-export `tier_effective_at`
- `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs` — `ServiceListItem.tier_effective_at_unix_nano` (literal at `:189`)
- `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/persistence.rs` — two test literals (`:312`, `:319`)
- `pulse-app/src/services_router.rs` — one snapshot → `priority_tier` + `tier_effective_at_unix_nano`
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_services_router.rs` — rise / fall / acknowledged / unaffected cases
- `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` — regenerated
- `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/constellation-types.ts` — `hueShiftSamples`
- `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/constellation-types.test.ts` — its pins
- `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ConstellationCanvas.tsx` — per-service anchored emission + reduced-motion repaint
- `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ConstellationCanvas.test.tsx` — re-pointed + new pins
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — `Cmd::SmokeHueShift`
- `xtask/src/external_resolve.rs` — helpers to `pub(crate)`, no behaviour change

Impact (research §Graph impact, rust plane regenerated this run): `ServiceListItem` has 11 reference sites, of which
3 are struct literals (`lifecycle/registry.rs:189`, `lifecycle/persistence.rs:312,319`). `list_with_states` is called
by `unit_services_router.rs:72,84,123` and, across the name-bridge, by `hooks/use-service-constellation.ts:34`.
`IncidentRegistry` has 1 implementor (grep `impl IncidentRegistry for` → 1).

These are the standard gate set (test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline) plus the webview gates, since the chunk
touches `pulse-app/ui/**`. The rust gates are NOT deferred: the chunk is Rust-touching, which discharges the
carried rust-gate PREREQ. The bindings regen runs after every default-features cargo op. `capability-drift` is the
last gate /implement runs; the operator entries after it regenerate nothing.
Pin #22 (the folded `cargo audit` standing deferral) is listed STRUCTURALLY, never as a pass/fail gate:
- a currency entry for the local advisory-DB copy `cargo audit` reads;
- the probe asserting the ratified RED SIGNATURE (`exit 1` + `duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`);

- the overlap pair: `cargo deny check advisories`, whose owned set is EMPTY since `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`,
  so exit 0 is expected; and `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` as its own invocation, the pass/fail gate
  (the security rule bans the combined form).

Session 66 is a between-point: the signature read IS the basis re-verification. The report records
`probe skipped per ratified interval (next: 67)` for the full form, and enumerates the DISTINCT `RUSTSEC-` ids.

No `role = 'smoke'` entry: the modify-set holds none of test-plan §3's boot-smoke trigger paths (`main.rs`,
`crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `observability.rs`, `tauri.conf.json`, `capabilities/`). The real app is booted anyway
by the self-verify entry and by the live leg, which is this chunk's warm boot of a user-visible surface.

The live leg (`smoke:hue-shift`) boots and stops its own app. Its non-priming probe is the release binary's
presence plus both OTLP ports refusing, so a stale app from an earlier run reads as a failed precondition. The
ui-smoke is `cargo xtask self-verify`: this is a UI chunk, and the harness exists.
Operator entries run in the OPERATOR PASS, never in /implement:
- the seeded hygiene probe;
- a clean-tree push;

- ONE draft PR (operator ruling). It fires `pull_request` CI now and on every later push. The builder never merges
  or closes it; its fate is the founder's.
- the CI read.

`ci.yml`'s wall-clock is unmeasured (no job has run in two months), hence the 3 600 s wait. The CI read's expected
verdict is green. A red read is fixed by further commits in the pass, per the template's operator rules.

Contract: `D:/dev/projects/conductor/contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` (pinned at Pulse `83d4060`,
captured 2026-09-13). Its §What a complete implementation looks like is the acceptance shape:

1. **Expose the tier's effective instant** (`tier_effective_at`) on the payload the constellation canvas already
   receives (`ServiceListItem`, produced by `services.list_with_states`), per the contract's two-case rule:
   - **rise** — an incident opens above the current maximum → that incident's `opened_at_unix_nano`
     (verified: `crates/triage/src/contract.rs:418`, `pub opened_at_unix_nano: i64` on `Incident`);
   - **fall** — every incident holding the maximum leaves the active set → the instant the last one left.
     `[premise-corrected: the contract names the broadcast's transitioned_at_unix_nano (broadcast.rs:41); the persist-cycle reconciler resolves through IncidentRegistry::mark_resolved and emits NO lifecycle event, and the broadcast has no subscriber, so that source misses a leave path. Every resolution path (incidents_router.rs:300, incident_observer.rs:67, persistence.rs:272) goes through mark_resolved, which stamps Incident.resolved_at_unix_nano and KEEPS the row in the in-memory registry (no remove/retain anywhere) — the fall instant is that field]`
     `[premise-corrected: the contract says "by resolution or acknowledgement"; list_active excludes ONLY Resolved (incident/registry.rs:213-221), so an Acknowledged incident stays active and keeps contributing its tier — the maximum falls ONLY on resolution]`
2. **Compute the emitted duration as paint instant − `tier_effective_at`**, millisecond resolution.

3. **Name the carrying field explicitly and admit it to the leaf's allowlist entry** (the leaf's admitted set is
   `duration_ms` + `severity_tier`; verified: the test `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_delegated_timing.rs`
   exists; the allowlist entry sits at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:990`).

4. **Emit per changed service**, not the slowest-wins maximum across the render pass — or carry a service
   identifier. The identifier option is closed by construction: `service` is an OTLP resource
   attribute and may never be a label (security-plan §Logging; obs-plan §5 cardinality — the canvas comment at
   `ConstellationCanvas.tsx:85-87` states this; `unit_observability_allowlist_delegated_timing.rs:74-93` bans
   the identifier fields on the leaf), so per-changed-service emission is the only admissible shape.

The contract's leaf choice: a corrected `duration_ms` on `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms` (preferred), or a
sibling leaf with the old one retired/documented superseded. The field that carries the duration is stated
literally either way.
**Coordinates re-verified at HEAD (P1):**

- Fire site: `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ConstellationCanvas.tsx:112-155` — `elapsedMs = nowMs -
  item.last_seen_unix_nano / 1_000_000` (`:142`), slowest-wins across `dots` (`:143-146`), tagged with the slowest
  dot's tier, one `recordConstellationHueLatency` per pass. Contract terms 1 (staleness) and 2 (slowest-wins) hold
  as written.

- Emit site (a refinement the contract did not name): the leaf is emitted by the TauRPC resolver
  `record_constellation_hue_latency` at `crates/ui-bridge/src/telemetry.rs:272-282` (`target:
  "metric.constellation.hue_update_ms"`), input `ConstellationHueLatencyInput` (`:122`).
- Tier derivation: `pulse-app/src/services_router.rs` — `list_with_states` (`:93`), `tier_rank` (`:80`).
- Lifecycle tick: `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/mod.rs:52` `DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 15 s`.

- `crates/triage/src/baseline/activity_floor.rs:84` `last_observed_unix_nanos` exists (the rejected fix
  candidate's anchor — the contract rules it insufficient; this chunk does NOT take that path).
**Mechanism claims folded as hypotheses (P3 closes):**

- `[premise-corrected: "that site holds … both timestamps" holds for the RISE only — list_with_states reads list_active, which excludes the resolved incidents whose resolved_at is the fall instant; the resolver needs an all-statuses listing of the workspace's incidents from the registry (one IncidentRegistry implementor, so the trait extension threads nowhere else)]` The contract's claim "That site holds the full `Incident` records at the moment it decides the tier, so both timestamps the rule below needs are already in hand there" (contract §The window), kept verbatim for the record.

- "An incident's `priority_tier` is immutable after opening" — VERIFIED at HEAD (mechanism, not the contract's count
  of eight, which is not copied): the only `.priority_tier =` field assignment in `crates/` + `pulse-app/` is the
  derived `ServiceListItem` one (`services_router.rs:97`); the dedupe path (`inference_runtime.rs:808-836`) calls
  `observe_reemission` and never rewrites the tier; the corpus incident UPDATEs (`corpus/src/contract.rs:652`,
  `:682`) set `status, updated_unix_nano, resolved_unix_nano, payload` / `read_unix_nano` only.

- "`last_seen_unix_nano` has no ingest-path writer …" (contract term 3) — NOT re-derived: the plan removes the hue
  observable's dependence on `last_seen_unix_nano` entirely, so nothing rests on it.

- `ServiceListItem` gaining a field is a bindings shape change, NOT a new TauRPC procedure — VERIFIED: the struct
  is the item type of the existing `services.list_with_states` payload and is never bincode-persisted
  (`lifecycle/persistence.rs::services_to_entries` converts it to `ServiceRegistryEntry`); 3 Rust struct literals
  break (`lifecycle/registry.rs:189`, `lifecycle/persistence.rs:312,319`); TS fixtures are unaffected (the field
  renders optional).

- The P-027 discovery effect is a SEPARATE `useEffect` (`ConstellationCanvas.tsx:88-110`) — VERIFIED separable;
  it stays byte-untouched.

- NEW (research): only the WIDGET canvas (`pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ConstellationCanvas.tsx`) emits P-025 — the
  dashboard copy (`dashboard/routes/traces/ConstellationCanvas.tsx`) calls no `recordConstellation*`; the fire
  site stays on the widget.

- NEW (research): under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the widget canvas paints ONCE at loop start
  (`frame-loop.ts:21-24`; the loop effect's deps are `[adapter, reducedMotion]`), so a later tier change is never
  repainted and no paint instant exists — the "paint" end of the window is undefined there (P4 fork).

- NEW (research): the webview polls `services.list_with_states` every 1 000 ms (`use-service-constellation.ts:22`),
  so the observable's floor includes ≤1 s of poll latency — part of the quantity the budget bounds, not an
  artifact.

title: B. CI workflow-parse fix (operator directive, folded)

data.head: ### B. CI workflow-parse fix (operator directive, folded)

body:
The directive (item 1) states CI has never started a job since at least 2026-07-25: three workflow files set a
WORKFLOW-level `env:` from `${{ runner.temp }}`, and the `runner` context is unavailable at workflow level (only
`github` `inputs` `secrets` `vars`). Verified at HEAD:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:12` `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/andromeda-pulse-ci-data`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:35` `… ${{ runner.temp }}/andromeda-pulse-release-data`
- `.github/workflows/update-channels.yml:53` `… ${{ runner.temp }}/andromeda-pulse-update-channels-data`
- Control: `.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` has no workflow-level `env:` (verified).

Fix direction per the directive: move the variable to where `runner` is available (job-level `env:`, or
`$RUNNER_TEMP` inside steps) — the HOW is research's.
`[premise-corrected: GitHub's context-availability table (fetched 2026-09-29) lists jobs.<job_id>.env → github, needs, strategy, matrix, vars, secrets, inputs — NO runner — so job-level env: fails parsing exactly as workflow-level does; runner is available only at step level (steps.env / run / with). The fix is a step writing ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$RUNNER_TEMP/… to $GITHUB_ENV right after harden-runner in each job, bash shell (the Windows matrix leg), so the existing ${{ env.ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR }} uses in later steps keep resolving and the boot-smoke's three verbs keep sharing one exported dir]` Acceptance: a push of this chunk's commit starts real jobs
(`ci.py conclusion` reads checks > 0 on that sha), which is a witness the parse failure cannot pass vacuously.
Further genuine failures the first real run surfaces are THIS chunk's findings, triaged by the plan's own rules,
not reasons to widen it (directive item 2).

Scope boundary on B: the fix touches only the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` placement in the three files (VERIFIED:
its only other uses are `${{ env.ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR }}` in upload `with.path` at `ci.yml:160,208` and
`release.yml:181`, which the step-level `env` context serves; `quality_gate_workflow.rs:185-210` requires ci.yml's
workflow-level `env:` block to keep `CI_RUN_ID` / `GIT_COMMIT_SHA` / `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT`, which stay).
`actionlint` is not installed on this host, so the committed local witness is a workflow self-lint test in
`pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` (no workflow- or job-level `env:` value references a step-only
context); the decisive witness stays the pushed run starting jobs.

body:
The operator ruled three forks at P4 (overseer, founder-delegated). Each widens the scope above only where the
outcome needs it.

- **Reduced-motion repaint, IN scope.** Without it the paint instant does not exist under reduced motion, so the
  P-025 sample would be untrue in that mode. The fix also keeps a11y-plan §6.

- **Witnessed-only samples.** A sample is emitted only when `tier_effective_at` ≥ the canvas mount instant. A

- **One draft PR as the CI carrier.** `ci.yml` triggers only on `pull_request` and `push: main`
