  trigger config changes. It stays an operator entry, never merged or closed by the builder; its fate is the
  founder's. §B's acceptance reads that PR run's checks on the pushed sha.

- **Leaned without asking:** the live leg lives in xtask (`smoke:hue-shift`), following the
  `external_resolve.rs` / `gap_resume.rs` precedent. This adds `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs`, `xtask/src/main.rs` and
  `xtask/src/external_resolve.rs` to the modify-set.
- IN: §A (observable), §B (CI parse fix), the U05 reflow, the two PREREQ discharges.

- OUT: grading P-025 (Conductor's live leg, operator-gated, never a CI gate); the P-027/P-026/P-030 sibling
  delegated-timing leaves beyond byte-preservation; the Halo State Pulse glow layer (deferred to the next version,
  ruling 2026-08-29); the `.gitattributes` re-checkout (founder's hand); any capability claim.

- No new TauRPC procedure, no new capability JSON grant, no new workspace dependency — VERIFIED by the file list in
  `research.md` (the `ServiceListItem` field rides the existing procedure; the hue input struct and its leaf stay
  unchanged — the contract's preferred option, a corrected `duration_ms`).

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-29T22:30Z
- **Chunk base (W182):** `a08ae29dcad7c05cd118be3476eaad37bd697231`. HEAD was here at take-up. Every diff-shaped probe below names this sha, never `HEAD~N`.
- **Claims:** no verification-matrix capability. The one unclaimed id, P-075 (the Conductor e2e drive), is not this chunk's (`matrix.py show --unclaimed`).

Fix the CAUSE of the credit-card false positive in the P-047 scrubber. Today the `credit_card` arm matches any
13–19 digits with ` `/`-` separators and does no checksum (`crates/security/src/scrubber.rs:116-121`). So a
date-time stamp such as the harness data-dir basename `rm-20260923-093840` redacts as a card. After this chunk
the arm redacts a digit run only when some window of WHOLE separator groups, with 13–19 digits in total, passes
the Luhn checksum. Every issued card number passes Luhn (ISO/IEC 7812); the measured value does not (sum 61).
This form is the FOUNDER's own answer at P4, clicked live on 2026-09-30 (the "Luhn on windows" option; he
had also chosen Luhn when the overseer asked him separately).
Research E6 (research.md) measured what the false positive did downstream:

- **The model's input.** The digest's `PROJECT: {cwd basename}` line lives inside `payload_summary`, which
  `Digest::scrubbed_clone` scrubs as ONE value. So the whole digest the model reads collapsed to
  `[redacted:credit_card]`, and the model diagnosed a card leak (Conductor `c97f697`,
  `rm-capture-b2.txt:440-459`).
- **The Report.** The Report's Project Context read `workspace=[redacted: credit_card]`.

Both consumers call `scrub_attribute` unchanged, so both inherit the fix with no consumer edit
(`pii_scrub_closure @ pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs:55`, `scrub_string @ crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs:337`).
The fix must not weaken real PII redaction. The rules that bound it:

- **Catalog shape.** The catalog stays at eight arms in the same order. `scrub_attribute` / `ScrubbedValue`
  stay byte-for-byte the same surface, and no field or consumer is exempted (security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Logging; arch §Conventions → Module visibility discipline).

- **Pins in both directions.** Known card positives, the measured false positive in its path and key forms,
  and the two consumer paths it reached (test-plan §4 security row).

1. **Rework the `credit_card` arm in `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs`** (`patterns()` `:116-122` and `scrub_attribute` `:41-48`).
   The arm becomes a two-stage check.
   - **Candidate.** A candidate is a `\b`-bounded run of ASCII digit groups joined by single ` ` or `-`: the
     shape the current regex already finds, widened to the maximal run so windowing sees every group. Use
     ASCII digits (`[0-9]`, or `(?-u:\d)`). The current `\d` is Unicode-aware, and a non-ASCII digit has no
     Luhn value.
   - **Windows.** Split the candidate at its separators into groups. A window is a run of CONSECUTIVE WHOLE
     groups whose digit count totals 13–19.
   - **Decision.** The arm matches iff at least one window of one candidate passes Luhn. Stop extending a
     window once it passes 19 digits.
   - **Order is preserved.** `scrub_attribute` still walks the arms in order, first match wins. The card arm
     keeps its slot after `email` and before `ssn`, and keeps the category label `"credit_card"`. Only the
     card arm's match predicate changes. The other seven arms and their regexes are untouched.
   - **Where the Luhn code goes.** The Luhn function and the window walk are private (`fn`, or `pub(crate)`
     at most) inside `scrubber.rs`. There is no new crate and no new module export.
   - **The arm comment.** Rewrite the arm's comment (currently "Doesn't check Luhn; intent is
     recall-over-precision") to state the new rule and why. Luhn is a structural validation like
     `provider_key`'s anchored prefix, never entropy scoring. The recall trade the founder accepted: a
     Luhn-invalid mistyped card number no longer redacts.
   - **P-047 literal.** Keep the literal `P-047` in the file header. `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json:62` anchors on it.

2. **Re-pin the recall corpus in `scrubber.rs` tests** (`scrubber_redacts_each_p047_category`, `:143-163`).
   - Replace the case `4532-1234-5678-9010` (Luhn sum 66, research E3) with the Luhn-valid `4532-0151-1283-0366`.
   - Add a NEW `#[rstest]` fn `scrubber_redacts_luhn_valid_card_forms`, asserting `Some("credit_card")` for:
     - `4532015112830366` (contiguous)
     - `4532 0151 1283 0366` (spaced)
     - `4111111111111111`
     - `378282246310005` (Amex 15)
     - `3782 822463 10005` (Amex 4-6-5)
     - `card=4111111111111111` (the JOINED `key=value` form the labels scrub feeds, security-plan "A THIRD scrub SHAPE")
     - `ref 12 4111111111111111` (a card after an unrelated group; research E4)
     - `4111 1111 1111 1111 22` (a card followed by an unrelated group)

3. **Pin the measured false positive in `scrubber.rs` tests.** Add a NEW `#[rstest]` fn
   `scrubber_allows_non_card_digit_runs`. It asserts `ScrubbedValue::Allowed` with the value byte-identical
   (the identity-corpus assertion form, `:209-216`) for:
   - `rm-20260923-093840` (the measured value)
   - `/tmp/rm-20260923-093840`
   - `C:\Users\runner\AppData\Local\Temp\rm-20260923-093840` (a Rust raw string)
   - `workspace=/tmp/rm-20260923-093840`
   - `PROJECT: rm-20260923-093840 (vcs=git)`
   - `1790699962319180900` (the b2 capture's nanosecond timestamp, sum 91)
   - `4532-1234-5678-9010` (the retired Luhn-invalid literal, kept as the documented precision boundary)

   A doc comment on the fn names the Conductor `c97f697` b2 capture as the origin. It uses a synthetic
   literal, never a captured extract (test-plan §11 Test Data).

4. **Pin the digest path in `pulse-app/tests/unit_digest_runtime_scrub.rs`.** Add two tests beside the existing two (`:8-20`), both driving the real `pii_scrub_closure()`:
   - `pii_scrub_closure_keeps_a_digest_whose_project_line_carries_a_date_stamp`: a multi-line payload in the
     digest's shape (`WINDOW: …` / `PROJECT: rm-20260923-093840 (vcs=git)` / `OVERALL: …`) comes back unchanged.
   - `pii_scrub_closure_still_collapses_a_digest_carrying_a_card`: the same payload plus a line holding
     `4111 1111 1111 1111` comes back as `[redacted:credit_card]`. This pins that the whole-value replacement
     is unchanged, so real redaction still fails closed.

5. **Pin the Report path in `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs` tests.** Add
   `assemble_report_keeps_a_date_stamped_workspace_verbatim` to the existing `#[cfg(test)]` module. For an
   incident whose `workspace` is `/tmp/rm-20260923-093840`, `assemble_report(…).project_context` equals
   `workspace=/tmp/rm-20260923-093840`. Build the incident with the module's existing fixture helper; no new
   helper is needed if one fits. Production code in `markdown.rs` is NOT edited.

6. **Mutation check (RED-before / GREEN-after), recorded in `chunks/2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive/evidence/`.**
   Run two temporary mutations, then revert each:
   - **(a) Luhn neutralized** (the predicate always true): `scrubber_allows_non_card_digit_runs` must go RED,
     proving the Luhn decision is what frees the measured value.
   - **(b) Windowing collapsed** (Luhn over the whole candidate's digits only): the
     `ref 12 4111111111111111` and `4111 1111 1111 1111 22` cases of `scrubber_redacts_luhn_valid_card_forms`
     must go RED, proving the window walk carries recall.

   Record each mutation's failing test names. Also record the pre-change run: the new
   `scrubber_allows_non_card_digit_runs` fails against the untouched arm, which is the RED-before
   (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging's verification form).
- none
- `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs` — the `credit_card` arm's match predicate (candidate run → group windows → Luhn), its comment, and the recall + false-positive `#[rstest]` pins (Steps 1–3)
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_digest_runtime_scrub.rs` — two digest-level pins through `pii_scrub_closure` (Step 4)
- `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs` — one test-module pin on `assemble_report` (Step 5; no production edit)

The standard gate set runs unconditionally, with `capability-drift` LAST among the cargo gates (test-plan §3
Per-chunk gate discipline). `pulse-app/ui/**` is untouched, so the npm webview gates are not listed.

- **Targeted selector (NEW).** Selects the five tests this chunk writes by name. Its baseline on the untouched
  tree is red (no such tests), which is its known-positive control.

- **Diff probes.** Both name the chunk base `a08ae29dcad7c05cd118be3476eaad37bd697231` (operator directive
  W182). One asserts that no manifest or lockfile changed (arch §Inherited Defaults → Validation: no new
  dependency). The other records the changed-file roster.

- **Boot smoke.** Not a gate here. /implement P3 runs it on the founder's word at P4 ("Run it", 2026-09-30).
  The prior chunk's host constraint (no `pulse-app` start, no bind on 4317/4318) is RELEASED by the founder.
  The smoke uses the
  standing warm-boot recipe:
  1. Warm `cargo build -p pulse-app` plus `cargo build -p ingest --example inject_demo`.
  2. Make ONE exported fresh data dir named `rm-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`-shaped. Launch
     `target/debug/pulse-app.exe` BY PATH with that dir as BOTH `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` and the cwd, so
     workspace detection yields the measured shape. Set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` in the app's own
     spawn env.
  3. Poll `:4317`, then seed with `./target/debug/examples/inject_demo.exe`, bounded to about 25 s.
  4. Read the `<data_dir>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl*` family. Assert 0 `app.panic.fatal`, 0 ERROR, and at
     least one `digest.assemble.request`, `interpretation.prompt.assemble` and `interpretation.incident.created`.
  5. Stop by the specific PID with PowerShell `Stop-Process`, and confirm `:4317`/`:4318` are closed.

  No log field carries scrubbed text (by design), so the smoke proves boot and data flow under the measured
  naming shape. The text equality is proved by the Step 2–5 pins. The (smoke) criterion's log family is
  produced by that P3 run, not by a listed entry (plan-template: the real boot smoke is /implement P3, not a
  gate). Its readings land in `chunks/2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive/evidence/`.

- **Step 6 mutation check (ONE-SHOT).** It mutates source and reverts, so it is never a gate. /implement runs
  it once and records both readings (RED-before plus the two mutations) in `evidence/`. The listed
  non-mutating targeted-selector entry guards the property on every re-run.

- **The CI half is operator-driven:** the hygiene read, the pre-push check, the commit+push, then the CI read
  of the pushed head (warm round ≈ 25.5 min per the last wrap, so the wait is 2400 s).

data.head: ## Intent (the working entry, verbatim title + hint)

body:
Scrubber path false positive — a digit run in a path or workspace key is not redacted as a card number, so
the model's PROJECT line stops reporting a credit-card leak that does not exist.

- Fix the CAUSE in the scrubber (`crates/security/src/scrubber.rs`), not at one consumer: the `credit_card`
  arm must stop matching a digit run that is not a card number — the measured instance being a data-dir
  basename `rm-20260923-093840` (a date-time stamp) inside a workspace key.

- A real card check replaces the bare 13–19-digit shape. Its exact form is a P4 decision over the candidates
  research laid out (research.md §Mechanism equalities E3–E5, §Open questions): Luhn over candidate windows,
  a separator-grouping grammar, or both. Luhn un-redacts the Luhn-invalid pin `4532-1234-5678-9010`
  (sum 66), and a greedy-match Luhn misses a card beside another digit group (E4), so windowing is required.

- Real PII redaction is NOT weakened: real (Luhn-valid) card numbers in every form the catalog targets stay
  redacted, and every other arm's known positive stays as it is. [amended at P5 val-1, intent-incomplete: the
  recall pin `4532-1234-5678-9010` is not a card number (Luhn sum 66, research E3). Under the founder's
  "Luhn on windows" answer (2026-09-30) it moves to the documented Allowed boundary and is replaced by the
  Luhn-valid `4532-0151-1283-0366`. The founder accepted the trade that a mistyped, Luhn-invalid card no
  longer redacts]

- Tests pin both directions: the known positives (real card-shaped values that must still redact) AND the
  measured false positive (`rm-20260923-093840`, and the workspace-key form it reached the model in) as
  `Allowed`. The false-positive corpus in `scrubber.rs` is the place such pins live (security rule §Logging &
  redaction: "the false-positive corpus … is what bounds it").

- In: the `credit_card` arm and its tests. [premise-corrected: no sibling arm is involved — `ssn` does not
  match `rm-20260923-093840` or its path/key forms (research E2), and once the card arm stops matching, no
  other arm claims the value]

- In: the paths by which the value reaches the model and the Report, READ and pinned end-to-end, not
  redesigned. [premise-corrected: there are two paths at HEAD, and the prompt's `<PROJECT>` block is not one
  of them — (a) the Report's `assemble_report` scrubs `incident.workspace` WHOLE → `workspace=[redacted:
  credit_card]` (the capture's spaced form, `markdown::scrub_string`); (b) the L4 digest block: the digest's
  `PROJECT: {cwd basename}` line lives inside `payload_summary`, which `Digest::scrubbed_clone` scrubs WHOLE,
  so one false match replaces the ENTIRE digest the model reads with `[redacted:credit_card]`; the prompt's
  `<PROJECT>` block itself carries `digest.workspace` UNSCRUBBED — research E6]

- Out: removing scrubbing from workspace keys or paths altogether (that would weaken redaction — the fix is
  precision in the card arm, not an exemption for a field). (security + arch + obs extracts concur)
- Out: the Conductor repo (read-only from here); Conductor's v3-09 series consumes the fix.

- Out: re-scrubbing or rewriting already-stored corpus rows (arch history: stored L4 text keeps the old
  placeholder; the report states that residual).

- Out: the whole-value replacement that makes one match wipe a whole digest. It follows from P-048's
  category-only `Redacted` and is a candidate separate route entry, not this chunk (research §Open questions
  NOTE).

- `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute` — the P-047 8-category catalog; the category COUNT, arm ORDER and
  signature do not change (verified: security extract + graph).

- Every consumer of `scrub_attribute` inherits the change, with no edit (verified: 12 production caller fns in
  buffer / interpretation / pulse-app, research §Graph impact).

- The card arm's shape ("13-19 digits … Doesn't check Luhn") is documented in the scrubber's own source
  comment (`scrubber.rs:116-117`), which this chunk rewrites. [premise-corrected: security-plan.md's body names
  `credit_card` only as a catalog member and never states the arm's shape, so any wrap amendment records the

Pulse ships under **MIT OR Apache-2.0**, copyright holder Turbolet85, in the same shape Conductor landed at

- the npm manifest and its lockfile root entry;

- the two distribution-channel manifests that `update-channels.yml` generates (Homebrew formula, Scoop manifest),
  each in its own dual-license syntax.

The Tauri bundles need no edit: `bundle.license` defaults to the Cargo value (research.md, tauri-utils 2.9.0
`config.rs:1633`).

**The Conductor precedent needs one correction.** Conductor's red-before/green-after rode cargo-deny, because it
REMOVED a `private = { ignore = true }` exemption. Pulse's `deny.toml` never set that key, so cargo-deny already
license-checks all 16 own crates at the base. This was measured with a scratch config without `"MIT"`, which rejects
every member (research.md §Patterns detected). A deny reading would be green at the base and green after, so it
proves nothing. The witness is instead a co-located **xtask test module**. It is RED at `1dfca74`, GREEN after, runs
in every CI round through the standard workspace nextest gate, and is mutation-checked per surface. The founder chose
this form at P4 through the overseer: "the smallest surface that still reds at 1dfca74, greens after, runs in every
CI round, and is mutation-checked per surface".

Supply-chain gates stay green with no relaxation: `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` passes (both identifiers
are in `deny.toml [licenses] allow`, :80-81). `check:npm-supply-chain` passes with the same standing exceptions.
Per security-plan §Dependency Security → CI integration and → npm channel, and test-plan §9 Pipeline structure →
Supply chain.

1. **Witness first (RED at base).** Create `xtask/src/license_check.rs` as a test-only module and declare it in
   `xtask/src/main.rs` beside the existing `mod` list (:9-20) as `#[cfg(test)] mod license_check;`.
   - **How it reads files:** it resolves the workspace root with the in-repo idiom
     `Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).parent()` (`xtask/src/main.rs:658`, `npm_gate.rs:314-319`).
   - **How it parses:** committed repo files only, no network (test-plan §11 Universal). JSON is parsed with the
     existing `serde_json` dependency. TOML is read as text, so the chunk adds no dependency and `Cargo.lock` does
     not move.
   - **Naming:** four `#[test]` fns, each name starting `license_`:
     - `license_texts_present_at_root` — both files exist.
       - `LICENSE-MIT` contains `Copyright (c) 2026 Turbolet85` and `Permission is hereby granted, free of charge`.
       - `LICENSE-APACHE` contains `Apache License`, `Version 2.0, January 2004` and
         `TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR USE, REPRODUCTION, AND DISTRIBUTION`.
     - `license_workspace_value_is_dual_and_inherited` — checks the root `Cargo.toml` and every member manifest.
       - The root `Cargo.toml`'s `[workspace.package]` section holds exactly `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`.
       - The `[workspace] members` array is parsed from the same file. The parsed list must be non-empty and must
         contain both `pulse-app` and `xtask`, a control against a vacuous parse.
       - For every member, that member's `Cargo.toml` carries the line `license.workspace = true` and no line beginning
         `license =` (no per-crate override, per arch §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]).
     - `license_npm_manifest_and_lock_root_agree` — `pulse-app/ui/package.json` `license` equals
       `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, and `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json` `packages[""].license` equals the same value.
     - `license_channel_manifests_carry_dual_license` — checks `.github/workflows/update-channels.yml`.
       - It contains `license any_of: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]` and `"license": "MIT|Apache-2.0"`.
       - It contains neither `license "MIT"` nor `"license": "MIT",`.
   - **RED reading:** run the witness selector (Test Commands, the `license_check::` entry) BEFORE any other edit and
     record the RED reading (4 of 4 failing) in `evidence/`. This is the red-before, taken against the base tree's
     surfaces.

2. **LICENSE texts.** Write `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE` at the root, byte-identical to Conductor's committed
   copies at `cdb7082`. `LICENSE-MIT` opens `Copyright (c) 2026 Turbolet85`. `LICENSE-APACHE` is the verbatim Apache
   License 2.0 (201 lines, md5 `1836efb2eb779966696f473ee8540542`); its appendix template line stays as the standard
   text. Copy them from the git objects (`git -C D:/dev/projects/conductor show cdb7082:LICENSE-MIT`, and the same
   for `LICENSE-APACHE`) with no network. Then confirm by md5 that the copies equal the source blobs, and that both
   are LF (`.gitattributes` `* text=auto eol=lf`).

3. **Cargo.** At `Cargo.toml:26` (`[workspace.package]`), change `license = "MIT"` to
   `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`. Touch no member manifest: all 16 already inherit it (research.md, 16
   `license.workspace = true` hits).

4. **npm.** Change `pulse-app/ui/package.json:6` to `"license": "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`. Make the same one-line edit to
   the lockfile's ROOT entry at `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json:10` (`packages[""]`) by hand. Do not run
   `npm install` or any lockfile regeneration, because the resolved vitest 4.1.11 / `@vitest/mocker` 4.1.11 versions
   must stay intact (tests-history). Leave `:60` (`node_modules/@asamuzakjp/css-color`) untouched.

5. **Channel manifests.** In `.github/workflows/update-channels.yml`, edit the generated heredoc texts only:
   - the Homebrew formula's `license "MIT"` (:196) becomes `license any_of: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]` (Homebrew
     Licence Guidelines' either-of form);

     "If the entire application is dual licensed, separate licenses with a pipe symbol (|)").

   `.claude/rules/security.md` §Supply chain + CI).
6. **GREEN.** Re-run the witness selector and record 4 of 4 passing.

8. **Run the gates** in the Test Commands order. `capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features workspace
   nextest (operator directive). The `--features mcp-server` bindings regen is the last cargo-adjacent entry, and the
   base-named bindings probe after it confirms `bindings/index.ts` ends byte-identical to `1dfca74`.

- `LICENSE-APACHE` — Apache License 2.0, verbatim (Conductor `cdb7082` bytes)
- `xtask/src/license_check.rs` — the four `license_*` witness tests (test-only module)
- `Cargo.toml` — `[workspace.package] license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` (:26)
- `pulse-app/ui/package.json` — `"license": "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` (:6)

Research listed two conditional touchpoints that the P4 fork (test module, not verb) and the no-new-dependency lean
retire: `xtask/Cargo.toml` (no `toml` dependency, because TOML is read as text) and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (no
new verb, so no CI step).

**Order is load-bearing.** `cargo xtask capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features
`cargo nextest run --workspace` (operator directive 2026-09-30). That run rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`
to the no-mcp shape, the recurrence recorded in the handoff's deferred `recurrence-despite-learning`. The
`--features mcp-server` `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen follows the workspace run as the last cargo-adjacent entry. A
base-named probe then asserts the bindings end byte-identical to `1dfca74`, because this chunk adds no procedure.

This departs from test-plan §3's "`capability-drift` runs LAST" wording, and the departure is recorded here and as
an expected amendment. It is safe because the targeted witness selector runs only tests whose names match
`license_check::`, so it constructs no TauRPC router and cannot regenerate the bindings.
`check:staged-artifacts`, and the staged half of `capability-drift`, read the git index, not the worktree.

- **Advisories:** `cargo deny check advisories` stays a separate observation and is not folded into the
  `bans licenses sources` gate (`.claude/rules/security.md` 2026-08-17). It is not a gate here because this chunk
  moves no dependency: the `Cargo.lock` probe asserts that.

- **The mutation check** (Step 7) mutates the tree, so it is a one-shot, not an entry. The listed non-mutating
  witness selector guards the property on every re-run.

- **Check 4 (8) ordering, resolved:** the `capability-drift` entry precedes the bindings regen (`role = 'build'`) on

  the later default-features workspace nextest rewrites. The regenerated artifact's verifier is the base-named

- **The CI half is operator-driven:** the hygiene read, then the local pre-push gate, then the commit+push, then the

- **Marker:** 2026-09-30-p-027-discovery-bound · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-30T08:24Z

On a freshly booted app, a service's first span must put its constellation dot on screen within P-027's ≤ 5 s
bound. Today the dot waits for the service registry's first 15 s lifecycle tick (measured first rise 9 986 ms at
2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable). The cause is in the discovery path. `ServiceRegistry` gains
entries only inside `tick_all` (heartbeat), a restart, an override or a corpus restore, never on span arrival
(`crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs:205-345`), and the heartbeat skips its immediate first tick
(`lifecycle/mod.rs:96`). The fix registers a service at its FIRST SIGHTING, through a third `SpanObserver`
adapter at the pulse-app boundary. The adapter consumes the scrubbed name the buffer tap already passes, respects
the baseline's `ACTIVITY_FLOOR_SERVICE_CAP`, and performs the same `Unknown → Bootstrapping` / `Activity`
transition the tick would have performed, only earlier. The 5 s budget, the heartbeat cadence and the P-027
observable are not changed (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns → Module dependency direction; security-plan
§Security Anti-Patterns → Logging, the `extract_service_name` choke point; obs-plan §8 delegated-timing leaves).

A new dev-host scenario leg, `cargo xtask smoke:discovery`, proves the bound against the real release binary on a
fresh data dir. It grades the interval from the first `duckdb.append {table_name: "spans"}` record (the
first-sighting instant) to the first `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` record (the paint), and it requires the
discovery record's own anchor to land on that first-sighting instant. It reads RED at the chunk base and GREEN
after the fix (per test-plan §3 Direct-binary smoke variant + the `smoke:hue-shift` paragraph). The P-025 hue
observable keeps its anchor and emission rule, and `cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift` must still PASS. Its fresh-boot
rise value is predicted to shorten, because the dot now exists before the incident opens.

Research falsified one scope premise, recorded in scope.md. At HEAD the P-027 mark's anchor
(`last_seen_unix_nano`) is stamped at tick time (`registry.rs:333-341`), so the discovery record cannot see the
gap it bounds. After the fix a brand-new service's first appearance has `last_seen` = its first-sighting
instant, so the existing mark then measures first-seen-to-dot for the case this chunk grades.

1. **Build the scenario leg FIRST, and read it RED at the chunk base.**
   - New `xtask/src/discovery.rs`, registered in `xtask/src/main.rs` as `smoke:discovery`: a `#[command(name =
     "smoke:discovery", about = …)]` variant `SmokeDiscovery` plus its dispatch arm, on the `SmokeHueShift` shape
     at `xtask/src/main.rs:93-97` / `:264`. Reuse the `crate::external_resolve` helpers exactly as
     `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs:29-32` does: `locate_app_binary`, `binary_age`, `build_injector`, `tempdir`,
     `spawn_app`, `wait_for_receiver`, `shutdown`, `wait_ports_released`, `log_family`, `LegOutcome`.
   - Runner sequence:
     1. Locate the release binary and print it with its age.
     2. Build the injector outside the timed section.
     3. Create a fresh data dir.
     4. Spawn the app and wait for the receiver.
     5. Poll the log family until a `services.list_with_states.request` record exists. That is the webview
        polling, an explicit signal, never a sleep. Bound the wait at 60 s; if it runs out → INCONCLUSIVE.
     6. Start `inject_demo --sustained --error-pct=0`. Every injector batch carries all five services
        (`crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs:333`), and a healthy feed keeps them live without forming a storm.
     7. Poll the log family until a `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` record appears, or until
        `OBSERVE_WINDOW` (30 s) has passed since the first `duckdb.append` record with
        `fields.table_name == "spans"`.
     8. Stop the injector and the app, and wait until the ports are released.
     9. Copy the log family to `target/discovery/{UTC stamp taken at invocation}/`.
     10. Judge the run and print the verdict.
   - PURE verdict `judge_discovery(lines)`, unit-tested in the same file:
     - A = the timestamp of the first `duckdb.append` record with `table_name == "spans"`.
     - P = the timestamp of the first `services.list_with_states.request` record.
     - D = the first `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` record at or after A.
     - Preconditions → INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS:
       - no A: "no spans were appended — the injector never delivered, or the append record never reached the log";
       - no P, or P > A: "the webview was not polling before the first span arrived — the interval would measure
         the webview mount, not discovery".
     - No D within `OBSERVE_WINDOW` of A → FAIL: "no discovery sample within 30 s of the first spans append — the
       dot did not appear, or its sample never reached the log". Word it as an observation, never a single cause
       (2026-08-29 harness rule).
     - `interval_ms = D.ts − A` and `anchor_error_ms = |(D.ts − D.duration_ms) − A|`.
     - PASS iff `interval_ms ≤ 5000` AND `anchor_error_ms ≤ 1000` AND the log holds 0 `app.panic.fatal` and 0
       `level == "ERROR"` records. Any failed half → FAIL, naming the half.
     - `observe_window_supports_verdict()` refuses (INCONCLUSIVE) an `OBSERVE_WINDOW` below
       `LIFECYCLE_TICK_S (15) + POLL_S (1) + 5`, so the RED reading is reachable (the 2026-08-28
       run-window-outlasts-threshold rule).
   - Printed lines (the report quotes them):
     - `smoke:discovery: first-sighting→dot interval_ms={n} anchor_error_ms={m} discovered_count={k}`
     - `smoke:discovery: within the 5000 ms bound: {yes|no}`
     - `smoke:discovery: log family preserved at {path}`
     - a last line of `smoke:discovery: PASS`, `smoke:discovery: FAIL — {why}` or
       `smoke:discovery: INCONCLUSIVE — {why}`.
     - Exits: 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 INCONCLUSIVE.
   - Unit tests in `xtask/src/discovery.rs` `mod tests`, over synthetic `json!` lines on the `hue_shift.rs` tests'
     shape: `judge_passes_within_bound_anchored_on_first_append` ·
     `judge_fails_over_bound_when_anchor_is_the_tick` (the RED shape: D 10 s after A, anchor 9.5 s after A) ·
     `judge_inconclusive_without_spans_append` · `judge_inconclusive_when_webview_not_polling_first` ·
     `judge_fails_without_discovery_sample_in_window` · `observe_window_supports_verdict_boundary`.
   - **RED reading at the base.** With the product source untouched, build `cargo build -p pulse-app --release`
     and run `cargo xtask smoke:discovery`. It must exit 1 with `within the 5000 ms bound: no`. Predicted:
     interval ≈ 10–16 s, anchor error ≈ 9–15 s. Record what it measures, not the prediction. Write the printed
     lines and the preserved path to `evidence/red-leg-at-base.md`. This follows MEASURE-FIRST (test-plan §3): the
     defect is latency-shaped, so the over-budget reading is the RED evidence of record, and no clean-log assertion
     binds RED.

2. **Registry: register at first sighting** (`crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs`).
   - Add a required method to `ServiceRegistry` (:74):
     `fn register_first_sighting(&self, service: &str, now_unix_nano: i64) -> Option<ServiceLifecycleEvent>`.
     Implement it on `InMemoryServiceRegistry` (:182), the only implementer
     (`grep -rn 'impl ServiceRegistry for' crates pulse-app` → 1 hit).
   - Semantics:
     - An empty `service` → `None`, matching :230 / :278 / :326.
     - An entry that already exists → `None`, and the entry is not touched.
     - Otherwise insert atomically through the DashMap entry API's vacant arm, so it races safely with `tick_all`'s
       `or_insert`. The new entry is `ServiceRegistryEntry { state: Bootstrapping, first_seen_unix_nano: now,
       last_seen_unix_nano: now, last_transition_unix_nano: now, manual_override: None }`.
     - Return `Some(ServiceLifecycleEvent { from_state: Unknown, to_state: Bootstrapping, trigger: Activity,
       transitioned_at_unix_nano: now, … })`. That is the event `tick_all` emits on a first observation
       (`next_natural_state(Unknown) = Bootstrapping`, :424).
     - Increment a registry-held `AtomicU64` first-sighting counter.
   - Add `fn take_first_sightings(&self) -> u64` to the trait: swap the counter to 0 and return the prior value.
   - Co-located tests, with the clock injected as a parameter per the triage convention:
     - `first_sighting_registers_bootstrapping_entry_listed_before_any_tick`: after one call, `list_all` holds the
       service with `state == Bootstrapping` and `last_seen_unix_nano == now`.
     - `first_sighting_returns_the_activity_event_once`: a second call returns `None`.
     - `first_sighting_drops_empty_service`.
     - `first_sighting_then_tick_emits_no_duplicate_event`: a following `tick_all` with a `Learning` snapshot emits
       no event for that service.

3. **Fold first sightings into the tick's transition aggregate** (`crates/triage/src/lifecycle/mod.rs`).
   - In `emit_tick_observability` (:155), add `registry.take_first_sightings()` to the `(Unknown, Bootstrapping)`
     bucket before the `triage.lifecycle.transition` records are emitted (:201-217).
   - The wire contract stays identical: same target, same `{from_state, to_state, count}` leaf, one record per
     bucket per tick. A first sighting keeps appearing as an `unknown → bootstrapping` count on the next tick, as
     it did when the tick performed it. No allowlist change.
   - Co-located test `first_sighting_transitions_fold_into_tick_aggregate`: register one first sighting, call
     `emit_tick_observability` under the existing capture shape at `mod.rs:351`, and assert one
     `triage.lifecycle.transition` record with `from_state = "unknown"`, `to_state = "bootstrapping"`,
     `count = 1`.
   - Re-export nothing new unless the adapter needs it. `ServiceLifecycleEvent` and `ServiceRegistry` are already
     on `triage::contract`; extend `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` only for a new public item.

4. **Baseline: a tracked-service query** (`crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs`).
   - Add `pub fn tracks_service(&self, service_name: &str) -> bool` beside `error_rate` (:374). It returns
     `self.services.contains_key(service_name)`, the same map `observe_span`'s cap guard reads (:292-298).

5. **The first-sighting adapter** (new `pulse-app/src/discovery_observer.rs` + `pub mod discovery_observer;` in
   `pulse-app/src/lib.rs`).
   - `DiscoveryObserverAdapter { registry: Arc<dyn ServiceRegistry>, baseline: Arc<BaselineState>, broadcast:
     Arc<ServiceLifecycleBroadcast> }` implements `ingest::observer::SpanObserver`, on the
     `BaselineObserverAdapter` shape (`pulse-app/src/baseline_observer.rs:30`).
   - `observe_span`:
     1. Return at once if the name is empty.
     2. Return if the registry already lists the service. This is the per-span cost: one DashMap read.
     3. Return if `!baseline.tracks_service(name)`, which keeps the cap.
     4. Call `registry.register_first_sighting(name, now_nanos)` and, on `Some(event)`, send it on
        `broadcast.sender()`, ignoring a send error as `lifecycle/mod.rs:121-124` does.
   - No tracing on this path: per-span emission is barred (obs-plan §11), and the fold in step 3 carries the count.
   - The adapter receives the SCRUBBED name the buffer tap passes (`crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:245`). It never
     re-extracts.

6. **Boot wiring** (`pulse-app/src/main.rs`).
   - Move the `CompositeSpanObserver` construction (:572-581) below `lifecycle_registry` (:677). Its first consumer
     is the buffer consumer spawn at :1177, so no consumer is reordered.
   - Compose `vec![baseline_adapter, restart_adapter, discovery_adapter]` with the discovery adapter LAST. The
     baseline must admit the service before the discovery adapter asks `tracks_service` in the same
     `observe_span` fan-out (`restart_observer.rs:80-98` iterates in `Vec` order).
   - The heartbeat spawn (:1483) and `DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL` are NOT touched.

7. **Adapter pins** (`pulse-app/tests/unit_span_observers.rs`, a new section on the file's existing sections'
   shape):
   - `discovery_adapter_registers_admitted_service_and_broadcasts`: the baseline observes first; the registry lists
     the service; one event is received on a broadcast receiver; a second span broadcasts nothing.
   - `discovery_adapter_skips_service_the_baseline_did_not_admit`: a baseline that does not track the name → the
     registry stays empty.
   - `discovery_adapter_composed_after_baseline_lists_service_on_first_span`: a `CompositeSpanObserver` built in
     boot order lists the service after ONE `observe_span`.

8. **The v0.2.0 P-027 notes line** (`docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json`, the P-027 entry's `notes`
   only).
   - Append one dated sentence: the `discovery_ms` anchor is the registry's `last_seen_unix_nano`, which since this
     chunk is stamped at the service's first sighting, so a brand-new service's first-appearance sample measures
     first-seen-to-dot; before this chunk it was the 15 s tick stamp.
   - Scenarios, ids and the delegation sentence are unchanged. `cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` stays green.

9. **GREEN.** Rebuild `cargo build -p pulse-app --release`, then:
   - run `cargo xtask smoke:discovery` → exit 0. Record the printed lines in `evidence/green-leg.md`.
   - run `cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift` → exit 0. Record rise/fall in `evidence/hue-shift-after.md` beside the prior
     chunk's 9 986 / 510 ms.
   - Predicted: the rise falls to ≤ ~2 s, because the dot exists before the incident opens, while the anchor
     errors stay ≤ 1000 ms. Record what it measures.
- `pulse-app/src/discovery_observer.rs` — `DiscoveryObserverAdapter`, the first-sighting `SpanObserver`
- `xtask/src/discovery.rs` — the `smoke:discovery` scenario leg (pure judge + runner + unit tests)

- `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs` — `register_first_sighting` + `take_first_sightings` on the trait and
  its one impl; four co-located tests

- `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/mod.rs` — fold `take_first_sightings()` into the `(unknown, bootstrapping)`
  transition bucket; one co-located test
- `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs` — `tracks_service`
- `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` — re-export only if step 3 adds a public item
- `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod discovery_observer;`
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — composite moved below the registry; discovery adapter composed last
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_span_observers.rs` — three adapter pins
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the `smoke:discovery` verb + dispatch arm
- `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json` — the P-027 notes sentence
Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact):
- `list_all` @ `pulse-app/src/services_router.rs:96` (its only production caller) is unchanged.
- `tick_all` @ `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/mod.rs:105` / `:139` is unchanged.

- `ServiceRegistry` has one implementer; its 41 `refs` are `Arc<dyn …>` holders plus test constructions of
  `InMemoryServiceRegistry`, so a new required method breaks no test double.
- `CompositeSpanObserver` @ `pulse-app/src/main.rs:578` is the single production construction.

The chunk touches `pulse-app/src/main.rs`, one of test-plan §3's boot-smoke trigger paths. Its `role = 'smoke'`
entry is `cargo xtask self-verify` against the release build, which boots, asserts and quits cleanly. On top of
that, `smoke:discovery` is the direct-binary smoke variant: release binary, fresh data dir, real OTLP, and on GREEN
0 `app.panic.fatal` / 0 ERROR plus a clean stop with the ports released. /implement P3's warm boot smoke still runs
per the standing directive.

No `pulse-app/ui/**` file changes. So there is no webview gate trio and no `cargo xtask test:a11y`; self-verify is
listed as the boot smoke, not as a UI gate. A probe below asserts that the webview tree is untouched.

The RED reading is a ONE-SHOT run at implement step 1: `cargo xtask smoke:discovery` against a release build of
the untouched product source, recorded in `evidence/red-leg-at-base.md`. It is not a listed entry, because the light
gate re-runs entries verbatim against the fixed tree. The listed `smoke:discovery` entry guards the property on
re-run (GREEN).

`capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features workspace nextest (operator directive 2026-09-30). The

The chunk adds no TauRPC procedure and no bridge-crossing field, so the measured close applies.

title: cargo fmt --check
body:
[[gate]]

  soft SLO budgets").

  event once, empty-name drop, no duplicate on the next tick, the tick fold, cap respected, boot-order
  composition, and the leg judge's PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE / window arms (per test-plan §8 Time; §10 Coverage —

  bindings regen last, and the chunk-base `git diff --quiet` close exit 0 (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate
  discipline).

- (arch) `triage`'s manifest gains no `ingest` / `pulse-app` dependency, and the first-sighting wiring lives at the
  pulse-app boundary. The W182 diff probe prints nothing for the manifests (per architecture §Cross-cutting
  Patterns → Module dependency direction).

- (arch) The dot stays sourced through `services.list_with_states` → `InMemoryServiceRegistry::list_all`, and no
  procedure or bridge-crossing field is added. The bindings close is byte-identical to the base (per architecture
  §Occupied Resources → Tauri IPC routes).

  `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:245`), registers only baseline-admitted services, and adds no tracing record
  carrying a service name (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; §Logging & Monitoring "What
  NEVER to log").

- (obs) No new target and no allowlist change. First sightings still surface as `triage.lifecycle.transition
  {from_state: unknown, to_state: bootstrapping, count}` on the tick, and `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms`

  - registered state `Bootstrapping`, leaned per `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/state_machine.rs` (the `Unknown`
    doc: "services seen via prior corpus but not yet observed in the current session");
  - the discovery anchor stays `last_seen`, leaned per test-plan §3 (the bindings close for a changed shape is

    class, no new crossing.

  Settings-sourced, hot-reload-classified cadence contract for every transition (config-watcher
  `partition_changed_keys`), and it still leaves up to a tick interval of latency.

- Registering at first sighting as `Unknown` — rejected: `Unknown` is defined as not yet observed this session,
  and the tick's own first-observation path yields `Bootstrapping`.

- A `first_seen_unix_nano` field on `ServiceListItem`, with the mark re-anchored on it — rejected for this chunk:

- Driving the leg with the arg-less finite storm — rejected: no incident is needed, and `--sustained --error-pct=0`
  keeps the five services live without one.

title: Mechanism re-derivation (the equality the design needs)

data.head: ## Mechanism re-derivation (the equality the design needs)

body: - **Defect, re-derived at HEAD (was `measured at` P-025).** For a service first seen at instant S on a fresh boot, the earliest instant it can be listed by `services.list_with_states` is the first `tick_all` after S, because no other path inserts on span arrival (`registry.rs:205-345`). The first tick fires 15 s after heartbeat spawn (`mod.rs:52`, `:96`). The dot then follows within one 1 s poll (`use-service-constellation.ts:22`). So first-seen-to-dot = (next tick − S) + ≤ 1 s, up to ~16 s, measured 9 986 ms. VERIFIED.

- **The equality the fix needs.** For every span whose scrubbed service name is non-empty and admitted by the baseline under `ACTIVITY_FLOOR_SERVICE_CAP`, the registry holds an entry for that name BEFORE `observe_span` returns. The observer runs in the buffer consumer on the batch's `now_nanos`, so the entry exists within milliseconds of S. `list_all` then lists it on the next poll, giving first-seen-to-dot ≤ ~1 s + paint.

- **The state it registers.** Per `state_machine.rs` the entry is `Bootstrapping`, the same state `tick_all` reaches on first observation (`next_natural_state(Unknown) = Bootstrapping`, `registry.rs:424`; pinned by `tick_all_first_observation_creates_bootstrapping_entry`). The registration yields the same `Unknown → Bootstrapping` / `Activity` event the tick would have emitted, with `first_seen = last_seen = last_transition = S`. The next tick finds the entry at `Bootstrapping`, and `from == to` under `Learning`, so no duplicate event is emitted (`registry.rs:350-352`).

- **The P-027 observable, after the fix.** The mark's anchor is `last_seen_unix_nano` (`ConstellationCanvas.tsx:106`). For a brand-new service's first appearance it equals S, until the first tick refreshes it (`registry.rs:338-340`, only when `current_quiet_duration_seconds == 0`). So the existing mark then measures first-seen-to-dot for the case this chunk grades, with no field and no bindings change. At HEAD the same anchor is the tick stamp, which is why P-025's run recorded a ~0.5 s discovery sample against a ~10 s true interval.

- **P-025 unaffected.** `hueShiftSamples` samples only tier changes anchored on `tier_effective_at_unix_nano` and skips a first-seen dot with no tier (`constellation-types.ts:258-269`). An earlier dot turns the fresh-boot rise from a first-appearance-with-tier sample into a witnessed none → tier change with the same anchor. The rise value shortens; the anchor, the emission rule and `smoke:hue-shift`'s ANCHOR verdict are untouched.

- **The leg's independent anchor.** On a fresh data dir with one injector, the first `duckdb.append {table_name: "spans"}` record is every service's first-sighting instant (the injector's first batch carries all five, `inject_demo.rs:333`). The first `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` record's timestamp is the paint instant. Both exist at HEAD, so the leg reads RED at the chunk base by the interval (≈ 10 s) and by the mark's anchor error (≈ 9 s). The webview's `services.list_with_states.request` record preceding that first append is the precondition that the webview was already polling.
- `pulse-app/src/discovery_observer.rs` — the first-sighting `SpanObserver` adapter over the registry, the baseline and the lifecycle broadcast
- `xtask/src/discovery.rs` — the `smoke:discovery` scenario leg: a pure judge plus the runner
- `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs` — the `ServiceRegistry` first-sighting method, its `InMemoryServiceRegistry` impl, and co-located tests
- `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/mod.rs` — fold first-sighting transitions into the tick's `triage.lifecycle.transition` aggregate, and re-export
- `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs` — a per-service tracked query for the cap check, if `error_rate` is not reused
- `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` — re-export any new public item
- `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod discovery_observer`
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — compose the adapter third in the `CompositeSpanObserver`, built after `lifecycle_registry`
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_span_observers.rs` — adapter pins
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — register `smoke:discovery` and its dispatch arm
- `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json` — the P-027 notes line on what the observable anchors

- none. The two forks research surfaced are decided by artifacts, and the leans are recorded for P4: the registration state is `Bootstrapping` per `state_machine.rs`'s `Unknown` definition; the discovery anchor stays `last_seen` because it equals the first-sighting instant for the graded case, and a `ServiceListItem` field would change the bindings shape, whose close test-plan §3 leaves "not yet specified".
Working-route entry (`andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/working-route.md:138`, taken up 2026-09-30), verbatim:

> P-027 discovery bound — a new service's first constellation dot appears within the 5 s bound, not at the
> registry's first lifecycle tick · CONTEXT: measured at 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable — first
> rise 9986 ms: a new service's first dot appeared only at the registry's first 15 s lifecycle tick, and the paint
> followed 4 ms after the dot existed; P-027 bounds discovery at ≤ 5 s and sits inside P-075, which Conductor return
> verifies, so this precedes that entry
Operator directive at take-up (2026-09-30, `/andromeda-phase` arguments), verbatim:

> P-027 discovery bound (:138). Measured in P-025: a new service first dot appears only at the registry first 15 s
> lifecycle tick (first rise 9986 ms), against P-027 discovery <= 5 s inside P-075. Fix the cause in the discovery
> path (not the budget), prove it with a live leg that measures first-seen-to-dot for a brand-new service on a fresh
> boot, and keep P-025 hue timing unaffected. capability-drift before the workspace nextest; diff-shaped probes name
> the chunk base (W182).

Freight folded (route.py pins, row 138): one `CONTEXT:` block (346 chars), quoted above in full. No `CARRY` / `PREREQ`
/ `BLOCKED-ON` / `WATCH` on this entry.

1. **The discovery-path fix.** A service that sends its first span on a freshly booted app gets a constellation dot
   within P-027's ≤ 5 s bound. The fix goes in the discovery path. The 5 s budget is not relaxed, and the P-027
   observable is not re-anchored to make the number smaller.

2. **A live leg** that measures first-seen-to-dot for a brand-new service on a fresh boot of the real binary. It
   grades the interval from the first `duckdb.append {table_name: "spans"}` record (the first-sighting instant) to
   the first `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` record (the paint), and it checks that the discovery record's own
   anchor (`timestamp − duration_ms`) lands on that first-sighting instant. It has a RED reading at the chunk base,
   where it must show the ~10 s latency, and a GREEN reading after the fix, which must be within 5 s (amended at the
   P3 premise closure: at HEAD the discovery record anchors on the tick, so it cannot grade itself; see below).

3. **P-025 hue timing unaffected.** The hue observable's semantics stay as they are: the
   `tier_effective_at_unix_nano` anchor, the one-sample-per-witnessed-change rule, and the fall bounded by the 1 s
   poll. `cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift` still PASSes after the fix.
- The 5 s P-027 budget and the 2 s P-025 budget are not changed.

- No Conductor-side work. P-075 (Conductor e2e + the four delegated timing caps) stays with the "Conductor return"
  entry; this chunk makes the Pulse side meet the bound Conductor will assert.

- The perf-budget gate, span-level redaction and real-model incident surfacing are separate route entries, not
  folded here.

title: Surfaces and contracts it touches (P3 premise closure, 2026-09-30)

data.head: ## Surfaces and contracts it touches (P3 premise closure, 2026-09-30)

body:
- The mechanism, as measured at P-025 (`evidence/green-leg.md` of
  2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable, marker text verbatim): *"The service registry lists a service
  only after its first lifecycle heartbeat (`DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL` = 15 s). So on a freshly booted
  app the dot, and therefore its hue, cannot exist until that tick. Paint followed the first non-empty poll by
  4 ms."* VERIFIED at HEAD. Registry entries are created only by `tick_all`, `set_state_on_restart`,
  `set_manual_override` and `set_state_on_corpus_restore`, never on span arrival
  (`crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs:205-345`). The heartbeat skips its immediate first tick
  (`lifecycle/mod.rs:96`), and the 1 s webview poll (`use-service-constellation.ts:22`) is the only other step
  between span arrival and dot.

- Sites (corrected by research): the fix site is the span-observer composition (`pulse-app/src/main.rs:572-581`,
  built after `lifecycle_registry` at `:677`) plus a first-sighting method on the `ServiceRegistry` trait. The
  heartbeat, its 15 s cadence and the `services.list_with_states` resolver are NOT changed. `ConstellationCanvas.tsx`
  is NOT changed.

- The fix's shape (decided at P3): event-driven registration at first sighting, through a third `SpanObserver`
  adapter at the pulse-app boundary. It consumes the scrubbed name the tap already passes
  (`crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:245`), registers only services the baseline admitted under
  `ACTIVITY_FLOOR_SERVICE_CAP`, and registers them as `Bootstrapping`, the state `tick_all` reaches on first
  observation. `state_machine.rs` defines `Unknown` as "seen via prior corpus but not yet observed in the current
  session". Tick-shortening is rejected: it would change a Settings-sourced, hot-reload-classified cadence contract for
  every transition.

- [premise-corrected: `registry.rs:333-341` stamps `last_seen_unix_nano` with the TICK instant, not span arrival] The
  P-027 observable's anchor at HEAD is the tick stamp, so the discovery record cannot see the gap it bounds (P-025's
  run recorded ~0.5 s against a ~10 s true interval). After the fix, a brand-new service's first appearance has
  `last_seen` = its first-sighting instant, so the existing mark measures first-seen-to-dot for the case this chunk
  grades. No `ServiceListItem` field, no bindings change, no allowlist change. The live leg grades against an
  independent backend anchor, the first `duckdb.append {table_name: "spans"}` record of a fresh-boot run, which
  exists at the chunk base. Residual (recorded, not fixed): a service that re-enters liveness later in a session is
  "discovered" again by the mark, anchored on a tick-refreshed `last_seen`. That is not a first discovery and is not
  graded here.

- P-025 interaction, VERIFIED (`constellation-types.ts:258-269`). `hueShiftSamples` skips a first-seen dot with no
  tier and samples tier changes anchored on `tier_effective_at_unix_nano`. With the dot present before the incident
  opens, the fresh-boot rise becomes a witnessed none → tier change with the same anchor, and its value shortens.
  The hue observable's anchor, its emission rule and the smoke:hue-shift ANCHOR verdict are unchanged.

- `cargo xtask capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features workspace nextest (test-plan §3 gate order, the
  playbook's superseding rule from 2026-09-30-dual-license).

- Diff-shaped probes name the chunk base explicitly, `71f3369976b1c3acb54d5012256e94d892e9b57b` (HEAD at take-up), per
  W182, never a relative ref.

- `71f3369` (2026-09-30-dual-license wrap commit, the only sha since the last flip): **in progress**, so no verdict
  was available at read time. `ci#36687259840` (pull_request) was running 12 of 13 checks; the oldest was
  `lint / test (windows-latest)` at 179 s. `secret-scan#36687259806` completed, success. Not a red and not a green. It
  is recorded unresolved and re-read at /implement or wrap.

- `P-027` is not an id in this version's matrix (`matrix.py show --id P-027` → no such capability id). It is a
  v0.2.0 id (`docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json`), delegated into this version through P-075.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-30T12:50Z

CI's perf-budget gate can fail today only in principle. `cargo xtask ci-gates` hands `xtask/ci/perf-slo-check.sh` one
boot-smoke log carrying 0 frame, memory and snapshot samples. The script reads every empty arm as NEUTRAL, and
`run_ci_gates` prints `perf-budget PASS`. That was measured live at `ci#36710506171` on the chunk base, job log
`:1591-1594` (research §CI measurements). This chunk makes the gate read real samples and fail on them, against the
unchanged obs-plan §10 budgets: frame p99 ≤ 33 ms, `metric.buffer.memory_bytes` max ≤ 512 000 000, snapshot p99 ≤
500 ms.

- The arms move into xtask as pure Rust graders. A REQUIRED arm with no readable sample FAILS, while the NEUTRAL
  tolerance stays for callers that expect nothing: `ci-gates` over the boot smoke, `pre-push:linux`'s seeded record,
  `perf:load-profiles` (per obs-plan §10 two-state posture + §11 SLO "NEVER define soft SLO budgets"; test-plan §1
  `perf-slo-check-arm-coverage`).

- **Memory and snapshot samples** come from a new in-process producer test in lint-test Linux. It uses the real
  observability sink, real loopback ingest, the real retention sweep, the real buffer tick emitter and the real
  snapshot path, with no window (obs-plan §10 snapshot row names "`xtask test` span aggregation").

- **Frame samples** come from the release binary booted on the Windows release job, with a harness-only WebView2 flag
  set that exposes a software WebGPU adapter. That set was measured on this host: 496 samples, p99 4.1 ms. Two other
  flag sets gave 0 (research §P4 frame-adapter probes).
The chunk also discharges the entry's two CARRYs and one finding:
- The release job owns its own `release-${{ runner.os }}` cache key (arch §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach).

- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` gets the boot end-status recorder, so `harness:status`'s `ended` is real on Windows
  (arch §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces; test-plan §3 `status`).

- `app.boot.gpu.check` stops claiming `gpu_available = false` on every host. It is a hardcoded constant
  (`pulse-app/src/window.rs:91-96`), and the chunk leaves no known-false boot record.

**What the memory budget measures, stated plainly (overseer's instruction).** obs-plan §10 row 3 names
`metric.buffer.memory_bytes` `value`. That gauge is `(rows_ingested − evicted) × 256 B`, written only by the
retention sweep (`crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:119`, constant `:153`). It is a row-count estimate, not process RSS.
The in-process sample therefore measures exactly the quantity the spec names. No gate bounds the app's RSS, before or
after this chunk, and the plan claims nothing about RSS. The fact goes to wrap as an obs-plan amendment.

1. **RED evidence at the base**, recorded before any edit in `chunks/2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples/evidence/red-at-base.md`:
   - Quote the recorded CI vacuity (run `36710506171`, sha `fb93fca`): `logs-boot-Linux` has 23 records and 0 samples
     of each target, and the job log `:1591-1594` shows three NEUTRAL lines then `ci-gates: perf-budget PASS`.
   - Quote the three frame-adapter probe readings from research.
   - Run nothing new (no slot). The listed gates re-derive GREEN.

2. **Grader module — new file `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs`.**
   - **Log reading.** Read EVERY member of the `agent-latest.jsonl*` family through `smoke::read_jsonl_lines`
     (`xtask/src/smoke.rs:519`, widened to `pub(crate)`), never `log_files.last()`.
   - **Arms.** Pure fns, one per arm: frame (`fields.duration_ms`, nearest-rank p99 = the ⌈0.99·n⌉-th smallest,
     ≤ 33.0) · memory (`fields.value`, max ≤ 512 000 000) · snapshot (`fields.duration_ms`, nearest-rank p99 ≤ 500.0).
   - **Arm states:**
     - `Pass`/`Fail` carry the stat and `n`.
     - `Neutral` means no record of that target.
     - `Unreadable` means a record of the target whose graded field is not a JSON number, for example `"<redacted>"`.
       This is the class the scripts' no-`jq` branch hid as NEUTRAL.
     - Memory samples with `value == 0` are counted but are NOT informative, because a zero is the pre-sweep
       placeholder. A memory arm with samples but none non-zero reads `Neutral` (`populated 0 of n`).
   - **Gate evaluation** takes the set of REQUIRED arms:
     - FAIL if any arm is `Fail` or `Unreadable`, or a required arm is `Neutral`.
     - Otherwise PASS if at least one arm is `Pass`.
     - Otherwise `NEUTRAL`. It is never PASS over empty input.
   - **Output.** One printed line per arm, e.g. `perf-budget: frame p99 4.1 ms <= 33 ms (n=496) PASS`, then a last
     line `perf-budget: PASS|FAIL|NEUTRAL`.
   - **Tests, 15 total, co-located.** Frame pass/fail/neutral (3); memory pass/fail/neutral plus
     zeros-are-not-informative (4); snapshot pass/fail/neutral (3); unreadable field → FAIL even when not required
     (1); required-but-empty → FAIL (1); all-empty with nothing required → NEUTRAL, not PASS (1); the nearest-rank
     index for n ∈ {1, 99, 100, 101} (1); the family read concatenates two date-suffixed members (1).

3. **Rewire the callers, then delete the scripts.**
   - `run_ci_gates` @ `xtask/src/main.rs:531` and `run_perf_load_profiles` @ `:839` call the grader in-process over
     all family members, with no required arms.
   - Retire `invoke_perf_slo_check` (`:705`). Replace the no-log `perf-budget DEFERRED (no criterion bench yet)` line
     (`:465`) with the grader's NEUTRAL line.
   - In `run_ci_gates`, the perf arm's all-empty outcome prints `perf-budget NEUTRAL` instead of PASS, and still does
     not fail the step. That keeps `pre-push:linux` (`xtask/src/pre_push.rs:249`) and the boot smoke green.
   - Delete `xtask/ci/perf-slo-check.sh` and `xtask/ci/perf-slo-check.ps1`.

4. **New verb `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir <DIR> --require <arm,arm>`.**
   - It grades `<DIR>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl*` with the given arms required.
   - Exits: 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 cannot-evaluate (no log family under `<DIR>/logs`, or an unknown arm name).
   - Register it beside `CiGates` in the `Cmd` enum.

5. **Producer test — new file `pulse-app/tests/perf_budget_samples.rs`, in its own nextest profile.**
   - **Setup.**
     - The data dir is `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/perf-budget-samples`. The test REMOVES it and recreates it first, so
       every run's log is its own.
     - `pulse_app::observability::init(dir)` installs the real sink, and its guard is held to the end so the tail
       flushes.
     - Real ingest runs over loopback gRPC with a real DuckDB, `run_consumer` and
       `buffer::retention::run_retention(conn, state, 60)` (cadence 10 s, first tick skipped).
   - **Drive.**
     - Send ≥ 25 000 spans over ≥ 25 s.
     - After each 10 s window, call `pulse_app::heartbeat::emit_buffer_tick` (`pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs:271`).
       This yields ≥ 2 memory samples taken after a sweep, so non-zero ones.
     - Generate 50 snapshots through `pulse_app::snapshot_runtime::load_curated_markdown` (`:138`, widened
       `pub(crate)` → `pub`). That is the production load → curate → `format_markdown` path at the Balanced (25k)
       budget, the obs-plan §10 row.
   - **Self-checks.** The test asserts only its own preconditions: spans landed, ≥ 2 ticks emitted with a non-zero
     gauge, 50 snapshots `Ok`. The budget verdict is `perf:budget`'s.
   - **nextest profile.** `.config/nextest.toml` gains `[profile.perf-samples]` with
     `default-filter = "binary(perf_budget_samples)"`. `[profile.default]`'s filter also excludes that binary, so
     workspace and coverage runs don't pay for the test.

6. **Frame leg — new verb `cargo xtask perf:frame-sample`, new file `xtask/src/perf_frame.rs`.**
   - **Scope.** Windows only; any other OS exits 2 with the reason.
   - **Preconditions.** `target/release/pulse-app.exe` and `target/release/examples/inject_demo.exe` exist, and
     :4317/:4318 refuse connections, since `inject_demo` hardcodes `127.0.0.1:4317` at
     `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs:307`. Otherwise exit 2.
   - **Launch.** Spawn the app by path on a fresh TempDir data dir. The CHILD's environment alone carries
     `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` and `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--enable-unsafe-webgpu
     --enable-features=Vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader`, the probe-3 set.
   - **Drive.** Poll the log family (not sleep) up to 60 s for a first frame sample. Then run
     `inject_demo --sustained` for 30 s, so dots render.
   - **Teardown.** Kill the injector, then the app by the pidfile pid, and confirm both ports are released.
   - **Grade.** Copy the family to `target/perf-frame/<UTC stamp>/`, then grade with `frame` required (memory is
     reported, not required, because the 600 s default retention gives a 100 s sweep cadence).
   - **Exits.**
     - 0 PASS.
     - 1 FAIL: 0 frames once the app is healthy is printed as `frame: 0 samples — no WebGPU adapter in this run`;
       also p99 > 33.
     - 2 INCONCLUSIVE: an unmet precondition, or the app is never healthy.
   - **Tests, 2.** The child environment carries the flag set and the data dir without mutating the parent's
     (pure env-builder fn); the non-Windows guard returns cannot-evaluate.

7. **CI wiring — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.**
   - **lint-test, Linux only**, after `cargo xtask perf:slo-load`:
     - `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile perf-samples`, reusing the test build.
     - `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir target/tmp/perf-budget-samples --require memory,snapshot`.
     - An `if: always()` upload of `target/tmp/perf-budget-samples/logs/` as `logs-perf-samples-${{ runner.os }}`.
   - **release job:**
     - Replace the restore-only cache step with `shared-key: release-${{ runner.os }}`, saving (no `save-if: false`).
     - Windows only, after the build: `cargo build --release -p ingest --example inject_demo`, then
       `target/release/xtask.exe perf:frame-sample` by path. This avoids `cargo xtask`'s debug rebuild of xtask.
     - An `if: always()` upload of `target/perf-frame/` as `logs-perf-frame-${{ runner.os }}`.
   - Update the header comment's cache budget (`:18-21`). No new `uses:` beyond the existing SHA-pinned
     rust-cache/upload-artifact, no `permissions:` change, no `continue-on-error`.

8. **Workflow self-lint — `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`.**
   - Add the three new gate commands (`--profile perf-samples`, `perf:budget --data-dir`, `perf:frame-sample`) to the
     no-`continue-on-error` list (`:160`).
   - One pin: the release job saves `release-${{ runner.os }}` and carries no `save-if: false`.
   - One pin: `[profile.default]` excludes `binary(perf_budget_samples)`.

9. **Windows boot end-status recorder — `scripts/agent-run.ps1` `boot`** (mirrors `agent-run.sh:71-99`).
   - **Wrapper.** Replace the direct `Start-Process` of the app (`:150`) with a hidden waiting wrapper, a child
     `powershell` started detached, which:
     - launches the app with the same redirects;
     - writes the app's pid to `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` beside the pidfile, ASCII with no BOM;
     - waits;
     - writes `exit N` (the app exit code) to `run/andromeda-pulse.exit`, ASCII with no BOM. That fits `read_ended`
       (`xtask/src/harness_status.rs:205`, ≤ 48 printable ASCII).
   - **Spawn record.** `boot` removes stale records first, polls the spawn record ≤ 5 s (50 × 100 ms), exits 1 with
     `boot: the app did not start (no spawn record)` when absent, and writes that pid to the pidfile.
   - **Failure path.** On a failed readiness poll, it prints `app ended: ` plus the exit record (or `app still running`) before
     `Invoke-Cleanup`.
   - **Unchanged.** The verb set, exit semantics and the `status`/`cleanup` field set stay as they are, which keeps
     the a11y harness's consumers whole.

10. **`app.boot.gpu.check` stops asserting what it never measures.**
    - `pulse-app/src/window.rs:91-96` drops the `gpu_available` field and keeps `wgpu_backend`. Its message states
      that this is the compile-target default backend and that no adapter probe runs here; the frame loop's adapter
      branch is the adapter evidence.
    - `wgpu_backend` stays because `xtask smoke` asserts it (`smoke.rs:440,474`) and `self-verify` needs the record
      (`self_verify.rs:115,141`). Leaned this way per research §Files inspected.
    - The allowlist leaf (`pulse-app/src/observability.rs:969-970`) becomes `["wgpu_backend"]`.
    - The two pins (`pulse-app/tests/observability_pins.rs:2772-2800`) change so that the pass test asserts
      `wgpu_backend` passes, and the redact test uses `gpu_available` as the now-non-allowlisted field.
- `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs` — the per-arm graders, gate evaluation, `perf:budget` verb body, 15 tests
- `xtask/src/perf_frame.rs` — the Windows frame leg (`perf:frame-sample`), 2 tests
- `pulse-app/tests/perf_budget_samples.rs` — the in-process memory + snapshot producer

- `xtask/src/main.rs` — `Cmd` entries for the two verbs; `run_ci_gates` and `run_perf_load_profiles` call the grader (callers: `run_ci_gates` @ `main.rs:531`, `run_perf_load_profiles` @ `main.rs:839`); `invoke_perf_slo_check` removed; `:465` line replaced; `mod` lines
- `xtask/src/smoke.rs` — `read_jsonl_lines` visibility `pub(crate)`
- `xtask/ci/perf-slo-check.sh` — deleted
- `xtask/ci/perf-slo-check.ps1` — deleted
- `pulse-app/src/snapshot_runtime.rs` — `load_curated_markdown` visibility `pub`
- `pulse-app/src/window.rs` — the `app.boot.gpu.check` field set + message
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — the `app.boot.gpu.check` leaf
- `pulse-app/tests/observability_pins.rs` — the two gpu-check pins
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the new workflow pins
- `.config/nextest.toml` — `[profile.perf-samples]` + the default exclusion
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — lint-test Linux producer + gate + artifact; release key + Windows frame leg + artifact; header comment
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the boot end-status recorder

- **Boot path.** The chunk touches `pulse-app/src/window.rs` and `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`, both test-plan §3
  boot-smoke trigger paths. The `role = 'smoke'` entry is `cargo xtask self-verify` against the release build. It
  opens a window, so it is an OPERATOR SLOT (scope §Operating constraints). /implement STOPS and asks before it, and
  before every `leg` entry below. /implement P3's warm boot smoke rides the same slot request.

- **Webview.** No `pulse-app/ui/**` file changes, so there is no webview gate trio. A probe asserts the tree is
  untouched.

- **RED.** RED at the base is the recorded CI run (step 1), not a listed entry: the light gate re-runs entries
  verbatim against the fixed tree. The grader's ability to fail is proven by the 15 per-arm pins, which include
  required-empty → FAIL and unreadable → FAIL.

- **Order.** `capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features workspace nextest, and the mcp-server bindings regen
  is the last cargo-adjacent entry, closed by the chunk-base `git diff --quiet` (playbook routine ordering rule). The
  chunk adds no TauRPC procedure and no bridge-crossing field.

- **CI half.** The two CI legs (lint-test Linux producer + gate; release Windows frame leg) are witnessed by the
  operator pass's CI read.

- **Cache.** The cache acceptance needs a SECOND round on the same sha, so the pass reruns that run once and reads it
  again.

- **Disk.** Heavy builds (release + workspace) re-measure disk first: under 60 GB free, `cargo clean --profile dev`
  before them (scope §Operating constraints).

- **ps1 `ended` leg.** It has no preceding liveness probe, and none exists that would not prime it: the leg boots its
  own app on non-default ports 14317/14318, so :4317/:4318 are not its precondition.

- **Cache evidence.** `evidence/ci-cache.md` is the operator pass's record of the report-only cache-usage entry,
  under the operator-entry evidence rule. No gate writes it.
