title: Mechanism re-derivations (the plan's load-bearing equalities, verified at HEAD)

data.head: ## Mechanism re-derivations (the plan's load-bearing equalities, verified at HEAD)

body:
1. **The Rust graph has exactly one runtime path to a non-zero process exit, and it does not yield `exit 1` here.**
   Sweep of every `Cargo.lock` package's registry `src/` (916 packages, 891 dirs present; `tests/examples/benches/bin`
   and `build.rs` skipped) for `process::exit(|libc::exit(|libc::_exit(` — script
   `scratchpad/exit_sweep.py`, re-run after a CRLF false-zero (host-shell, recorded). Runtime hits in pulse-app's graph:
   `tao-0.35.0/.../linux/event_loop.rs:998` `process::exit(exit_code)` (and its macOS :202 / Windows :230 twins),
   `tauri-2.11.0/src/app.rs:578` (the `AppHandle::exit` fallback, same code), `tauri-plugin-updater-2.10.1/src/updater.rs:865`
   (`exit(0)`). The rest are build-time (`cc`, `tauri-build`, `tauri-codegen`, `tauri-plugin` build), docs (`csv`), test
   harnesses (`proptest`, `rusty-fork`), or other platforms (`objc2-*`). tao's code comes from `ControlFlow::ExitWithCode`;
   the only `ExitWithCode(1)` is a queued `Event::LoopDestroyed` (`event_loop.rs:1127`) with no Linux sender (grep
   `LoopDestroyed` over `tao-0.35.0/src` → only the loop's own handling + `event.rs` definitions); tauri-runtime-wry sets
   `ControlFlow::Exit` (code 0) on every exit request (`lib.rs:3205, :4329, :4372`). A panic exits 101. So a bare
   `exit 1` with 0 `app.panic.fatal` is, by elimination over the Rust graph, a NATIVE `exit()` (GTK/GDK/WebKitGTK/glib)
   — the class only an at-exit hook can see. This is a classification of the candidate set, NOT a cause of the 69f0b93
   death, which stays unexplained.

2. **No record emitted on the event-loop exit path is guaranteed to reach the file.** `Builder::run` → `App::run` →
   runtime `run` → tao `run` → `process::exit(exit_code)` (`tauri-2.11.0/src/app.rs:1338` docs: "the process is exited
   directly using std::process::exit"; tao :997-998). `process::exit` runs no destructors, so `main`'s `_guard`
   (main.rs:293) is never dropped. The file is written by a separate worker thread draining a channel
   (`non_blocking`, lossy by default, `DEFAULT_BUFFERED_LINES_LIMIT` 128 000, non_blocking.rs:67, :232); the ONLY flush
   handshake is `WorkerGuard::drop` (non_blocking.rs:283-300: `send_timeout(Shutdown, 100 ms)` then wait up to 1000 ms).
   An event enqueued immediately before `process::exit` therefore races the worker — whether it lands is UNMEASURED and
   is the RED leg's first measurement at /implement. `App::run_return` (app.rs:1397) returns the intended exit code
   instead of exiting, which gives Rust code a place to emit, drop the guard (flush), then exit with the same code.

3. **An at-exit hook sees both `process::exit` and a native `exit()`, but not the code.** Rust's `process::exit` calls the
   platform `exit`, which runs `atexit` handlers; a C `exit(1)` from GTK runs them too; `_exit`, a signal kill and
   `TerminateProcess` do not. `libc-0.2.186` binds `atexit` for `unix/mod.rs` and `windows/mod.rs`; glibc's `on_exit`
   (which passes the status) is NOT bound by the crate (grep `pub fn on_exit` → only haiku's `on_exit_thread`). Other
   threads are still alive while `atexit` handlers run, so a handler that drops a guard held in a static can drain the
   worker — the equality to MEASURE at /implement: an induced `libc::exit(1)` after `init` leaves exactly one cause record
   in `agent-latest.jsonl*` after the child has ended.

4. **Signals end the process with no record today.** No handler is installed (grep above). The harness `cleanup` sends
   TERM (verification-harness.md:25); the wrapper records `signal N (NAME)`. SIGKILL and Windows `Stop-Process -Force`
   (TerminateProcess) are unloggable by construction.

5. **Pre-sink failures cannot reach the file by construction**: the runtime `.expect` (main.rs:288) and the logs-dir
   `.expect` (observability.rs:2624) panic before the subscriber exists — the default hook prints to stderr, which the
   harness captures in `boot.log`.

6. **P-075 content fidelity has exactly one payload-varying read-back value under deterministic L4**: the triggering
   cue's full-hex fingerprint inside `retrieve_telemetry_slice.fingerprint_refs`, beside the constant `det-*` triple;
   every L4-authored field is a fixture constant; `incident_events` reaches no MCP tool (a Pulse 0.4.0 residual
   candidate); runtime-STATE fidelity (`mark_incident_resolved` + `query_incident_list` active-set membership) is the
   other live-proven axis (Conductor `.andromeda/architecture.md:62,93`; master-route.md:107). Pulse-side, the
   fingerprint threading is the [Fault Identity] invariant (CLAUDE.md; arch-history 2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-
   completeness).

data.head: ### PREREQ — exit-cause logging (operator-directed at the 2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing wrap, 2026-10-01)

body: - "every non-zero exit path of pulse-app logs its cause before exiting, so the next unexplained death names itself".

- "the Linux CI boot smoke's app ended `exit 1` 0.27 s after `boot: ready`, before any webview IPC, with no panic and
  no ERROR beyond the keyring line to say why (1 of 2 attempts at `69f0b93`: `ci#36893004900` job 110472991644; its
  single re-run on the same sha read `running-healthy`); cause unexplained, no confining mechanism identified".
  COORDINATES VERIFIED at take-up against the prior chunk's record
  (`chunks/2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing/evidence/operator-pass.md` §Red 2): the failed job 110472991644,
  `"ended": "exit 1"` (the app's own code, not a signal), 40 records over 0.27 s, 0 `app.panic.fatal`, ERROR only
  `corpus.open.error {error_kind: KeyringUnavailable}`, no webview-originated record; re-run job 110496296816 read
  `running-healthy`.

- The exit is not one of pulse-app's own Rust exit sites — VERIFIED, and widened at P3 (research.md §Mechanism
  re-derivations 1): `pulse-app/src` has one explicit exit, `tray.rs:271` `app.exit(0)`; across the whole lockfile graph
  (916 packages swept) the only runtime non-zero path is tao's `process::exit(exit_code)`, whose code is 0 on every exit
  tauri-runtime-wry requests, and a panic exits 101. By elimination a bare `exit 1` with 0 `app.panic.fatal` is a NATIVE
  `exit()` (GTK/GDK/WebKitGTK/glib) — seen only by a hook that runs at exit. Public twin of the signature: YUI #729
  (silent exit 1 under Xvfb, cause unknown, closed not planned) — research.md §Scope. This classifies the candidate set;
  it does NOT explain the 69f0b93 death.

- "Every non-zero exit path" is enumerable — VERIFIED; the classes and how each ends (research.md §Mechanism
  re-derivations 2-5): (a) event-loop exit — tao `process::exit(code)`, no destructor runs, so `main`'s `_guard`
  (main.rs:293) never drops and the non-blocking worker is never flushed; a record emitted just before it races the
  worker (loss UNMEASURED — the RED leg's first measurement); `App::run_return` returns the code to Rust instead;
  (b) native `exit()` — runs `atexit` handlers (bound by `libc` 0.2.186 on unix and windows; the exit status is NOT
  available there — glibc `on_exit` is unbound); (c) panic — `app.panic.fatal` exists; main-thread unwinding drops the
  guard; (d) signals — no handler today; SIGTERM/SIGINT are hookable on Unix, SIGKILL and Windows `Stop-Process -Force`
  are unloggable by construction; (e) pre-sink failures (main.rs:288 runtime `.expect`, observability.rs:2624 logs-dir
  `.expect`) can reach only stderr / `boot.log` by construction. Tray Quit (`app.exit(0)`) and window close (hide to tray)
  are not non-zero exits.

- The witness can fail — VERIFIED shape: the re-exec form (testing.md:260 — `current_exe()` with `--exact`, state through
  env, the child writes to a temp sink, a skip-clean guard, `--no-capture` once to prove the child ran) induces each
  loggable class in a child and reads `agent-latest.jsonl*` after the child has ended — CI-runnable, no window. At base the
  cause record is ABSENT (no exit-cause target exists at HEAD), the block-shaped RED (testing.md:290). The Linux runner
  class stays unreproducible here; the CI boot smoke is the runner-side observer.

- Logging discipline applies — VERIFIED: own exact allowlist leaf (no bare `app` key, observability.md:65), closed-enum /
  integer / basename fields only, guard under `pulse-app/tests/`, dual-site registration (obs-plan §6 + §8) as an

title: Part 1 — PREREQ: the source-lint verb (no operator slot)

data.head: ### Part 1 — PREREQ: the source-lint verb (no operator slot)

body:
1. **New verb `check:english-sources`** in `xtask/src/source_lint.rs`, registered in `xtask/src/main.rs` beside
   `check:npm-supply-chain`.
   - **Scope:** the same five roots and three extensions as today's step (`crates`, `pulse-app/src`, `pulse-app/tests`,
     `pulse-app/ui/src`, `xtask/src`; `.rs`/`.ts`/`.tsx`), and the same range U+0400–U+04FF, written NUMERICALLY in the
     source so the verb's own file holds no Cyrillic.
   - **Output, per hit:** one GitHub annotation line on stdout,
     `::error file={path},line={n}::Cyrillic character in source - {path}:{n}: {line}`. Every non-ASCII char of `{line}`
     is rendered as `\u{XXXX}` and the line is capped at 120 chars, so the verb's whole output is ASCII by construction
     and no console code page can fail it.
   - **Verdict:** then ONE pretty-JSON verdict `{verdict, hits, files_scanned}` on stdout, with the twin at
     `target/english-sources/report.json`.
   - **Exit:** 0 `clean` · 1 `findings` · 2 `cannot-evaluate` (a root absent or unreadable — never a clean pass).
   - **Tests:** co-located unit pins in `source_lint.rs` `mod tests` over TempDir fixtures, every fn name carrying
     `english_sources`:
     - a hit renders file:line and is pure ASCII;
     - a clean tree exits 0;
     - a missing root exits 2;
     - a hit outside the five roots is ignored;
     - a `.md` file under a root is ignored.

2. **ci.yml:** replace the inline `shell: python` "No Cyrillic in sources" step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:83-111`)
   with a plain named `run: cargo xtask check:english-sources` step in the same position of the `lint-test` matrix. Its
   English-only comment is kept. No `uses:` is added, workflow `permissions:` is untouched (security-plan §Dependency
   Security → CI integration), and the two workflow self-lint guards stay green (test-plan §9).

3. **pre-push stage:** add a `source-lint` stage to `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` `Stage` / `Stage::ALL`, second after
   `script-modes`, running `cargo xtask check:english-sources` in the distro clone. That gives six stages; the stage
   binds no port, starts no `pulse-app` and reads no new env var (the registered `pre-push:linux` contract, arch
   §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces). It is red on any non-zero exit.

4. **One-shot RED/GREEN proof, recorded in `evidence/prereq/`.** Plant a Cyrillic literal in a scanned path, record
   both readings, revert the plant.
   - **Reading 1:** `cargo xtask check:english-sources` exits 1 and prints the ASCII annotation naming file:line.
   - **Reading 2:** the verb's captured stdout decodes as strict ASCII — a scratchpad python script runs the verb and
     calls `stdout.decode('ascii')`, which raises on any non-ASCII byte. Output that is pure ASCII is identical under
     cp1252 or any other ANSI code page, so this decode is the behavioural witness the tests §1
     `harness-encoding-relay-coverage` class asks for, and it is stronger than setting `PYTHONIOENCODING` (which only
     shows one code page).
   - **Then:** the revert reads exit 0.
   - **Planted literal:** keep it out of the evidence file (escape it); the file records the command and its two exits.

title: Part 3 — the measurement instrument (no operator slot to build; its run is Slot 1)

data.head: ### Part 3 — the measurement instrument (no operator slot to build; its run is Slot 1)

body:
8. **Expose the renderer** in `crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs`, so the probe renders synthetic digests through
   the REAL code instead of a copied template.
   - `render_payload` becomes `#[doc(hidden)] pub`.
   - The cue-summary builder at `:266-270` is extracted to a `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn cue_summary(&AttentionCue) -> String`
     that `assemble()` calls.
   - Neither change alters the rendered text, and the existing in-crate render tests stay green unchanged.
   - **Re-exports:** `triage` exposes only its `contract` module (`crates/triage/src/lib.rs:11-17`; arch §Conventions →
     Module visibility discipline), so both fns are re-exported through `crates/triage/src/digest/mod.rs` (beside its
     existing `pub use assembler::{…}`, `:33`) and then `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` (beside its
     `pub use crate::digest::{…}`, `:137`). The render inputs (`DigestProjectContext`, `DigestServiceRow`,
     `DigestCueRef`) are already reachable there. No new crate edge: pulse-app already depends on triage.

9. **The probe** — new `pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe.rs`, a dev-only tool that is neither a test nor a gate, on
   the `crates/ingest/examples/inject_*` precedent.
   - **Inputs:** it resolves the model and llama-cli paths through the product's own guarded resolution
     (`validate_path_input` `:547`, the hardware-profile binary choice). It logs BASENAMES only, never a full path
     (security-plan §Logging), and exits 2 `INCONCLUSIVE` when an L4 env var is unset or unresolvable.
   - **Digests:** it renders the three SYNTHETIC storm digests below through `render_payload` + `cue_summary` and
     composes prompts with `build_primary_tier_prompt`. Every string is ASCII and synthetic; no captured telemetry is
     used (test-plan §11).
     - **S1:** `checkout-api` at 100% errors — the `inject_demo` default shape.
     - **S2:** 1 of 4 services at 35% errors.
     - **S3:** 1 of 4 at 12% errors with p99 at 4x its siblings.
   - **Generation:** each prompt runs through `build_llama_cli_args` (+ the arm's extra args) as ONE spawn per
     generation, with the same bounds as production (`-n`, `-st`, outer timeout, `kill_on_drop`).
   - **Per generation it records** `{arm, shape, run, decision, severity, is_resolution_summary, would_create,
     first_keys}`:
     - `would_create` = the producer predicate (`decision != dismiss && severity != none && !is_resolution_summary`);
     - `first_keys` = the first three JSON keys of the raw output, which reads the grammar's key order (research E5);
     - a parse failure counts as `would_create = false` with `decision = "parse_failed"`.
   - **What it never writes:** no title, symptom, hypothesis, justification or raw output to disk or stdout.
   - **Output:** the per-generation rows go to `target/l4-decision-probe/{stamp}/runs.json`, plus one summary line per
     arm, `arm {A}: would_create {k}/{n} · decision {surface}/{dismiss}/{watch} · severity_none {m} ·
     resolution_summary {r}`.
   - **Verdict:** with `--min K`, a last line `l4-decision-probe: verdict: PASS|FAIL · would_create {k}/{n}` and exit
     0/1.
   - **Arms:** `--arms` selects among A0–A5 (table below) plus `shipped` (HEAD's prompt and args with no transform).
     `--n` sets runs per shape.

10. **Arms.** Each arm differs from A0 in ONE factor, and its transform lives in the probe, so the whole matrix runs on
    the untouched base.
| arm | factor | transform |
| A0 | baseline | HEAD render, HEAD prompt, HEAD argv |
| A1 | sampling | A0 + `--temp 0` (greedy; the run is deterministic, so its 10 runs per shape also measure seed behaviour) |
| A2 | digest status line | A0 with ONLY the `OVERALL:` line made truthful (the Step 13 rule) |
| A3 | digest quantities | A0 with ONLY the cue line carrying the cue's magnitude ×baseline, absolute value and persistence |
| A4 | guidance | A0 with ONE added ASCII sentence in the conventions stating when a signal warrants `surface` |
| A5 | field order | A0 with `decision` / `severity` moved after `hypotheses` in the schema passed to `--json-schema-file` AND embedded in the prompt |

body:

    - **Defect not reproduced:** `r(A0) ≥ 27` → the defect did not reproduce at HEAD (span-level redaction may have

        order → A4 guidance.

title: Part 6 — Slot 2: GREEN (OPERATOR SLOT — /implement STOPS and asks)

data.head: ### Part 6 — Slot 2: GREEN (OPERATOR SLOT — /implement STOPS and asks)

body:
15. **STOP and ask the operator for Slot 2.** State it as: "~15 min: (a) `l4_decision_probe --arms shipped --n 10
    --min 27` (~4 min, no window, no ports); (b) one end-to-end storm — warm debug `pulse-app.exe` booted by the
    operator on a fresh exported data dir with the real model (opens the app window, binds :4317/:4318 — shared with
    conductor-builder), then the arg-less `inject_demo` storm and a ≤ 240 s read of the log family (~8 min)."
    - **Gate entries:** the Test Commands entries marked `leg` below are this slot.
    - **Report:** the combined `would_create` count, with A2's own Slot 1 delta beside it (`r(A2) − r(A0)`), per the
      overseer's attribution rule.

16. The standard gate set below, then `gate.py scope` (implement P4). Record the four mutation checks and both slots in
    `evidence/`.
- `xtask/src/source_lint.rs` — the `check:english-sources` verb + its unit pins (Step 1)
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_incident_skip.rs` — the skip leaf guard (Step 6)
- `pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe.rs` — the measurement instrument (Step 9)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the python step → `cargo xtask check:english-sources` (Step 2)
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — register the verb (Step 1)
- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` — the `source-lint` stage (Step 3)

- `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` — the skip emits at its three silent exits (Step 5); the producer's two callers
  are unchanged (`create_incident_from_l4_output` @ `inference_runtime.rs:258`, plus 44 test sites, research.md §Graph
  impact — the signature does not change)
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — the exact leaf (Step 6; a boot-smoke trigger path, covered by the Slot 2 boot)
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_incident_producer.rs` — skip-reason pins (Step 7)
- `pulse-app/tests/observability_pins.rs` — only if the skip target joins the collected pins set there (Step 6)

- `crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs` — expose the renderer (Step 8); the OVERALL rule (Step 13); A3's
  `cue_summary` (Step 14). `render_payload` has 4 in-fn callers + 1 test (`assembler.rs:341`, `:365`, `:380`, `:396`,
  `:1017`)
- `crates/triage/src/digest/mod.rs` + `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` — the two re-exports the probe needs (Step 8)
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_digest_runtime_scrub.rs` — the fixture's OVERALL wording (Step 13)
- `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` — the probe's `[[example]]` (Step 9)

- Branch-conditional (Step 14):
  - `pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs` + `pulse-app/tests/unit_llamacli_inference.rs` — A1.
    `build_llama_cli_args` @ `llamacli_inference.rs:759` is its 1 production caller, with 9 test sites.
  - `crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs` + `crates/interpretation/src/schema.rs` + `pulse-app/tests/unit_inference_runtime.rs`
    + `pulse-app/tests/integration_generation_damper.rs` — A4 / A5.
  - `crates/interpretation/src/schema.json` + `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs` — A5.

No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the three webview npm gates are excluded (test-plan §3). The chunk adds no
TauRPC procedure, so the bindings close is the base-identity probe.

**Boot smoke.** `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` IS on the boot-smoke trigger list (testing.md `boot-smoke-coverage`).
The direct-binary form is Slot 2's end-to-end leg: the operator boots the warm debug binary on a fresh exported data
dir, and the 0-panic / 0-ERROR read below covers it.
**No headful UI change**, so there is no self-verify entry.

**One-shot runs at /implement, never entries here:** the four mutation checks (Steps 6, 7, 13, 14), the PREREQ plant
(Step 4) and Slot 1's arm matrix (Step 11). Each mutates source or measures the untouched base, so it runs once and its
readings live in `evidence/`.

**Live legs (`leg` entries) are Slot 2.** `pulse-app` and the model run only in the operator's slot. /implement never
launches either without the word, and the light gate never re-runs a leg.
**The CI read** spans the operator pass by construction.

title: Mechanism re-derivations (the plan's load-bearing equalities, verified at HEAD)

data.head: ## Mechanism re-derivations (the plan's load-bearing equalities, verified at HEAD)

body:
- **E1 — "dismissed" is an inference from silence.** For a storm digest whose parse is `ok`, "no
  `interpretation.incident.created`" holds for ALL four skip outcomes above.
  - **Conductor's basis:** "parse `ok`, no incident outcome" (attempt-ledger `:57-58`, `:64-66`), i.e. the silence.
  - **What it cannot separate:** `decision=dismiss`, `severity=none`, `is_resolution_summary=true` and no-cue. Nothing
    in Pulse's log tells them apart today (`inference_runtime.rs:762-767` returns before any emit).

- **E2 — every storm digest tells the model the system is nominal.**
  - **Chain:** a storm cue is `Autonomous` → it takes the Tier1 cycle (`coordinator.rs:395`) → `lww_mode =
    Tier1NeverLww` (`assembler.rs:226`) → `active_incident_bypass = false` (`:236`) → the payload line is
    `OVERALL: nominal (…; 1 cue(s))` (`:643-647`). This holds for EVERY Tier1 digest, independent of the storm's size.
  - **Witness:** the fixture literal at `pulse-app/tests/unit_digest_runtime_scrub.rs:24` carries exactly that line.

- **E3 — the cue line carries no quantity.** It reads `[autonomous] exception_storm — exception_storm scope_id=<svc>`.
  The detector's magnitude and absolute value are not in the prompt (`assembler.rs:266-270`). The SERVICES row still
  carries `error%` and p99 (`:653-662`).

- **E4 — no sampling control.** llama.cpp's own defaults apply: `temp 0.80` / `top_k 40` / `top_p 0.95` /
  `min_p 0.05` / `seed 0xFFFFFFFF` (b9305 `common.h` and `llama.h`, fetched).

- **E5 — the decision is generated before any analysis, IF the grammar follows the schema's property order.**
  - **What is read at HEAD:** `decision` is listed before `title` / `symptom` / `hypotheses` in `schema.json`.
  - **What is not read here:** whether llama.cpp's json-schema-to-grammar keeps listed property order or sorts it. That
    stays a hypothesis. The live half reads the generated key order off the raw output directly.

  - a new xtask scenario leg, rejected: xtask cannot link pulse-app's runner.

  decision before writing any reasoning — unverified whether llama.cpp's grammar keeps that order (read live)]

1. **PREREQ:** a Cyrillic literal in source is (a) reported READABLY by CI on every runner OS, Windows included,
   naming file:line, and (b) caught by `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` before a push, so it can no longer pass the local
   gate green and fail CI.

2. **Surfacing:** when the real L4 model reads a storm digest of the kind that should become an incident, it decides
   to surface it reliably — the cause of the dismissals is MEASURED and named first, and the fix addresses that
   measured cause, never a tuning loop run until a sample passes.

- **The source-lint pair.** The Cyrillic check prints its findings without depending on the console's code page
  (ASCII-safe output: escaped codepoints, or a UTF-8-reconfigured stream), and the same check is reachable from
  `pre-push:linux`. [VERIFIED as needed (both defects re-derived above); the SHAPE — one xtask verb shared by CI and a
  new pre-push stage, or the inline ci.yml python made UTF-8-safe with pre-push duplicating it — is a P4 fork]

- **The no-incident outcome becomes observable.** [added by research — premise correction above] Every L4 generation
  whose parse is `ok` but which creates no incident records WHICH of the four skip outcomes fired, as bounded labels only
  (`decision`, model severity, `is_resolution_summary`, `skip_reason`), never digest, prompt or model text. Without it
  neither this chunk's live half nor Conductor's next series can tell a dismissal from a `severity: none` or a stray
  `is_resolution_summary: true`.

- **A discriminating measurement of the dismissals** across the four named candidates. Its OFFLINE half needs no
  operator slot: what the composed prompt says about surface vs dismiss vs watch (`crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs`
  — the decision guidance at `:88-150`), what a storm digest carries into the prompt, what thresholds gate a storm
  digest's creation, and what the incident-creation predicate rejects (`pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:737-763` —
  `Decision::Dismiss` skips creation). Its LIVE half — running the real model over storm digests and recording each
  decision with its justification — runs only in an operator-granted slot. [VERIFIED feasible: the env-gated
  `pulse-app/tests/integration_real_llama_cli.rs` already drives `LlamaCliInference` directly against a composed prompt —
  no app boot, no ports, skip-clean without the three L4 env vars (unset in the agent shell; the operator supplies them in
  the slot). The prompts are SYNTHETIC storm digests in the exact render format, never captured telemetry (test-plan
  §11). The vehicle's shape — a measurement-only env-gated test or an xtask leg — is a P4 fork]

- **The fix, chosen from the measurement** — candidates the entry names: the prompt's surface/dismiss guidance, the
  digest's content, a creation threshold, or deterministic sampling arguments. [inferred — which one(s) is decided by
  the measurement; the plan states the decision rule in advance. The digest branch has a no-new-struct path:
  `assembler.rs:266-270` builds the cue summary from the full `AttentionCue`, so its quantities can enter the text without
  touching `DigestCueRef`]

- **The false `OVERALL: nominal` line is corrected regardless of the measurement** [added at P5 validation-1,
  intent-incomplete: the overseer's founder-delegated answer at P4 — "a status line the code knows is false must never
  stay in the model input, whatever its measured effect … nothing deferred"]. A0 is recorded on the untouched base
  first, arm A2 measures the corrected line alone, and the GREEN reading reports the combined change with A2's delta
  beside it.

- **A pinned regression witness** for the fix that does not depend on a live model where the cause is offline-testable
  (e.g. a prompt-composition or args-vector assertion), plus the live re-measurement as the outcome evidence.
  [VERIFIED shape: every candidate fix has an offline-pinnable artifact — the `render_payload` text, the prompt
  constants (`PROMPT_VERSION_*` bump), the `build_llama_cli_args` vector; a real-model generation cannot be a committed
  gate (test-plan §10 zero-flake)]

- No retune-until-pass: the prompt, thresholds or sampling are changed only for a measured reason, and the
  re-measurement count is fixed in the plan before it runs.

- Every run that launches pulse-app, a window, or the model binary is an operator slot — the chunk stops and asks,
  stating the run's expected length. Nothing in plan or implement assumes a slot is free.

- The Conductor repo is read-only from here; its measurements are cited by coordinate, never copied, and never treated
  as a HEAD fact for this repo.
- Detection and redaction (`security::scrubber`) are untouched — the span-level chunk already shipped the honest input.

- The model, the llama.cpp build (b9305) and the GBNF/JSON-schema constraint path are not swapped by this chunk.
  [VERIFIED — arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] locks them; sampling args inside
  `build_llama_cli_args` are within that decision, a model or build swap is not]

- Incident identity stays coalesce-per-cue-identity `(kind, scope, scope_id)`; a predicate change alters only WHETHER an
  incident is created (arch §Fault Identity).

- A prompt-text change also reaches Investigate (`investigate_router.rs:248` is the second production caller of
  `build_primary_tier_prompt`), so its pins move with it.

An incident's lifecycle events — the `incident_events` rows the corpus records on every status VALUE change inside
the guarded `update_incident_status` transaction — become readable through the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` stdio sidecar as
a NEW ninth tool, `retrieve_incident_events(incident_id)` (founder ruling 2026-10-02, relayed by the pc overseer: the
boundary widening is ratified and the shape is a ninth tool). The read is a bounded, ordered projection of the ledger
exactly as chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep decided it — status transitions only, no event at
creation (overseer, founder-delegated, P4 2026-10-02) — carrying only the closed `event_kind` label and
`occurred_unix_nano`, never the payload column (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging, the
`incident_events` NO-SCRUB boundary; arch §Occupied Resources → At-rest posture).

P-075 is then re-verified on a fresh Conductor round against this chunk's binary, its content fidelity extended to the
events read back through MCP (route CARRY; founder ruling 2026-10-02). The matrix tool cannot reopen a verified cap
from a non-owning chunk (research.md §Files inspected, `matrix.py`), so the re-verification is THIS chunk's own
acceptance criterion with its evidence in `evidence/`, and a `matrix#P-075` notes line at wrap (overseer,
founder-delegated, P4 2026-10-02).

The second CARRY corrects a spec claim, not code: obs-plan and its leaves state an APP stderr + file sink, while
`pulse-app/src/observability.rs::init` (`:2634-2659`) builds the file layer only. The sidecar's own stderr + file sink
(`crates/mcp-server/src/tracing_setup.rs:248-275`) is true and stays. The correction rides `Expected amendments
(wrap)`; no source file changes for it.

1. **An incident-event row type and its read** — in `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`, add a plain row type for one
   event (`event_kind: String`, `occurred_unix_nano: i64`; derive like `IncidentRowRaw`) and a `CorpusWriter` method
   `load_incident_events(incident_id: i64, limit: u32) -> Result<Vec<…>, Error>` beside `load_incident_by_id`, with a
   doc comment naming its cross-process consumer. Implement it on `Corpus` (`contract.rs:464`, the trait's only impl —
   `grep -rn 'CorpusWriter for' crates pulse-app xtask` = 1): one prepared statement selecting `event_kind,
   occurred_unix_nano` FROM `incident_events` WHERE `incident_id = ?1` ORDER BY `id` ASC LIMIT `?2`, `?` placeholders
   only, `Error::QueryFailed` on any rusqlite error. The `payload` column is NOT selected (it is
   `cell_encrypt(key, &[])` by construction in `update_incident_status`; scope §What it builds). No DDL, no
   `SCHEMA_VERSION` change.

2. **Corpus pins** (co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, every fn name carrying `load_incident_events`), seeding
   through the PRODUCTION writer (`save_incident` + `update_incident_status`), never a hand INSERT into
   `incident_events` except where the case needs an out-of-set kind: (a) a fresh incident reads `[]`; (b) two
   transitions read `[acknowledged@T1, resolved@T2]` in order with the exact timestamps written; (c) another
   incident's events are excluded; (d) `limit` bounds the count (three transitions, limit 2 → the first two);
   (e) a declined stale write adds nothing (reads the same as before it).

3. **Tool constant and roster** — in `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs`: `TOOL_RETRIEVE_INCIDENT_EVENTS =
   "retrieve_incident_events"`, appended to `ALL_TOOL_NAMES` (`:53-62`); a `dispatch_tool` match arm (`:169-180`);
   `result_type_label` → `"incident_events"` (`:562-574`); `result_count_for` → the `events` array length
   (`:576-600`). The tool rides `dispatch_tool`'s single emission site (`:182-214`), so the response, metric and error
   records need no new target and no allowlist change (`tracing_setup.rs:56-103`: the `mcp` module key covers
   `mcp.tools.call.*`; the exact `metric.mcp.tool_call_duration_ms` leaf already carries `value, method,
   result_count`).

4. **The dispatcher** — `dispatch_retrieve_incident_events(ctx, arguments)`: `require_incident_ctx` →
   `parse_args::<IncidentIdArgs>` → `load_incident_row` (the existing existence check: absent or undecryptable →
   `"incident not found"`, -32603, the same shape as `retrieve_report`) → `ctx.corpus.load_incident_events(row.id,
   INCIDENT_EVENTS_READ_LIMIT + 1)` mapped through `short_reason`. Response: `{"incident_id", "events":
   [{"event_kind", "occurred_unix_nano"}], "total", "truncated"}` — at most `INCIDENT_EVENTS_READ_LIMIT` events,
   `truncated` true when the limit+1-th row exists. `INCIDENT_EVENTS_READ_LIMIT` is a module const of 256 (an authoring
   bound: the ledger holds one row per status VALUE change over three statuses, so a real incident sits orders of
   magnitude below it). `event_kind` is coerced on egress: a value equal to `triage::contract::incident_status_label`
   of one of `IncidentStatus::{Active, Acknowledged, Resolved}` passes; anything else becomes `"unknown"` — never
   passed through (security-plan 2026-09-30 precedent: coerce on output). No workspace filter, the same posture as
   `retrieve_report` / `retrieve_telemetry_slice` / `mark_incident_resolved` (scope §Boundaries). No field of the
   response is logged.

6. **The `tools/list` manifest** — in `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`: rename `tools_list_with_8_tools` (`:124`) to
   the count-free `tools_list_manifest` (the count is about to be false in its name) and add the ninth entry —

   call `:213`); `ALL_TOOL_NAMES.len()` there self-updates.

7. **The sidecar subprocess roster** — `crates/mcp-server/tests/sidecar_subprocess.rs` `sidecar_tools_list_returns_8_tools_with_names`
   (`:81-128`): count 9, the new name asserted; rename the fn to drop the count.

8. **`crates/mcp-server/tests/incident_events_subprocess.rs`** (new; `#![cfg(feature = "mcp-server")]`; binary via
   `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_andromeda-pulse-mcp")`, the `sidecar_subprocess.rs:9-11` form; every fn name carrying

  `event_kind` / `occurred_unix_nano` the production writer recorded, `[]` for a fresh incident, excludes other
  incidents, honours `limit`, and never selects the payload column — the Step 2 pins pass in the
  `cargo nextest run --workspace --features mcp-server --profile ci --success-output immediate -E 'test(/incident_events/)'`
  entry (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources → Corpus SQLite database; security-plan §Data Protection).

- (arch) A real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess lists 9 tools including `retrieve_incident_events`, and its
  `tools/call` returns the events BODY for a seeded incident and a JSON-RPC error (-32603, `incident not found`, no path)
  for an unknown id — Step 8 arms (a)-(b) and Step 7, in the targeted and `package(mcp-server)` entries (per
  architecture.md §Conventions → Error response schema (MCP); §Standard Contracts → MCP server — spec-conformant).

- (security) The response carries only `event_kind` from the closed status-label set (an out-of-set value reads
  `unknown`), `occurred_unix_nano`, `total`, `truncated` and `incident_id` — no payload, no ciphertext, no client text —
  Step 5's coercion pin and Step 8 arm (a) (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging, the `incident_events`
  NO-SCRUB boundary).

- (obs/security) After a `retrieve_incident_events` call, the sidecar's stderr and its `agent-latest.jsonl*` family
  carry the tool name and `result_type` rendered and 0 occurrences of the seeded timestamps or the title canary —
  Step 8 arm (c) (per obs-plan §4 Scenario P3, §8 Default-deny posture; security-plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER
  to log"; test-plan §1 `security-vector-coverage: MCP response body redaction`).

- (security) The tool is reachable only through the double gate: the sidecar binary is `required-features =
  ["mcp-server"]` and `validate_double_gate()` runs before any dispatch (`andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:96-108`); the existing
  `sidecar_env_unset_exits_cleanly_without_stdio` leg stays green in the `package(mcp-server)` entry — by construction,
  no new path (per security-plan §API Security "MCP feature double-gate").

- (tests) The new pins are collected by name (the `cargo nextest list --workspace --features mcp-server --profile ci -E 'test(/incident_events/)'`
  entry) and the subprocess leg RAN rather than skipped on this host (the targeted entry's `lacks` atom), so neither

data.head: # Scope — Incident events readable through MCP

body: **Marker:** `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp` · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Polish & ship: verification
**Working entry (verbatim title + hint):** Incident events readable through MCP — an incident's lifecycle events read back through the MCP sidecar, so the P-075 round's content fidelity covers them

- An MCP read surface over the corpus `incident_events` table: an incident's lifecycle events (the rows `CorpusWriter::update_incident_status` records on every status VALUE change, inside the guarded transaction — `event_kind` = the new status label, `occurred_unix_nano`, an empty encrypted payload) become readable through the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` stdio sidecar for a named incident.

- The surface shape is open at scope time: a NEW MCP tool (a ninth tool beside the eight at `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:45-62`) or a widening of an existing incident tool's response. `query_incident_list` lists ACTIVE incidents only, so it can never show a resolved incident's `resolved` event; Conductor's readiness gate pins required tools against a contract manifest (Conductor `.andromeda/architecture.md:93`). P4 resolves the fork (a contestable lean → AskUserQuestion). The founder ruling 2026-10-02 (relayed by the pc overseer) fixes THAT the events become MCP-readable in 0.3.0, not the tool shape.

- [premise-corrected: research.md §Files inspected — `CorpusReader` carries only `inspect`/`path` (`contract.rs:186-192`); every incident read the sidecar performs is a `CorpusWriter` method and `IncidentToolContext` binds `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` (`tools.rs:70-74`)] A corpus read path for the events: the only `SELECT … FROM incident_events` today is the test helper `event_kinds` inside `#[cfg(test)]` (`contract.rs:1404-1416`) — no production reader exists. The read lands beside its sibling incident reads (`load_incident_by_id` et al.) on the `CorpusWriter` surface the sidecar already binds, NOT on `CorpusReader`; one impl (`Corpus`, `contract.rs:464`), no mock implements the trait, no new crate edge (`mcp-server → corpus` exists).

- The read is bounded and honest: the events of ONE incident, oldest first (`ORDER BY id`), with a bounded count; `event_kind` is a closed status-label set — every production writer passes a `triage` `status_label` value (`active` / `acknowledged` / `resolved`), and a value outside it is coerced to a sentinel on egress, never passed through. [premise-corrected: the payload is empty by construction (`cell_encrypt(key, &[])`, `contract.rs` `update_incident_status`) and carries no information, so the read does not SELECT the payload column at all — nothing to decrypt, no ciphertext reachable] An unknown incident id reuses `load_incident_row`'s existence check and returns the same `"incident not found"` error (JSON-RPC -32603) as `retrieve_report`.
- The sidecar's double gate holds: compile-time `--features mcp-server` AND runtime `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` (security.md §MCP feature double-gate).

- MCP tool response bodies are NEVER logged (CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings); the new read's tracing carries a bounded result count and type label only (the `result_type_label` / `result_count_for` pattern at `tools.rs:562/576`).
- MCP errors stay standard JSON-RPC 2.0 error objects with sanitized messages (`short_reason`).
- No TauRPC procedure, port, capability JSON or webview change is in scope — the surface is the stdio sidecar only.

- No corpus schema change: `incident_events` already exists (SCHEMA_VERSION 2, `schema.rs:69-77`) and has a production writer since chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep. Measured: an incident's CREATION records NO event — `save_incident` inserts the incident row only, and `status_value_change_records_one_lifecycle_event_per_transition` pins an empty event list right after it (`contract.rs:1419-1440`). The read surface therefore shows status transitions only; an incident read before its first transition has zero events, so P-075's events assertion is non-vacuous only AFTER a transition (the round's `mark_incident_resolved` produces exactly one `resolved` event). Whether to also record an opening event is a P4 fork.

- The incident tools read an id without a workspace filter (`load_incident_by_id`, used unfiltered by `retrieve_report` / `retrieve_telemetry_slice` / `mark_incident_resolved`); the events read follows the same posture.

- **CARRY (P-075 re-verification):** P-075 is re-verified after this entry — its content-fidelity acceptance extends to the incident events read back through MCP, proven by a fresh Conductor round against this entry's binary (founder ruling 2026-10-02, relayed by the pc overseer; the new MCP read surface is the founder's word).
  - P-075 is `status: verified` in the 0.3.0 matrix (ref: Conductor 2a494804, CI#36970919487, round on Pulse S 03ec944; `chunk` = 2026-10-01-conductor-return). Measured on `matrix.py`: `claim` refuses a verified cap (`:209-210`), `refine` refuses any chunk but the owner (`:274-275`), and only `note` writes at any status (`:355-365`, ref/acceptance untouched). So THIS chunk has no tool path that reopens P-075 or rewrites its acceptance/ref; HOW the founder's "re-verified" is recorded is a P4 fork for the operator, resolved before any matrix write.
  - The fresh Conductor round runs against this chunk's operator pre-CI commit binary, in the same form as 2026-10-01-conductor-return (`evidence/round-request.md` names the binary and the graded assertion set; `evidence/round-binary.md` records S and the build command); its evidence is cited on the overseer's word. Conductor-side work (a new round assertion over the events, and adding the new tool to Conductor's pinned contract manifest if a ninth tool lands) is executed in that repo, never from here.

No test-plan site depends on an app stderr sink (the §3 `2>&1 | tee` stream is nextest's output). Phase never amends spec sources, so the obs-plan amendment and the leaf corrections ride this chunk's `Expected amendments (wrap)`; the plan carries a by-construction check that names the measured init. - **Marker:** 2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-04
- **Chunk base:** `76d6ccacf3eb238dca39ff2e939c7cd96c7aa13a` (HEAD at P4)

The first-ever corpus key is created by a get → generate → set sequence with no compare-and-set (`crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs:155-172`). Concurrent first-run processes each mint and store their own key, and the last write wins. Measured at HEAD (research.md §Measured): in 5 of 5 rounds, 8 concurrent children against one empty test-scoped entry minted 8 distinct keys, and 7 of the 8 returned a key the store no longer held. A process that encrypts rows under such a key hands its peers undecryptable rows. The 2026-10-02 MCP leg read them as `incident not found`, and the boot disposition retires them as orphans.
This chunk makes creation a **locked create-or-read**, per the founder ruling of 2026-10-04 (fix it with a locked create-or-read):

- `OsKeychainBackend` takes an exclusive `std::fs::File::lock` on a lock file whose name is a function of the credential entry. The name embeds the first 16 hex characters of BLAKE3 over service + account.
- The lock file lives in a per-user directory: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on Linux, `std::env::temp_dir()` elsewhere.
- Under the lock the process gets the entry. On `NoEntry` it generates, sets, and **reads back**. It returns the key the store holds, then unlocks.

Every concurrent first-run process therefore ends on one key, the one the store holds afterwards. The lock covers separate processes and threads in one process alike: `File::lock` excludes a second handle on the same path, measured on rustc 1.95.0 (research.md §Measured).

The lock location is a **boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-04 (relayed by the overseer)**. It is a second product-written artifact outside the resolved data dir, after the `~/Downloads` export sink. The location is keyed to the credential entry because research falsified the data-dir premise. The race is keyed on the ONE per-user credential entry `(com.andromeda.pulse, corpus-key)`, and the measured symptom came from processes with DIFFERENT data dirs. A data-dir lock would have left that case open.
The change is confined to `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs`:

- The constructor, the `KeychainBackend` trait, the `Corpus::open` mapping (any `KeychainError` → `Error::KeyringUnavailable`) and both construction sites (`pulse-app/src/main.rs:340`, `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:66`) are unchanged.
- The fail-closed custody posture holds (per security-plan §Secret Management → Runtime; architecture §Occupied Resources → Corpus SQLite → At-rest posture).
- Lock failure surfaces through the existing boot records (`corpus.open.error` in the app, `mcp.boot.corpus.init` in the sidecar). No new log target is added (per obs-plan §8 corpus leaves).

1. **Lock-path derivation (pure, testable).** In `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs`, add private helpers:
   - **(a) Lock directory**, from two injected inputs (the raw `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` value and the `temp_dir()` path), so every branch is testable without mutating the process environment. This mirrors `resolve_key`'s argument-injection precedent at `keychain.rs:172-175`.
     - On Linux (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`): `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset or empty after trim → the temp dir. Set → it must be absolute, `canonicalize()` must succeed, and it must be a directory. Otherwise → `Err(KeychainError::Unavailable)`. Set-but-unusable FAILS CLOSED and never falls back, on the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` precedent (arch history 2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals: "a set-but-unresolvable root rejects everything").
     - On every other OS: the temp dir.
     - The temp dir is canonicalized and must be a directory, else `Unavailable`.
   - **(b) Lock file name** `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-{h}.lock`. `{h}` is the first 16 lowercase hex characters of `blake3` over `service`, a `0x00` separator byte, and the `service_id` (account). The name is deterministic, ASCII, and distinct per service and per account.

2. **Locked create-or-read in `fetch_from_os_store`** (`keychain.rs:155`):
   - Resolve the lock path (Step 1) BEFORE any keyring call.
   - Open the lock file: create, write, no truncate; on Unix mode `0o600` via `std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt`. Take `File::lock()` (exclusive, blocking).
   - Under the lock: `get_password` → `Ok` decodes and returns. `NoEntry` → `generate_random_key` → `set_password` → `get_password` again, return the READ-BACK decoded key. A read-back that fails or does not decode → `Err(KeychainError::Failed)`.
   - Release the lock explicitly (`unlock`) before returning on every arm. Drop also releases it.
   - Failures map into the existing unit variants: lock-dir resolution failure → `Unavailable`; open or lock failure → `Failed`. They carry no path, no key bytes and no `Display` of an OS error.
   - The lock file is never deleted by the product: deleting it after unlock would let a later opener lock a different inode than a waiter. It holds no content.
   - `resolve_key` is unchanged. A lock failure is a store-side `Err`, so it degrades exactly like an unreachable store: the passphrase fallback only when configured, otherwise the error. That keeps the fail-closed side (security-plan §Secret Management → Runtime). No unlocked generate-and-set path remains.

3. **Concurrent re-exec witness** (co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `keychain.rs`, extending the re-exec precedent at `keychain.rs:393-456`). Every new test fn name carries the token `race_free` (the gate filter). The two fns are `corpus_key_race_free_child_resolves_after_barrier` and `corpus_key_race_free_across_concurrent_first_run_processes`. The witness:
   - Uses a test-scoped service `andromeda-pulse-test-{pid}-race-free`.
   - Probes the store WITHOUT creating the entry: `keyring::Entry::new(&service, "corpus-key")` then `get_password()`. `NoEntry` → the store answers and the entry is absent, so proceed. Any other result → `eprintln!("[skip] no OS credential store on this host; concurrent-creation leg not run")` and return. An `Ok` (a leftover entry) deletes it and proceeds, never asserting over a pre-seeded key.
   - Spawns 8 children of the current test binary (`--exact` the child fn, `--nocapture`), each with its own sink path under one `TempDir` and the service in the CHILD's environment, and a stdin pipe.
   - The child is inert unless both of its env vars are set (the `child_writes_its_resolved_key` shape, `keychain.rs:393-406`). It blocks reading one line from stdin (the barrier). It then resolves the key through `OsKeychainBackend::new(service).fetch_or_create_key("corpus-key")` and writes the hex to its sink.
   - The parent releases the barrier only after all 8 are spawned, by writing a line to each stdin and closing it. No `sleep` is used for synchronization.
   - After every child ends, the parent reads the stored key (`get_password`, decode) and the test-scoped lock file's metadata (the Step 1 path for this service: it exists, length 0). It then deletes the entry AND that lock file BEFORE asserting, so a failure cannot pollute the operator's store.
   - It asserts:
     - every child exited 0;
     - all 8 sinks exist (in-arm child-ran proof; a missing sink fails, never counts as agreement);
     - exactly 1 distinct key across the 8;
     - that key equals the stored key;
     - the lock file existed and was empty (content-free).
   - Keys are compared in-process and never printed (test-plan §11 Universal; security rules §Logging & redaction).

5. **Mutation and RED-at-base controls (one-shot at /implement, never listed as gates).** Write Step 3's witness FIRST and run it against HEAD's unlocked `fetch_from_os_store`. It must go RED with more than 1 distinct key (research measured 8 of 8). Then land Steps 1-2 and see it GREEN. Then restore the unlocked get-then-set as a mutation: the witness must go RED again. Restore. Record each reading (distinct count, returned-not-stored count, exit) in `evidence/mutation-checks.md`, the key digests at most, never a key.

6. **Doc comments.** In `keychain.rs`, update the `OsKeychainBackend` doc (`:117-125`) and `fetch_from_os_store` to state the locked create-or-read. Name the lock location rule (per-user directory, entry-keyed name, content-free, never deleted) and the residuals listed under Implementation notes. Keep it ASCII-only (`cargo xtask check:english-sources`).
- none

- `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs` — Steps 1-4 and 6: the lock-path helpers, the locked create-or-read in `fetch_from_os_store`, the concurrent re-exec witness, the lock-path and fail-closed pins, and the doc comments. `OsKeychainBackend::new`, the `KeychainBackend` trait, `resolve_key` and `KeychainError`'s variants are unchanged, so no caller is touched. That covers `OsKeychainBackend::new` at `pulse-app/src/main.rs:340`, `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:66` and 3 test files, and `Error::KeyringUnavailable` in 14 files (research.md §Graph impact, derived by grep since the graph is unavailable).

The standard gate set runs in the test-plan §3 order: capability-drift before the default-features workspace nextest, then the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen, then the base-identity bindings close, since no procedure is added. The chunk's own gates come first, all under `--workspace` (test-plan §11 run-scope rule):
- the targeted witness/pin run with its collection proof;
- the `corpus` package suite;
- the three cross-process MCP legs that open the production entry, as a regression check under `--features mcp-server`;
- the scope guard.
Absences, each with its reason:
- No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the webview gates are absent.

- No boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `observability.rs`, `crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `tauri.conf.json`, `capabilities/*.json`; the scope-guard entry proves it), so the boot smoke does not bind (test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate).
- There is no harness live leg and no self-verify. The witness's real processes are re-executed test binaries inside the unit entry.

- No dependency is added (`std` file locking plus `blake3`, already a `corpus` dep), so `cargo deny` / `cargo audit` are not listed locally. The CI `supply-chain` job runs them, and the operator CI read asserts it green.

- CI runners have no credential store, so the witness clean-skips there. Its non-skip proof is the dev-host entry's `lacks [skip]` atom (test-plan §1 `mcp-incident-read-back-cross-process-coverage` precedent).

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot evaluate on the Linux dev host, because it drives every stage through `wsl.exe` (`xtask/src/pre_push.rs:23`). Under the founder deviation of 2026-10-04, its six stages run NATIVELY by hand before the push, as in the two predecessor chunks. They are the six `operator` entries after hygiene, in `Stage::ALL` order, each in the stage isolation of `Linux::cmd`.
Two founder-ruled 2026-10-04 differences from the predecessor's literal form:
- Stage 3 runs with `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` pointed at a fresh, per-invocation path under `target/pre-push/`. The ruling is to isolate the cache, never delete `~/.cache/puppeteer`.
- Stage 6 seeds a per-invocation data dir with no `rm`.

Because stage 5 (a default-features workspace test run) re-emits the bindings in the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the base-identity close are RE-FIRED as `operator` entries after stage 6 and before the push. This is the stage-ORDER lesson the handoff carries.
ONE-SHOT controls at /implement, never listed (they mutate source and revert; the light gate re-runs entries verbatim):
- the witness's RED-at-base read against HEAD's unlocked get-then-set;
- the mutation check that restores it after the fix (Step 5).

Both readings go in `evidence/mutation-checks.md`, which the second criterion names. That file has no listed producer by construction: /implement writes it from those two runs. The listed, non-mutating `race_free` targeted entry guards the property on every re-run.

The CI read waits 2400 s, against the last measured green run's wall-clock of 1718 s (`a69030a`); its timeout is 2400 + 180. Targeted feature-gated entries carry 5400 s for a cold `--features mcp-server` workspace build.

- A lock under the resolved data dir — rejected by founder ruling 2026-10-04. The race is keyed on the per-user credential entry, and processes with different data dirs (the measured case) would stay racy.
- An in-process `Mutex` / `OnceLock` alone — rejected: the topology has at least two processes on one entry (arch extract anti-pattern).

- Read-back alone, with no lock (set, then adopt whatever the store holds) — rejected: a process may already have returned and used its own key before a later writer overwrote it, so it only narrows the window. Measured: 7 of 8 returned a key the store no longer held.

- Falling through to an unlocked generate-and-set, or to an ephemeral per-process key, on a lock failure — banned. It reproduces the orphaning (security-plan §Secret Management → Runtime). A lock failure is a store-side `Err` and nothing else.
- A third-party file-lock crate — not needed. `std::fs::File::lock` is stable on the pinned 1.95.0 and its exclusion was measured (research.md §Measured).
- Deleting the lock file after use — rejected: it creates a new-inode race between a waiter and a later opener. The file is content-free and persistent.

- Running the MCP legs against a FRESH production entry — rejected as destructive. Deleting `com.andromeda.pulse/corpus-key` would orphan the operator's real corpus. The fresh-store concurrency claim is proven by the test-scoped witness instead, and the MCP legs run as a regression check with the entry present.
- Changing `OsKeychainBackend::new`, the trait, or the construction sites — unnecessary. The backend already holds the entry identity (service plus the per-call account).

  - (4) `File::lock` blocks without a timeout. A peer stuck inside the store call (for example a Secret Service unlock prompt) stalls other first-run openers until it ends; the OS releases the lock if the peer is killed.

title: Scope — Corpus key creation is race-free

data.head: # Scope — Corpus key creation is race-free

body: **Marker:** `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free` · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Polish & ship: verification
**Working entry (verbatim title + hint):** Corpus key creation is race-free — concurrent first-run processes end up sharing one corpus key

- First-ever corpus key creation in `OsKeychainBackend::fetch_from_os_store` (`crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs:155-172`) becomes a **locked create-or-read**, as the founder ruled on 2026-10-04. Today the function calls `entry.get_password()` and, on `keyring::Error::NoEntry`, generates a random key and calls `entry.set_password(...)` with no compare-and-set. Each concurrent first-run process that sees `NoEntry` mints its own key, and the last write wins.

- The outcome: when N processes resolve the corpus key concurrently against an EMPTY credential store, every one of them ends with the SAME 32-byte key, and that key is the one the store holds afterwards. No process returns a key the store no longer holds.

- The lock has to work ACROSS processes (the measured case is concurrent test processes; the production case is a first-boot app plus its MCP sidecar). An in-process `Mutex` alone cannot close it. An exclusive `std::fs::File::lock` held across get → (generate → set) → read-back closes it: the API is stable on the pinned 1.95.0, and a second handle on the same path is excluded even in the same process (research.md §Measured, `lockprobe.rs`).

- After the set, the key the process returns is the key read back from the store (or is verified equal to it), so a write that still lost a race the lock did not cover can never hand back a key the store does not hold. `get_password` after `set_password` is available on the same `keyring::Entry` (`keychain.rs:156-166`).

- [premise-corrected: the race is keyed on the credential ENTRY `(com.andromeda.pulse, corpus-key)`, one per OS user, not on the data dir — every cross-process test leg opens that one entry from a DIFFERENT per-test data dir, and the measured symptom came from exactly such processes (research.md §Measured)] The lock's location must be a function of the credential entry for the outcome above to hold for ALL concurrent first-run processes. A lock under the resolved data dir closes only processes that resolve the same data dir (the default app + sidecar pair) and leaves the measured case open. `OsKeychainBackend::new(service)` already holds the entry identity (service, plus the `service_id` passed per call), so a per-entry lock needs no new constructor input and no change at the construction sites (`pulse-app/src/main.rs:340`, `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:66`). Where the lock file lives (per-user location vs the data dir) is P4's fork (research.md §Open questions).

- A witness that reproduces the race and goes RED on HEAD's get-then-set: several real processes (or a barrier-synchronized set) resolving a key against one shared, initially empty store must agree on one key. It must not pass vacuously: if the platform store is absent, the witness either skips with a `[skip]` line or runs against a store the test controls; it never reads as a green.

- The passphrase fallback (`resolve_key`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE`; `derive_key_from_passphrase`, `keychain.rs:241`) is deterministic (BLAKE3-derived) and so has no create race. It stays as it is. The lock covers only the OS-store creation path.
- No change to the key format (`encode_key` / `decode_key`, 32 bytes hex), the service / account naming, the cell-level AES-256-GCM scheme, the corpus schema or `SCHEMA_VERSION`.

- The fail-closed posture stays: a transient store failure with no passphrase configured still surfaces the store's error and never invents a key (doc comment on `OsKeychainBackend`). A lock that cannot be acquired is a failure, not a reason to fall through to an unlocked create.

- `corpus::disposition` (the boot-time inventory-then-purge of rows orphaned under a lost key) is untouched. This chunk prevents NEW orphaning at creation; it does not change how existing orphans are retired.
- Logging: no key material, no full path (a lock-file path, if one is added, is logged by basename only, per `.claude/rules/security.md` §Logging & redaction).

- Path discipline: a lock-file directory taken from any environment variable (a data dir, or a per-user runtime/temp dir) is canonicalized before use and asserted to be a directory. The lock file holds no content. No new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*_PATH` var is introduced unless P4 finds one necessary.

- No TauRPC procedure, port, capability JSON, webview or MCP tool change. Workspace deps: none — `std` file locking on the pinned 1.95.0, and `blake3` (already a `corpus` dep) if the lock name hashes the entry identity (research.md §Files inspected).

- **CONTEXT (verbatim):** `OsKeychainBackend::fetch_from_os_store` (`crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs`) gets, then on `NoEntry` generates and sets with no compare-and-set, so concurrent first-run processes each mint a key and the last write wins (mechanism by code reading, not measured as a race); measured symptom at 2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp (`evidence/mutation-checks.md`): a fresh Linux credential store read `incident not found` on seeded ids with one key `created = modified`, then green on the identical tree with the key present; pre-existing since 2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence; founder ruling 2026-10-04: fix it with a locked create-or-read
  - Coordinates re-verified at HEAD: `fetch_from_os_store` at `keychain.rs:155`; its `NoEntry` arm at `:160` calls `set_password` at `:164` with no read-back. `evidence/mutation-checks.md:115-127` of the named chunk records the `-32603 incident not found` red, the single key `created = modified = 2026-10-03 21:54:52`, and the green `--only 3` re-run with the key present (`modified` unchanged).
  - **Mechanism claim (verbatim marker kept): "mechanism by code reading, not measured as a race".** VERIFIED by measurement at HEAD (research.md §Measured): 5 of 5 rounds of 8 concurrent children against one empty test-scoped entry minted 8 distinct keys, and 7 of 8 returned a key the store no longer held.

title: Plan — 2026-10-04-declared-rust-floor-matches-the-code: "The declared Rust floor matches the code"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-04-declared-rust-floor-matches-the-code: "The declared Rust floor matches the code"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-04-declared-rust-floor-matches-the-code · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-04T21:45Z
- **Chunk base:** `46b600a7f06fe1abe0d4bb93d0e559f49dbdb380` (HEAD at P4; every base-reading entry names it)
- **Matrix:** no capability claimed — `matrix.py show --unclaimed` reads `unclaimed 0 of 22`; this entry advances none

The workspace declares `rust-version = "1.85"` while nothing below 1.95.0 can build it. The entry's CONTEXT measured
the workspace's OWN code floor at ≥ 1.89 (`std::fs::File::lock`), but research found the dependency graph sets the
floor higher. 28 resolved packages declare `rust-version = "1.95.0"`: wasmtime 48.0.5 and its internal crates,
cranelift 0.135.5 and pulley 48.0.5 (`cargo metadata --offline`, research.md). `pulse-app` depends on `plugins`
non-optionally (`pulse-app/Cargo.toml:51`). This chunk raises the declared floor to `1.95`, the pinned channel's
major.minor, without moving the toolchain or any dependency (per architecture §Stack and Technologies, Primary
language row; §Established Decisions [Primary Language]).

Raising the declared floor also raises clippy's MSRV, which switches ON two MSRV-gated lints. At MSRV 1.95.0, clippy
raises `manual_is_multiple_of` ×2 and `collapsible_if` ×18 across 13 files, which would red the `-D warnings` gate.
Measured with a scratch `CLIPPY_CONF_DIR` config at P3; research.md §Patterns detected lists every site. The chunk
fixes each site in place and adds no suppression (per security-plan §Dependency Security → CI integration). The one
function-scoped `#[allow(clippy::incompatible_msrv)]` (`crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs:268`) and its stale comment
go, since `File::lock` is below the new floor.

The floor is kept honest by a witness the overseer chose at P4 (founder-delegated): an xtask `#[test]` asserting
that the declared floor equals `rust-toolchain.toml`'s channel at major.minor. Every pinned-toolchain build then
proves the declared floor by construction, covering syntax, APIs and dependencies. An overstated floor costs
nobody, because Pulse ships an app, not a published crate. The chunk also discharges the folded CARRY. The skip
arm of `corpus_key_survives_a_real_process_boundary` takes the corpus-key lock before the store call fails and
returns before its cleanup, so every store-less run leaves a pid-named lock file behind. The fix removes the TEST's
own lock file on that arm. The product's never-delete contract and its lock-dir resolution stay untouched (per
architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem locations → Out-of-data-dir lock file; security-plan §Data Protection
→ "Corpus-key lock file").

1. **RED readings at base (one-shot, before any edit).**
   - Write the CARRY witness from Step 5 first and run it against the untouched skip arm. It must read RED: one
     `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-*.lock` is left in the child's `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. Record the reading in
     `evidence/mutation-checks.md`.
   - The floor witness from Step 3 needs no separate RED run. At base it compares `1.85` with `1.95`, and the
     listed collection plus targeted entries show it green only after Step 2.

2. **Raise the declared floor.**
   - `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package]`: `rust-version = "1.85"` → `rust-version = "1.95"`. One line; all 16 members
     inherit it via `rust-version.workspace = true`, and no member manifest changes.
   - `rust-toolchain.toml` is NOT touched.
   - `Cargo.lock` must not change: `resolver = "2"` is not MSRV-aware, and the scope guard asserts this.

4. **Remove the stale guard** in `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs`. Delete the `#[allow(clippy::incompatible_msrv)]` at
   `:268` and the two-line comment at `:266-267` that justifies it ("the workspace `rust-version` (1.85) trails the
   pin"). `fetch_with_lock_dir` keeps its signature and body. Its callers are `fetch_from_os_store` @
   `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs:263` and the fail-closed test @ `:749` (research.md §Graph impact), and neither
   changes.

5. **The CARRY: the skip arm leaves no lock file (test-only).**
   - **Fix.** In `corpus_key_survives_a_real_process_boundary` (`keychain.rs:524`), the `let … else` skip arm
     (`:532-535`) removes the test-scoped lock file before it prints `[skip]` and returns. It uses the same
     `default_lock_dir()` + `lock_file_name(&service, "corpus-key")` + `remove_file` form the success arm already uses
     at `:555-557`. The lock file is the TEST's pid-scoped service name, never the product's.
   - **Witness.** A new `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` test `corpus_key_skip_arm_leaves_no_lock_file` in the same
     `mod tests`:
     1. It creates a fresh `tempfile::TempDir`.
     2. It re-executes the current test binary with `--exact keychain::tests::corpus_key_survives_a_real_process_boundary
        --nocapture`, with `env_clear()` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set to the TempDir.
     3. It captures the child's output and asserts the pair (child output contains
        `[skip] no OS credential store on this host; cross-process leg not run`, count of `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-*.lock`
        files in the TempDir) == (true, 0).
     The `[skip]` half proves the arm ran, so the witness cannot pass vacuously (test-plan §4 corpus crate: a skip
     count is never proof). The mechanism is the Linux rule at `keychain.rs:131-150`: a set, absolute, canonicalizable
     `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is the lock dir. With the environment cleared there is no `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and no
     `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`, so Secret Service is unreachable and the child's backend returns `Err` (research.md
     §Patterns detected).
   - The env difference lives only in the child: no `set_var` in the parent (test-plan §11 Mocking; the re-exec form
     at `keychain.rs:540-545`). Code text is ASCII only.

6. **Fix the MSRV-gated lint sites** surfaced by clippy at MSRV 1.95.0 (research.md §Patterns detected; re-derive with
   `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` after Step 2):
   - `manual_is_multiple_of` → `.is_multiple_of(10)`, at `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs:262` (`sum: u32`, `:248`)
     and `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs:395`.
   - `collapsible_if` → a let-chain at each of the 18 sites, keeping branch order and every early return: `crates/corpus/src/db.rs:21`
     · `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:553` · `crates/ingest/tests/grpc_loopback.rs:150` ·
     `crates/mcp-server/src/tracing_setup.rs:110,115,120` · `crates/triage/src/incident/registry.rs:251` ·
     `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:130,664,869` · `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:2452,2457,2462`
     (`FieldAllowlist::for_target`) · `pulse-app/src/window.rs:229` ·
     `pulse-app/tests/security_mcp_response_body_redaction.rs:148` · `xtask/src/main.rs:1447,1448` · `xtask/src/smoke.rs:66`.
   - `cargo clippy --fix` may apply them, but read every hunk: each change must be a semantic no-op. No
     `#[allow]` / `#[expect]` is added anywhere (Constraints).

8. **Remove the `/tmp` lock residue and record it** (overseer review, founder-delegated, 2026-10-04: "remove it
   inside the chunk and record it"). After Step 5 lands, write `evidence/residue-removal.md`. Re-derive, never copy:
   - The pre-state: `ls -l --time-style=full-iso /tmp/andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-*.lock`. At take-up this was one
     0-byte, `0o600` file, `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-c2875066785cd2b7.lock`.
   - That no process holds it: a scan of `/proc/[0-9]*/fd` symlinks for the name counts 0.
   - `rm -- /tmp/andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-c2875066785cd2b7.lock`, the exact name and nothing globbed.
   - The post-state: the same `ls` lists no such file.
   Removing it is safe whatever its origin, because only an unheld file is removed and the next opener recreates an
   empty one. The product's never-delete rule governs the product code path racing live peers, not a stale file on
   an idle host. Its origin is decided by the operator census after native pre-push stage 5 (Test Commands):
   test-scoped lock names hash the test pid and never repeat, while the cross-process MCP legs that open the
   PRODUCTION service `com.andromeda.pulse` (research.md sweep record) create the product-named file in `/tmp`
   under `env -i`. The same name reappearing therefore means the residue was the product's own lock, re-created by
   design. Any other name, or none, is recorded as read.

9. **Run the gate block** in its order. The boot smoke runs UNATTENDED under Xvfb on the granted slot
   (Test Commands).
- `xtask/src/rust_floor.rs` — the floor witness `#[test]` module (Step 3)
- `Cargo.toml` — `[workspace.package] rust-version = "1.95"` (Step 2)
- `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs` — drop the `incompatible_msrv` allow + its comment (Step 4); skip-arm cleanup + the Linux re-exec witness (Step 5); one `collapsible_if` site is not here
- `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs` — `is_multiple_of` (Step 6)
- `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` — `is_multiple_of` (Step 6)
- `crates/corpus/src/db.rs` — let-chain (Step 6)
- `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs` — let-chain (Step 6)
- `crates/ingest/tests/grpc_loopback.rs` — let-chain (Step 6)
- `crates/mcp-server/src/tracing_setup.rs` — let-chains ×3 (Step 6)
- `crates/triage/src/incident/registry.rs` — let-chain (Step 6)
- `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` — let-chains ×3 (Step 6)
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — let-chains ×3 in `FieldAllowlist::for_target` (Step 6; boot-smoke trigger)
- `pulse-app/src/window.rs` — let-chain (Step 6)
- `pulse-app/tests/security_mcp_response_body_redaction.rs` — let-chain (Step 6)
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — `mod rust_floor;` (Step 3) + let-chains ×2 (Step 6)
- `xtask/src/smoke.rs` — let-chain (Step 6)

The standard gate set runs in the test-plan §3 order. `capability-drift` precedes the default-features workspace
nextest. The `--features mcp-server` bindings regen and the base-identity bindings close come last, since no
procedure is added. The chunk's own entries come first:
- the two collection proofs and their targeted runs (the floor witness; the skip-arm witness);
- the `corpus` package suite and the observability pins over the edited `for_target`;
- the floor and suppression probes, the scope guard and the log-target census;
- the English-sources gate.
Absences and bindings, each with its reason:
- No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the webview gates are absent.

- No package is added or upgraded, and `Cargo.lock` is guarded unchanged. So `cargo deny` / `cargo audit` are not
  listed locally; CI's `supply-chain` job runs them, and the operator CI read asserts it green.

- **The boot smoke BINDS.** `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` is a test-plan §3 boot-smoke trigger path (test-plan.md:334),
  and Step 6 edits its `FieldAllowlist::for_target`. It takes the Linux direct-binary form of the predecessor
  `2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland`, a GREEN leg only:
  - **Slot and display (overseer review, founder-delegated, 2026-10-04).** Ports 4317/4318 are granted for this
    chunk, and conductor-builder stays idle until its wrap. The founder is not at the desk, so the leg runs
    UNATTENDED under Xvfb in the host's standing form: `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11 xvfb-run -a …`, with
    the whole leg body run inside the virtual display so the app is started and killed by its own pid.
  - **The real-display (native Wayland) leg is NOT run this chunk.** The predecessor chunk's legs carry the native
    Wayland witness of the render posture. This leg's subject is the boot, the allowlist and the ports.
  - **Pass rule:** 30 s up, 0 ERROR, 0 `app.panic.fatal`, ports released, and the `app.boot.render.posture` record
    READ and RECORDED with whatever value it holds. The value is not asserted.
  - **Expectation correction (measured at P5, recorded):** `render_posture::decide` keys only on Linux plus a preset
    lever (`pulse-app/src/render_posture.rs:39-45`), not on Wayland or NVIDIA. So under Xvfb with the lever unset the
    record most likely reads `applied`: the lever is set and is inert without the NVIDIA Wayland driver. The review
    expected a non-`applied` reading. Either reading passes this rule.
  - Ahead of the leg: a `build` entry, then a non-priming port probe.
  - It runs AFTER the workspace nextest and BEFORE the bindings regen, because a default-features `pulse-app` run
    re-emits the no-mcp bindings.
  - Both the probe and the leg are `leg = 'operator'`: they bind :4317/:4318, so /implement fires each once on the
    granted slot, and the wrap's light gate never re-runs them.
  - `cargo xtask self-verify` is a Windows/WRY harness and is not this chunk's smoke.

- **Residue census after native stage 5:** a report-only `operator` entry lists `/tmp`'s corpus-key lock files
  after stage 5. It is the origin read for Step 8's removed file: the same name reappearing means the product's own
  lock, created by the production-service MCP legs under `env -i`. Its `expect = []` is deliberate, because the
  listing's content depends on which legs stage 5 ran.

- There is no harness live leg and no self-verify. The CARRY witness's real processes are re-executed test binaries
  inside its unit entry.

- The CARRY witness is `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`. The macOS and Windows CI legs therefore do not collect it, and
  CI's Linux runner has no credential store, so the witness's child skips there as designed. The witness asserts the
  skip, so it is meaningful on CI too.

- The MSRV-gated lint sites were measured on Linux arms only. CI lint-test lints `cfg(windows)` /
  `cfg(target_os = "macos")` arms this host cannot lint, so a red there is fixed by an operator fix commit on top. The
  scope guard's file list is then exceeded by exactly those files, and the report records them.

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot evaluate on this Linux host (`wsl.exe`, `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`). As in the
predecessor chunks (founder deviation 2026-10-04), its six stages run NATIVELY by hand before the push, as the six
`operator` entries after hygiene. Stage 5 re-emits the no-mcp bindings, so the regen and the base-identity close are
RE-FIRED as `operator` entries after stage 6.

ONE-SHOT controls at /implement are never listed, because they mutate source and revert: Step 1's RED reading and
Step 7's mutation checks (a)–(c). Their readings go in `evidence/mutation-checks.md`, which has no listed producer by
construction. The listed, non-mutating targeted entries guard the same properties on every re-run.

The CI read waits 2400 s, against the last measured green wall-clock of 1498 s (`126788c`, the predecessor report);
its timeout is 2580. Setup 5a read both later shas `in progress`.
