body:
- (tests) The posture decision is pinned per arm with injected inputs: `decide(true, false)` → `applied`,
  `decide(true, true)` → `preset_honoured`, `decide(false, _)` → `not_applicable`. The run
  `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci -E 'binary(unit_render_posture) | binary(unit_observability_allowlist_render_posture)'`
  exits 0, and its collection proof lists both binaries (per test-plan §3 `status` classify pattern; §4
  Conventions; §11 Mocking).

- (tests/security) The re-exec witness runs the REAL `set_var` path in fresh processes. With the lever absent, the
  child reports `applied` and a post-call value of `1`. With `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=0` preset, the child
  reports `preset_honoured` and the value is still `0` (never overwritten, never parsed). Each child's child-ran
  marker is asserted (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management; security-plan §Input
  Validation "CLI / env var inputs" row).

- (arch) The apply call is the first non-comment statement of `main()`, ahead of the tokio runtime build at
  `pulse-app/src/main.rs:285`. Its placement probe reads `last line 1` (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns →
  Module dependency direction; research.md §Conventions — the edition-2024 `set_var` precondition).

- (obs/security) `app.boot.render.posture` resolves to its own exact leaf whose field set equals
  `{posture, lever}` in both directions. `for_target("app")` stays `None`. The emit-site capture equals the leaf for
  all three postures, at WARN for `preset_honoured` only. No field carries the preset value or a path (per obs-plan
  §8 PII Scrubbing default-deny + §6 once-per-boot rows; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (arch/scope) The scope guard over the chunk base prints nothing. Only `main.rs`, `lib.rs` and `observability.rs`
  change among tracked files, and no dependency, toolchain, workflow, capability or `pulse-app/ui/**` file changes
  (per architecture §Occupied Resources: no port, procedure, capability identifier or feature).

- (tests/layouts) **GREEN leg, boot smoke on native Wayland:** on the dev host (NVIDIA GA102 · Hyprland ·
  WebKitGTK 2.52.6), with `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` unset in the launch env, the leg prints `ended=alive` across
  its 60 s window, together with `gdk_error71=0`, `posture=applied`, `errors=0`, `panics=0` and `ports_after=0`.
  This is RED→GREEN against the P3 RED arms A1–A3 at base `ffb62f0` (3/3 `ended=died` at ~2.0 s, exit 1). The
  printed lines go in `evidence/render-posture-legs.md` (per test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate (conditional) + Direct-binary
  smoke variant; layout-templates §Primary screens — the P3 arms' 4/4 windows-navigated reading is the layout witness
  for the surviving posture).

- (tests) **PRESET leg, the discriminating control:** with `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=0` preset, the leg prints
  `ended=died`, `gdk_error71=1`, `posture=preset_honoured`, `panics=0` and `ports_after=0`. That proves the preset is
  honoured, and that this lever is the operative variable (per test-plan §3 Direct-binary smoke variant, RED/GREEN
  on separate fresh data dirs).

- (tests) Mutation checks (a)–(c) of Step 7 each turn their named pins RED, recorded in
  `evidence/mutation-checks.md` (per test-plan §11 — a pin must be shown to discriminate).

- (tests) The full standard gate set passes, and after the `--features mcp-server` regen
  `git diff --quiet ffb62f0823e6e4fe23f7ebb235e1d803a9fb23a1 -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` exits 0 (per
  test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

- (tests/a11y) CI is green on the pushed HEAD (`ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD` → `verdict: green`): the Linux `boot`
  job under xvfb boots with the default applied, and the `a11y` job is green on all three OSes with zero new
  violation tuples (per test-plan §9 Build failure conditions; a11y-plan §3 CI integration).

- (design) No doc, README or log text added by the chunk claims that the Halo State Pulse glow renders, and the
  posture record's labels name no glow layer (per design-system §Brand Identity Signature element).

- Spec anchors (from the extracts):
  - architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Module dependency direction · Config management; §Occupied Resources
    (Environment variables; `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS` GPU-posture precedent); §Project Intent.
  - security-plan §Threat Model Summary (CLI input); §Input Validation ("CLI / env var inputs"); §Security
    Anti-Patterns → Logging · Code Patterns · Universal.
  - obs-plan §3 Tracing init; §6 Log Coverage; §7 Error Capture & Reporting (Process-end cause); §8 PII Scrubbing.
  - test-plan §3 (Per-chunk gate discipline, Boot-smoke gate, Direct-binary smoke variant, Process-end witness
    form); §4 Conventions; §9; §11.
  - design-system §Brand Identity; §Surface: desktop-webview → Platform-Specific Notes (Linux).

| E | `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES=/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/50_mesa.json` | alive → TERM | 143 | 60.7 s | `MESA-EGL: warning: egl: failed to create dri2 screen` | 1 | 4/4 | `no_navigator_gpu` ×2 |
In every arm the OTLP ports bound before the end (`ports_seen_up=1`), 0 `app.panic.fatal`, 0 ERROR records.
**What the measurement establishes (and its limits):**
- The default-posture death REPRODUCES deterministically on this host: 3/3 at ~2.0 s, exit 1 (n = 3; the 2026-10-02 round's n = 1 is now n = 4 with it).

- Four single-variable levers each prevent it (n = 1 each). Their common factor is that each removes NVIDIA's EGL explicit-sync path on a native Wayland surface: no DMA-BUF EGL surface (B), implicit sync (C), no Wayland surface at all (D), no NVIDIA EGL (E). **So `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` is a LEVER, not the cause**; the cause is consistent with NVIDIA's EGL explicit-sync path (egl-wayland2) under WebKitGTK 2.52 on native Wayland, which matches the Linger#135 account on this exact driver and WebKitGTK version. The protocol violation is raised by the compositor; which protocol message violates the rule was NOT captured (no `WAYLAND_DEBUG` arm) — stated as unmeasured.
- D and E stay ALIVE on a DEGRADED render path (GBM buffer allocation failures; Mesa cannot drive the NVIDIA device), so they are measurement controls, never remedies.

- WebGPU is absent (`no_navigator_gpu`) under B, C, D and E alike, so no lever costs WebGPU here; WebKitGTK 2.52 exposes no `navigator.gpu` on this host. The default arms died before any adapter record, so the default posture's own adapter outcome is unrecorded.

- Measured on ONE host. Exposure on other NVIDIA + Wayland hosts (other compositors, egl-wayland without egl-wayland2, older WebKitGTK) is UNMEASURED; no confining mechanism beyond the four-lever pattern is identified.

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (270–330, 1100–1130, 1560–1576) — `main()` builds the multi-thread tokio runtime at `:285` (worker threads spawn at `build()`), enters it, then `resolve_data_dir` `:292`, `observability::init` + `hold_log_guard` `:293`, `install_exit_hook` `:294` (spawns `pulse-exit-reporter`), signal listener `:296`, `window::emit_boot_spans` `:299`; `tauri::Builder::default()` `:1112`; `run_return` `:1574`.

- `pulse-app/src/window.rs` (40–102) — `emit_boot_spans` emits `app.boot.webview.init {webview_backend}` (compile-target label `GTKWebKit` on Linux), `app.boot.gpu.check {wgpu_backend}`, `app.boot.tray.init {tray_api}`.
- `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` (1–40) — the `pub mod` list a new module joins.

- `crates/interpretation/src/hardware.rs` (128–162) — `detect_gpu_present` Linux arm probes only `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so` and `/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so`; on this Arch host libcuda is `/usr/lib/libcuda.so`, so the L4 probe reads GPU-absent here (side finding, outside this chunk).
- `/usr/lib/libgdk-3.so.0` (gtk3 3.24.52, disassembled) — see Patterns detected.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` (23–130) — `boot` captures the app's stdout+stderr to `$DATA_DIR/logs/boot.log` (`:79`), so the Gdk line lands there under the harness.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`:444` comment, apt `xvfb` rows) — the Linux `boot` job runs under one `xvfb-run` (X11), so CI never takes the native-Wayland path.

- `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp/evidence/round-result.md:43-51` and Conductor `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-03-p-075-re-round-on-incident-events/evidence/round-ledger.md:30-34,133` at Conductor `f5076ad` — the same single launch (pid 590369), now superseded by the 7-arm measurement above.

title: Graph impact (rust plane built this phase: 8613 nodes / 41898 edges, 72 s)

data.head: ## Graph impact (rust plane built this phase: 8613 nodes / 41898 edges, 72 s)

body: - **emit_boot_spans** — 1 caller: `main()` @ `pulse-app/src/main.rs:299` — the boot-record emit site a posture record sits beside.

- **observability::init** — callers `main()` @ `pulse-app/src/main.rs:293` plus three tests (`pulse-app/tests/e2e_p003_panic_hook_propagation.rs:51`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs:57`, `pulse-app/tests/perf_budget_samples.rs:115`) — unchanged signature; no threading.
- **install_exit_hook** — `main()` @ `pulse-app/src/main.rs:294` + 4 re-exec tests in `pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs` — unchanged.
- **detect_webview_backend** — `emit_boot_spans` @ `pulse-app/src/window.rs:89` + `pulse-app/tests/unit_window_shell.rs:14,38` — unchanged.

- The change is ADDITIVE: one new call at the head of `main()` and one emit after `observability::init`; no existing signature changes, so there is no caller set to thread. Trace: `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T09-36-17Z-phase/tree-query-2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland.json`.

- **GDK `_exit(1)` on a Wayland dispatch error** (`libgdk-3.so.0` `_gdk_wayland_display_queue_events`, offsets `0x5a42b`–`0x5a48e`): `wl_display_dispatch_pending` < 0 → `errno` → `g_log_structured_standard` with the format `Error %d (%s) dispatching to Wayland display.` → `mov $0x1,%edi; call _exit`. errno 71 = EPROTO (the compositor sent a fatal protocol error). This is why the death leaves no `app.exit`: `_exit` runs no `atexit` handler, matching obs-plan §7's stated unloggable set. The scope's mechanism hypothesis is VERIFIED.

- **Nothing sets these levers today**: `grep -rn -E 'set_var|WEBKIT_|GDK_BACKEND|__NV_|DMABUF' pulse-app/src crates/*/src` → 0 production hits (every `set_var` hit is inside a test module); the registry sources `wry-0.55.0`, `tao-0.35.0`, `tauri-2.11.0`, `tauri-runtime-wry` → 0 hits for `WEBKIT_DISABLE|__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC|GDK_BACKEND`.

- **Env-layer boot posture shape** (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`): trimmed read, a closed outcome, announced once per boot, never a panic — the shape a launch posture copies (arch-history 2026-08-16, 2026-08-26).
- **Deferred emit**: a decision taken before the sink exists must be carried as a value and emitted after `observability::init` (no `tracing` subscriber exists at the head of `main()`).

- **Edition-2024 `set_var` precondition**: `std::env::set_var` is `unsafe`; its precondition (no other thread reads/writes the environment concurrently) holds ONLY before `tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().build()` at `pulse-app/src/main.rs:285`. The lever write must be the first statement of `main()`, not merely before `observability::init`. A `// SAFETY:` comment names that ordering.

- **Child inheritance**: WebKitGTK renders in child processes (`WebKitWebProcess`, `WebKitNetworkProcess` — seen as `pulse-app` children in Conductor's ledger :124); a parent `setenv` before they spawn reaches them through the inherited environment. Whether an in-process `set_var` (vs a shell-exported variable, which arms B/C used) reaches NVIDIA's EGL at load time is the equality the GREEN leg must measure — not assumed.

- **Pure decision function, injected inputs** (test-plan §3 `classify` pattern; testing.md §11 Mocking): the posture choice takes the preset value and the OS as parameters; tests never mutate process env.
- **pulse-app tests live in `pulse-app/tests/*.rs`** (`[lib] test = false`; the dead-lib-src ratchet is a flat zero for lib sources, `main.rs` exempt) and the new lib module carries no `#[test]`.

- **Allowlist**: a new `app.boot.*` target needs its own EXACT leaf (no bare `app` key exists — `grep -A1 'by_target.insert(' pulse-app/src/observability.rs` lists 15 `app.*` keys, none bare), guarded in `pulse-app/tests/` by exact-resolve + two-way field-set equality + a fallback discriminator.
- **ASCII-only sources** (`cargo xtask check:english-sources`).
- `pulse-app/src/render_posture.rs` — the Linux launch-posture decision (pure fn over the preset value + OS) and the head-of-`main()` apply step returning the decision for the deferred emit.
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_render_posture.rs` — the decision pinned per arm with injected inputs.
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_render_posture.rs` — the posture record's exact-leaf guard.
- `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod render_posture;`
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — apply the posture as the first statement of `main()`; emit the posture record after `observability::init`.
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — the posture record's exact allowlist leaf in `AllowList::production()`.

- Which remedy shape ships (founder ruling: a default, detect and fall back, or document) and which lever (`__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` vs `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`) → blocks: plan-decision (P4 fork; the file lists above hold for the two in-process shapes — a "document"-only outcome drops all six and has no README to land in, since none exists at the repo root).

- Does an in-process `set_var` at the head of `main()` reach NVIDIA's EGL in the UI process and the WebKit children the same way the shell-exported variable did in arms B/C? → blocks: implementation-scope (the GREEN leg on the operator slot measures it; a NO falls back to the documented shape).

title: Scope — Linux launch stays up on NVIDIA + Wayland

data.head: # Scope — Linux launch stays up on NVIDIA + Wayland

body: **Marker:** `2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland` · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Taken up:** 2026-10-04

Linux launch stays up on NVIDIA + Wayland — the default Linux launch survives on an NVIDIA GPU under a Wayland
compositor.

Two halves, in order, per the founder ruling 2026-10-04 ("measure the cause first, then ship a default, detect and
fall back, or document"):

1. **Measure the cause.** On the dev host (NVIDIA GA102 / RTX 3090 · Hyprland · WebKitGTK 2.52.6 · native Wayland),
   establish by real-display launches whether the Gdk `Error 71 (Protocol error) dispatching to Wayland display`
   death at the default posture REPRODUCES, how reliably, and which lever(s) prevent it — enough to say whether the
   DMA-BUF renderer is the CAUSE or only a LEVER that hides another one. The measurement is the chunk's first
   deliverable and its result decides half 2.

2. **Ship the remedy the measurement supports** — exactly one of the ruling's three shapes:
   - **a default** — the Linux launch sets the measured lever before GTK/WebKit initialise, on every Linux host;
   - **detect and fall back** — the lever is applied only where the measured trigger condition holds (e.g. an NVIDIA
     driver under a Wayland session). The detection signal is still unchosen: it is the P4 fork, decided from the
     measurement in research.md (fixed-literal candidates seen on this host: `/sys/module/nvidia`,
     `/proc/driver/nvidia`; session: `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`XDG_SESSION_TYPE`);
   - **document** — if no in-process remedy is sound, the limitation and the workaround are stated where a Linux user
     meets them.
   Which shape ships is a P4 fork, decided from the half-1 result, never from the hypothesis.
- Linux only. macOS and Windows launch paths are unchanged.

- A value the user (or a harness) has ALREADY set for the lever's env var is honoured, never overwritten — verified as
  a consequence of arch §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management (process env outranks built-in defaults).

- No port, TauRPC procedure, capability JSON or corpus change — verified: the change is additive (one call at the head
  of `main()`, one emit after `observability::init`; research.md §Graph impact). If the remedy is a product env
  read/write, it is a new entry in arch §Occupied Resources (env vars) — a wrap amendment, not a phase edit.

- Not in scope: the Halo glow layer, WebGPU frame budgets, and any non-NVIDIA or X11-session failure (none has been
  observed). A measurement that turns one up is recorded and routed, not absorbed.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-04-retry-storm-interpretation-names-its-cause · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-04T14:05:00Z
- **Chunk base:** `e71dba539a7d0379d960b49b37b2cf3538de6ec2`

- **Founder rulings (live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer):** Q1 — ship the deterministic cause in this
  chunk; the prompt framing becomes its own WHAT-only route entry, measured on the restored model. Q2 — the cause
  lands in the TITLE, written at the producer as `{Cause label}: {model title}` with an ASCII separator; existing
  rows stay unprefixed.

Half 1, the measurement, is complete (research.md §Half 1). On the Conductor d3 series the retry fact reached the
model: the Tier1 digest carried `[autonomous] retry_storm — retry_storm scope_id=…` and the prompt embedded it
verbatim. It was lost at the model, which most likely restated an older, active error-rate-spike incident that the
digest's CORPUS MATCHES put in front of it. That last step is inferred from the Timeline's line shape and the
timestamps, not measured; the real model is absent from this host. What IS a measured product fact at HEAD: the
incident and its report carry NO deterministic field that names the cause. Title, Symptom, Timeline and Hypotheses
are all model-authored, and `incident.kind` is rendered nowhere (`markdown.rs:115-329`).

Half 2 closes that structural gap, per the founder's Q1/Q2 rulings. When the L4 producer writes an incident or its
interpretation, the title becomes `{Cause label}: {model title}`, where the label is a closed, ASCII,
human-readable name for the incident's cue kind (`Retry storm` for `CueKind::RetryStorm`). The same grounded title
goes into the persisted L4 JSON at all three write paths: creation, dedupe refresh and resolution final write. The
report header, the Findings rows, the MCP list / `retrieve_report` and the digest's corpus-match lines all read one
of those two fields, so an incident born of a retry storm names the retry everywhere, whatever the model wrote.
Incident identity, the prompt, the report projection and every type and binding are unchanged (arch §Established
Decisions [Fault Identity]; arch §Occupied Resources; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

**Not moved by this chunk, recorded per the founder:** Conductor's v3-09 grades the rank-1 model HYPOTHESIS
statement (Conductor `…/2026-10-01-interpretation-re-proven-after-the-incident-surfacing-fix/report.md:162-167`). A
deterministic title does not change that statement, and no step here fabricates a hypothesis. The model-side remedy
is the new route entry (Implementation notes).

1. **The cause label — `crates/triage/src/contract.rs`.** Add `pub fn cue_cause_label(kind: CueKind) -> &'static str`
   beside `CueKind` (`contract.rs:184-197`). It is an exhaustive `match`, so a future variant fails to compile until
   labelled. Labels, ASCII only: `ErrorRateSpike` → `Error-rate spike` · `LatencyRegression` → `Latency regression` ·
   `RestartEvent` → `Restart event` · `ServiceWentSilent` → `Service went silent` · `RetryStorm` → `Retry storm` ·
   `ReflectionTrend` → `Reflection trend`. It lives in `contract` because cross-crate exposure is through the
   contract module only (arch §Conventions; the existing `cue_kind_label` is snake_case for tracing and is not
   re-exported, `contract.rs:39-52`).

2. **Pin the label — `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` `mod tests` (`:663`).** Add
   `cause_label_names_retry_only_for_retry_storm`. Over all six variants it asserts: the label is non-empty and ASCII,
   and its lowercase form contains `retry` IF AND ONLY IF the kind is `RetryStorm`. Each variant is listed through
   an exhaustive match helper, so a new variant cannot be skipped.

3. **The grounding helpers — `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs`.** Add `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn
   grounded_title(kind: CueKind, model_title: &str) -> String`, returning `format!("{}: {}", cue_cause_label(kind),
   model_title)`. Add a private `fn grounded_output(parsed: &L4Output, kind: CueKind) -> L4Output`: a clone of
   `parsed` with `title` replaced by `grounded_title(kind, &parsed.title)`, every other field untouched. Grounding
   happens BEFORE scrubbing. The label is a closed ASCII literal that no P-047 arm matches, so the scrub still masks
   only the model's words.

4. **Ground at creation and on dedupe refresh — `create_incident_from_l4_output` (`inference_runtime.rs:763-930`).**
   Once `kind` is derived (`:792-804`), build `let grounded = grounded_output(parsed, kind);` and use it for:
   - the dedupe refresh, `scrubbed_l4_json(&grounded)` in place of `scrubbed_l4_json(parsed)` at `:844`;
   - the new incident's `title: scrub_text(&grounded.title)` at `:883`;
   - `resolution_summary_text: scrubbed_l4_json(&grounded)` at `:906`.
   `detail` (the symptom), the skip predicate, identity, severity, the evidence union and every obs emit stay
   byte-identical. A deduped incident's `title` is not rewritten. It keeps the grounded title from its creation, as
   it keeps its model title today.

5. **Ground the resolution final write — `attach_resolution_summary_to_incident` (`inference_runtime.rs:624-654`).**
   After the id parse, read the incident's kind with `registry.get(id)`, returning early on `None` exactly as the
   later `attach_resolution_summary` error would. Serialize `scrubbed_l4_json(&grounded_output(parsed, kind))`
   instead of `scrubbed_l4_json(parsed)`. A Resolved incident's report then keeps the cause in its header.

6. **Move the two pins that assert the old contract — `pulse-app/tests/unit_incident_producer.rs`.** Strengthen
   them to the grounded truth; never relax them. At `:456-459` the surviving coalesced title becomes
   `"Retry storm: storm A"` (the test's cue is `RetryStorm`, `:410-421`). At `:695-698` the masked title becomes
   `"Error-rate spike: error referencing [redacted: email] in title"` (cue `ErrorRateSpike`, `:671`).

7. **New producer pins — `pulse-app/tests/unit_incident_producer.rs`.** Each name carries `names_its_cause` so the
   targeted entry selects them, and each reuses the file's `fresh()` / `digest_with_cue` / `l4_output` helpers:
   - `incident_title_names_its_cause_for_a_retry_storm` — a `RetryStorm` cue with a model title that never says
     "retry" (`Error Rate Spike in ws`). The persisted and registry `title` are both `Retry storm: Error Rate Spike in
     ws`, and the `title` parsed back from `resolution_summary_text` is the same string.
   - `incident_title_names_its_cause_without_retry_for_an_error_rate_spike` — an `ErrorRateSpike` cue: the title is
     `Error-rate spike: …` and its lowercase form does NOT contain `retry`. This is the discriminating half, so a
     constant prefix cannot pass.
   - `incident_title_names_its_cause_on_dedupe_refresh` — a second generation on the same identity. The refreshed
     JSON title is the grounded SECOND model title, and the incident's own `title` keeps the first.
   - `incident_title_names_its_cause_in_the_resolution_summary` — `attach_resolution_summary_to_incident` on a
     `RetryStorm` incident: the attached JSON's title is `Retry storm: {resolution title}`.
   - `incident_title_names_its_cause_for_a_reflection_digest` — a Reflection digest: `Reflection trend: …`.
   - `incident_title_names_its_cause_and_still_masks_secrets` — a model title carrying a keyed canary
     (`password=hunter2`) AND a bare canary (an `sk_live_` token over the arm's length floor). Both are absent from
     the persisted title and the JSON, and the title still begins `Retry storm: ` (security-plan §Security
     Anti-Patterns → Logging, the both-classes canary rule).

8. **Report pins over the real projection — `pulse-app/tests/integration_interpretation_attach.rs`.** Each name
   carries `names_its_cause` and runs the real producer, then `assemble_report` + `serialize_report`, the single
   projection behind both TauRPC `get_report` (`incidents_router.rs:479`) and MCP `retrieve_report`
   (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:390`):
   - `report_names_its_cause_for_a_retry_storm_incident` — the markdown's first line is
     `# Diagnostic Report: Retry storm: {model title}`. An `ErrorRateSpike` incident's first line does NOT contain
     `retry` (lowercase).
   - `report_names_its_cause_under_the_deterministic_runner` — the same pair, driven by
     `pulse_app::deterministic_inference::CANNED_L4_OUTPUT_JSON` parsed as the model output. It asserts the FIRST
     LINE only. The canned rank-1 hypothesis says "retry storm" for every incident (`deterministic_inference.rs:48`),
     so a whole-document check would pass vacuously (research.md, the deterministic-path trap).

9. **Measure first, then mutate (one-shot, at /implement, recorded in `evidence/mutation-checks.md`).** Write the
   Step 7-8 pins and run them against the untouched producer: they must go RED (the title equals the bare model
   title). Land Steps 1-5 and they turn GREEN. Then revert Step 4's `title:` line alone to
   `scrub_text(&parsed.title)`: the creation pins (Step 7 first, second and sixth bullets, plus Step 6's two pins)
   must go RED while the dedupe and resolution pins stay green. Restore, and record both readings.
- none
- `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` — `cue_cause_label` + its exhaustive pin (Steps 1-2).
- `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` — `grounded_title` / `grounded_output` and the three grounded write paths (Steps 3-5).
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_incident_producer.rs` — two strengthened pins + six new producer pins (Steps 6-7).
- `pulse-app/tests/integration_interpretation_attach.rs` — two report pins over the real projection (Step 8).

research.md's other listed files — `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs`, `prompt.rs`, `schema.rs` and
`pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_incident_tools.rs` — belonged to the branches the founder did not choose. They stay
untouched, and the scope-guard entry asserts it.

Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact): `create_incident_from_l4_output` @ `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:266`
is its only production caller, and its test callers live in 8 `pulse-app/tests/` files. A title-only change moves
exactly the two pins in Step 6: a grep of `\.title` across those 8 files shows no other title assertion
(`unit_incident_producer.rs:457,691-701` hold them all; the others only set fixture titles). `assemble_report` @
`incidents_router.rs:479` and `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:390` is unchanged and reads the grounded JSON.

The standard gate set runs in the test-plan §3 order. capability-drift runs before the default-features workspace
nextest. Then come the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen and the base-identity bindings close, since no
procedure is added. The chunk's own gates come first, all under `--workspace` (the test-plan §11 run-scope rule):
- the collection proof for the new pins;
- the targeted pin run;
- the two touched test binaries plus the `triage` package, as the regression run;
- the scope guard and the print-site census.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the webview gates are absent. The Findings title span already ellipsizes
  (`FindingsWindow.tsx:77-83`), so a longer title needs no render change.

- No boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `observability.rs`, `crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `tauri.conf.json`,
  `capabilities/*.json`; the scope guard proves it), so the boot smoke does not bind (test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate).

- There is no harness live leg and no self-verify. Every remedy branch is proven in-process, including the
  deterministic-runner report pin.

- No dependency is added, so `cargo deny` / `cargo audit` are not listed locally. The CI `supply-chain` job runs
  them, and the operator CI read asserts it green.

- No real-model entry: the model is absent from this host, and a real-model generation is never a gate (test-plan
  §1 `l4-decision-probe-arg-parse-unit-coverage`).

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot evaluate on this Linux host, because it drives every stage through `wsl.exe`
(`xtask/src/pre_push.rs`). Under the founder deviation of 2026-10-04, its six stages run NATIVELY by hand before the
push, as in the three predecessor chunks. They are the six `operator` entries after hygiene, each in the stage
isolation of `Linux::cmd`. Stage 3 takes a fresh per-invocation `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` under `target/pre-push/`, and
stage 6 a per-invocation data dir, with no `rm` (founder rulings 2026-10-04). Stage 5 re-emits the no-mcp bindings,
so the regen and the base-identity close are RE-FIRED as `operator` entries after stage 6 and before the push.

ONE-SHOT controls at /implement, never listed, because they mutate source and revert: Step 9's red-before-green run
and its mutation check, both written to `evidence/mutation-checks.md`, which the second criterion names. The listed,
non-mutating `names_its_cause` entry guards the property on every re-run.

The CI read waits 2400 s, matching the predecessor's measured wall-clocks (≤ 1718 s at `a69030a`); its timeout is
2400 + 180.

- (tests) The half-1 measurement is recorded in research.md §Half 1: the digest and prompt layers are VERIFIED to
  carry the retry, the render layer is VERIFIED to carry no deterministic cause, and the model layer is stated as an
  inference (not a measurement) with its basis. The verdict keys on content (the digest line, the prompt text, the
  report fields), never on log cleanliness (per test-plan §3 Direct-binary smoke variant; §2 Agent-runnable
  invariants).

- (tests) The Step 9 red-before-green and mutation readings are recorded in `evidence/mutation-checks.md`. The new
  pins go red on the untouched producer and green after Steps 1-5. Reverting Step 4's `title:` line reddens the
  creation pins while the dedupe and resolution pins stay green (per test-plan §4 Conventions; §1, the one-time-proof
  class).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci -E 'test(/names_its_cause|cause_label_names_retry/)'` returns
  0, after the collection-proof entry lists the four named pins (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

- (arch) For a `RetryStorm`-triggered incident, the persisted `Incident.title` and the `title` inside
  `resolution_summary_text` both read `Retry storm: {model title}`, at creation, on dedupe refresh (JSON) and in the
  resolution summary. For an `ErrorRateSpike`-triggered incident neither contains `retry`
  (`incident_title_names_its_cause_*`; per architecture §Established Decisions [Fault Identity] — identity
  unchanged, only the interpretation text).

- (arch) The rendered report's first line names the cause through the unchanged single projection (`assemble_report`
  → TauRPC `get_report` and MCP `retrieve_report`), under both a model-shaped output and the deterministic runner's
  canned output (`report_names_its_cause_*`; per architecture §Standard Contracts MCP server, §Occupied Resources
  `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`).

- (arch) The incident identity tuple and the coalesce predicate are unchanged. The two coalesce pins at
  `unit_incident_producer.rs:405-470` still hold one incident (per architecture §Established Decisions [Fault
  Identity]).

- (security) A model title carrying a keyed canary (`password=…`) and a bare canary (`sk_live_…`) is masked in the
  persisted title and in the JSON, and the `Retry storm: ` prefix survives intact
  (`incident_title_names_its_cause_and_still_masks_secrets`; per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (security) No TauRPC procedure, MCP tool or capability is added. `cargo xtask capability-drift` is clean,
  `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` is unchanged, and the bindings close exits 0 (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary).

- (obs) No emit site changes. The print-site census reads 0 added `tracing::` / print lines, and the
  `interpretation.incident.created` / `.skipped` leaves are byte-unchanged (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing
  default-deny).

- (layouts) No surface, section, focusable element or render file changes, and the report keeps its six sections
  (the scope guard excludes `pulse-app/ui/**` and `markdown.rs`; per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-webview →
  §Primary screens).

- (tests) The standard gate set passes in its stated order, and the bindings close
  `git diff --quiet e71dba539a7d0379d960b49b37b2cf3538de6ec2 -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` exits 0 (per
  test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

- (tests) The operator CI read `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 2400` reads `verdict: green`, and its run id is
  named in the report (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

- No verification-matrix capability is claimed: `matrix.py show --unclaimed` reads `unclaimed 0 of 22`, and this
  chunk advances none to `verified`.

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [Fault Identity] · [LLM Inference Runtime] · §Occupied
  Resources (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`) · §Conventions (module visibility) · §Standard Contracts (MCP
  server); security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging · §Input Validation (L4 argv prompt) · §Threat Model
  Summary; obs-plan §8 · §11 Logs; test-plan §3 · §4 · §1 (one-time-proof class); layout-templates §Primary screens;
  design-system §Typography (not engaged: no render change); a11y-plan §1 / §3 (conditional, not engaged: no render
  change).

- Research files inspected: `crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs`, `crates/triage/src/digest/retrieval.rs`,
  `crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs`, `crates/interpretation/src/schema.json`,
  `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs`, `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs`, `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs`,

  three-path scrub), `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction` (per-leaf masking keeps the prefix), `2026-08-17-incident-fingerprint-producer-repaired`
  (the cue → producer threading precedent), `2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing` (the predecessor series),
  `2026-08-22-pii-scrubber-recall` / `2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels` (the both-classes canary).

- A prompt change (naming the triggering cue, framing corpus matches as past/other incidents) — rejected for THIS
  chunk by the founder (Q1). It cannot be proven without the real model, and it becomes its own route entry.

- Render-time prefixing (in `assemble_report`, the list projections or the corpus-match line) — rejected by the
  founder (Q2). Existing rows stay unprefixed, and `markdown.rs` is untouched.

- A new `Report` field or "Cause" line — rejected (Q2). It would change the TauRPC payload type, the bindings and
  the webview.

- Prefixing only `Incident.title` without the persisted JSON — rejected. The report header renders the L4 JSON's
  `title` (`markdown.rs:262`), so the cause would show in the Findings rows but not the report.

- Skipping the prefix when the model title already says "retry" — rejected. It is a heuristic over model text, and
  the deterministic shape is the point.

- Fabricating a cause hypothesis or editing the model's ranked hypotheses — rejected. That would be untrue to the
  model output; Conductor's v3-09 is not moved by this chunk (Goal).
- Re-keying incident identity on the cue kind or fingerprint — banned (arch §Established Decisions [Fault Identity]).

- Rewriting existing corpus rows to add the prefix — rejected (Q2: existing rows stay unprefixed). No migration
  either way.

- **Route note (wrap, founder Q1, 2026-10-04):** route-resolve mints a NEW WHAT-only working-route entry for the
  prompt framing. Its substance: an incident's interpretation treats corpus matches as past or other incidents and
  names the triggering cue, measured on the restored real model. It is placed AFTER "The L4 hardware probe finds
  CUDA on Arch-layout hosts" and AHEAD of "The declared Rust floor matches the code". Its measurement rides the dev
  probe `pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe.rs`, which records bounded labels only and would need a bounded
  `names_trigger`-style label (no title text). Its premise is research.md's inferred model-layer mechanism; it is
  not a measured one.

- **Recorded per the founder:** Conductor v3-09 grades the rank-1 model hypothesis, which this chunk does not move.
  The chunk report states this in its Outcome.

- **Cross-repo note:** Conductor's static fixture `conductor/crates/conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs:77`
  pins `"title":"Deterministic verification incident"`. It is a literal JSON string, unaffected by this repo, but a
  LIVE deterministic harvest against this build reads `{Cause label}: Deterministic verification incident`. This is
  relayed to the overseer at the wrap; Pulse edits nothing in Conductor.

- **Prompt-size effect, stated as a prediction:** new titles grow by at most 21 bytes (`Service went silent: `, the
  longest label + separator). They reach the prompt through at most `DIGEST_CORPUS_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT` = 5 corpus lines
  (`assembler.rs:687-692`), so at most +105 bytes against the 16 384-byte `MAX_PROMPT_BYTES`, with ~9.2 KiB headroom
  (security-plan §Input Validation, L4 argv row; the 6 932 B maximum measured at
  `2026-08-27-idle-observer-generation-damper`). No re-measure is owed. The labels are ASCII, so the argv-transport
  rule holds.

- **Side effect, stated not claimed:** corpus-match lines for new incidents now carry the cause label (for example
  `Error-rate spike: Error Rate Spike in X — 3m ago, active`), which may make a differently-kinded match easier for
  the model to tell apart. That effect is unmeasured, and it belongs to the new route entry's measurement.

- **Deterministic-runner oddity, recorded not fixed:** the canned rank-1 hypothesis says "retry storm" for every
  incident (`deterministic_inference.rs:48`). Step 8 pins only the first line for that reason.
- **The boot-smoke WATCH** (scope) is observation only: the operator CI read records it, with no criterion attached.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Occupied Resources (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` entry) — the
  incident title and the persisted L4 JSON title are cue-grounded `{Cause label}: {model title}` at the producer in
  every mode, so a deterministic storm incident reads `Retry storm: Deterministic verification incident`.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Established Decisions [Fault Identity] — note beside the producer
  threading that the cue KIND, not only its fingerprint, now reaches the incident text (title), while identity is
  unchanged.

title: Half 1 — where the retry fact is lost (the measurement)

data.head: ## Half 1 — where the retry fact is lost (the measurement)

body:
The four candidate layers from scope.md, each closed against code at HEAD (`e71dba5`) and against the recorded d3
capture (Conductor `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-01-interpretation-re-proven-after-the-incident-surfacing-fix/evidence/rm-capture-d3.txt`, read-only):

1. **The digest CARRIES the retry — verified.** For a Tier1 digest triggered by a `RetryStorm` cue with
   `scope_id = S`, the assembler builds exactly one `DigestCueRef` from the triggering cue
   (`crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs:261-272`), and `render_payload` emits it under `ATTENTION CUES:` as the line
   `  [autonomous] retry_storm — retry_storm scope_id=S` (`assembler.rs:676-686`, kind label `:551-560`, summary
   `cue_summary` `:605-610`), plus `OVERALL: anomalous` (`:652-663`). The cue leaves the digest only when the token
   hard cap forces truncation (`:372-387`); the d3 prompt that fed incident 10 measured `token_count=6979`
   (capture line for `interpretation.prompt.assemble t=2026-10-01T20:04:53.604Z`), under the cap.

2. **The prompt presents it as one line among others — verified.** `build_primary_tier_prompt`
   (`crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs:182-256`) inserts the digest verbatim between `<DIGEST>` markers. Nothing in
   the role (`:85-91`, "severity classifier"), the conventions (`:96-103`) or the output reminder (`:108-112`) ties
   `title` / `symptom` / the rank-1 hypothesis to the triggering cue, and the schema's own descriptions are generic
   (`title`: "Short human-readable incident title"; `symptom`: "Observable behavior summary" —
   `crates/interpretation/src/schema.json`, read by `json.load` at HEAD). The prompt's `corpus_retrieval` argument is
   always `""` (`pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:420,426`); past incidents reach the model INSIDE the digest, as its
   `CORPUS MATCHES:` section (`assembler.rs:687-692`).

3. **The model is where it was lost — inferred from recorded evidence, strongly supported, NOT measured.**
   - The d3 report's Timeline reads `Error Rate Spike in <workspace-key>: 3m ago, active`. That is the shape of a
     digest CORPUS MATCHES line, `[{fingerprint}] {title} — {age}m ago, {outcome}`
     (`crates/triage/src/digest/retrieval.rs:136-148`), with the title and the age/outcome tail carried over.
   - Timestamps fit exactly one prior incident: incident 7 opened `1790884889849546600`, 203.75 s before incident 10
     (`1790885093604447300`) — "3m ago" — and is the only one the capture marks `seen_active=true`. Its open instant
     equals the 20:01:29.849Z `interpretation.prompt.assemble` of the Tier2 digest whose
     `digest.assemble.request` carried `cue_kind=error_rate_spike` (capture `:539`, `:557`), created at 20:01:33.908Z
     with `severity=error priority_tier=autonomous`. An error-rate-spike incident, active, 3 minutes older.
   - Why it could reach incident 10's digest but not its Previously Seen: the digest's selection keeps a candidate
     whose `scope_id` matches ANY current Q1 service (`assembler.rs:286-287`; `select_corpus_matches`
     `retrieval.rs`), while the report's Previously Seen keeps only the incident's OWN scope
     (`select_previously_seen`; incidents_router `get_report` `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs:460-468`). The d3
     report lists only #2 there — consistent with incident 7 sitting on a sibling scope.
   - So: the retry fact reached the model (layers 1-2), and the model's Title / Symptom / Timeline / rank-1 hypothesis
     restate a competing, differently-kinded active incident's title. **Incident 7's title is not in the capture, so
     "the model copied it" is a hypothesis fitted to text shape and timestamps, not a measurement.** Whether the model
     would name the retry WITHOUT that corpus line (the counterfactual) needs the real model — not measurable on this
     host (overseer note 2026-10-04: no GGUF, no llama-cli under `~`).

4. **The render has NO deterministic carrier of the cause — verified.** `assemble_report`
   (`crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs:249-329`) takes `title` / `symptom` / `timeline` / `hypotheses` from the
   parsed `L4Output` (all model-authored); without one, from `incident.title` / `incident.detail` — which the producer
   also set from the model (`inference_runtime.rs:883-884`). `incident.kind` (the cue kind, `RetryStorm` here, set from
   `digest.attention_cues.first()` at `inference_runtime.rs:794-800`) is rendered NOWHERE in the report
   (`serialize_report`, `markdown.rs:115-237`). The Findings rows show `incident.title` (`incidents_router.rs:60`;
   `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/FindingsWindow.tsx:236`, `FindingsDropdown.tsx:215`).

**Verdict for half 1:** the retry is not lost in the digest or the prompt's inputs; it is lost at the model, and the
product has no deterministic field that would carry it past a model that drops it. The second half is a product fact
at HEAD, independent of the model; the first half is inference over one recorded generation (n = 1 incident).

**A deterministic-path trap (load-bearing for P4):** the canned `L4Output` of the deterministic runner
(`pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs:43-53`) carries the rank-1 statement "Deterministic fixture hypothesis: the
retry storm originates in the synthetic verification scope." for EVERY incident, whatever its cue. Any check that a
deterministic-mode report "names the retry" passes vacuously — it must also show that a non-retry incident does NOT
name it.
- `crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs` (195-495, 545-715) — Tier1 digest = one triggering cue; ATTENTION CUES line shape; CORPUS MATCHES scope selection over all Q1 services; truncation order.
- `crates/triage/src/digest/retrieval.rs` (1-150) — `select_corpus_matches` (any current scope) vs `select_previously_seen` (own scope); `format_corpus_match_line` shape.
- `crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs` (1-270) — section order; role/conventions/reminder text; `corpus_retrieval` slot.
- `crates/interpretation/src/schema.json` (title/symptom/timeline/hypotheses descriptions) — generic field guidance.
- `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs` (80-330) — `Report` struct, `serialize_report`, `assemble_report` (single source for TauRPC + MCP, P-038).
- `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` (755-900) — identity from the first cue; `title`/`detail` from the model.
- `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs` (50-65, 440-480) — list title source; report assembly + Previously Seen.
- `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs` (43-53) — canned title / symptom / timeline / hypotheses.
- `crates/triage/src/cue/classify.rs` (45-75) — `cue_kind_label` exists (pub in `cue`) but is NOT re-exported through `triage::contract` (`contract.rs:39-52`).
- `crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs` (120-140) — cue `scope_id` per family (service name; operation name for latency).
- `pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe.rs` (1-40) — the dev-only real-model probe; it records bounded labels only and deliberately writes no title/symptom/hypothesis text.
- Conductor `…/evidence/rm-capture-d3.txt` (395-560) and `report.md` (155-175) — the d3 report body, incident table and the log window.

title: Scope — Retry-storm interpretation names its cause

data.head: # Scope — Retry-storm interpretation names its cause

body: **Marker:** `2026-10-04-retry-storm-interpretation-names-its-cause` · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Taken up:** 2026-10-04

Retry-storm interpretation names its cause — an incident born of a retry storm names the retry, not only an
error-rate spike.
Two halves, in order, per the founder ruling 2026-10-02 ("the fix follows the measurement"):

1. **Measure why.** Establish, from evidence this host can produce, why an incident whose triggering digest carried a
   `retry_storm` cue was interpreted as "Error Rate Spike" with no retry named (Conductor d3, 2026-10-01). The
   measurement must say WHERE the retry fact is lost, among these candidate layers (closed at P3 — research.md
   §Half 1):
   - **the digest** — VERIFIED it carries the retry: a Tier1 digest holds exactly the triggering cue, rendered as
     `[autonomous] retry_storm — retry_storm scope_id=S` under ATTENTION CUES, plus `OVERALL: anomalous`
     (`assembler.rs:261-272,652-686`). It ALSO carries CORPUS MATCHES selected on any current Q1 service scope, which
     can put a differently-kinded active incident's title in front of the model (`assembler.rs:286-287`).
   - **the prompt** — VERIFIED it presents the cue only as that one digest line: no role, convention, reminder or
     schema description ties `title` / `symptom` / the rank-1 hypothesis to the triggering cue (`prompt.rs:85-112`,
     `schema.json`).
   - **the model** — `[inferred]` (hypothesis, strongly supported, not measured): d3's Timeline
     `Error Rate Spike in <workspace-key>: 3m ago, active` has the corpus-match line shape
     (`retrieval.rs:144-147`), and only incident 7 (an active error_rate_spike incident opened 203.75 s earlier) fits;
     its title is not in the capture. The counterfactual needs the real model, absent on this host.
   - **the render** — VERIFIED it has no deterministic carrier: Title / Symptom / Timeline / Hypotheses are all
     model-authored, and `incident.kind` is rendered nowhere in the report (`markdown.rs:115-329`).
   The measurement is the chunk's first deliverable; its result decides half 2.

2. **Ship the remedy the measurement supports** — so an incident born of a retry storm names the retry. The shape
   (digest content, prompt framing, deterministic grounding of a field from the cue, or a combination) is a P4 fork
   decided from the half-1 result, never from a hypothesis.

- The incident's identity tuple `(kind, scope, scope_id)` is decided (arch §Established Decisions [Fault Identity])
  and is not reopened; this chunk concerns what the incident's interpretation SAYS, not how incidents coalesce
  (verified: identity comes from `digest.attention_cues.first()` at `inference_runtime.rs:794-800`, untouched by any
  remedy branch in research.md).

- No new port, TauRPC procedure, capability JSON, corpus table or MCP tool is expected (verified for the branches
  research found: a render-side change in `assemble_report` reaches TauRPC and MCP through the existing projection).
  A new `Report` FIELD would change the TauRPC payload type and the generated bindings — if a remedy needs one, it is
  surfaced at P4, not absorbed silently.

- Not in scope: the L4 hardware probe on Arch hosts (its own route entry, next), the real-model availability on this
  host (a founder desk act), and the Conductor-side grading (`v3-09` is Conductor's matrix entry, not Pulse's).
- A finding that some OTHER cue kind loses its cause the same way is recorded and routed, not absorbed.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-04-supply-chain-advisories-on-wasmtime-resolved · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-04T01:03Z
- **Chunk base:** `5988a5f80b7280081fdeb12d9eca16bfa32f4de9` (HEAD when this plan was written; every git-reading guard below names it)

Turn the CI `supply-chain` job green again by moving `wasmtime` off 48.0.3, the version RUSTSEC-2026-0325 /
-0326 / -0327 name, with no advisory ignore (founder ruling 2026-10-03 / 2026-10-04). The job went red on
`5988a5f` (`ci#37165927619`, job 111328669434) at its `rustsec/audit-check` step. That step runs first, so the
deny, Cranelift, npm and `cargo auditable` steps behind it were never measured on that sha.

The fix is a source fix in the form security-plan §Dependency Security → CI integration requires for a finding
with a stated safe upgrade. The workspace requirement moves to `"48.0.4"`, the advisories' first patched release
inside the current major, and the ordinary `cargo update -p wasmtime` moves the lockfile. A provenance entry is
added beside the pin in the `Cargo.toml` block. The plugin runtime decision (architecture §Established Decisions →
[Plugin Runtime]) is unchanged, and so is the sandbox posture (security-plan §API Security plugin-host row;
§Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection): Cranelift on x86_64, `epoch_interruption(true)`, the per-Store
`ResourceLimiter`. The toolchain stays at 1.95.0, which keeps 49.x out of reach (49.x needs rustc 1.96).
Research measured the whole bump in a scratch worktree of the chunk base (research.md §Measured):
- 35 lockfile packages move, all inside the wasmtime family, with none added or removed.
- `cargo audit` goes from exit 1 (the three ids) to exit 0.
- `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` stays green with warnings identical to HEAD.
- `cargo deny check advisories` goes from exit 1 to exit 0.
- The Cranelift assertion holds, and the plugins tests pass 61/61 against wasmtime 48.0.5 with no source change.
The chunk's outcome is the CI job reading green on this chunk's own commit, every step having run.

1. **Bump the requirement.** In `Cargo.toml:134`, change `wasmtime = { version = "48.0.3", features = ["component-model"] }` to `version = "48.0.4"`. The feature list `["component-model"]` stays exactly as it is: add no feature and no backend flag.

2. **Record the provenance.** In the comment block directly above the pin (`Cargo.toml:119-133`), append one entry after the existing "Moved to 48 for RUSTSEC-2026-0316 …" lines, in the same form. It names RUSTSEC-2026-0325 (mis-typed tag imports, GC heap corruption), RUSTSEC-2026-0326 (missing GC rooting across `try_call`) and RUSTSEC-2026-0327 (unvalidated async-lifted callback result count, native stack overflow). It also states the advisories' safe upgrade as printed (`>=48.0.4, <49.0.0` or `>=49.0.2`), that 49.x needs rustc 1.96 while the toolchain is pinned at 1.95, and that the lockfile resolves 48.0.5, which differs from 48.0.4 only by an artifact-publishing fix. The entry is plain ASCII: write the arrow as `->`, because `cargo xtask check:english-sources` gates every source annotation.

3. **Move the lockfile.** Run `cargo update -p wasmtime` (no `--precise`). The expected result is the measured delta (research.md §Measured; diff at `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T00-48-08Z-phase/research-bump.diff`): `wasmtime` 48.0.3 -> 48.0.5 plus 34 family packages, nothing added or removed. A delta that touches any package outside the family, or adds or removes one, is a STOP: report it, do not widen.

4. **Prove the gates** — the `## Test Commands` entries below, in order. No source file changes. If any entry needs a `crates/plugins` source edit to go green, that is a STOP and a scope report, not an in-chunk fix: research measured none needed.

5. **Record the evidence** in `chunks/2026-10-04-supply-chain-advisories-on-wasmtime-resolved/evidence/`:
   - `advisory-record.md` — the `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check advisories` readings before (chunk base) and after: the advisory DB's count and last commit, and the vulnerabilities as DISTINCT `RUSTSEC-` ids. The warnings go in the same form, written as "set identical to the prior enumeration" (or the differing ids), with no running ordinal (security-plan §Dependency Security → CI integration, the counting rules).
   - `lockfile-delta.md` — the 35-package delta from `git diff 5988a5f80b7280081fdeb12d9eca16bfa32f4de9 -- Cargo.lock`, by package and version.
- none (the evidence files under the chunk dir are records, not codebase files)
- `Cargo.toml` — the wasmtime requirement `"48.0.3"` -> `"48.0.4"` (`:134`) and one ASCII provenance entry in the block above it (`:119-133`)
- `Cargo.lock` — the wasmtime-family update `cargo update -p wasmtime` produces (35 packages, version and checksum lines only)

These are the gates for a dependency bump. The bump's own subject comes first: the resolution probe, the
advisory-DB currency control, `cargo audit`, the two `cargo deny` invocations kept separate (security rule
2026-08-17), the Cranelift assertion and the no-ignore and lockfile-family guards. Then the plugins regression net,
the standard test-plan §3 set in its order (capability-drift before the default-features workspace nextest; the
`--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step; the base-identity bindings close, since no
procedure is added), and the operator pass.
Absences, each with its reason:
- No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the webview gates are absent.

- No boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `observability.rs`, `crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `tauri.conf.json`, `capabilities/*.json`; the scope-guard entry proves it), so the boot smoke does not bind (test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate).
- There is no live leg and no self-verify (no UI change).

- `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` is not listed locally because `cargo auditable` is not installed on this host. The CI `supply-chain` job runs it, and the operator CI read asserts that job green.

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot evaluate on the Linux dev host, because it drives every stage through `wsl.exe`
(`xtask/src/pre_push.rs:23`). By founder ruling 2026-10-04 (given live at this plan's review), its six stages run
NATIVELY by hand before the push, recorded as the same deviation as 2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp
(`evidence/operator-pass.md`, Gate 18). They are the six `operator` entries after hygiene, in `Stage::ALL` order:
script-modes, source-lint, npm, clippy, test, ci-gates. Each runs in the stage isolation of `Linux::cmd`: `env -i`
with only HOME, a Linux PATH and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=target/pre-push/data`, the WSL form's own data path, which
is gitignored. The first failing stage stops the run and the push; the operator re-runs them before every fix push.
Two differences from the WSL form, as before: the stages run in the working tree rather than a synced clone, and
they share this host's `target/` and `~/.cache`. Porting the verb is the route entry "pre-push:linux runs natively
on Linux". The stage readings go into `evidence/operator-pass.md`.

`evidence/advisory-record.md` and `evidence/lockfile-delta.md`, which a criterion and Step 5 name, have no producing
entry by construction. /implement writes them from the recorded outputs of the `cargo audit`, `cargo deny check
advisories` and lockfile-guard entries above (and from the chunk base's readings in research.md §Measured). They are
records of listed gates, not runtime artifacts a leg emits.

The CI read waits 2400 s, against the last green run's wall-clock of 1718 s (`a69030a`, read at the predecessor's
Setup); its timeout is 2400 + 180.

title: Measured: the bump, end to end (scratch worktree of `5988a5f`, removed after; evidence in the phase run dir)

data.head: ## Measured: the bump, end to end (scratch worktree of `5988a5f`, removed after; evidence in the phase run dir)

body: - **Lockfile delta** — `Cargo.toml` requirement `"48.0.3"` → `"48.0.4"`, then `cargo update -p wasmtime`: 35 packages moved, every one inside the wasmtime family (`wasmtime` / `wasmtime-environ` / 14 `wasmtime-internal-*` / `pulley-*` 48.0.3 → 48.0.5; 13 `cranelift-*` 0.135.3 → 0.135.5; `wasm-compose` / `wasm-encoder` / `wasm-metadata` / `wasmparser` / `wasmprinter` / `wit-component` / `wit-parser` 0.254.0 → 0.254.2). No package added or removed. Cargo printed `wasmtime v48.0.3 -> v48.0.5 (available: v49.0.2, requires Rust 1.96.0)`. Diff: `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T00-48-08Z-phase/research-bump.diff` (522 lines, 70 `version` lines = 35 × 2 — re-derived: `grep -c '^[-+]version'`).

- **The caret resolves 48.0.5, not 48.0.4.** `version = "48.0.4"` is the requirement `^48.0.4`, and the ordinary update takes the newest compatible release, 48.0.5. Landing exactly 48.0.4 would need `cargo update -p wasmtime --precise 48.0.4`. Per the v48.0.5 release notes the two differ only in the release-artifact publishing fix; both carry the eight 48.0.4 security fixes. Decided at P4.

- **`cargo audit`** — at HEAD: exit 1, vulnerabilities `RUSTSEC-2026-0325 / -0326 / -0327`. On the bump: exit 0, vulnerabilities `[]`. Both against the same DB as CI (1290 advisories, last-commit `ef6173cb`, 2026-10-03T10:14:03+02:00). `CARGO_HOME` is unset here, so the gate's copy is `$HOME/.cargo/advisory-db`. Warnings unchanged on both: unmaintained `RUSTSEC-2024-0370 / -0436 · 2025-0075 / -0080 / -0081 / -0098 / -0100 / -0141`, unsound `RUSTSEC-2024-0429 · 2026-0221` (set identical to the CI run's printed list).

- **`cargo deny check bans licenses sources`** (cargo-deny 0.20.2 locally; CI's action builds 0.19.2) — exit 0 at HEAD and on the bump, `bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`. The warning lines are byte-identical between the two (`diff` empty; nine `warning[wildcard]` rows on workspace path deps), and no `unnecessary-skip` appears, so every wasmtime-family skip is still needed and none became stale.

- **`cargo deny check advisories`** — at HEAD: exit 1, three `error[vulnerability]` (the three wasmtime ids) plus ten `warning[advisory-not-detected]` (`RUSTSEC-2024-0411` … `-0420`). On the bump: exit 0, the same ten `advisory-not-detected` warnings and no error. Those ten stale ignore entries pre-exist this chunk, are identical on both sides, and are outside its subject (this observation is a note, not a scope item).
- **Cranelift assertion** — `cargo tree -p wasmtime | grep -q cranelift` exit 0 on the bump.

- **Plugins regression net** — `cargo nextest run -p plugins --profile ci` in the scratch worktree with its own target dir (no workspace build in it, so the `-p` run-scope trap does not apply): compiled `wasmtime v48.0.5` and `cranelift-codegen v0.135.5`, `61 tests run: 61 passed, 0 skipped`, no `warning:` / `error` line, 28 s wall. Log: `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T00-48-08Z-phase/research-plugins-nextest.txt`. No source change was needed.

- **npm gate** — `cargo xtask check:npm-supply-chain` at HEAD: exit 0, `"verdict": "green"` (883 licenses checked, 2 excepted, 0 violations). It sits behind the audit step in CI and so was unmeasured at `5988a5f`; locally it is green now.

- **Not measured here:** `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` (`cargo auditable` is not installed on this host: `cargo auditable --version` → `no such command`). The workspace release build under the bump is covered by the CI step only, unless implement installs the tool.

- For THESE inputs — the advisory DB at `ef6173cb` and a `Cargo.lock` resolving `wasmtime` ≥ 48.0.4 inside 48.x — `cargo audit` yields exit 0 with zero vulnerabilities, because each of the three advisories states patched `>=48.0.4, <49.0.0` (printed in the CI log's per-advisory table). Verified by measurement above, at the criterion's grain (the three named ids, not "an advisory"). The frame that decides it is the advisory's `patched` range, read from the CI run's own table and reproduced locally.
- none
- `Cargo.toml` — the wasmtime requirement `"48.0.3"` -> `"48.0.4"` and one provenance comment entry for RUSTSEC-2026-0325 / -0326 / -0327 (ASCII)
- `Cargo.lock` — the 35-package wasmtime-family update produced by `cargo update -p wasmtime`

- Exact resolution: lockfile at 48.0.5 (what the ordinary `cargo update -p wasmtime` yields under requirement `"48.0.4"`) vs. pinned to 48.0.4 with `--precise` → blocks: plan-decision (P4; the file list is the same either way).

title: Scope — Supply-chain advisories on wasmtime resolved

data.head: # Scope — Supply-chain advisories on wasmtime resolved

body: **Marker:** `2026-10-04-supply-chain-advisories-on-wasmtime-resolved` · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.3.0 · **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Polish & ship: verification
**Working entry (verbatim title + hint):** Supply-chain advisories on wasmtime resolved — the supply-chain gate is green again with no advisory ignore

- The `wasmtime` dependency moves off 48.0.3, the version RUSTSEC-2026-0325 / -0326 / -0327 name, to a patched release. The workspace pin is `wasmtime = { version = "48.0.3", features = ["component-model"] }` (`Cargo.toml:134`), consumed by `crates/plugins` (`wasmtime.workspace = true`, `crates/plugins/Cargo.toml:12`); `Cargo.lock:8543-8544` resolves `wasmtime` 48.0.3.

- The advisories' patched ranges, as the CI run printed them: `>=48.0.4, <49.0.0` OR `>=49.0.2`; unaffected `<47.0.0`. [premise-corrected: research.md §Measured — 48.0.5 also exists (same day, rust-version 1.95.0; per its release notes it differs from 48.0.4 only by an artifact-publishing fix), and requirement `"48.0.4"` resolves to 48.0.5 under the ordinary `cargo update -p wasmtime`] The requirement floor is 48.0.4, the first patched release inside the current major. Which release the lockfile lands on is a P4 decision: 48.0.5 by the ordinary update, or exactly 48.0.4 with `--precise`. 49.x is out of reach while the toolchain is pinned at `1.95.0` (`rust-toolchain.toml`), since 49.x needs 1.96 (stated by the entry and by the predecessor chunk's report).

- 48.0.4 and 48.0.5 are both published on crates.io (not yanked) with `rust_version` 1.95.0. The `wasmtime-*` / `cranelift-*` family moves in the same lockfile update: 35 packages, all inside the family, none added or removed. `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` stays green with warnings byte-identical to HEAD, and no skip becomes unnecessary (research.md §Measured).

- No source change in `crates/plugins` is needed: the plugins tests compile against wasmtime 48.0.5 / cranelift-codegen 0.135.5 and pass 61/61 with no warning (research.md §Measured). That covers `Engine` / `Config` with `epoch_interruption(true)`, Cranelift as default on x86_64, the Component Model linker and the per-Store `ResourceLimiter`.

- The `Cargo.toml` comment block above the pin (`:119-133`, the advisory-history provenance in the form the security rule requires for a source fix) gains the 48.0.3 → 48.0.4 bump with the three RUSTSEC ids and the advisory's stated solution.

- The outcome is the gate: `cargo audit` exits 0 (a plain pass/fail gate since chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable), `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` stays green, `cargo deny check advisories` names no `wasmtime` id, and the CI `supply-chain` job (audit + deny + auditable) reads green on this chunk's commits.

- **No advisory ignore** (founder ruling 2026-10-03 / 2026-10-04): no `[advisories] ignore` entry in `deny.toml`, no `--ignore` / `audit.toml` exception for the three ids. The security rule already forbids ignore-listing a finding that has a stated safe upgrade, and this one has one.
- The toolchain pin stays at `1.95.0`. Moving to wasmtime 49.x (and so to rustc 1.96) is out of scope.

- The wasmtime security posture holds unchanged: Cranelift stays enabled on x86_64 (no non-Cranelift feature flag), `epoch_interruption(true)` stays, the WIT capability scoping and the `ResourceLimiter` caps are untouched (`.claude/rules/security.md` §Plugin host + WASM sandbox).

- `multiple-versions = "deny"` is never relaxed and the `tonic` canary is never skipped. A new duplicate this bump introduces gets an ID-scoped, reasoned `[bans] skip` entry only if it cannot be fixed at the source.

- The other ten findings the CI audit printed as WARNINGS, not vulnerabilities (8 unmaintained, 2 unsound: RUSTSEC-2024-0370 / -0429 / -0436, 2025-0075 / -0080 / -0081 / -0098 / -0100 / -0141, 2026-0221) are not this chunk's subject. They did not fail the job (`Found 3 advisories, 8 unmaintained, 2 unsound` → `3 vulnerabilities found!` / `10 warnings found!`). The chunk leaves their dispositions as they are.
- No TauRPC procedure, port, capability JSON, corpus schema, webview or MCP change.

- **CONTEXT (verbatim, re-verified):** RUSTSEC-2026-0325 / -0326 / -0327 on `wasmtime` 48.0.3, published 2026-10-02, red the CI `supply-chain` job on S `4a26ad8` and S2 `cdb6c1e` with `Cargo.lock` unchanged since `a69030a` (measured at 2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp: `ci#37069724167`, `ci#37157540938`; its report's Decisions name 48.0.3 → 48.0.4 as the target; the toolchain is pinned at 1.95 and 49.x needs 1.96); founder ruling 2026-10-03 / 2026-10-04: its own chunk, placed right after that chunk, no advisory ignore.
  - Re-verified at HEAD: the pin and the lockfile read 48.0.3 (coordinates above); the toolchain reads `1.95.0`. The three ids and their patched range were re-read first-hand from the CI run of `5988a5f` (below), the commit after the two the CONTEXT names. The S / S2 run ids are carried as the CONTEXT states them; this scope did not re-open those two runs.
  - "49.x needs 1.96" is re-measured: crates.io lists `rust_version` 1.96.0 for 49.0.0, 49.0.1 and 49.0.2, and `cargo update` prints `available: v49.0.2, requires Rust 1.96.0` (research.md §Files inspected, §Measured). Arch's "49.0.1 needs Rust 1.96" is therefore also true, and 49.0.2, the first patched 49.x, needs the same.

The failing job's log (`gh api …/actions/jobs/111328669434/logs`, saved stripped at `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T00-48-08Z-phase/ci-supply-chain.log`) shows the job failed at the `rustsec/audit-check` step with `3 vulnerabilities found!`: RUSTSEC-2026-0325 / -0326 / -0327, all `wasmtime` 48.0.3, advisory DB 1290 advisories, last-commit `ef6173cb`, updated 2026-10-03. Reason: HttpError: Resource not accessible by integration` (with the action's own "executed from the forked repository" warning).
