asks for the cause to be named from evidence a run produced, closed, and for a run in which the app ends by itself
to say why in what the job keeps.

**Which of the two plans this is (inputs#I3): the second kind.** The early exit did not reproduce on this host: 0
self-ends in 51 boots across three arms (research.md, "The local reproduction"). No run has named a cause, so this
plan closes none and claims no capability. It delivers what makes the next run show its cause:

1. `boot` reports ready only after a TCP handshake on both resolved OTLP ports (the open gap of test-plan §3,
   5-command implementation, Readiness signal).

2. The smoke reads the app after its windows have settled, by the app's own record, instead of at whatever instant
   `status` runs. Every run then reads past the point where both reds ended, so equal source reads the same.

3. When the app ends by itself, the job says how it ended, whether it left an `app.exit` record, whether its
   display and its session bus were still reachable, and keeps what the display server itself printed.

A control on this host shows why the third item is the instrument to build: with the virtual display stopped, the
app ended `exit 1` with no `app.exit` record and nothing new in `boot.log`, 2 of 2, which are the reds' three facts
(research.md, the controls table). It is a control. Whether the runner's display goes away is what the first CI run
under this plan reads.

No product code changes. P-129 stays in the pool: with no named cause it is not claimed at this wrap whatever the
count of greens, the entry stays open, and the count of consecutive green runs goes on as runs come, to eleven
(inputs#I3).

1. **Write the pins first and read them red.** In the new module `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, the in-file tests
   for both verdicts (steps 2 and 3), one per arm; in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, the pins of step
   7. Run the two test targets and keep the red reading in `evidence/`.

2. **The readiness verdict, `cargo xtask harness:ready`.** A pure decision over three inputs: the existing status
   verdict (reused from `xtask/src/harness_status.rs`, whose `classify`, `pid_alive`, `newest_family_member`,
   `read_ended` and path resolution are made reachable from the sibling module; `classify`'s one production caller
   is `run @ xtask/src/harness_status.rs:43`), and whether each of the two receivers accepts a TCP connection on
   `127.0.0.1` at the port resolved from `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT`
   (defaults 4317 and 4318), each attempt bounded at one second. One JSON object on stdout with the verdict
   (`ready` · `not-ready` · `ended` · `cannot-evaluate`), the pid, the exit record when the app ended, and one
   closed label per receiver (`accepting` · `refusing`). Exit 0 only on `ready`; 1 on `not-ready` and `ended`; 2 on
   `cannot-evaluate`. `ready` requires `running-healthy` and both receivers accepting. The probe is pinned against
   a real loopback listener on an ephemeral port and against a port nothing listens on.

3. **The settle verdict, `cargo xtask harness:settled`.** It polls, bounded by `--timeout-seconds` (default 30),
   until one of three things is true, then prints one JSON object and writes the same object to
   `logs/harness-settled.json` under the resolved data dir:
   - the app's pid is no longer alive → `ended`, exit 1;
   - the log family `agent-latest.jsonl*` holds an `app.boot.window.navigation` record for each of the four window
     labels (`compact-widget`, `main`, `findings`, `report`; emitted once per label 5 s after boot by
     `spawn_navigation_check`, `pulse-app/src/window.rs:270-300`, whether or not the window navigated) and the pid
     is alive → `settled`, exit 0;
   - the timeout passes → `not-settled`, exit 1.
   The object carries, on every arm: the verdict; the pid; `ended` (the exit record, read through `read_ended`);
   `app_exit_record` (`present` · `absent`, whether the log family holds an `app.exit` record);
   `windows_settled` (0 to 4); `display` and `session_bus`, each `reachable` · `gone` · `unset` · `unknown`.
   - `display`: `DISPLAY` unset → `unset`; a local display (`:N` or `:N.S`) → a connection attempt to the X
     socket of that number, `reachable` or `gone`; any other form → `unknown`.
   - `session_bus`: `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` holding a `unix:path=` address, else the `bus` socket under
     `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` → a connection attempt, `reachable` or `gone`; neither variable set → `unset`; any other
     address form → `unknown`.
   - No value of any of the three variables is printed or written, only the label.
   - A `--timeout-seconds` below 8 is refused as `cannot-evaluate`, exit 2: the settle record cannot exist before
     5 s, so a shorter window could never read `settled`.
   The decision is a pure function over the probe results, pinned per arm; the two address parsers are pinned on
   each form above; the socket probes are pinned against a real Unix listener in a temp dir and against an absent
   path.

4. **Declare both verbs** in `xtask/src/main.rs` beside `harness:status` (declared at `:50`) and dispatch them.
   `harness:status` keeps its verdict object, its four arms and its exit codes untouched.

5. **`scripts/agent-run.sh` `boot` polls the readiness verdict.** The poll at `:105-116` calls `cargo xtask
   harness:ready` in place of `harness:status`, under the same threaded variables and the same
   `HARNESS_STATUS_TIMEOUT`. The ready lines are unchanged. On the failure path (`:117-134`), when the app is still
   alive it prints one line naming that the receivers never accepted, with the two ports, before the existing
   cleanup; when the app is gone the existing `app ended:` line stands. `status` and `cleanup` are not changed. The
   file stays git mode 100755.

6. **`scripts/agent-run.ps1` `boot` mirrors step 5**: the poll at `:186-199` calls the readiness verdict, and the
   failure path gains the same one line. This edit has no witness: no CI job and no dev host runs the script. The
   report says so.

8. **The green leg.** Run the listed smoke entry on a fresh data dir: `boot` exits 0, the settle verdict reads
   `settled` with `display` `reachable`, `status` reads `running-healthy`, `cleanup` reads `clean`. From that run's
   data dir record in `evidence/`: the instants of both `app.boot.otlp.*.bind` records and of the first record (so
   boot-to-ready is measured with the handshake inside the 10 s window), the four navigation records, the content
   of `logs/xvfb.log`, the count of `ERROR` records and of `app.panic.fatal`.

9. **The control leg.** Run the listed display-lost entry: the display server is stopped by pid right after ready.
   The settle verdict must read `ended`, `"ended": "exit 1"`, `app_exit_record` `absent`, `display` `gone`. Record
   the printed object and the content of `logs/xvfb.log` in `evidence/`. The before-reading is research's control
   on the untouched tree: `status` printed `"ended": "exit 1"` and nothing about the display.

10. **Read both `logs/xvfb.log` files for telemetry.** If either holds anything of a watched service's telemetry,
    stop and say so (inputs#I3). Record what each holds.
11. **The standard gate set**, then the report. The operator pass follows (see Test Commands).
- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` — the readiness verdict and the settle verdict, their probes and their pins
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the two verbs declared and dispatched
- `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` — its helpers made reachable from the sibling module; behaviour unchanged
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — `boot` polls the readiness verdict; one new failure line
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the same change, mirrored, unwitnessed
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the boot job's smoke step alone
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the pins of the smoke step's shape

The chunk's own probes come first, then the two live legs, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order:
`capability-drift` before the default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the
last cargo-adjacent step, and the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure. The operator
pass follows.

The two live legs boot the release app on this host under a virtual display. Each moves the receivers to 14317 and
14318 through the two port variables, so the shared ports 4317 and 4318 are never bound; each unsets
`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` so the window opens on the virtual display; each writes a fresh data dir under `target/`. The
`boot` verb rebuilds the release binary itself, so the legs read the tree as it stands. A reading taken under heavy
host load says so in the evidence.
Absences, each with its reason:
- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched.

- No local pre-push gate: `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot run on this host (test-plan amendment
  `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`); CI is the gate the push meets.

- No bus-stopped leg in the fence: it needs a private bus daemon and a config file that is not in the tree. The
  `session_bus` label is pinned at unit level against a real Unix listener; research ran the live control once.
- No Windows leg: nothing runs `scripts/agent-run.ps1` here or in CI.

- No targeted nextest entry: step 1 runs the two test targets as the red-before-green pair; the workspace entry
  runs the same tests on every re-run.

On the untouched tree both live legs read red: `harness:settled` does not exist yet. The control leg's exit code is
not what decides it, since `xvfb-run` itself returns non-zero when its display server is already gone; its
`contains` atoms decide it.
**The operator pass, in this order.**
1. The hygiene entry, then the pre-CI commit, then the build-branch push.

2. The CI read of the pushed tip, whole, **report-only**. This run is the first in which the smoke reads the app
   past its windows' settle on a runner, and it may end either way. It is recorded as it ends and never re-run.

3. Three report-only reads of that run by its id, as `<id>`: the jobs listing; the boot job's log lines that carry
   the settle verdict, the readiness line and the cleanup token; the run's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact, downloaded
   under `target/`, with `harness-settled.json` and `xvfb.log` printed.

4. **The stop.** If the settle verdict of that run reads `ended` or `not-settled`, the pass stops and says what the
   job kept: the exit record, `app_exit_record`, `display`, `session_bus`, and what `xvfb.log` holds. Naming the
   cause from it and closing it are the operator's next word; nothing is fixed on top without it. If it reads
   `settled`, the run is green reading 1 of the count to eleven and the chunk goes to the wrap.

Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry
writes one.

body:
- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot` exits 0 only when the readiness verdict reads `ready`: the status verdict
  `running-healthy` and a TCP handshake on both resolved ports at `127.0.0.1`. The decision is pinned per arm in
  `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, red before the function exists and green after, and the green leg's `boot` exits 0
  inside the 10 s default with both `app.boot.otlp.*.bind` records in its log (per test-plan §3 5-command
  implementation → `boot` → Readiness signal; architecture.md §Occupied Resources → Network ports).

- (tests) On a failed readiness poll with the app still alive, `boot` names that the receivers never accepted and
  runs `cleanup`; with the app gone it prints `app ended:` as before (per test-plan §3 5-command implementation →
  `boot` → Exit code).

- (tests) The entry `d="target/boot-smoke/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-green" …` (the green leg) passes: the settle
  verdict reads `settled`, `status` reads `running-healthy`, `cleanup` reads `clean`, and the leg's log family
  under `target/boot-smoke/` holds four `app.boot.window.navigation` records, 0 `app.panic.fatal` and 0 `ERROR`
  other than the corpus-open record a host without a keyring writes (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline →
  Direct-binary smoke variant; obs-plan §10 CI gates).

- (obs, the clause of P-129 this plan builds without claiming it) A run in which the app ends by itself says why in
  what the job keeps: the entry `d="target/boot-smoke/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-display-lost" …` (the control)
  prints the settle verdict `ended` with `"ended": "exit 1"`, `app_exit_record` `absent` and `display` `gone`, and
  the same object is in that run's `logs/harness-settled.json` (per obs-plan §7 Error classes captured; obs-plan §9
  Telemetry artifact handling).

- (arch) `cargo xtask harness:status` keeps its verdict object's fields, its four arms and its exit codes: its
  existing in-file pins pass unchanged in `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (per architecture.md
  §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces).

- (arch, security) The diff against `277d65d` holds the seven listed files and no other: no product source, no
  webview source, no capability file, no manifest. The chunk adds no product-consumed environment variable, port,
  TauRPC procedure or capability; the two new files the job keeps sit under the data dir's `logs/` and the product
  never reads them (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources → Filesystem locations and → Environment variables;
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input).

- (security) The settle verdict and `logs/harness-settled.json` carry closed labels, a pid, a count and the bounded
  exit record only; no value of `DISPLAY`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` or `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and no path. Both local
  legs' `logs/xvfb.log` and the CI artifact's are read, and none holds anything of a watched service's telemetry
  (per security-plan §Logging & Monitoring → What NEVER to log; inputs#I3).

- (security, arch) `ci.yml` still holds six independent jobs on `ubuntu-22.04`; against the base only the boot
  job's smoke step differs; the edit adds no `uses:` line, permission, soft gate, retry or job edge; the workflow
  self-lint tests pass (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Secrets; architecture.md §Infrastructure
  Patterns → CI/CD approach).

- (a11y) The `a11y` job is unchanged against the base, and its verdict on the run the pass reads is recorded
  beside the boot-smoke verdict (per a11y-plan §3 CI integration).

- (tests) The pushed tip's CI run is read whole and recorded with its boot-smoke verdict and the settle verdict its
  boot job printed, whichever way it ends; it is not re-run (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates → Zero-flakiness
  budget; inputs#I1 item 5).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` returns 0, the standard gate set passes in its stated order,
  and the bindings close reads byte-identical to the base (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).
- **No capability is claimed.** P-129 stays pooled with a dated ledger note (inputs#I3).

- Spec anchors the plan rests on (from the extracts): test-plan §3 5-command implementation (`boot` Readiness
  signal, Exit code, Timeout; `status` Exit code semantics; `cleanup` Verification), test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate
  discipline, test-plan §9 CI Integration → Pipeline structure, test-plan §10 Quality Gates, test-plan §11 Test
  Anti-Patterns; architecture.md §Occupied Resources (xtask CLI surfaces, Filesystem locations, Network ports,
  Environment variables), §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach; obs-plan §7 Error classes captured, §9
  Telemetry artifact handling, §10 CI gates; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns (Logging, Input, Secrets),
  §Logging & Monitoring; a11y-plan §3 CI integration; design-system: no anchor is acted on (no window change).

- Research files inspected: `scripts/agent-run.sh`, `scripts/agent-run.ps1`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
  `xtask/src/harness_status.rs`, `xtask/src/main.rs`, `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`, `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`,
  `pulse-app/src/main.rs`, `pulse-app/src/render_posture.rs`, `pulse-app/src/window.rs`,
  `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, the test-plan key file `5-command-implementation.md`.

- A retry, a re-run or a soft-fail around the smoke — hides the end this chunk has to name (test-plan §11; the
  smoke step is gating by an operator-approved amendment).
- A fixed sleep to give the app life — the settle read waits on the app's own record, bounded, or on its end.
- Stopping the app sooner so the smoke never reaches the webview — it would read green every time and show nothing.

- Any change under `pulse-app/src`, `pulse-app/ui` or `crates` — no run has named a cause; a fix aimed at one no
  run has shown is not this chunk's outcome (inputs#I1 item 2).

- A product-side switch or environment default for the harness's benefit (disabling the accessibility bridge,
  compositing or the tray in the product) — a boundary widening, and it would change what ships.

- A new field or arm on `harness:status`, or a sixth `agent-run` verb — both are registered contracts; the two new
  verdicts are their own xtask verbs.
- A new script under `scripts/` for the smoke sequence — unpinned by the mode check and a second harness surface.

- A syscall tracer in the job — not validated on this host (none is installed) and not yet shown to be needed; it
  is the next instrument if a run ends with the display and the bus both reachable.

- Printing or storing the value of `DISPLAY`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` or `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or uploading the
  data dir's `run/` — `run/workspace-key` holds a workspace path.
- Fixing on top of a red first run without the operator's word — the pass stops there.

- Naming a cause from the display-lost control — it shows what a lost display looks like here, not that the
  runner's display goes away.

- The local legs need `xvfb-run`; it is on this host (`/usr/bin/xvfb-run`, its `-e FILE` flag read from
  `xvfb-run --help`). `strace` is not.

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` `cleanup` removes its data dir only when the dir's name matches `agent-run-*`
  (`scripts/agent-run.sh:230`), so the legs' dirs under `target/boot-smoke/` stay for the evidence read.

- The app's four navigation records appear 5 s after boot; measured on this host at 5.17 s after the first record
  (research.md). The settle verdict's default window of 30 s leaves room for a slow runner.

- On a host with a keyring the green leg's log holds no `corpus.open.error`; on a host without one it holds that
  one `ERROR` (every CI log does). The criterion counts `ERROR` records other than that one.

- Once the smoke lets the app live about 6 s, the boot job's `ci-gates` line for the frame arm is expected to name
  the adapter outcome on every run. Predicted: `frame: cannot-evaluate: 0 samples, no WebGPU adapter
  (no_navigator_gpu)` in place of the run-dependent line; record what the run prints.
- Host load was 22 to 33 during research's boots; if the legs run under similar load the evidence says so.

- For the wrap's route card, not an amendment: this plan claims nothing, so the entry's requirement stays open.
  The count of consecutive green boot-smoke runs goes on as runs come, to eleven, and three count as closing only
  after a cause is named from a run and closed (inputs#I3). The two red runs' artifacts `11613618010` and
  `11632850540` expire 2026-10-23.

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §3 5-command implementation — the Readiness signal clause (the gap closed,
  the handshake read through `harness:ready`, the "(log parse)" words), the `boot` Command body's `/dev/null`
  sentence (true of the wrapper's own streams; the app's output goes to `logs/boot.log`), the Timeout clause's
  measured boot-to-ready.

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §9 CI Integration — the Boot smoke row's step sequence; test-plan §1 — the
  one-line `boot` summary and the pending trigger `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage` (the new
  failure line and the ps1 edit have no committed shell-level test).

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Occupied Resources — xtask CLI surfaces (`harness:ready`,
  `harness:settled`, the changed `boot` text), Filesystem locations (`logs/xvfb.log`, `logs/harness-settled.json`,
  harness-written, never product-read), Environment variables (the three system variables the harness tool reads
  by presence).

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §9 Telemetry artifact handling — what the boot job's artifact holds;
  obs-plan §10 — the statements of how long the CI app lives and what the frame line reads.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging — the `ui.webgpu.adapter`
  paragraph's "some runs only" sentence; → Input — the two new harness-written files in the state-file class.

**Chunk:** Boot smoke's early exit found and closed — the cause of the app ending itself after ready named from run evidence; boot ready waits for the receivers (P-129)
**Date:** 2026-10-09T19:53:51Z
**Commits:** `e2931127 chore(2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed): operator pre-CI commit` (the one commit since the chunk base `277d65db`; basis `git log --format='%h %s' 277d65db..HEAD`)

**What this chunk is, in one paragraph.** No run has named the cause of the early exit, so this chunk closes none
and claims no capability (the plan's "second kind", inputs#I3). It built three things: `boot` reports ready only
after both OTLP receivers accept a connection; the CI smoke reads the app after its windows have settled, or at its
end; and a run in which the app ends by itself says what the job saw of the exit record, the `app.exit` record, the
display and the session bus, and keeps the display server's own output. No product code changed.

- **Files:** seven, all in research's two lists (basis: `gate.py scope` at this wrap, `changed 7 · listed 7`,
  base `277d65db`).
  - New: `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` (660 lines).
  - Modified: `xtask/src/main.rs` · `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` · `scripts/agent-run.sh` ·
    `scripts/agent-run.ps1` · `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`.
  - Nothing under `pulse-app/src`, `pulse-app/ui`, `crates`, `pulse-app/capabilities`, no manifest, no lockfile
    (basis: the plan's scope-guard entry, `git diff --name-only 277d65d… -- crates pulse-app xtask scripts …` with
    the seven files excluded: exit 0, no output, at implement).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **Two new xtask verbs**, declared at `xtask/src/main.rs:53-65` and dispatched at `:273-274`:
    - `cargo xtask harness:ready` → `harness_ready::run_ready` (`xtask/src/harness_ready.rs:47-85`). One pretty-JSON
      object on stdout: `verdict` (`ready` · `not-ready` · `ended` · `cannot-evaluate`), `pid`, `ended` (the exit
      record, only when the verdict is `ended`), `otlp_grpc` and `otlp_http` (each `accepting` · `refusing`, `null`
      on `cannot-evaluate`). Exit 0 on `ready`, 1 on `not-ready` and `ended`, 2 on `cannot-evaluate`.
      `ready` requires the status verdict `running-healthy` AND a TCP connection accepted on `127.0.0.1` at each
      port resolved from `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT` (defaults 4317 / 4318),
      each attempt bounded at one second. The pure decision is `decide_ready` (`:132-140`).
    - `cargo xtask harness:settled [--timeout-seconds N]` (default 30) → `harness_ready::run_settled` (`:87-122`).
      It polls every 200 ms until one arm holds, prints one pretty-JSON object and writes the same object to
      `logs/harness-settled.json` under the resolved data dir (`keep_verdict`, `:366-378`; written only when that
      `logs/` dir already exists). Arms: the pid is dead → `ended`, exit 1; the log family holds an
      `app.boot.window.navigation` record for each of the four window labels (`compact-widget`, `main`, `findings`,
      `report`) and the pid is alive → `settled`, exit 0; the timeout passes → `not-settled`, exit 1; no pid, an
      unprobeable pid, no resolvable data dir, or a `--timeout-seconds` below 8 → `cannot-evaluate`, exit 2. The
      pure decision is `decide_settled` (`:166-182`). Fields on every arm: `verdict`, `pid`, `ended`,
      `app_exit_record` (`present` · `absent`), `windows_settled` (0 to 4), `display` and `session_bus` (each
      `reachable` · `gone` · `unset` · `unknown`).
  - **Three system variables read by the harness tool, by presence, labels only:** `DISPLAY`,
    `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (`parse_display` `:271-292`, `parse_session_bus` `:294-315`).
    A local display (`:N`, `:N.S`) is probed as the X socket of that number; a `unix:path=` bus address, else the
    `bus` socket under the runtime dir, is probed by a Unix-socket connect. No value of any of the three is
    printed or written. **They are read by xtask only; the product binary's reads are unchanged.**
  - **`harness_status.rs` helpers made crate-visible, behaviour unchanged:** `resolve_paths`, `pid_alive`,
    `end_file`, `read_ended`, `read_pid`, `newest_family_member` became `pub(crate)`; `resolve_data_dir`
    (`xtask/src/harness_status.rs:139-141`) and `env_path` (`:132-137`) were extracted from `resolve_paths`.
    `harness:status` keeps its verdict object, its four arms and its exit codes; its 13 in-file pins pass
    unchanged. Remaining callers: `classify` and the probes now have two production callers each
    (`harness_status::run` and `harness_ready`).
  - No TauRPC procedure, no port, no product-consumed environment variable, no capability.
- **Crates / modules:** one module added, `xtask::harness_ready`. No crate added, removed or renamed.
- **Dependencies:** none added, none bumped. `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` untouched.

- **Schema / config:** none in the product. Two harness-written files are new under the data dir's `logs/`:
  `logs/harness-settled.json` (the settle verdict, written by `harness:settled`) and `logs/xvfb.log` (the display
  server's own error output, written by `xvfb-run -e` in the CI smoke step and in the plan's two live legs). The
  product never reads either. `run/` is still not uploaded.
- **Spec-master edits:** none.

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - **How long the CI app lives before the smoke stops it.** Stated as 0.57 s to 1.40 s (`grep -E '1\.40 s|0\.57 s|1\.4 s'`:
    architecture 1 · security-plan 1 · test-plan 1 · obs-plan 1 · the test-plan key file
    `5-command-implementation.md` 1). Measured on `ci#37979648967`: 5.494 s from the app's first record to its
    `app.exit` (the smoke's own `cleanup`).
  - **How many CI boot-job logs hold `ui.webgpu.adapter`.** Stated as "four of seven" / some runs only
    (`grep -E 'some runs only|four of seven|three of seven'`: architecture 1 · security-plan 1 · test-plan 2 ·
    obs-plan 1). Under the new step the smoke reads past the adapter request on every run that reaches the settle
    verdict; measured on one run: 2 records, both `no_navigator_gpu`.
  - **Boot-smoke readings of 2026-10-09:** nine, two red (was eight, two red, at the plan). The ninth,
    `ci#37979648967`, is green.
  - **Workspace test count:** 2826 passed, 0 skipped at implement (`cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`);
    24 are new (20 in `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, 4 in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`). No master
    states the total.
  - **xtask verbs:** two more (`harness:ready`, `harness:settled`).
- **Dev-tool versions:** none.

- **Harness / gate surface:**
  - **`scripts/agent-run.sh` `boot`** polls `cargo xtask harness:ready` in place of `harness:status` (same threaded
    `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE` / `_LOGFILE`, same `HARNESS_STATUS_TIMEOUT`, default 10 s). The ready lines are
    unchanged. On a failed poll with the app alive it prints the existing `app still running (pid N) but never
    reported healthy` line and, **only when the last readiness verdict held a `refusing` label**, one more:
    `the receivers never both accepted: OTLP gRPC 127.0.0.1:{port}, OTLP HTTP 127.0.0.1:{port}`. With the app gone
    the existing `app ended:` line stands. `status`, `cleanup`, `run`, `logs` are unchanged. Still five verbs.
    Git mode 100755 in the index.

title: The recorded CI runs (re-read at P3)

data.head: ### The recorded CI runs (re-read at P3)

body: Five `logs-boot-Linux` artifacts were downloaded and read record by record: red `ci#37924991598` (`b3ac58a`), red `ci#37961031489` (`f36a2ac`), green `ci#37945548047` (`569604b`), green `ci#37954318153` (`b3e5859`), green `ci#37971913620` (`277d65d`).

- The entry's first `CARRY:` holds on re-read. Both red logs end on a webview-originated record (`ui.webgpu.adapter`, `outcome: no_navigator_gpu`) and hold no `app.exit` and no `app.panic.fatal`. Every green log ends on `app.exit` with `signal: sigterm`, the smoke's own `cleanup`.
- All five `boot.log` files hold one line, the accessibility-bus warning. No run's `boot.log` holds anything else.

- Up to the webview's calls, a red log and a green log that got that far hold the same record sequence. In the two greens the app was stopped 0.13 s and 0.20 s after its last webview-originated record. In red `ci#37924991598` the last record is at 11:47:59.228Z and `status` printed `not-running` about 0.4 s later.

- **This chunk's first reading:** `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` ended `success` on `ci#37971913620` (`277d65d`, job `113960407205`, 18:14:43Z to 18:23:33Z). Ready printed at 18:23:27.03Z, `status` read `running-healthy` 0.32 s later, `cleanup: clean` followed. Its log holds 42 records and no webview-originated record, so the app was stopped before the webview's first call. The whole run read `verdict: green · checks 7/7 · wall 1190 s` (`ci.py conclusion`, re-read at P3). That makes two reds in eight readings.

- **No recorded run shows the app alive more than 0.27 s after the webview's first call.** Four of the eight logs never reach that call. So the eight runs cannot say whether a green run would have stayed up.
- The CI log lines carry `ci.run.id` and `git.commit.sha` (both keys present in all five logs).

- **What the job keeps:** the artifact is `${ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR}/logs/` and nothing else (`ci.yml:391-398`): `agent-latest.jsonl.{date}`, `boot.log`, `build.log`. The wrapper's exit record sits under `run/` and is not uploaded; it reaches the job log only through the `ended` field of the `status` verdict. The display server's own error output is not kept anywhere: `xvfb-run` sends it to `/dev/null` unless `-e FILE` is given (`xvfb-run --help`, line 9, read on this host; the job passes no `-e`, `ci.yml:380`).

The job's three verbs were run on this host under `xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 1280x1024x24"`, with the release binary rebuilt at `277d65d` by the boot verb itself (2 m 31 s, the first boot). Three stated differences from the runner: the OTLP ports moved to 14317 and 14318 through `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_{GRPC,HTTP}_PORT`, so 4317 and 4318 were never bound; `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset, so the window opened on the virtual display; a fresh data dir per boot. Host load was 22 to 33 throughout (the `load1` column of the summaries; other builders' cargo was running). The summaries are in the phase run dir, `repro-*.tsv`.
| Arm | Boots | What was varied | Self-ends | Reading |

| The CI sequence unchanged (boot, status, cleanup) | 21 | nothing | 0 | 21 of 21 green; every boot was stopped before the webview's first call (0 of 21 logs hold `ui.webgpu.adapter` or `ui-bridge.ready`; 41 records each) |

| Hold: boot, then 15 s watching the exit record, then status, cleanup | 20 | the app is left alive | 0 | 20 of 20 lived 15 s and ended on the smoke's SIGTERM with an `app.exit` record; 297 to 305 records |

| Hold under an empty private session bus | 10 | a `dbus-daemon` with no service directory, so the keyring and the accessibility bus answer `ServiceUnknown` | 0 | 10 of 10 lived 15 s; the log takes the runner's shape (`corpus.open.error KeyringUnavailable`, the three persist warnings, the same accessibility-bus line in `boot.log`) |
**The early exit did not reproduce on this host: 0 self-ends in 51 boots.** Thirty of those boots lived well past the point where both red runs ended.
Two controls, each stopping something the app depends on 5 s after ready:
| Control | Boots | How the app ended | `app.exit` record | New line in `boot.log` |

| The private session bus stopped | 3 | `signal 15 (TERM)`, within 1 ms of the stop, 3 of 3 | present (`signal`, `sigterm`), preceded by a WARN "D-Bus message processing error: … disconnected from D-Bus?" | none |
| The virtual display stopped (`Xvfb` by pid) | 2 | `exit 1`, within 0.1 s of the stop, 2 of 2 | **none** | **none** |

- **The display-stopped control is the first local run with the reds' signature.** `status` printed `"ended": "exit 1"`, `"verdict": "not-running"`; the log ends on an ordinary record (`triage.cue.tick`) with no `app.exit`; `boot.log` gained nothing. Those are the three facts both red runs show.

- It is a control, not a reproduction. It shows what a lost display connection looks like in what the job keeps. It does not show that the runner's display goes away, and no recorded run can show it either way: the display server's errors are discarded and nothing reads whether it is alive after the app ends.

- The bus-stopped control ends the app too, but with a record and by signal, so on this host a lost session bus does not look like the reds. The runner's library versions differ (Ubuntu 22.04 against glib2 2.88.3, dbus 1.16.2, webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6 here, `pacman -Q`), so this excludes nothing about the runner.

- An end by `exit()` would be recorded: the `atexit` hook hands off to the reporter thread (`pulse-app/src/observability.rs:2838-2882`, witnessed by `pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs`). An end by `_exit` is on the record's stated unloggable list (`observability.rs:2715-2717`). The display-stopped control therefore ends through a path of that unloggable class; which function calls it was not measured (no tracer is installed on this host: `strace` absent, checked with `command -v`).

- `scripts/agent-run.sh:105-116` prints `boot: ready` when `cargo xtask harness:status` exits 0, with no port probe. The same script already probes both resolved ports through `/dev/tcp` in `cleanup` (`:211-216`).
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1:186-199` has the same gap: ready is printed when `Invoke-Status` returns, and its `cleanup` already probes with `System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient` (`:83`).
- `harness:status` derives its verdict from the pid file, that pid's liveness and the log family's mtime (`xtask/src/harness_status.rs`, `classify` and `run`). Receiver bind is not an input.

- The app logs `app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind` and `app.boot.otlp.http.bind` 0.17 s to 0.35 s after its first record (three CI logs and two local boots read). In three local hold boots read record by record, the webview's first call came 0.8 s to 1.4 s after the first record.

- **A signal the app already emits says its windows settled.** `pulse-app/src/window.rs:260-296` emits `app.boot.window.navigation` once per window 5 s after boot (`NAVIGATION_SETTLE`), with `window_label`, `navigated`, `reason`. In every local hold boot all four labels (`compact-widget`, `main`, `findings`, `report`) appeared at 5.17 s after the first record. No CI log has ever held this record, because the smoke stops the app within 1.40 s.
- The `a11y` job does not run the `boot` verb: `agent-run` appears in `ci.yml` on lines 382 to 384 only, all in the boot job (`grep -n agent-run .github/workflows/ci.yml`).

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` (full) — the five verbs; the waiting wrapper sends the app's stdout and stderr to `logs/boot.log` (`:79`), and the subshell's own streams to `/dev/null` (`:89`); the readiness poll (`:105-116`); the failure path (`:117-134`); the cleanup port probe (`:211-216`).
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` (140-214) — the Windows twin of the boot verb; same readiness poll.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (325-398) — the boot job: the smoke step (`:375-385`), `ci-gates` (`:388-389`), the upload (`:391-398`).
- `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` (outline and the function list) — `run`, `classify`, `pid_alive`, `ps_state_is_live`, `read_ended`, `end_file`, `newest_family_member`, with their in-file pins.
- `xtask/src/main.rs` (the verb list) — `harness:status` is declared at `:50`.
- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` (27, 207-234) — the `script-modes` stage reads the git mode of `scripts/agent-run.sh` alone.
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` (2700-2915) — the `app.exit` record: `record_exit`, `exit_after_event_loop`, the `atexit` hand-off, the signal listener.
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (278-300, 1556-1579) — `main()`'s order and the `run_return` tail.
- `pulse-app/src/render_posture.rs` (full) — the one prior Linux launch end closed in the product; a native-toolkit `_exit(1)` on another surface.
- `pulse-app/src/window.rs` (the settle lines, by grep) — the post-settle navigation record.
- `.andromeda/registries/contracts/test-plan/5-command-implementation.md` (1-12) — the `boot` clauses: Readiness signal with the open gap, Exit code, Timeout.
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` (428, by grep) — the one test line that names the boot job's upload.

title: Scope — Boot smoke's early exit found and closed

data.head: # Scope — Boot smoke's early exit found and closed

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates
**Working entry (`working-route.md:15`):** "Boot smoke's early exit found and closed — the cause of the app ending
itself after ready is named; equal source reads the same (P-129)", with two `CARRY:` blocks folded below.
**Chunk base:** `277d65d` (HEAD at take-up, equal to its upstream). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this
sha, never HEAD.

Requirement P-129 reads: "the CI boot smoke ends the same on equal source: the cause of the app ending by itself
shortly after ready on the runner is found and closed, and the job no longer reads red where nothing it builds
changed" (`matrix.py show --id P-129`, read at take-up). The `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` job read red on two of
eight runs of 2026-10-09 on source the job does not distinguish. This chunk finds out why the app ends, from
evidence a run produced, closes that cause, and makes a run in which the app ends by itself say why in what the job
keeps. It also closes the readiness gap the same logs showed: `boot` reports ready before the OTLP receivers bind.

The operator's direction for this chunk (inputs#I1, the pc overseer's phase directive; inputs#I2, the invocation
word): the cause is named from evidence a run produced; the early exit is reproduced, and its rate measured, before
any approach is chosen; the plan card is printed at P5 and the chunk stops there for the operator's `yes`.

- **The cause of the app ending itself after ready is named** (the entry; P-129's acceptance: "named from evidence a
  run produced, not inferred"). A fix aimed at a cause no run has shown is not this chunk's outcome (inputs#I1
  item 2).

- [premise-corrected: 0 self-ends in 51 local boots across three arms, research.md "The local reproduction"] **The
  early exit did not reproduce on this host.** The relay's "hypothesis: the early exit reproduces locally at some
  rate" (inputs#I1 item 3) was measured at P3: 21 boots of the CI sequence unchanged, 20 boots holding the app 15 s,
  10 boots holding it under an empty private session bus that gives the log the runner's shape. No boot ended by
  itself. Host load was 22 to 33 during the readings (inputs#I1 item 7). So the cause is named from a runner's run,
  and this chunk's first work is what makes a runner's run able to show it.

- **What the job keeps today cannot show the cause, so the job is made to keep what would** (inputs#I1 item 2: "the
  exit path that writes no record is itself the finding"). Verified at P3:
  - The uploaded artifact is the data dir's `logs/` alone. The wrapper's exit record under `run/` is not in it. The
    display server's own error output is discarded by `xvfb-run`'s default, and nothing reads whether the display
    is still there after the app ends.
  - A control on this host produced the reds' three facts exactly: with the virtual display stopped 5 s after
    ready, the app ended `exit 1`, wrote no `app.exit` record, and added nothing to `boot.log`, 2 of 2. A second
    control, the session bus stopped, ended the app by SIGTERM with a record, 3 of 3, which is not the reds'
    signature. Both are controls. Neither shows what happens on the runner.
  - So a run in which the app ends by itself must say, in what the job keeps: how the app ended, whether it left an
    `app.exit` record, whether its display was still reachable, whether its session bus was still reachable, and
    what the display server itself printed. P-129 asks for this as a standing property ("a run in which the app
    ends by itself says why in what the job keeps").

- **The smoke reads the app after its windows have settled, not at whatever instant `status` happens to run.**
  Verified at P3: the smoke stops the app within 1.40 s on the runner, four of eight CI logs never reach the
  webview's first call, and 21 of 21 local boots of the unchanged sequence were stopped before it. No recorded run
  shows the app alive more than 0.27 s after that call. The app already emits a record when its windows have
  settled (`app.boot.window.navigation`, once per window, 5 s after boot); the smoke waits for it, bounded, or for
  the app's end. With that, equal source reads the same on every run: either the app lives past the point where
  both reds ended, or it ends and the job says what it saw.

- **The cause is closed, and equal source reads the same** (the entry; P-129). The acceptance names "a stated number
  of consecutive runs of equal source" reading green. Ruled at P4 (inputs#I3): the number is three, made by the
  operator pass's own pushes, and it counts only once a cause is named from a run and closed. With no named cause
  P-129 is not claimed at this wrap whatever the count ("three greens pass an unfixed job about 42 percent of the
  time"); the chunk then delivers what makes the next red show its cause, the entry stays open, and the count runs
  on as runs come, to eleven consecutive greens.

- Added at P4: **this plan is the second kind.** No run has named a cause, so the plan closes none and claims no
  capability. It delivers the readiness repair, the settle read and the kept evidence, and it reads its first CI
  run. If that run names a cause, the pass stops and says so; closing it is planned from that evidence.

- **`boot` reports ready only after it confirms a TCP handshake on the bound ports** (the entry's second `CARRY:`;
  inputs#I1 item 4: "The harness contract's clause (a TCP handshake on the bound ports) stays the contract").
  Verified at P3: `scripts/agent-run.sh:105-116` prints `boot: ready` when `cargo xtask harness:status` succeeds,
  with no port probe; the status verdict takes no port as input.
  - Verified at P3: the Windows twin has the same gap (`scripts/agent-run.ps1:186-199`). The two scripts are
    recorded as one surface in lockstep, and no CI job and no dev host runs the Windows one. The readiness decision
    therefore moves into xtask, where it is pinned, and each script changes the one verb it polls; the Windows edit
    is mirrored and stated as unwitnessed.

- **`ci#37971913620` on `277d65d` is this chunk's first reading of the job: green** (inputs#I1 item 5). Read at P3:
  `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` `success`, job `113960407205`; the app was stopped before the webview's first call
  (42 records, none webview-originated), so this green says nothing about whether the app would have stayed up.
  Every CI run this chunk reads is recorded with its boot-smoke verdict. A run is a reading and is never re-run for
  a green.

- **The records that describe the smoke and the boot verb are corrected at the wrap, not here.** Phase amends no
  spec source. Known sites: test-plan §3, 5-command implementation (the Readiness signal clause and its open gap,
  the `boot` Command body's statement that the wrapper's streams go to `/dev/null`, which is true of the wrapper
  and not of the app, whose output goes to `logs/boot.log`); test-plan §9, the Boot smoke row; architecture
  §Occupied Resources, xtask CLI surfaces and Filesystem locations; the obs-plan and security-plan sites that state
  how long the CI app lives.

title: The two causal claims the freight carries

data.head: ## The two causal claims the freight carries

body:
- [premise-corrected: no recorded run decides it; none shows the app alive more than 0.27 s after the webview's
  first call, research.md "The recorded CI runs"] From the entry's first `CARRY:`: "hypothesis: the app ends itself
  a few hundred milliseconds after the webview's first calls on the runner, and the job reads red when status comes
  late enough to see it; not shown: a cause, or that the end is the window's and not the engine's". It stays a
  hypothesis. The plan rests on no part of it: the settle wait reads every run past that point, whichever way the
  hypothesis falls.

- **The measured readings hold on re-read.** From the same block: "measured 2026-10-09 on the boot job's application
  logs of seven runs ...: red on ci#37924991598 (b3ac58a) and ci#37961031489 (f36a2ac), green on five; on both reds
  boot printed ready and status read the app ended, exit 1, within 0.7 s; the red logs hold no record the green
  logs lack, no app.panic.fatal and no app.exit, and boot.log holds the one accessibility-bus warning all seven
  hold". Verified at P3 on five downloaded artifacts and the red job's own log (`ci#37961031489`, job
  `113923604622`: ready at 16:52:59.36Z, `"ended": "exit 1"` at 16:53:00.03Z). The count is now eight readings, two
  red. The two red runs' `logs-boot-Linux` artifacts `11613618010` and `11632850540` expire 2026-10-23.

- **P-129 is this entry's one capability, and this plan does not claim it** (inputs#I3). Its acceptance asks for a
  cause named from a run and closed; no run has named one. One clause of it is built and proven here without a
  claim: a run in which the app ends by itself says why in what the job keeps. P-129 stays in the pool with a dated
  note. P-129 is PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word (the ledger's note; the handoff).

- **The window is not removed or rewritten** (inputs#I1 item 6). It leaves at `Window's gates retired` and `Window
  retired` (Epoch 2). If the cause sits in the window alone, this chunk names it, closes it at the smallest place
  that makes equal source read the same, and says what of it leaves with the window anyway.

- **No product code changes under this plan as written.** The readiness verdict, the settle verdict and the kept
  evidence are harness and job work. A product change to close a named cause is planned when the cause is named.

- **A boundary widening halts for the founder's own word** (inputs#I1 item 8). None is planned. Ruled at P4
  (inputs#I3): the two files the job newly keeps are routine harness evidence, "the same class as boot.log,
  harness-written, never read by the product, registered at the wrap", with one stop: "If the display server output
  is seen to carry anything of a watched service telemetry, stop and say so."
- **No CI run is re-run for a green** (inputs#I1 item 5; the handoff).

- **`Pre-push check native on Linux` and `No CI step reads nothing` are the next two entries**
  (`working-route.md:17`, `:19`). Their work is not this chunk's, even with `ci.yml` or `scripts/agent-run.sh` open.

- **Ports 4317 and 4318 are shared with conductor-builder** (the handoff's host note). Every local boot of this
  chunk moves the receivers to 14317 and 14318 through the two port variables, so the shared ports are never bound.

- **The plan card is printed at P5 and the chunk stops there for the operator's `yes`** (inputs#I1 item 8,
  inputs#I2).

- carry: measured 2026-10-09 on the boot job's application logs of seven runs (record:
  2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request's report, Outcome, watches): red on ci#37924991598
  (b3ac58a) and ci#37961031489 (f36a2ac), green on five; on both reds boot printed ready and status read the app
  ended, exit 1, within 0.7 s; the red logs hold no record the green logs lack, no app.panic.fatal and no app.exit,
  and boot.log holds the one accessibility-bus warning all seven hold; in the four logs that hold webview-originated
  records status read 0.23 s and 0.27 s after the first of them (app alive) and 0.49 s and 0.67 s after (app ended);
  the smoke stops the app within 1.40 s of its first record on every run, so no green log shows it alive longer;
  hypothesis: the app ends itself a few hundred milliseconds after the webview's first calls on the runner, and the
  job reads red when status comes late enough to see it; not shown: a cause, or that the end is the window's and not
  the engine's; the two red runs' logs-boot-Linux artifacts 11613618010 and 11632850540 expire 2026-10-23.
  **Absorbed as:** the chunk's subject, in "What the chunk builds" and "The two causal claims" above.

- carry: the harness contract's boot readiness signal says boot confirms a TCP handshake on the bound ports, and the
  shipped scripts/agent-run.sh reports ready on the harness:status verdict alone; on ci#37964887106 ready printed
  12 ms after the app's first record and the app was stopped having logged neither app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind nor a
  tick (measured 2026-10-09; test-plan §3, 5-command implementation, records the gap as open with this entry as
  owner); ready before the receivers bind is the engine's own matter too (the operator's word at the card,
  2026-10-09). **Absorbed as:** the readiness bullet above. The harness's readiness is this chunk's; what the
  engine itself reports before its receivers bind (the `ready` and `health` envelopes) is not changed here.

title: Second fold source — the CI verdict read at Setup 5a

data.head: ## Second fold source — the CI verdict read at Setup 5a

body: The last master flip is HEAD itself (`277d65d`), so one sha was read through `ci.py conclusion`:

- `277d65dbb51a`: **verdict not yet available** at Setup (in progress at 2026-10-09T18:18Z, `ci#37971913620`). It
  settled during this phase and was read again at P3: `verdict: green · checks 7/7 · wall 1190 s`, boot smoke
  `success`. Nothing is folded from it as a red. It is this chunk's first reading of the job, recorded above.
- none — the entry carries no `BLOCKED-ON` (`route.py pins`: its two blocks are both `CARRY:`).

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-09T14:22:56Z
- **Chunk base:** `0b61bfbef575eeb56909ea5e31bdcb8cc66ee74b` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped entry below names it.

The `ci` workflow stops running on Windows and macOS. Its two matrix jobs, `lint-test` and `a11y`, become
single-runner Linux jobs, and the `release` job, which has no Linux leg, leaves whole. The seven step conditions
that are always true on a Linux-only workflow leave with them, and so do the comments that describe the other
systems' runners. Every gate step stays, in its order (intent R7, requirement P-113; architecture §Infrastructure
Patterns → CI/CD approach; test-plan §9 Pipeline structure).

The chunk also records what one run costs, per job, before and after, read from the runs themselves (the entry;
inputs#I1 item 5). The before-reading is `ci#37934330231` on the chunk base. The removal is not expected to shorten
a round: in all eight runs read at take-up the longest job is a Linux job that stays (research.md, the per-job
table). What leaves is runner time, close to half of each run's job-seconds, and six checks.

Two things that read `ci.yml` in the tree are kept true: the workflow self-lint loses the test whose subject is the
`release` job and gains two pins, one that the workflow names no other system and one that the Linux release build
keeps its witnesses now that `release` is gone.

1. **Tests first, in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`.**
   - Delete `ci_workflow_release_job_owns_and_saves_its_cache_key` (`:100-112`). Its subject is the `release` job.
   - In `data_dir_export_precedes_every_consumer` (`:411`), the expected job count of `ci.yml` becomes 6 (`:413`).
     The two other rows of that table are untouched.
   - Add `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only`: every line of the workflow whose trimmed text starts with `runs-on:`
     reads `runs-on: ubuntu-22.04`, there is at least one such line, and no line, ASCII-lowercased, contains
     `macos`, `windows`, `matrix.os` or `runner.os ==`. The failure message names the first offending line number.
   - Add `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses`: the `supply-chain` job block contains
     `cargo auditable build --workspace --release`, and the `boot` job block contains
     `cargo build --workspace --release --features mcp-server`. It reads both blocks through `workflow_job_block`
     (`:79`), which keeps that helper's one caller (its only caller today is the test that leaves,
     `workflow_job_block @ pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs:102`).
   - Follow the file's own shape: `str::lines()` and line equality, no YAML parser, no new dependency.

2. **Read the tests red against the workflow as it stands.** One run, before any workflow edit:
   `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci -E 'binary(quality_gate_workflow)'`. Expected:
   `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only` fails (20 lines carry an other-system token at the base) and
   `data_dir_export_precedes_every_consumer` fails (7 jobs found, 6 expected); the witness pin passes, since both
   builds are already there. Record the failing and passing test names and the two failure messages in
   `evidence/red-before.md`, with any host path replaced by a labelled placeholder.

3. **Edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.**
   - The header comment above `jobs:` (`:18-21`) states the cache budget for the jobs that remain: one target cache
     for `lint-test` and one for `boot`; `a11y`, `mcp-test` and `supply-chain` restore read-only; `coverage` keeps
     the registry only. It names no other system.
   - `lint-test` (`:23-29`): `name: lint / test (ubuntu-22.04)`, `runs-on: ubuntu-22.04`, and the `strategy` block
     leaves, in the form `mcp-test` and `boot` already have (`:245-246`, `:393-394`).
   - `lint-test` steps: the condition `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` leaves at `:60`, `:122`, `:128` and `:132`. The
     three perf step names lose their trailing "(Linux only)" and keep the rest (`:121`, `:127`, `:131`). The
     comment above the "No Cyrillic in sources" step keeps its account of why the scan is an xtask verb and loses
     the clause about the Windows runner's code page (`:86-88`).
   - The `release` job leaves whole, with the two comment lines above it (`:191-242` and the blank line after).
   - `a11y` (`:301-307`): `name: a11y (ubuntu-22.04)`, `runs-on: ubuntu-22.04`, the `strategy` block leaves; the
     condition at `:334` leaves.
   - `supply-chain` and `coverage`: the condition on the system-library install step leaves (`:514`, `:579`).
     Nothing else in either job changes; the audit step and its token (`:493-496`) are not touched.
   - Unchanged everywhere: every `uses:` line, the workflow-level `permissions:`, every step's order, every
     `shell: bash`, every name and key that carries `${{ runner.os }}`, `node-version`, the four
     `apt-get install` lists, the three `continue-on-error` baseline downloads, every `if: always()` and every
     `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`.
   - A comment line at two-space indent inside `jobs:` must not end in a colon: the job count at
     `quality_gate_workflow.rs:424-429` reads such a line as a job.
4. **Read the tests green** with the same call as Step 2, then run the whole gate block.

5. **One mutation check of the witness pin**, a one-shot at implement: in the working tree, drop `--release` from
   the `supply-chain` build step, run the Step 2 call, confirm `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses`
   reads red, restore the line, confirm `git diff --quiet` on the file against the Step 3 result. Both readings go
   to `evidence/mutation-checks.md`. Apply the mutation with the Edit tool and confirm it is present before the run.

6. **Write `evidence/ci-wall-clock.md`**: the before-reading's per-job table (scope.md) with its run id, sha and
   event, the eight-run summary (research.md), and the boot-smoke verdict of each run read. Leave the after-reading
   as a named section the operator pass fills.

7. **Operator pass** (after /implement's report, before the wrap): the hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the push,
   the CI read, then the three reads of the after-run. Whoever drives it appends to `evidence/ci-wall-clock.md` the
   after-run's per-job table from the jobs entry's output, the run id, and its `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` verdict,
   and records each operator entry's exit and atoms in `evidence/operator-pass.md`.
- none

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the two matrix jobs become single-runner Linux jobs; the `release` job leaves; seven
  always-true conditions and the other-system comments leave. Keep the SHA pins, the step order and the resolved
  names (research.md §Patterns detected).

- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — one test leaves, the job count reads 6, two pins are added. Keep the
  file's line-anchored reading (research.md §Patterns detected).

The chunk's own probes come first, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order: `capability-drift` before the
default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, and
the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure. The operator pass follows.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No boot-smoke entry: neither file is on the boot-smoke trigger list (test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline), and
  the chunk boots no app. The boot smoke that matters here is the CI job's, read in the operator pass.
- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched.

- No local pre-push gate: `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` needs `wsl.exe` and cannot run on this host (test-plan
  amendment `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`); CI's `lint-test` job is the gate the push meets.

- No liveness probe and no live leg: the chunk drives no external process. research.md's harness slot reads `none`
  for that reason.

- No targeted nextest entry: Steps 2 and 4 run the one test binary as implement's red-before-green pair, both
  readings in `evidence/red-before.md`; the workspace nextest entry runs the same tests on every re-run.

- Step 5's mutation edits source and reverts, so it is a one-shot at implement, both readings in
  `evidence/mutation-checks.md`; `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses` in the workspace nextest
  entry guards the property on re-run.

Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry
writes one. The three reads of the after-run take the run id the CI read prints for the `ci` workflow, as `<id>`.
The jobs read is report-only: its rows are the after-reading's table and assert nothing by themselves. The steps
read asserts that no step of any job reads other than `success`, which is how the before-run reads on its six
Linux jobs (research.md).

The CI read asserts green. If `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` reads red on a tree whose source it does not exercise
differently, that is the folded watch's recurrence: it is recorded with its job id and log reading, the run is not
re-run to obtain a green, and the wrap dispositions it.

chunk one invocation runs the same six stages, in the same order, in the working tree, and prints the same kind of

architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces; test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

The `wsl.exe` hop and the distro clone leave `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`, with everything that existed only for them: the
patch sync, the clone's cache cap, the apt-package probe, the Viola Node path. The check keeps what made it honest:
its pins are read from the repository, an unmet pin is `cannot-evaluate` and never green, every stage gets a
constructed environment and its own data dir, no stage starts `pulse-app` or binds a port.

No stage leaves: the window, its bridge and the credential store stand today (inputs#I1 item 2). Stage by stage,
the later entry that removes or changes it is named in Implementation notes. P-113 is advanced by one item of its
observed gap (the `wsl.exe` hop) and stays pooled.

1. **Node 24 on this host, on the operator's word.** The check keeps ci.yml's Node pin (step 5), and this host holds
   only Node 26. Run `mise install node@24` once: a user-level install under the home directory, nothing
   system-wide. Record in `evidence/` the version it resolved (`mise where node@24`, then that directory's
   `bin/node --version` and `bin/npm --version`), the home directory spelled `~` in what is written down. This is
   the one host change of the chunk, and it is the operator's
   own word (the operator (the pc overseer), 2026-10-09: "Node 24 comes as a user-level install (mise install node@24)
   that the implement run may make itself on this word - nothing system-wide; record the version it resolves").

2. **The hop and the clone leave** `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`: the constants `WSL`, `DISTRO`, `CLONE_DIR`,
   `CACHE_CAP_BYTES` and `NODE_BIN`; `distro_home`; the `Linux` struct with its `wsl.exe` command wrapper; the
   distro-side half of `sync` (clone, fetch, reset, clean, patch apply, the tree-id comparison) and the patch file it
   wrote; `cache`; `wsl_path`. `rust_channel` keeps its name and signature (its caller is
   `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` @ `xtask/src/rust_floor.rs:69`); `run` keeps its signature (its caller
   is `main` @ `xtask/src/main.rs:342`).

3. **The host guard.** The check evaluates on Linux alone. A pure decision takes the operating-system name as an
   argument and answers supported or not; `drive` asks it with the build's own name. Any other system reads
   `cannot-evaluate` with reason `not-linux`. The reason `not-windows` leaves.

4. **Head and tree.** The verdict keeps `head` (the HEAD sha) and `tree` (the tree id of HEAD plus the working tree,
   computed through a temporary index so the real index is never touched) with their present meaning; the host-side
   half of `sync` that computes them stays, and its temporary index lives in the per-run area of step 7. A git read
   that fails reads `cannot-evaluate` with reason `tree-unreadable`.

5. **The provisioning check, native.** Its pins stay read from the repository: the Rust channel from
   `rust-toolchain.toml` and the Node major from ci.yml (`node_major`); either unreadable is `pins-unreadable`, as
   today. Every probe runs in the stage environment of step 6, so what is probed is what the stages will find.
   Required, each named in `missing[]` when absent:
   - the pinned Rust channel in `rustup toolchain list`, then `cargo +{channel} clippy --version` and
     `cargo +{channel} nextest --version`;
   - `node --version` whose major equals ci.yml's pin, named `node:{pin} (found {version})` as today, and
     `npm --version` answering;
   - `git` and `cc` on the stage PATH;
   - a Python 3 interpreter (`python3`, else `python`, printing `Python 3`): the `test` stage fails without one.
   The decision (probe results in, the list of missing pieces out) is a pure function. Anything missing reads
   `cannot-evaluate` with reason `provisioning-missing`. The verb installs nothing and prints no install command.
   What leaves: the read of ci.yml's apt list (`apt_packages`), `installed_packages`, the `dpkg-query` probe,
   `remediation`, and the probes for `jq` and `xvfb-run`.

6. **The stage environment.** One function builds the exact variable set a stage child receives; children are
   spawned with a cleared environment plus that set:
   - `HOME`: the developer's home, read from the verb's own environment;
   - `PATH`: `{HOME}/.cargo/bin`, then the directory of the first `node` executable on the verb's own PATH, then
     `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`. With no `node` on the verb's PATH the node directory is left out and step 5 names
     Node as missing;
   - `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`: `target/pre-push/run/data` under the repository root, absolute;
   - for the `npm` stage only, `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR`: `target/pre-push/run/puppeteer`, absolute.
   Nothing else crosses. The session bus address, the runtime dir and the display variables are not in the set, so
   the stage reaches no OS credential store, exactly as the `env -i` form did. The search for `node` on a PATH value
   is a pure function over its arguments.

7. **The per-run area.** `target/pre-push/run/` belongs to the verb. At the start of every run it is removed and
   created again, and it holds `puppeteer/`, `data/` and the temporary index. So the browser cache is fresh on every
   run and nothing accumulates. A removal or creation that fails reads `cannot-evaluate` with reason
   `run-dir-unusable`. The report twin stays at `target/pre-push/report.json`. Nothing else under `target/pre-push/`
   is touched, and `~/.cache/puppeteer` is never touched.

9. **The bindings are put back as found.** The `test` stage rewrites the tracked file
   `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`. A helper takes a file path and a stage action: it reads the file's bytes (or
   notes that the file is absent), runs the action, and then puts the file back to what it read, whichever way the
   action ended (success, failure, or a command that could not be spawned); a file absent before is removed again. The
   `test` stage runs inside it. A restore that fails makes the stage red with reason `restore-failed:bindings`, never
   green. No regen stage is added (the operator (the pc overseer), 2026-10-09: "No stage that exists only for the
   bridge … the restore runs whichever way the test stage ends, and is itself pinned by a test").

10. **The verdict document.** Members: `verdict`, `reason`, `head`, `tree`, `stages[{name, ok, ms}]`, `missing[]`.
    `cache` and `remediation` leave with the clone and the apt line. No member carries a value of an environment
    variable or a path: `missing[]` entries are tool names and tool-reported versions.

11. **The verb's own text.** The module doc comment of `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` and the `about` string of
    `PrePushLinux` in `xtask/src/main.rs` (`:262-264`) describe the native check: the six stages, the three exits,
    the pins, no second system. The comment at `main.rs:570-572` stays as it is.

13. **The controls.** Before the first graded use, each new decision is mutation-checked once, by hand, the mutation
    confirmed present before the run and reverted after: the host guard inverted; the Node comparison neutralised;
    one variable added to the stage environment; the restore skipped. Each must turn its pin red. The readings go to
    `evidence/mutation-checks.md`.

14. **The live readings.** The gate block's two live entries are run and their output kept in `evidence/`: the
    `cannot-evaluate` reading with no Node on PATH, and the green reading with Node 24 first on PATH, with the load
    average read before and after it and each stage's `ms` copied from the verdict. A timing is written with its
    load beside it and is not a budget.
- none

- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` — steps 2 to 12: the hop and the clone leave; the host guard, the provisioning check, the
  stage environment, the per-run area, the stage runner, the bindings restore and the verdict document become
  native; the tests follow. The three-exit `Verdict`, `Stop`, the report twin and the stage names keep their shape.
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — step 11: the `about` text of `PrePushLinux`.

The standard gate set comes first, in test-plan §3 order: `capability-drift` before the default-features workspace
nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen after it, and the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk
adds no procedure. The chunk's own entries follow: a source census, a probe that Node 24 is installed, the two live
runs of the verb with the load average read around the green one, a read of the report twin, a second bindings
close and the scope guard.

The two live runs come after the regen on purpose. The green run executes the `test` stage, which rewrites the
bindings and must put them back; the bindings close after it and the scope guard after that are what show the check
left the working tree as it found it. The green run costs a browser download of about 1 GB and a full workspace
test run; its timeout is one hour.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is in the file lists. The `npm` stage's
  writes there (`node_modules`, `dist`) are gitignored.
- No boot smoke: no boot or setup path is touched (test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).
- No targeted nextest entry: the workspace entry runs the new pins on every re-run.

- No entry for the folded boot-smoke watch: it is an observation, read by the wrap from the CI run the operator
  pass reads.

- The mutation controls of step 13 change source and revert it, so they are one-shot runs at /implement with both
  readings in `evidence/`; the workspace entry guards the same pins on every re-run.

On the untouched tree the chunk's own asserting entries read red, the scope guard aside: the verb answers
`not-windows`, the two files still name the hop, and Node 24 is not installed. Each reading is in its entry's
`baseline`.

**The operator pass, in this order.** The hygiene entry; the pre-CI commit; the green live entry once more on the
committed tree (the local pre-push gate before a push); the build-branch push; the CI read of the pushed tip. A CI
red whose only failed check is the boot smoke is the watch's recurrence: it is read by the watch's own terms
(`harness-settled.json`, `xvfb.log`), brought to the operator, and not fixed on top.
