- **Package manager**: `pacman`; no `dpkg-query`, no `apt-get`.

- **Ignored paths**: `git check-ignore -q` exits 0 for `pulse-app/ui/dist`, `pulse-app/ui/node_modules` and
  `target/pre-push`; exit 1 for `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (tracked).

- **What the hand-runs left**: `target/pre-push/` holds ten per-run puppeteer caches of 963 MB each, ten data dirs
  and seven small logs, 9.4 GB in all (`du -sh target/pre-push`). Each cache holds a chrome and a
  chrome-headless-shell folder for 148 and for 152, and the 148 zip files.

- **The developer's shell**: carries `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`;
  carries no `RUST*`, `CARGO*`, `CC`, `CXX` or `PUPPETEER*` variable.

- **Build-script environment tracking in the workspace's own crates**: `crates/triage/build.rs:52-53` (two
  variables of its own) and Tauri's `TAURI_CONFIG` / `REMOVE_UNUSED_COMMANDS` (the last `pulse-app` build output).
  None of them is set in the developer's shell or in the constructed stage environment. Whether a stage run on the
  shared `target/` rebuilds anything a developer build had current is not measured; the hand-runs recorded no
  stage timings.

- **The `test` stage rewrites the tracked bindings file.** `cargo xtask test` is the default-features workspace
  nextest (`main.rs:444-467`); under default features the `emit_taurpc_bindings` router omits the `mcp` namespace
  and `taurpc` writes `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` on every `Router::into_handler()` (test-plan §3
  Per-chunk gate discipline; `rules/testing.md` 2026-05-13). The frame that produces the write is the test binary,
  whatever environment it runs in, so a constructed environment does not prevent it.

- **The credential-store legs skip in a stage whose environment has no session bus.** The legs print
  `[skip] no OS credential store …` and return (`crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs:535`, `:610`, `:625`); with
  `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` absent no Secret Service answers. A constructed environment holding `HOME`, `PATH` and
  the stage's own variables is that case, as `env -i` was (test-plan amendment
  `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`).

- **`ci-gates` over the seed reads four lines, none of them a fail.** The seed is one `app.boot.ready` record and
  two `ingest.tick` records 15 s apart (`pre_push.rs:44-51`): three records, no panic record, one tick gap of
  15 000 ms against 45 000 ms, no perf sample. The recorded reading of that stage, run natively: "zero-spans PASS (3
  records) · zero-panic PASS · heartbeat-gap PASS (max 15000 ms vs 45000 ms) · perf-budget NEUTRAL" (the operator
  pass above, row 31). The seed's doc comment still names "the perf-budget script's empty-metric-stream path"; that
  script was deleted at chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples and the grader is in-process.

- **`npm ci` does not write the lockfile** (npm's own contract for the command), so the `npm` stage's writes are
  `node_modules` and, through `npm run build`, `ui/dist`.
- none — the native path lives in the module that holds the verb today
- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` — the hop and the clone leave; the host guard, the provisioning check, the stage runner, the stage environment and the verdict document become native; the tests follow
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the verb's `about` text describes the native check

- Which Node major must the host hold for the check to evaluate: ci.yml's pin (24), which this host does not
  have, or the host's own (26)? → blocks: plan-decision — it decides whether the check can read green on this host
  without the operator installing a Node 24, and so whether P-103's verdict is reachable at /implement.

- How is the `test` stage's rewrite of the tracked bindings file undone now that no clone absorbs it: by putting
  back what the stage found, or by a regen stage after it? → blocks: plan-decision — it decides whether the check
  gains a stage and a feature-graph build on every run.

title: Scope — Pre-push check native on Linux

data.head: # Scope — Pre-push check native on Linux

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates
**Working entry (`working-route.md:17`):** "Pre-push check native on Linux — surviving stages run on the dev host; the
second-system hop and its distro clone leave (P-103, P-113)"
**Chunk base:** `8f655ca` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this sha, never HEAD: the
operator pre-CI commit moves HEAD before the wrap re-runs them.

Intent F16 (`andromeda-pulse-0.4.0/intent.md:396-399`) observes that `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` needs `wsl.exe` and
that on the Linux dev host its stages are run by hand, and expects "the check a developer runs before a push runs
natively on the Linux dev host over the stages that survive this version's removals". Requirement P-103 repeats it
(`requirements.md:73`), carried from 0.3.0 by the founder's ruling (`.andromeda/residuals.md:21`). This is the fourth
chunk of 0.4.0 and the second of the four entries that carry P-113.

- **The check runs natively on the Linux dev host and gives a verdict.** Read at take-up, at `8f655ca`:
  `xtask/src/pre_push.rs::drive` returns `cannot-evaluate` with reason `not-windows` on any host but Windows
  (`pre_push.rs:146-148`), so on this host the verb can only print that. After the chunk one invocation runs the
  stages on the host it is started on, with no second operating system involved.

- **The second-system hop and its distro clone leave** (the entry's words). Verified at P3, by reading
  `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` whole; the hop and the clone are:
  - the hop: the constants `WSL` and `DISTRO` (`:23-24`), `distro_home` (`:315-328`), and `Linux::cmd`, which wraps
    every stage command and every probe in `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --exec /usr/bin/env -i` (`:274-292`);
  - the clone: `CLONE_DIR` (`:25`), the distro-side half of `sync` (the clone, fetch, reset, clean, patch apply and the
    tree-id comparison, `:433-455`; its host-side half computes the tree id of HEAD plus the working tree through a
    temporary index, `:396-431`, and needs no second system), `cache`, the clone's own `target/` against a 40 GiB cap
    (`:26`, `:458-469`), and `wsl_path` with its test (`:487-501`, `:720-735`);
  - `NODE_BIN` (`:29-32`), the Viola repository's user-local Node install inside the distro, which the spec records
    as a cross-project fragility (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, the `pre-push:linux` row).
  - `rust_channel` stays whatever happens to the rest. Verified at P3 from the code graph (`tree-query` trace, rust
    plane, 2 rows): the module has two callers outside itself, `main` at `xtask/src/main.rs:342` (`run`) and the test
    `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` at `xtask/src/rust_floor.rs:69` (`rust_channel`).

- **The surviving stages run on the dev host** (the entry's words). The verb has six stages today, in order
  (`pre_push.rs:196-203`): `script-modes` · `source-lint` (`cargo xtask check:english-sources`) · `npm` (`npm ci`,
  then `npm run build`, in `pulse-app/ui`) · `clippy` · `test` (`cargo xtask test`) · `ci-gates` (over a seeded fresh
  data dir). First failure stops.
  - The chunk makes the check native for what stands TODAY and says, stage by stage, which later entry removes it; it
    removes no stage for a surface that still exists (inputs#I1 item 2).
  - [premise-corrected: inputs#I1 item 2 says "several of the six exist for the window and leave in Epoch 2
    (`Window's gates retired`)"; read from the stages and the route, no stage's subject is named by one entry alone,
    and three later entries share them.] Stage by stage, as read at P3 (`working-route.md:35`, `:42`, `:44`, `:46`,
    each entry's own words before its freight):
    - `script-modes` asserts `scripts/agent-run.sh` is git mode 100755, because CI runs it by path. The only workflow
      lines that do are the boot job's (`ci.yml:385-388`; `grep -n 'agent-run' .github/workflows/*.yml`: 3 lines), and
      "a11y and boot CI jobs … leave" at `Window's gates retired` (`:42`, P-083).
    - `source-lint` scans five roots (`xtask/src/source_lint.rs:24`). One of them, `pulse-app/ui/src`, is the webview
      interface that leaves at `Window retired` (`:44`, P-083). The stage has no entry that removes it.
    - `npm` installs the UI package and builds `ui/dist`, which Tauri embeds (`pulse-app/tauri.conf.json:7`). The
      "webview interface" leaves at `Window retired` (`:44`); the "npm tree" is named by `Desktop distribution
      retired` (`:46`, P-114).
    - `clippy` covers the whole workspace under `--all-features`. No entry removes it.
    - `test` runs the default-features workspace suite. Its credential-store legs leave with the "credential-store
      key" at `Corpus encryption at rest retired` (`:35`, P-085); its rewrite of the generated bindings leaves with
      the "IPC routers" at `Window retired` (`:44`), and the "bindings" checks at `Window's gates retired` (`:42`).
    - `ci-gates` grades a seeded log with the unchanged `cargo xtask ci-gates`. Its CI counterpart is a step of the
      boot job (`:42`), and its "frame" arm is named there too. No entry removes the verb itself.

- **What the hand-run of the six stages had to do on this host**, each "a fact for the plan and none a design"
  (inputs#I1 item 1; the same facts ride `.andromeda/residuals.md:21` as its items (a), (b), (c), (e)). Each evidence
  pointer was spot-checked at P3; none was re-run.
  - "stage 3 needed a fresh per-run `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` under `target/pre-push/` (the browser's extraction stopped
    partway even in a fresh cache)". Verified at P3 against
    `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-04-supply-chain-advisories-on-wasmtime-resolved/evidence/operator-pass.md`
    (rows 28: red on the shared cache, green on a fresh one) and against the host: `target/pre-push/` holds ten such
    caches, 963 MB each (`du -sh target/pre-push/puppeteer*`), 9.4 GB with their data dirs. The founder's ruling of
    2026-10-04 rides the residual: isolate the cache under `target/`, never delete the shared one. Why extraction
    stops is unmeasured. Item (e): plain `npm ci` exits 1 against the shared cache, `PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci`
    exits 0 (measured at 2026-10-06-npm-supply-chain-gate-is-green-again; not re-run).
  - "the bindings regen had to be re-run after stage 5". Verified at P3: the default-features workspace run rewrites
    `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to the no-mcp shape (test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline states the
    mechanism; the same operator pass records the clobber), and that file is tracked
    (`git check-ignore -q`: exit 1). The clone used to absorb the rewrite; natively it lands in the working tree.
  - "stage 5's `env -i` drops the session bus, so the credential-store tests skip there". Verified at P3 by pointer:
    the skip line stands at seven sites in four files (`grep -rn -c 'no OS credential store' crates pulse-app/tests`),
    and a clean skip is a pass that nextest's counts do not show (test-plan amendment
    `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`).

- **The provisioning check is written for an apt distro, and its package list is not what this host needs.**
  Verified at P3. It reads its pins from the repository (the Rust channel, ci.yml's `node-version` major, ci.yml's
  first `apt-get install` list) and probes `rustup`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo nextest`, `node --version`, `which` for
  four tools and `dpkg-query` for the apt list (`pre_push.rs:332-389`); a missing piece is `cannot-evaluate` with one
  `sudo apt-get install` line (`:591-598`). Measured on this host (`ID=omarchy`):
  - `dpkg-query` and `apt-get` are not on PATH; `pacman` is.
  - `libxdo` is absent (no `/usr/lib/libxdo*`, `pacman -Q xdotool`: not found) while ci.yml's list names
    `libxdo-dev`; the workspace builds and tests green on this host without it: `Cargo.lock` names no `libxdo` crate
    (`grep -n 'name = "libxdo' Cargo.lock`: no line), the release binary built today links none (`ldd … | grep -c
    xdo`: 0), and the previous chunk's report records clippy and the workspace suite green here (2826 passed,
    `chunks/2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed/report.md:301`, `:318`). The eight other libraries of
    the list answer `pkg-config --exists`.
  - Of the four probed tools, no stage calls `jq` or `xvfb-run` (`grep -rn -l -w jq` and `grep -rn xvfb-run` over
    `xtask`, `scripts`, `.github`: the only users are `pre_push.rs` itself, a criterion script and the CI boot step).
  - The `test` stage needs a Python 3 interpreter (`pulse-app/tests/unit_l4_grammar.rs` fails without one), which
    the check does not probe. `python3` is at `/usr/bin/python3`.
  - `node --version` prints `v26.8.2`, the only Node the host's `mise` holds, with npm 11.19.1; every job of `ci.yml`
    pins `node-version: '24'` (`ci.yml:65` and five more). The Rust channel 1.95.0 is installed and active.
  What the native check requires of the host, and how it names a missing piece, is the plan's.

- **The stages ran in a clone under `env -i`; natively they run where the developer works.** Verified at P3. Today
  every stage command gets `HOME`, a fixed `PATH` and one data dir, and "nothing of this host's environment crosses"
  (`pre_push.rs:271-273`, `:216-223`); the hand-runs kept that form with `env -i` (the last plan that carried them:
  `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-05-l4-runs-on-a-small-current-model-chosen-by-measurement/plan.md:382-415`).
  With the clone gone the stages read and write the working tree itself:
  - `npm ci` deletes and reinstalls `pulse-app/ui/node_modules`, and a failed run leaves it empty (the same operator
    pass: "The first stage-3 run removed `pulse-app/ui/node_modules` before failing"); `npm run build` rewrites
    `pulse-app/ui/dist`. Both are gitignored.
  - `clippy` and `test` build into the developer's `target/`.
  - `test` rewrites the one tracked file named above.
  - `ci-gates` reads the data dir the verb seeds: `seed` removes and recreates it, so the stage grades the three seed
    records alone (`pre_push.rs:472-483`, `:44-51`).
  The developer's shell on this host carries `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `DISPLAY` and
  `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, and no `RUST*`, `CARGO*`, `CC` or `PUPPETEER*` variable (`env`, names only).

- **The verdict contract is kept**: one pretty-JSON verdict on stdout with a twin at
  `target/pre-push/report.json`, exit 0 green · 1 red · 2 cannot-evaluate, a missing tool `cannot-evaluate` and never
  green, stage output on stderr, no stage starting `pulse-app` or binding a port (`pre_push.rs:1-11`). Verified at P3
  against architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces (the arch extract). Two of the verdict's members
  describe the clone (`cache{…}`, and `remediation` as one apt line); whether each stays is the plan's to state.

- [premise-corrected: the module holds ten tests, not nine — `grep -c '#\[test\]' xtask/src/pre_push.rs` reads 10.]
  **The module's own tests follow the code.** Those of a helper that leaves leave with it, and what the native path
  adds is pinned where `xtask`'s tests run (co-located, test-plan §2).

- **A timing the check takes on this host says under what load it was taken** (inputs#I1 item 5: other builders run
  heavy cargo here).

- **The records that describe a WSL-hosted check are corrected at the wrap, not here.** Phase amends no spec source;
  the plan carries them as expected amendments.

- **P-103 is this entry's own.** Its acceptance reads "On the Linux dev host one check runs natively before a push,
  over every stage that survives this version's removals, with no second operating system involved, and gives a
  verdict." Whether this chunk alone proves it is decided at P4 and P5.

- **P-113 is advanced, not claimed.** Its observed gap lists "the `wsl.exe` hop in `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`" among
  nine items; this chunk removes that one. Two later entries carry the rest: `One place on a node`
  (`working-route.md:33`) and `Other operating systems retired from the code` (`:56`). The ledger's note on P-113
  (2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone, phase P5) already names this split.

- **CI's own steps are not this chunk's** (inputs#I1 item 4). `No CI step reads nothing` (`working-route.md:19`,
  P-128) is the next entry. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is read for its pins and not edited.

- **No stage leaves for a surface that still exists** (inputs#I1 item 2). The window, its bridge and the credential
  store stand today; their stages stay until the entries that remove them.

- **No other retirement of another operating system.** The `.ps1` scripts, the `pwsh` spawns, the Windows path
  handling, the link hints, the linker override and the library-test workaround stay; they are
  `Other operating systems retired from the code`'s (`working-route.md:56`).
- **No sixth `agent-run` verb.** The check stays an `xtask` verb (test-plan §3's five-command discipline).

- **A boundary widening halts for the founder's own word** (inputs#I1 item 6). A stage that would reach something
  the check does not reach today (the session bus and through it the OS credential store, the developer's own data
  dir, a port) is a question, not a decision of this chunk.
- No run binds 4317 or 4318 without the operator's word (the handoff's host note). The check binds no port today.
- At P5 the plan card is printed and the phase stops for the operator's `yes` (inputs#I1 item 6).

- watch: the CI boot smoke ending by itself after ready — exit 1, no `app.exit` record, a fraction of a second after
  the webview's first calls; no cause named (1/11; since 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed). An
  observation: no acceptance criterion, no plan task, no gate entry. The block's own terms stand as written on the
  entry: on a recurrence read what the job kept (`harness-settled.json`, `xvfb.log`) and mint the entry that closes
  the named cause; retirement by count puts P-129 to the operator at that wrap's card; a reading is of equal source
  only while both tips stand; the two red runs' artifacts `11613618010` and `11632850540` expire 2026-10-23.
  - Readings at this take-up (inputs#I1 item 3), each from the boot job's own log, fetched to a file through
    `gh api --allow-escape-sequences …/actions/jobs/{id}/logs`: two more, both green and both `settled` (below). No
    recurrence. The tally is the wrap's to re-author.

title: Plan — 2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request: "Supply-chain job same on push and pull request"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request: "Supply-chain job same on push and pull request"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-09T16:25:19Z
- **Chunk base:** `b3e58597dbe9f10e541c0bc1d122b8647ba8c62a`. Every diff-shaped probe names it, never HEAD.
- **`main`:** `60ef43c6859cb35a9f9ee5664ab892339cffdf4f`, the base of the second branch.

- **Revised at P5** on the founder's ruling of 2026-10-09 (inputs#I3, inputs#I4): the witness is the push run on
  `main`; no trigger is added.

The `supply-chain` job of the `ci` workflow fails on a push and passes on a pull request for the same tree. The
cause is measured (research.md, the two job logs and the action's source at its pinned commit): the
`rustsec/audit-check` action tries to create a check run, the token may not write one, and the action swallows
that denial only on a pull-request event. It bites whenever the audit has something to report, and the tree
carries 10 informational warnings, so it bites on every push.

The chunk replaces the action with a plain `cargo audit` step. That step publishes nothing, receives no token and
reads no event, so it ends the same on both events by construction: exit 0 when clean, 1 on a vulnerability, 2 when
it could not evaluate. No permission is widened; the step's token input is removed (per security-plan §Secret
Management, GitHub Environment scoping; security-plan §Dependency Security, CI integration).

The repair lands in two places. On the build branch it ships with the chunk. A second branch, cut from `main`,
carries the same repair and the test that holds it, nothing else of 0.4.0, into a pull request the founder merges
by his own hand. His merge is a push to `main`; that push run is the witness, where the defect showed. **A green
pull-request run does not witness this repair** (inputs#I1 item 2): the old step passed there too. This departs
from the direction at `security-plan.md:226` for this repair, on the founder's ruling (founder, 2026-10-09, by
dialog — relayed verbatim by the pc overseer; inputs#I3).

1. **Write the shared pin first, in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`.** Two insertions, at places whose
   surrounding lines are the same on `main` (research.md), because the second branch must hold these hunks byte
   for byte:
   - in `ci_workflow_test_gates_no_continue_on_error`, add `"cargo audit",` on the line after `"cargo deny
     check",` (`quality_gate_workflow.rs:240`);
   - immediately before the `#[test]` of `ci_workflow_env_includes_ci_run_id` (`:277-278`), add
     `ci_workflow_audit_step_is_a_plain_run_step`. It cuts the `supply-chain` job with `workflow_job_block`, then
     the step whose name line is `      - name: cargo audit (RustSec advisory DB)`, up to the next `      - name: `
     line or the block's end. It asserts that the step holds the line `run: cargo audit` and holds no `uses:`, no
     `with:`, no `token`, no `continue-on-error` and no `||`; that the job block holds no `permissions:` key; and
     that the whole workflow holds no `rustsec/audit-check`. Its message names security-plan §Dependency Security
     (CI integration) and P-120.

2. **Read it red.** Run the one test binary, narrowed with `-E` under `--workspace` (never `-p`: test-plan
   amendment `2026-08-15-tier-1-incident-path-investigation`): `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci -E
   'binary(quality_gate_workflow)'`. The new test fails against the workflow as it stands (the step holds `uses:`
   and `token`). Record the failing line in `evidence/red-before.md`.

3. **Edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the audit step only** (`:426-429`): keep the name line and replace `uses:`,
   `with:` and `token:` by the one line `run: cargo audit`. The step is exactly two lines, with no comment line
   added, so the hunk is the same on both branches. The trigger block is not touched.

4. **Read it green.** The same command as step 2; all tests of the binary pass. Record the line beside the red
   reading.

5. **Capture the second branch's content now, before any build-only edit**, in the chunk's `evidence/` folder:
   - `main-hotfix.patch`: `git diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ b3e58597dbe9f10e541c0bc1d122b8647ba8c62a --
     .github/workflows/ci.yml pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, as it reads at this moment (2 files, 3
     hunks: the step, the gate-list line, the pin). The two prefix flags are stated because this host's git writes
     `c/` and `w/` otherwise (`diff.mnemonicPrefix` is true). The patch is never typed or edited by hand:
     research.md's trial shows that a pin differing by one token between the branches conflicts at the version's
     merge.
   - `main-hotfix-commit.txt`: the commit message for `main`. A conventional `fix(ci):` subject; a body saying
     what the step was and is, and naming the red push run `37907730264` on `60ef43c`; the attribution trailer the
     session's rules give.
   - `main-hotfix-pr.md`: the pull request's body. What it changes (the two files), why (the two runs), that it
     carries nothing else of 0.4.0 and leaves `main`'s three-system matrix as it is, how it was checked, and that
     the founder merges it; the attribution footer the session's rules give.

6. **Add the build-only pin**, `ci_workflow_triggers_are_pull_request_and_push_on_main`, immediately before the
   `#[test]` of `nextest_load_profiles_profile_preserves_zero_flake_posture` (`:148-149`). It reads the lines from
   `on:` to the next column-0 key and asserts that, comments and blank lines aside, they are exactly
   `  pull_request: {}`, `  push:` and `    branches: [main]`. It pins the block as it stands, so it is green from
   its first run; its control is step 7's mutation.

7. **Two one-shot mutations, each reverted before the gate block**, both readings of each in
   `evidence/mutation-checks.md`:
   - add `continue-on-error: true` to the audit step: `ci_workflow_test_gates_no_continue_on_error` and
     `ci_workflow_audit_step_is_a_plain_run_step` fail;
   - add `  workflow_dispatch: {}` to the trigger block: the trigger pin fails.

8. **Write the control lockfile** `evidence/audit-control.lock`: a version-3 lockfile of two packages, a root
   package `control` depending on `time`, and `time 0.1.43` from the crates.io registry (the content research.md
   measured). It is evidence, not source: it is not named `Cargo.lock`, so no dependency scanner reads it. Record
   `cargo audit --version` and the control's reading in `evidence/audit-control.md`, and say there that the
   control ran on this host, not on a runner.
9. **Run the gate block.** The operator pass follows /implement's report.
- none
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the audit step becomes a plain run step
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the audit-step pin, one more gate substring in the soft-fail ban, the trigger pin

The chunk's own probes come first, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order: `capability-drift` before the
default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, and
the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure. The operator pass follows.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No boot-smoke entry: neither file is on the boot-smoke trigger list (test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline), and
  the chunk boots no app. The boot smoke that matters here is the CI job, read in the operator pass.
- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched.

- No local pre-push gate: `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot run on this host (test-plan amendment
  `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`); CI is the gate each push meets.
- No liveness probe and no live leg: the chunk drives no external process (research.md, the harness slot).

- No targeted nextest entry: steps 2 and 4 run the one binary as the red-before-green pair; the workspace nextest
  entry runs the same tests on every re-run.

- Step 7's mutations edit the workflow and revert, so they are one-shots at implement; the three tests in the
  workspace nextest entry guard the properties on re-run.

- No local run of `main`'s tests on the second branch's tree: it would be a cold build of a second checkout. Its
  gate is its own pull-request run, which runs `main`'s whole workflow on three systems; the local entries prove
  only that the patch applies to `main` and equals what the build tree holds.

The control entry and the three patch entries read files steps 5 and 8 write: on the untouched tree those files
are absent and the entries read red. `cargo audit` reads the advisory database over the network. If an advisory is
published between two readings, a red there is the gate working, not this chunk's defect: it is recorded, not
re-run, and dispositioned at the wrap.
**The operator pass, in this order.**
1. The hygiene entry, then the pre-CI commit, then the build-branch push.

2. The second branch: one entry confirms `main` has not moved, cuts `hotfix/p-120-audit-step` from it in a scratch
   worktree, applies the patch, commits with the prepared message and removes the worktree. Two reads follow before
   anything else leaves the host: the branch differs from `main` in the two files only, and the build branch
   still merges cleanly into it. Then the branch is pushed and its pull request into `main` is opened, ready for
   review, not a draft.

3. The build branch's pull-request run is read, whole; then the second branch's pull-request run, whole. Each is
   followed by its audit step's conclusion and its report-only jobs listing, by run id, as `<id>`.

4. **The founder-attended stop.** When the second branch's run is green the pass stops and says so, with the pull
   request's number. The operator brings it to the founder. Nothing is merged and nothing is pushed to `main` by
   the pass. If that run is red in a job the repair does not touch, the reading is recorded as it stands and
   brought to the operator the same way; it is not re-run.

5. After his merge, on the operator's word: `main` is fetched and read to hold the repair; the push run on its new
   tip is read, scoped to the `supply-chain` check. This is the witness. Then that run by its id, as `<id>`: the
   audit step's conclusion, the job log holding cargo audit's scan line, the job log holding no check-run denial,
   the runner image lines (report-only, for the evidence), and the jobs listing (report-only).

6. The meeting of the branches on the real commits: the build branch merges cleanly into the new `main`; pull
   request #40's own mergeable word is recorded.

No run is re-run to obtain a green. The witness read is scoped to the `supply-chain` check so that it does not
hang on a job the repair does not touch; the jobs listing beside it says whether every job of that push run is
`success`, and the report states that word for `main` as a whole. `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` and the `a11y` rows
are read from all three listings and recorded as read; a red boot smoke on equal source is the folded watch's
recurrence and goes to the wrap.

Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry
writes one.

- (capability) `verification-matrix.json#P-120` — the push run on `main` that the founder's merge makes reads
  green in the `supply-chain` check (the `ci.py conclusion --sha origin/main` entry, asserting the `push` event),
  its `cargo audit (RustSec advisory DB)` step `success`, its job log holding cargo audit's scan line and no
  `Resource not accessible by integration` (the step entry and the two log entries); the pull-request run of the
  build branch is green on the same repair, its audit step `success` (the `--sha HEAD` read and its step entry);
  the step is `run: cargo audit` with no action, no token and no soft-fail (the audit-step probe and the pin
  `ci_workflow_audit_step_is_a_plain_run_step`); and `cargo audit --file` on the control lockfile ends 1 naming
  `RUSTSEC-2020-0071`, on this host (the control entry). The acceptance names both run ids.

- (security) The workflow-level `permissions:` block reads `contents: read` alone and no job carries a
  `permissions:` key — the base-comparison probe and the audit-step probe (per security-plan §Secret Management,
  GitHub Environment scoping; per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns, Secrets).

- (security) The edit adds or changes no `uses:` line and the workflow holds no `secrets.` reference — the
  diff-add probe and the `grep -c -E 'rustsec/audit-check|secrets\.'` entry (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns, Secrets; per security-plan §Bootstrap phases, `dep-security-ci-gate`).

- (security) The audit step turns red on an advisory above warning: the control entry ends 1 with one distinct
  `RUSTSEC-` id in its log. The tree that ships carries no change to `deny.toml`, no audit ignore flag and no
  lockfile change — the scope guard (per security-plan §Dependency Security, CI integration).

- (security) `step-security/harden-runner` remains the first step of `supply-chain` — the base-comparison probe:
  the audit step is the job's only step that differs (per security-plan §Bootstrap phases, `dep-security-ci-gate`).

- (arch) `ci.yml` still holds six jobs, each on `ubuntu-22.04`, with no matrix and no `needs:`, and its trigger
  block is unchanged — the two job probes and the base-comparison probe (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns
  → CI/CD approach).

- (arch) `supply-chain` writes no cache key and its `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` step is unchanged
  against `b3e5859` — the base-comparison probe and `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses` (per
  architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach).

- (arch) The chunk adds no Rust outside one test file, no workspace member and no environment variable — the scope
  guard (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Cargo workspace crate names).

- (tests) The standard gate set passes in order, closing with `git diff --quiet
  b3e58597dbe9f10e541c0bc1d122b8647ba8c62a -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` exit 0 (per test-plan §3
  Per-chunk gate discipline).

- (tests) Every test that reads `ci.yml` passes inside `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`, the two new
  pins, `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only` and `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses` among them (per

title: Mechanisms the plan rests on, each stated as the equality it needs and how it was read

data.head: ## Mechanisms the plan rests on, each stated as the equality it needs and how it was read

body:
- **The defect.** On a push, `rustsec/audit-check` v2.0.0 fails the step when the check-run create call is denied
  and there is something to report; on a pull request it does not. Frame: `src/reporter.ts:176-205` at the pin —
  `reporter.startCheck('queued')` inside a `try`; the `catch` prints and returns (or throws only on `stats.critical
  > 0`) when `process.env.GITHUB_HEAD_REF` is set, else `throw error`. `src/main.ts:87-89` returns before the
  reporter when nothing was found; `:98-102` routes every non-`schedule` event to `reportCheck`. Both arms are in
  the two logs above. `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` is set on a pull-request event and unset on a push: this is how GitHub
  describes its default variables, recalled and not fetched at P3; the two logs are consistent with it.

- **"Critical" in that action** is a vulnerability whose `advisory.informational` is null
  (`src/reporter.ts:95-107`); warnings never count (`:115-130`). So the step as it stands fails on a vulnerability
  and not on the 10 informational warnings.

- **The replacement's exits.** `cargo audit` on cargo-audit 0.22.2, measured on this host 2026-10-09 (the local
  `cargo audit --version` prints 0.22.2, the version the runner image lists):
  - a scratch lockfile of two packages naming `time 0.1.43`: exit 1, `ID: RUSTSEC-2020-0071`, `error: 1
    vulnerability found!` (read under the name `Cargo.lock` and again under another file name through `--file`:
    the same);
  - the project's `Cargo.lock`: exit 0, `Scanning Cargo.lock for vulnerabilities (916 crate dependencies)`,
    `warning: 10 allowed warnings found`; the 10 distinct ids are RUSTSEC-2024-0370, -2024-0429, -2024-0436,
    -2025-0075, -2025-0080, -2025-0081, -2025-0098, -2025-0100, -2025-0141, -2026-0221 (`grep -o` over the output,
    sorted unique), the same ten the pull-request log prints;
  - `--file` naming a file that does not exist: exit 2.
  The advisory database it read is the one under `~/.cargo/advisory-db` (`CARGO_HOME` is unset on this host, so the
  two spellings name one directory), 1296 advisories, the same count both CI logs print.

- **The same posture as today.** The action fails on a vulnerability only; plain `cargo audit` exits 1 on a
  vulnerability and 0 on informational warnings unless `--deny warnings` is passed. The plan passes no flag.

- **A `run:` step fails on a non-zero exit.** The Cranelift step of the same job relies on it (`ci.yml:436-437`,
  `… || exit 1`). No `continue-on-error` stands on the audit step, and the plan's pin keeps it so.

- **The founder's merge makes the push run that witnesses.** A merge into `main` is a push to `main`, and `ci.yml`
  runs on it (`:3-6`, the same block on `main`). The base's red run is the instance: `ci#37907730264`, event
  `push`, made by the merge of PR #39.

- **Three commits, three runs, and how the reader names each.** `ci.py conclusion` reads a sha's runs and prints
  each run's event in its `runs:` line (read on `60ef43c`: `runs: secret-scan#37907730180 push completed/success ·
  ci#37907730264 push completed/failure`; on `b3e5859`: `ci#37954318153 pull_request in_progress/-`; on `569604b`
  with `--wait 30 --name supply-chain`, a settled green: `569604be1f07 verdict: green · checks 1/7` and `runs:
  secret-scan#37945547982 pull_request completed/success · ci#37945548047 pull_request completed/success`). The
  build branch's tip, the second branch's tip and `main`'s merge commit are three different shas, so no read can
  meet another's run; each read still asserts its event word.

- **The second branch is the build branch's own diff, applied to `main`.** Measured in a scratch clone (git
  2.55.0; the project's repository not written): the diff of the build branch against `b3e5859` for the two
  files, taken when it holds only the audit-step edit, the pin and the gate-list line (3 hunks, 51 lines),
  passes `git apply --cached --check` on an index read from `60ef43c` (exit 0), and the tree it writes there
  equals the tree of the same edits made directly on `main` (`3809cc759901398ee34644e387734d5603bdee2a` both).
  `git apply` places the hunks by context, and the context is the same on both branches (above). Two facts about
  the patch file itself, measured there: this host's git writes its headers with the prefixes `c/` and `w/`
  (`git config --get diff.mnemonicPrefix`: true), so a count of files reads the `diff --git` lines (2), and the
  patch is taken with `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` to read the usual way; and `git apply --check --reverse`
  of the patch exits 1 on the build base without the edits, 0 on the edits plus the build-only pin, and 1 on a
  pin differing by one token.

- **How the two branches meet again, measured by trial merges** (`git merge-tree --write-tree`, the same scratch
  clone; `main-after` is `60ef43c` plus the second branch merged with a merge commit, as PR #39 was merged;
  `build-after` is `b3e5859` plus this chunk's edits):
  - `main-after` with `build-after`: clean, exit 0; the merged tree equals `build-after`'s tree, whole. The
    version's eventual merge takes the repair once and changes nothing else for it.
  - `main-after` with the build branch as it stands at `b3e5859`: clean, exit 0; the merged workflow holds one
    `run: cargo audit` line and no action line, the merged test file one pin. So pull request #40 keeps a
    computable merge even if `main` receives the repair before the build branch is pushed.
  - `60ef43c` with `b3e5859`, today: clean, exit 0.
  - The control, `main-after` with a build branch whose pin differs from `main`'s by one token (`token:` for
    `token`): exit 1, `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`. The clean
    readings hold only while the shared hunks are byte-identical.

- **Where the build-only pin goes.** The trigger pin is inserted before
  `nextest_load_profiles_profile_preserves_zero_flake_posture` (`quality_gate_workflow.rs:148-149`), inside the
  region the previous chunk already changed on the build side alone (`@@ -98,16 +98,50`); `build-after` in the
  trial carried it there and merged clean.

- **The cache and `main`'s workflow.** `main`'s workflow still holds the `release` job and the two matrices, so its
  runs restore, and may save, the keys the build branch no longer uses. The two rounds this chunk runs on that
  workflow are therefore expected to touch the four orphaned entries on `refs/heads/main`. A forecast: the wrap's
  cache listing measures it.

- `audit-check|actions-rust-lang/audit` over `*.md`, `*.yml`, `*.rs`, `*.toml`, `*.json` outside `target/`,
  `node_modules`, the chunk folders, the run dirs and the amendment sidecars: 12 hits · 1 changed (`ci.yml:427`) ·
  11 no-change — 2 spec-master lines corrected at the wrap (`security-plan.md:216`, `:259`); 4 lines of earlier
  phase artifacts under `.andromeda/phases/` (history); 2 handoff lines (the wrap's); `intent.md:403` and
  `verification-matrix.json:493` (their coordinate `:493-496` is the step's place on `main`, where it still
  stands); `working-route.md:13`, the frozen entry's own freight.

- `ci\.yml` readers (`grep -rln` over `*.rs`, `*.sh`, `*.ps1`, `*.yml`, `*.py`, `*.toml`, `*.json` outside
  `target/`, `.andromeda/` and the chunk folders): 6 files · 1 changed (`quality_gate_workflow.rs`) · 5 no-change
  — `a11y_perf_workflow.rs` and `pre_push.rs` read nothing the edit moves; `release.yml:47` and
  `update-channels.yml:69` name the file in a comment each; `verification-matrix.json` names it in P-120's
  `observed_gap` text.
- none
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the audit step becomes a plain run step
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the audit-step pin, one more gate substring in the soft-fail ban, the trigger pin
- none

title: Scope — Supply-chain job same on push and pull request

data.head: # Scope — Supply-chain job same on push and pull request

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates
**Working entry (`working-route.md:13`):** "Supply-chain job same on push and pull request — fails on a finding,
never on its own reporting; repair witnessed on a push (P-120)", with three freight blocks folded below.
**Chunk base:** `b3e5859` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this sha, never HEAD: the
operator pre-CI commit moves HEAD before the wrap re-runs them (inputs#I1 item 6).

Requirement P-120 reads: "the supply-chain job ends the same on a push as on a pull request; it fails on a finding
and never on its own reporting; the repair is witnessed where the defect shows" (`matrix.py show --id P-120`, read
at take-up). `main` has been red since the push that merged PR #39 (`60ef43c`). This chunk repairs the `cargo
audit` step of the `supply-chain` job on the build branch, carries the same repair to `main` through a separate
pull request the founder merges, and reads the push run his merge makes.

**The founder's ruling, 2026-10-09** (inputs#I3; founder, 2026-10-09, by dialog — relayed verbatim by the pc
overseer; the review word that brought it is inputs#I4). Asked whether the red `main` is repaired now by a separate
small pull request or stays red until the whole version merges, he picked «Чиним main сейчас (Рекомендую)». The
option as he read it: the builder prepares a separate pull request into `main` with this workflow repair alone and
the test that holds it; he merges it by his own hand; the real push to `main` reads green, and that push is the
witness of the repair where the defect shows. The cost he accepted: his hand on the merge, the chunk waits for it,
one more CI round on `main` with its three-system matrix, the plan rewritten, and a departure from
`security-plan.md:226` ("reaches `main` with the version") for this repair.

- **For the same tree, the `supply-chain` job ends the same on a push as on a pull request** (the entry). The step
  in question, read at take-up at `b3e5859`: `cargo audit (RustSec advisory DB)`, `rustsec/audit-check` pinned at
  `69366f33c96575abad1ee0dba8212993eecbe998` (v2.0.0), passed `token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`
  (`ci.yml:426-429`). The workflow's top-level `permissions:` is `contents: read` alone (`ci.yml:8-9`), and the job
  sets none of its own (`ci.yml:400-474`).

- **The step fails on a finding and never on its own reporting** (the entry). Both halves need a witness: a run
  that stays green when the report cannot be published, and a control that the step still turns red on an advisory.
  - Verified at P3: a green run alone cannot witness the second half, since a step that never fails also "ends the
    same" on both events. The control exists and discriminates. Measured on cargo-audit 0.22.2, the version the
    runner image lists (`Ubuntu2204-Readme.md`, image `20261004.315.1`, "Cargo audit 0.22.2"): a scratch lockfile
    naming `time 0.1.43` exits 1 with `RUSTSEC-2020-0071` and `error: 1 vulnerability found!`; the project's own
    lockfile exits 0 with `warning: 10 allowed warnings found`; an unreadable lockfile exits 2. Three exits, and
    "cannot evaluate" is not a pass. The control is local, on this host; the operator accepted that (inputs#I3,
    point 3), and the report says so.

- **The repair is witnessed on a push, where the defect showed** (the entry; P-120's third clause).
  - Verified at P3: the build branch gets no push-event run. `ci.yml:3-6` triggers on `pull_request` and on a push
    to `main` only, and the branch's 12 runs are all `pull_request` events (`gh api
    …/actions/runs?branch=build/andromeda-pulse-0.4.0`, grouped by event, read 2026-10-09T16:03Z). A green
    pull-request run does not witness the repair, and the plan says so (inputs#I1 item 2).
  - [premise-corrected: the founder's ruling of 2026-10-09, inputs#I3] **The witness is the push run on `main`
    that the founder's merge makes.** The plan first read at P5 obtained the witness on a dedicated ref through a
    new `push-witness/**` trigger and left `main` red; both are withdrawn. The trigger block of `ci.yml` stays as
    it is.
  - Added at P5: **a second branch carries the same repair to `main`.** It is cut from `origin/main` (`60ef43c`,
    equal to the remote's `refs/heads/main`, re-read at P5) and holds the audit-step change and the test that holds
    it, nothing else of 0.4.0. Its pull request into `main` is opened ready for the founder's merge; the builder
    never merges it and never pushes to `main`. `main`'s workflow keeps its three-system matrix and its seven jobs;
    that is not this chunk's to change there.
  - Added at P5: **the operator pass has a founder-attended stop.** After the second branch's pull-request run is
    green the pass stops and says so; the operator brings it to the founder; after his merge the pass reads the
    push run on `main` and its `supply-chain` job. That reading, named by run id, is P-120's witness.
  - Added at P5: **the two branches meet again without a conflict, measured.** Trial merges in a scratch clone
    (git 2.55.0, nothing pushed, the project's repository not written): with the repair byte-identical on both
    sides, the version's merge into a `main` that already holds it is clean and the merged tree equals the build
    branch's tree; a `main` that holds it merged with the build branch as it stands today is clean too, so the
    draft pull request #40 keeps a computable merge and its runs keep firing whichever lands first. The control: a
    pin that differs by one token between the two branches conflicts in the test file. So the second branch is
    made from the build branch's own diff, never typed twice.

- **The cause is now a measured fact of this chunk.** Two sources stated it; both are closed against the two runs
  and the action's source at its pinned commit:
  - Verified at P3, with one correction of precision. The relay's `hypothesis:` read "on a push the step tries to
    create a check run the token may not write; on a pull request the same denial is swallowed" (inputs#I1 item 1).
    Push run `37907730264` on `60ef43c`, job `113745162405`: the token reads `Contents: read`, `Metadata: read`
    (log `:23-24`); the step prints `No vulnerabilities were found`, `10 warnings found!`, `Found 8 unmaintained, 2
    unsound`, then `##[error]Resource not accessible by integration - …/checks/runs#create-a-check-run` (`:657-660`)
    and fails; the nine steps after it are `skipped`. Pull-request run `37904682919` on `0e45d58`, job
    `113735187440`: the same token and the same three lines, then `##[error]Unable to publish audit check! Reason:
    HttpError: Resource not accessible by integration`, "Posting audit report here instead." and `No critical
    vulnerabilities were found, not marking check as failed` (`:698-701`, `:889`); the step succeeds. The source
    (`src/reporter.ts:176-205` at the pin) catches the failed check-run call and falls back to printing only when
    `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` is set, which is every pull-request event; otherwise it rethrows. [premise-corrected: the
    denial bites only when there is something to report. `src/main.ts:87-89` returns before any API call when the
    audit finds no vulnerability and no warning; the tree carries 10 informational warnings, so the call is made on
    every run today.]
  - Verified at P3: the matrix's `observed_gap` states the same mechanism, and it holds. Its second coordinate
    names the step where `main` has it (`ci.yml:493-496` at `60ef43c`, re-read at P5); on the build branch the step
    stands at `ci.yml:426-429`.

- **The repair widens nothing.** Verified at P3: the step becomes a plain `run: cargo audit`, with no third-party
  action and no token. The binary is on the runner as the job stands (the push log calls
  `/home/runner/.cargo/bin/cargo audit` 0.15 s after the action starts, with no install); the operator accepted the
  step without an install (inputs#I3, point 4), and the runner image's version is recorded in the evidence. The
  workflow-level `permissions:` block and every job's token stay as they are, and the step no longer receives the
  token at all. The widening that would also turn the push run green, a job-level `checks: write`, is not needed
  and would not meet the entry: with it the push path still fails whenever the check-run call fails
  (`src/reporter.ts:204`), so the job would still end on its own reporting. No boundary widening is planned
  (inputs#I1 item 3, inputs#I2; the playbook's pattern at `.andromeda/playbook.md:118`).

- **What reads `ci.yml` in the tree is kept true.** Verified at P3 (`grep -rln 'ci\.yml'` over the Rust, script,
  workflow, manifest and JSON files outside `target/`, `.andromeda/` and the chunk folders): two test files and one
  xtask module read the workflow's content.
  - `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs:151-160` pins `permissions:` and `contents: read` inside the first 40
    lines; `:119-149` pins every `uses:` line to a 40-character sha.
  - `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs:131-146` pins the `supply-chain` job's auditable build; `:233-276`
    bans `continue-on-error: true` on a listed set of gate commands, and `cargo audit` is not in the list. No test
    pins the audit step's action, its token or the trigger block.
  - `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` reads the Node major and the first `apt-get install` list; the repair touches neither.
  - Read at P5 on `main` (`60ef43c`): the same holds there. `a11y_perf_workflow.rs`, `xtask/` and `Cargo.lock` are
    byte-identical on the two branches; `main`'s `quality_gate_workflow.rs` has the helper and the soft-fail ban
    the pin needs, and no test of `main` pins the action or the token.

- **No other workflow carries the step.** Verified at P3 (`grep -n -E 'audit-check|rustsec'` over the four workflow
  files: one line, `ci.yml:427`). `secret-scan.yml:29` hands the token to gitleaks as an environment variable; its
  push run on `60ef43c` succeeded (`secret-scan#37907730180`), so it does not share the defect. `release.yml` and
  `update-channels.yml` hold no audit step.

- Added at P3, re-cut at P5: **the pins, in the test file that already pins the workflow.**
  - On both branches, identical: the audit step is a plain `run:` step with no action, no token input and no
    soft-fail, and the job carries no `permissions:` block; `cargo audit` joins the no-`continue-on-error` list. The
    pin is written before the edit and read red against the workflow as it stands.
  - On the build branch only: the trigger block is pinned as it stands, `pull_request` and a push to `main`, so no
    other event can be added unseen.

- **The records that describe this step are corrected at the wrap, not here.** Phase amends no spec source. The
  known sites: security-plan §Dependency Security, CI integration (`security-plan.md:216`) and §Bootstrap phases
  `dep-security-ci-gate` (`:259`), both naming `actions-rust-lang/audit`; `security-plan.md:226`, whose direction
  this repair departs from on the founder's ruling; architecture's CI/CD approach key file, for the step and the
  cache reading; test-plan §9's Supply chain row, which names no `cargo audit` step at all.

- **`No CI step reads nothing` (P-128) is two entries later** (`working-route.md:17`): the baseline downloads and
  the uploads that find no file are its work, not this chunk's, even with the same file open (inputs#I1 item 5).

- **`boot`, `a11y`, `lint-test`, `mcp-test` and `coverage` are not touched**, on either branch. Inside
  `supply-chain`, the `cargo deny` step, the npm gate and the auditable build are not this chunk's subject.

- **`main` receives the repair and its test, nothing else.** Its three-system matrix, its `release` job and its
  other tests stay as they are; they leave `main` when the version reaches it.

- **The builder never merges the pull request into `main` and never pushes to `main`.** The merge is the
  founder's hand (inputs#I3).
- **Nothing outside the tree is deleted.** The six orphaned cache entries are re-read at the wrap, not removed.
- **A boundary widening halts for the founder's own word**, at P4 (inputs#I1 item 3, inputs#I2). None is planned.

title: Plan — 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine: "Agent harness drives the console engine"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine: "Agent harness drives the console engine"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T15:18:02Z
- **Chunk base:** `8394da4f2585e9ba7c5b2f197c4fa3e81f393d35`. Every diff-shaped probe names this sha, never HEAD.

The console engine, `andromeda-pulse-engine`, has existed since the chunk before this one, and the agent harness
still builds, spawns and grades the window app alone. This chunk aims the harness at the engine: `boot engine`
starts it, `status engine` says whether it is up, `cleanup` ends it by signal and `logs` reads its log, and a
check over that log grades the run on the four readings the entry names (no panic, no heartbeat stall, exactly
one process-end record, the memory budget) plus the drain-progress reading the entry carries (per test-plan §3
5-command implementation, obs-plan §10 CI gates, obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks).

Research found that most of the harness already serves either program: `status`, `cleanup`, `logs` and
`harness:ready` act on the pid file, the log family and the two ports, which both programs write the same way.
Only `boot` names a binary, and only `harness:settled` waits for window records. So the work is three things.
First, `boot` and `status` take the program as a word, and the verdict they read names the program the log
itself records, so a verb pointed at the wrong program's data dir says so instead of grading it. Second, a new
check reads the engine's log after the run has ended, with every arm pinned red on a constructed log, and a
second new verb holds the run until its log holds what the check reads — a boot of a few seconds holds one tick
per target and could never fail a gap check. Third, one cycle verb runs the whole sequence on its own data dir
and ports; the gate block runs it on the dev host and the `boot` CI job runs it on every push, which is what
makes the heartbeat reading of obs-plan §10 enforced by a CI step again.

The freight was cut in two at P4 on the operator's answer (inputs#I2). The second entry, which the operator
mints at this chunk's wrap, holds what is listed under "Left for the second chunk". P-086 is advanced by this
chunk and not claimed.

title: How five verbs serve two programs until Epoch 2 (inputs#I1 item 2)

data.head: ## How five verbs serve two programs until Epoch 2 (inputs#I1 item 2)

body:
- `boot` with no word starts the window app, as today. `boot engine` starts the console engine. Any other word
  is usage, exit 2.
- `status` with no word reads the window app's run; `status engine` reads the engine's.

- `cleanup` and `logs` take no word. They act on the data dir they are given: the pid the pid file holds, the
  two resolved ports, the log family. What keeps them on the right program is the data dir, one per run.
- `run` is the test suite, unchanged; it already runs the engine through `integration_console_engine`.

- `cargo xtask harness:settled` stays the window's until `Window's gates retired` (`working-route.md:48`): its
  verdict needs four window records. The engine's counterpart is `harness:engine-settled`.

- What forbids a verb from quietly grading the wrong program: every verdict that grades a run reads the
  `app.boot.engine` record of that run's own log, whose `program` field is `window` or `console`
  (`pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs:415`), and compares it with the program it was asked for. `boot` and `status`
  always ask (the bare word asks for `window`), so nothing is implied. A mismatch is the verdict
  `wrong-program`, exit 1; a log with no such record is a mismatch too.

title: Finding and ending the engine (inputs#I1 item 4)

data.head: ## Finding and ending the engine (inputs#I1 item 4)

body:
The verbs find the engine by `run/andromeda-pulse.pid` under the data dir they are given, which the engine
writes itself, and end it with SIGTERM through `cleanup` (SIGKILL after five seconds). `One place on a node`
(`working-route.md:39`) replaces both: operator-set places for the pid file, the stores and the log, and a
`stop` command. No command word is added here.

Each new arm's pin is written first and run red before the code that turns it green (the targeted entry of the
gate block is the vehicle; both readings go to `evidence/`).

1. **The injector takes its port from the registered variable.** In `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs`
   the endpoint port comes from `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` (unset: 4317, as today; a value that is not a
   port from 1 to 65535: a usage error, exit 2, nothing sent). The host stays `127.0.0.1`. The decision is a
   pure function with pins in the example's own `mod tests`, which the workspace run collects
   (`crates/ingest/Cargo.toml:74-77`).

2. **The status verdict names its program.** In `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` add a pure reader that returns
   the `program` of the LAST `app.boot.engine` record in the log family (`window`, `console`, or `unknown` when
   the family holds none or the field is anything else). The verdict JSON gains a seventh member, `program`.
   `run` takes the asked program as an optional argument: when one is asked and the reading differs, the
   verdict is `wrong-program`, exit 1. `cannot-evaluate` (paths unresolvable) and `not-running` (no pid, or a
   dead one) keep precedence: a run that is not there is not graded. `classify` keeps its signature
   (13 test sites call it; research, Graph impact). Pins: the reader on a constructed family (last record
   wins, none is `unknown`, a non-family file beside it is not read), and the decision per arm.

3. **Readiness carries the same reading.** In `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` `run_ready` takes the asked program
   and passes it on; its JSON gains the `program` member; `decide_ready` maps a `wrong-program` status to the
   verdict `wrong-program`, exit 1. `run_settled` and its eight-member verdict are not touched. Pins per arm.

4. **The engine's log check and its settle read**, new file `xtask/src/engine_log.rs`, two verbs.
   - `cargo xtask harness:engine-settled [--timeout-seconds N]` (default 60; below 20 refused as
     `cannot-evaluate`, since one tick interval is 15 s). It polls the pid and the log family until the log is
     gradeable: the boot record reads `console`, the pid is alive, the family holds at least two records of
     each of `ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick` and `connection.tick`, and at least one `metric.buffer.memory_bytes`
     sample with a non-zero `value`. Verdicts: `settled` exit 0 · `ended` (the pid is dead) exit 1 ·
     `wrong-program` (the record reads `window`) exit 1 · `not-settled` (the timeout passed) exit 1 ·
     `cannot-evaluate` exit 2. One JSON object on stdout with the members
     `verdict`, `pid`, `program`, `ingest_ticks`, `buffer_ticks`, `connection_ticks`, `memory_samples_populated`.
     It writes no file.
   - `cargo xtask check:engine-log` reads the log family under the resolved data dir after the run has ended,
     and the harness's exit record beside the pid file through the existing bounded reader `read_ended`. It
     prints one line per arm and a last line `engine-log: PASS`, `engine-log: FAIL` or
     `engine-log: cannot-evaluate`; exit 0 · 1 · 2. A FAIL on any arm is exit 1; with no FAIL, a
     cannot-evaluate on any arm is exit 2. Lines carry closed labels, counts, a member's file name and a line
     number — never a record's text, a path or an environment value. The arms, in order:
     - **family** — no `agent-latest.jsonl*` member: cannot-evaluate, nothing else graded. Members that hold no
       record: FAIL.
     - **program** — the family holds exactly one `app.boot.engine` record and it reads `console`: PASS. It
       reads `window`: FAIL. None: cannot-evaluate. More than one: cannot-evaluate (one cycle per data dir; a
       gap read across two boots would be false).
     - **panic** — an `app.panic.fatal` record at ERROR: FAIL, named by file name and line. The predicate is
       the one `ci_gates.rs:85` holds; share it, do not copy it.
     - **heartbeat-gap** — for each of the three engine tick targets: fewer than two records is
       cannot-evaluate; a gap over 45 000 ms between two consecutive records of one target is FAIL, naming the
       target and the gap; else PASS with the largest gap. `viz.tick` and `plugins.tick` are not graded.
     - **progress** — `ingest_progress::evaluate` over the family: a stall announcement that is not a recovery
       is FAIL; no `buffer.tick` is cannot-evaluate; and a run whose largest `rows_ingested` is 0 is FAIL (no
       span landed).
     - **process-end** — exactly one `app.exit` record, and it is the last record of the family: PASS. Two or
       more, or a record after it: FAIL. None: FAIL, on one of two named arms — `unloggable-end` when the
       harness's exit record reads `signal 9 (KILL)`, `end-not-recorded` otherwise.
     - **budget** — the memory arm of `perf_budget` (`grade_arm`, `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs:166`), required:
       over 512 000 000 B, a non-numeric field, no sample or only zero samples are each FAIL. One line says the
       frame and snapshot arms are not graded for a console engine, which has no producer for either.
   Pins, each a constructed log family in a temp dir: every arm red on its failing input, green on a passing
   one, and every cannot-evaluate input; the whole check green on one complete console log; the same verdict
   with an unrelated file beside the family; the exit code per overall verdict; the floor of the settle
   timeout. A red input for the heartbeat arm holds no ERROR record: the defect is block-shaped.

5. **The two verbs and the two flags are wired** in `xtask/src/main.rs`: the module lines, `--program` on
   `harness:status` and `harness:ready` (values `window`, `console`), `harness:engine-settled`,
   `check:engine-log`, and the cycle verb of step 7.

6. **`boot` and `status` take the program word**, in `scripts/agent-run.sh` (git mode 100755 kept).
   - `boot` with no word: as today, and its readiness poll now asks `--program window`.
   - `boot engine`: pre-builds `cargo build --bin andromeda-pulse-engine --release` and xtask outside the timed
     window, spawns `target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine run` by path under the same waiting wrapper (the
     spawn record and the exit record are written as for the window app), and polls
     `cargo xtask harness:ready --program console`. It never reads `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB`: the
     engine's spawn line carries no preload whatever the variable holds, and no witness file is created.
   - `status engine` threads `--program console`; `status` with no word threads `--program window`.
   - The usage text names the two forms. `cleanup`, `logs` and `run` are not edited.
   `scripts/agent-run.ps1` is not edited: no job and no host runs it, and it leaves with `Other operating
   systems retired from the code`. The engine arm is sh-only, like the exit-witness arm before it.

7. **One cycle as a verb**, new file `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs`:
   `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle [--data-dir DIR] [--grpc-port N] [--http-port N]`. Defaults: a fresh
   `target/engine-cycle/` directory named by the UTC second it starts, ports 24317 and 24318. It refuses, as
   `cannot-evaluate` exit 2 and before anything is started: port 4317 or 4318, a data dir that already holds a
   log family, a host that is not Linux. Then, in order: build the injector
   (`cargo build -p ingest --example inject_demo`); `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot engine`; start
   `target/debug/examples/inject_demo --sustained --error-pct=0` by path; `harness:engine-settled`; end the
   injector by its own child handle; `bash scripts/agent-run.sh status engine`;
   `bash scripts/agent-run.sh cleanup`; `check:engine-log`. `cleanup` runs whatever the verbs before it
   returned, and after a failed `boot` the verbs between are skipped. Every child gets a cleared environment
   plus a fixed set, pinned by set equality: `HOME`, `PATH`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`,
   `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT`,
   `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_RETENTION_SECONDS` (60, so the first retention sweep, which sets the memory gauge, runs at
   10 s) and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` (a value made for the run, never printed or written), and
   `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` only when the verb's own environment holds it — passed on so that the
   run shows `boot engine` ignoring it. No session bus, runtime dir or display variable, so no child reaches
   the credential store. The verdict is one JSON object with the members `verdict` (`pass` | `fail` |
   `cannot-evaluate`), `boot`, `settled`, `status`, `cleanup`, `check` (each the verb's exit, or null when
   skipped), `error_records` (the count of ERROR records in the family) and `witness_file` (`absent` |
   `present`). `pass`, exit 0, needs all five exits 0, `error_records` 0 and `witness_file` `absent`. The
   children's own output passes through, so the check's lines are in the verb's output. Pins: the refusals,
   the child environment's set, the verdict decision per arm, and the member set.

8. **The pre-push seed's doc comment is made true** in `xtask/src/pre_push.rs:30-31`: it says the seed holds
   one boot record and two ticks and that the stage reads the record count and the panic read over it. The
   stage itself is not changed here.

9. **The `boot` job runs the cycle and keeps the engine's log**, in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after the
   `cargo xtask ci-gates` step: a step named `Console engine cycle` with `if: always()` running
   `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle --data-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/andromeda-pulse-engine-data"`, and after the
   existing upload a second upload with `if: always()`, the name `logs-engine-` followed by the runner's
   system, the path of that data dir's `logs/` and `if-no-files-found: error`. No soft-fail key, no
   third-party action beyond the upload action already pinned by sha, no word `windows` on any line. The job's
   release build already builds the engine binary. Pins in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`: the
   step exists in the `boot` job, runs that verb on a data dir of its own, runs whatever the steps before it
   returned, sits after `ci-gates`, carries no soft-fail key; the upload exists under its own name.

10. **The live readings.** Run the cycle entry of the gate block on the dev host and keep its output in
    `evidence/`; run the window smoke entry, since the window path of `boot` and `status` now asks for its
    program.
- `xtask/src/engine_log.rs` — `check:engine-log` and `harness:engine-settled`, with their pins
- `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs` — `harness:engine-cycle`, with its pins
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — the program word on `boot` and `status`; the engine spawn; the witness never on the engine
- `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` — the `program` member and the `wrong-program` arm
- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` — the same reading in the readiness verdict
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the two flags, the three verbs, the two module lines
- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` — the seed's doc comment
- `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` — the endpoint port from the registered variable
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the cycle step and the engine log upload in the `boot` job
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — pins for both

The chunk's own guard, pins and two live entries come first, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order
(`capability-drift` before the default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen
as the last cargo-adjacent step, the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure), then
the local pre-push check, then the operator pass.

**The engine cycle** is the runtime gate of this chunk. It starts its own engine and ends it, on ports 24317
and 24318 and a fresh data dir under `target/engine-cycle/`; it never binds 4317 or 4318. The entry first
builds the exit-witness library and names it in the verb's environment, so the run shows `boot engine` leaving
it unloaded.

**The window smoke** is listed because the window path of `boot` and `status` changes (the program is now
asked). It is the series of two boots on this host in its recorded form: each under its own virtual display,
the receivers on 14317 and 14318, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset, a fresh data dir under `target/boot-smoke/`.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No product boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `engine_boot.rs`, `console.rs`, `observability.rs`), so no
  boot-smoke gate is owed for the product; the two live entries above are the harness's own.

- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched. The `a11y` job's verdict
  is read from the operator pass's run.

- No local `cargo audit` or `cargo deny` entry: no dependency is added and the scope guard holds `Cargo.lock`
  unchanged; the `supply-chain` job reads both on the operator pass's run.
- No one-shot mutating control: each arm's red reading is a committed pin on a constructed log.

- No retry anywhere. A cycle that reads red, or a boot that ended by itself, stops the pass and goes to the
  operator.

**The operator pass, in this order.** The hygiene entry; the pre-CI commit; the local pre-push check again;
the merge-base probe; the build-branch push; the CI read of the pushed tip, asserted green; the run's
`logs-boot-Linux` artifact, with the series verdict, the smoke's settle verdict, every kept witness file read
whole and the window's boot record; the run's `logs-engine-Linux` artifact, graded again by
`check:engine-log` on this host. A line of a witness file holding anything beyond its shape stops the pass. A
red is fixed by a further commit on top and read again.

body:
- (tests) `boot engine` starts `target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine run` by path and returns 0 on the
  `ready` verdict asked with `--program console`; `status engine` reads `running-healthy` on it; `cleanup`
  prints `cleanup: clean`; shown by the entry `… cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` reading
  `"verdict": "pass"` on ports 24317 and 24318 (per test-plan §3 5-command implementation).

- (tests) A verb asked for one program and pointed at a run of the other reads `wrong-program`, exit 1, and a
  log with no boot record reads the same; pinned per arm in `harness_status.rs` and `harness_ready.rs`, run by
  `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --no-tests=fail` (per test-plan §3 PID file).

- (obs) Each arm of `check:engine-log` is pinned FAIL on a constructed log before the check is read green:
  a panic record at ERROR; a gap over 45 000 ms between two consecutive ticks of one engine target; a stall
  announcement, and a run where no span landed; zero, two, and a not-last `app.exit`; a memory sample over
  budget, no sample, and only zero samples. Run by the entry
  `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --no-tests=fail -E 'package(xtask) and test(/^(engine_log|engine_cycle)::/)'`,
  red before the code and green after, both readings in `evidence/` (per obs-plan §10 CI gates).

- (obs) No arm reads PASS over an input it cannot grade: an absent log family, fewer than two ticks of a
  target, no `buffer.tick`, no boot record and two boots in one family each read cannot-evaluate, exit 2; a
  log whose boot record reads `window` fails; `viz.tick` and `plugins.tick` are never graded on a console log
  (per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks; obs-plan §10 Load-profile constraints).

- (security) A run ended by SIGKILL lands on the named arm `unloggable-end` and a run with no exit record on
  `end-not-recorded`, both FAIL; no line of the check or of the three verdict objects holds a path, a record's
  text or an environment value, and each object's member set is pinned (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Logging; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input).

- (security) The engine's spawn line carries no preload: the cycle run with the witness library named reads
  `"witness_file": "absent"`; the cycle's children get the pinned environment set and no session bus; the
  console program's command line is still `run` | `version` (the scope guard holds `pulse-app/src` unchanged)
  (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input; security-plan §Input Validation).

- (arch) The chunk's code lands in `xtask/`, `scripts/agent-run.sh`, one dev example and tests, with no new
  workspace member, no new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` name and no product source changed; the scope-guard entry
  prints nothing (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Cargo workspace crate names; architecture §Occupied
  Resources → Environment variables).

- (tests) The `boot` job runs `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` on every push, whatever its earlier steps
  returned, with no soft-fail key, and uploads the engine's log family under its own name, failing on no
  file; pinned in `quality_gate_workflow.rs`; witnessed by the run the entry
  `python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 2700` reads
  green, whose run id the report names, and by the operator entry that grades the downloaded
  `logs-engine-Linux` artifact again (per test-plan §9 Build failure conditions; obs-plan §9 Telemetry
  artifact handling).

- (a11y, tests) The window app's harness path stands: the window smoke entry reads `all-settled` on two
  boots, the `a11y` job's steps and artifact names are unchanged and no path under `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/`
  is in the diff (the scope guard), and bare `boot` still starts the window app, so every a11y-plan sentence
  that says so stays true (per a11y-plan §3 CI integration; a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).

- (tests) The standard gate set passes in the listed order, and
  `git diff --quiet 8394da4f2585e9ba7c5b2f197c4fa3e81f393d35 -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` exits 0
  after the regen (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

- **P-086 is advanced, not claimed** (`verification-matrix.json#P-086`). Shown by this chunk: the engine,
  started by a harness verb with no display variable and no session bus, runs detached from its starter, is
  found by its pid file, answers a state read, takes telemetry over its gRPC receiver and is ended by signal,
  and its own log is graded on every push. Not shown, and carried by `working-route.md:37`, `:43`, `:45` and
  `:81`: running in the background as a service; every kind of finding 0.3.0 detected; one incident for a
  sustained storm; automatic resolution.

  discipline · test-plan §9 Pipeline structure · test-plan §9 Build failure conditions · test-plan §1 Pending
  coverage triggers · obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks · obs-plan §7 Error classes captured · obs-plan §9 Telemetry
  artifact handling · obs-plan §10 CI gates · obs-plan §10 Load-profile constraints · obs-plan §10 Performance
  budgets · architecture §Occupied Resources (xtask CLI surfaces, Process / service identity, Environment
  variables, Filesystem locations, Network ports) · architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach ·
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input and → Logging · security-plan §Input Validation · a11y-plan
  §3 CI integration.

- Research files inspected: `scripts/agent-run.sh`, `xtask/src/harness_status.rs`,
  `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, `xtask/src/ci_gates.rs`, `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs`,
  `xtask/src/ingest_progress.rs`, `xtask/src/main.rs`, `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`,
  `xtask/src/harness_series.rs`, `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.sh`, `pulse-app/src/console.rs`,
  `pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs`, `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs`, `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs`,
  `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs`, `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs`.
- External inputs: inputs#I1 (the operator's phase directive), inputs#I2 (the operator's answers at P4).
- A new variable to select the program — a second word on the verb needs no new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` name.

- A sixth `agent-run` verb, or a cycle script beside it — test-plan §3 places a check outside the five verbs
  as a `cargo xtask` verb.

- Re-arming `cargo xtask ci-gates` with heartbeat and budget arms — its contract says two arms over the
  window boot's log, where neither could fail; the engine's readings live in their own verb.

- Calling `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.sh` for the engine — it ignores `connection.tick` and passes on no
  tick and on one tick. The script and its one caller are not touched.
- `harness:settled` given a console arm — its eight-member verdict is pinned and it leaves with the window.

- A trigger in the product for a panic or an exit — retired on the operator's answer (inputs#I2); a product
  input added for the harness is the playbook's Boundary widening pattern.

- The exit witness on the engine's spawn line — its classification is PROVISIONAL and stated for the window
  app's spawn alone.

- Loosening `check:ingest-progress`'s own NEUTRAL arm — it is listed unconditionally in every gate block,
