  5 additions applied: 2026-08-23 (`run` is the test suite, never a telemetry send; one exported data dir per leg;
  the producer built first and run by path), 2026-08-30 (a default data dir keyed on `$$` differs per invocation,
  so one exported `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` serves every verb of a cycle), 2026-08-28 (a leg's window must outlast
  the threshold its verdict reads), 2026-08-29 (a harness's negative finding needs a second source), 2026-05-14
  (a log dir reused across boots carries earlier records into a family read).

- **Platform issues consulted:** none — no runner-only bullet (the one run read at take-up was in progress, not
  red) and no CI-reading entry outside the operator leg.

- **External inputs:** `inputs#I1` — the operator's phase directive for this chunk (eight points) ·
  `inputs#I2` — the operator's three answers at P4 (the cut, C4's first half retired, the three harness readings
  classified routine).

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` (full, 300 lines) — the five verbs. `boot` is the only verb that names a program
  (`cargo build --bin pulse-app --release` at :61, `APP_BIN="target/release/pulse-app"` at :77); it loads the exit
  witness onto the spawn line when `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` names a file (:48-55, :94-96). `status`
  (:169-177) shells `cargo xtask harness:status`; `cleanup` (:179-265) ends the pid the pid file holds with TERM,
  a 5 s liveness poll, then KILL, and takes its token from pid liveness and the two resolved ports; `logs`
  (:267-290) resolves the `agent-latest.jsonl*` family. None of the last three names a program.
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` (the two program names, :133, :155) — the mirror; no job and no dev host runs it.

- `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` (:1-260) — `run()` takes no argument; `classify(pid, alive, newest_log)` is pure;
  the verdict JSON has six members; `read_ended` is the bounded exit-record reader.

- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` (outline) — `run_ready()` = the status verdict plus a TCP accept on both resolved
  ports; `run_settled` waits for an `app.boot.window.navigation` record for each of four labels (`WINDOW_LABELS`,
  :37), a condition a windowless program can never meet.

- `xtask/src/ci_gates.rs` (full) — two arms over the family (`evaluate`, :95): at least one record, no
  `app.panic.fatal` at ERROR; exit 0 / 1 / 2; an absent family is `CannotEvaluate`.

  samples are all zero as NEUTRAL (`populated 0 of n`), which a required arm turns into FAIL; `family_members`
  (:298) takes files by the `agent-latest.jsonl` prefix alone.

- `xtask/src/ingest_progress.rs` (full) and `xtask/src/main.rs` (:489-526) — `evaluate` returns `Neutral` when
  the stream holds no `buffer.tick`; the verb prints `check:ingest-progress: NEUTRAL — …` and exits 0.

- `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.sh` (full) — grades `ingest|buffer|viz|plugins.tick` (never `connection.tick`),
  exits 0 with a "trivially passes" line on no log and on no tick, and reads one tick per target as gap 0, PASS.

- `xtask/src/main.rs` (:606-770) — `invoke_heartbeat_check` (:614) is called from `run_perf_load_profiles`
  alone (:742).

- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` (:20-40, :262-282, :519-524) — `SEED_LOG` holds three records (one `app.boot.ready`,
  two `ingest.tick` 15 s apart); the sixth stage writes it and runs `cargo xtask ci-gates`.

- `pulse-app/src/console.rs` (full) — the grammar is `run` | `version`; `run` never returns and ends by signal.

title: Graph impact (from the code-graph query; plane `rust`)

data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; plane `rust`)

body:
- **`run_ready`** — 1 caller, `main()` at `xtask/src/main.rs:264` — a parameter added to it threads through one
  call site (query 1 of `tree-query-2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine.json`).

- **`harness_status::run`** — 1 caller, `main()` at `xtask/src/main.rs:264` (read in the file; the bare name
  `run` collides across modules, so it was not keyed in the query).

- **`classify`** (the one in `harness_status.rs`) — called by `harness_status::run` (:42), `run_ready`
  (`harness_ready.rs:55`) and 13 test sites in the two files. Its signature is left as it is: the program reading
  is a separate function, so no test site moves.

- **`family_members`** — 3 production callers (`ci_gates::evaluate`, `run_perf_budget`, `perf_frame`); reused
  unchanged by the new module.

- **Name check** — `engine_log`, `engine_cycle`, `engine_settled`: 0 rows in `symbol` (query 2 of the same trace);
  the names are free.

- **A pure decision pinned per arm, the probe pinned apart** (`harness_status.rs:83`, `harness_ready.rs:138`):
  the shape every new arm here takes.
- **Three exits, an absent input never a pass** (`ci_gates.rs:39-46`): 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 cannot-evaluate.
- **A failure line of coordinates, never content** (`ci_gates.rs:68`): member file name and line number.

- **A window that cannot reach its verdict is refused up front** (`harness_ready.rs:167`,
  `timeout_supports_verdict`).

- **The log names its own program** (`engine_boot.rs:415-440`): the one in-log fact that tells a window boot's
  log from a console boot's. It is written before the receivers bind, so it is in the log before a readiness read
  can succeed.

- **A spawned child under a cleared environment** (`integration_console_engine.rs:44-55`,
  `pre_push.rs` stage children): no session bus, so no leg reaches the OS credential store; the corpus then needs
  `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` or it opens absent with an ERROR record.

- **xtask verbs are formalized contracts** (`xtask/src/main.rs:47-260`, clap `name = "…"` with an `about`); a new
  verb declares its arms and exits in its module doc, like `ci_gates.rs:1-8`.
- **xtask tests are co-located `mod tests`** (xtask is not `pulse-app`; its unit binary runs under nextest).

- **Workflow pins live in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`** and read `ci.yml` by lines; no line of
  `ci.yml`, a comment included, may hold the tokens `windows`, `macos`, `matrix.os` or `runner.os ==`
  (`ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only`, :105).
- **ASCII-only sources** (`cargo xtask check:english-sources` scans `xtask/src`).

body:
- **Which verbs already serve the console engine unchanged.** `status`, `cleanup`, `logs` and `harness:ready`
  read the pid file, the log family, the exit record and the two ports — all written the same way by either
  program through `engine_boot::init_process` and the boot wrapper. Only `boot` (it names the binary) and
  `harness:settled` (it waits for window records) are program-specific.

- **What `cleanup` does to the engine.** TERM first; the engine's signal listener writes `app.exit` and re-raises
  the same signal; the wrapper then records `signal 15 (TERM)`. A KILL escalation leaves no `app.exit` by
  construction and the wrapper records `signal 9 (KILL)`.

- **What a short engine run holds.** The first tick of each target is written at boot and the second 15 s later,
  so a run shorter than about 16 s holds one tick per target and no consecutive pair. With the default 600 s
  retention the first sweep is at 100 s; with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_RETENTION_SECONDS=60` (the registered minimum) it
  is at 10 s, so the `buffer.tick` at 15 s carries a non-zero memory sample when spans landed before the sweep.

- **Which budget arms have a producer in a console run.** Memory: yes, one sample per `buffer.tick`. Snapshot:
  no (its one emitter is the snapshot generator, which a console run never calls). Frame: no (webview-originated).

- **The existing gap script cannot grade a console log as the plan needs.** It ignores `connection.tick`, passes
  on no tick and on a single tick, and reads no `app.boot.engine` record.

- **The exit witness would ride onto the engine.** `boot` loads it on whatever it spawns when the variable is
  set, and the CI `boot` job exports that variable for every later step of the job.
- **The injector cannot reach a leg on other ports.** Its endpoint is fixed at 4317.

- **No program-level trigger exists for a panic or a C `exit()` of the console program.** Its inputs are two
  command words, the registered variables and OTLP payloads; none reaches a panic or `exit()` short of a defect.
  Search: `grep -n 'panic!\|process::exit\|unwrap()\|expect(' pulse-app/src/console.rs
  pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs` finds one hit, `console.rs:71`, the runtime-build `expect` — it
  fires before the log sink exists, so it can leave no record, and no input reaches it.

- **The a11y job calls no harness verb.** `grep -n 'agent-run\|harness:' .github/workflows/ci.yml` finds the verbs
  in the `boot` job's steps alone; `cargo xtask test:a11y` writes nothing a family read takes (the family is
  matched by the `agent-latest.jsonl` prefix).

- **The release engine binary is not on the dev host** (`ls target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine`: absent);
  `target/release/pulse-app` is, so the release dependency set is warm and the first engine pre-build is a link.
- `xtask/src/engine_log.rs` — the check over the console engine's log family and the read that says when that log is gradeable
- `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs` — one cycle of the verbs on the console engine, on its own data dir and ports, as an xtask verb
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — `boot` and `status` take the program word; the witness is never loaded onto the engine
- `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` — the verdict names the program its log records, and refuses the wrong one
- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` — the readiness verdict carries the same program reading
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the program flag on the two harness verbs, the three new verbs, the module lines
- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` — the seed's doc comment says what the seed holds and what the stage reads
- `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` — the endpoint port comes from the registered gRPC port variable
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the engine cycle step and its log upload in the `boot` job
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — pins for the engine cycle step and its upload

- none — the three plan-decision questions research carried were answered at P4 (inputs#I2): the freight is cut
  in two and the second chunk's files left these lists; the console program's own panic and at-exit witness is
  retired with its reason, no trigger built; the three new harness readings are routine on the operator's
  reading. The cycle is an xtask verb, not a script: test-plan §3 places a check outside the five verbs as a
  `cargo xtask` verb (the `pre-push:linux` precedent), and a verb needs no new variable.

title: Scope — Agent harness drives the console engine

data.head: # Scope — Agent harness drives the console engine

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates
**Working entry (`working-route.md:31`):** "Agent harness drives the console engine — five verbs target it, verdict
arms pinned by tests; panic, heartbeat-gap, process-end, budget checks grade its log (P-086)"
**Chunk base:** `8394da4f` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this sha, never HEAD.

The engine has been a console program, `andromeda-pulse-engine` (`run` | `version`), since the chunk before this
one. The agent harness has not followed it: the five verbs of `scripts/agent-run.sh` build and spawn
`target/release/pulse-app` by path, and the checks that read a boot's log read the window app's. This chunk aims
the harness at the console engine, so that an agent can start it, ask whether it is up, read its log and end it by
the same five verbs, and so that the checks which grade a run read the engine's own log and can fail on it. The
window app and its boot job stand beside it until Epoch 2.

title: What the chunk builds (the entry's own words)

data.head: ## What the chunk builds (the entry's own words)

body: - **Five verbs target it.** `boot`, `run`, `status`, `cleanup` and `logs` drive `andromeda-pulse-engine`.

- **Verdict arms pinned by tests.** Each verdict a verb or a check can return has a test that fails if the arm
  stops returning it.

- **Panic, heartbeat-gap, process-end, budget checks grade its log.** Four checks read the console engine's log
  family: no panic record, no heartbeat stall, exactly one record of how the process ended, and the budget arms.

body:

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T04:40:09Z
- **Chunk base:** `95d17008a9a7cc9dad50cea26ef265c8aa4a4f4b`. Every diff-shaped probe names this sha, never HEAD.

The CI boot smoke reads red on most runs because the app ends by itself in its first second on the runner. Two
runs kept the ending call (`ci#38019133294`, 7 of 8 boots; `ci#38022477393`, 5 of 8), and research named the cause
behind it (research.md, The cause): the app uses Xlib from two threads, GTK's main thread and a device-event thread
that `tao 0.35.0` starts on X11, and never initialises Xlib's thread support. The runner's Xlib
(`libx11-6 1.7.5-1ubuntu0.3`) does not do that when it loads; the dev host's 1.8.13 does. On the runner's Xlib a
reply is lost inside the app, Xlib raises an I/O error on a healthy connection, and GDK's handler calls `_exit(1)`.
With the runner's Xlib package swapped in on the dev host, 19 of 24 boots self-ended with the runner's call chain;
with `XInitThreads()` called first in the app process, 0 of 8.

This chunk does two things. First it repairs the series verdict's undercount: a boot that ends by itself before
the boot verb reads ready is counted `ended` and listed with its exit record and its `exit_witness` label, and the
smoke's own boot is listed the same way (per test-plan §1 Pending coverage triggers →
`harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage`; architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces).
Then it closes the cause where it is, on the operator's ruling (inputs#I3, inputs#I4): the app calls
`XInitThreads()` as the second statement of `main` on Linux, right after the render-posture step, before any thread
exists and before anything reaches Xlib. The defect is in what ships: the same app ends the same way on any host whose
Xlib is older than 1.8.

**How the close is read (inputs#I1 item 2, inputs#I3).** On the runner, on equal source: three consecutive
attempts of the one pull-request run of the operator's pre-CI commit, each building the same merge commit, eight
boots an attempt, 24 boots. The without arm is the two runs before the change: 12 of 16 boots self-ended (7 of 8
and 5 of 8), a per-boot rate of 0.75 (`boot-series.json` and the witness files of both runs, research.md). At that
rate an unclosed job passes one attempt of eight boots with probability 0.25^8 = 1.5e-5 and all 24 boots with
0.25^24 = 3.6e-15. At the lower of the two runs' rates alone (5 of 8) the 24 boots pass at 6.0e-11; at the lowest
rate this job has ever read (4 of 12 first boots before the series existed, P-129's notes, not re-derived) they pass
at 5.9e-5. On the dev host the same variation is read once more by /implement on the built change: eight boots
under the runner's Xlib, which passed 0 of 4 series at the base (three at P3, and the close leg's own baseline at
P5: 7 of 8 self-ended).

Run no workspace suite ahead of the gate block: a default-features run rewrites the tracked bindings and reddens
the scope guard and `capability-drift` (the prior chunk's `evidence/local-legs.md`).

1. **The series counts a before-ready self-end** (`xtask/src/harness_series.rs`).
   - After a cycle whose settle verdict file is absent, `run_boot` reads what the boot left in its own data dir:
     the app pid from `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` (`harness_status::read_pid`), the exit record from
     `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (`harness_status::read_ended`) and the witness label for that pid
     (`harness_witness::label(Some(boot_dir), pid, ended)`). `BootRecord` carries the two values beside `settle`.
     No second parser: the three readers are the ones the settle verdict uses, unchanged.
   - One pure decision says whether that record is an end the app made itself. It is, when an exit record exists
     and is neither `signal 15 (TERM)` nor `signal 9 (KILL)`. Those two are the boot verb's own cleanup ending an
     app that was still running at the readiness timeout (`scripts/agent-run.sh:215-227`); the app never turns a
     signal into an exit code. No exit record is no own end.
   - `classify` counts a boot `Ended` when its settle verdict reads `ended` (as today) or when it has no settle
     verdict and the decision above holds. Everything else is unchanged: `Settled` needs a `complete` cycle,
     the rest is `Other`. `decide_series` and `exit_status` are not edited; `self-ended` follows from the class.
   - `boot_entry` fills `ended` and `exit_witness` from the own-end read when the boot has no settle verdict.
     `verdict`, `app_exit_record` and `windows_settled` stay null for such a boot: no settle read ran, and the
     entry does not invent one. Both values pass through `bounded_label`.
   - The smoke: when the top data dir holds no `logs/harness-settled.json`, `run` makes the same read over the top
     data dir, and `series_payload` lists ordinal 1 with `cycle` `smoke` when that read holds an own end. Ordinal
     1 stays out of the counts, as registered.
   - The member sets, the `cycle` labels, the verdict set, the exit codes, `KEPT_FILES` and `CYCLE_SCRIPT` do not
     change (impact: every caller of `classify`, `boot_entry`, `run_boot` and `series_payload` is inside
     `xtask/src/harness_series.rs`, research.md Graph impact).

3. **Xlib's thread support, initialised before any thread** (new `pulse-app/src/xlib_threads.rs`, declared in
   `pulse-app/src/lib.rs`).
   - One function, Linux only, resolves `XInitThreads` in the library named `libX11.so.6` through the `libc`
     crate's dynamic-loader calls and calls it once. `libc` is already a direct dependency
     (`pulse-app/Cargo.toml:46`); no manifest and no lockfile line changes.
   - It returns one closed value: initialised · library not found · symbol not found · refused (the call returned
     0) · not applicable (not Linux). Every arm but the first is inert: nothing is logged, nothing panics, the
     start goes on. A host with no Xlib has no X11 window path to protect.
   - The library name is a parameter of an inner function the test can call, hidden from the docs; the product
     entry passes the one constant.
   - It reads and sets no environment variable and emits no log record. No subscriber exists at that point, and
     the value is not carried to one.
   - The module's header comment says why it exists (Xlib older than 1.8 needs the call when two threads use it;
     `tao` starts the second thread) and that it leaves with the window: the route entry `Window retired`.

4. **`main` calls it second** (`pulse-app/src/main.rs:278-279`; inputs#I4). `render_posture::apply_linux_default()`
   stays the first statement of `main`, as ratified, and `pulse-app/src/render_posture.rs` is not touched, its
   comments included. The call is `main`'s second statement, directly after it and before
   `tokio::runtime::Builder` builds any thread. The first statement reaches no Xlib and starts no thread: its body
   is `cfg!`, `std::env::var_os` and `std::env::set_var` (`render_posture.rs:50-62`, read whole at P5), and its
   record is emitted later (`main.rs:302`). `XInitThreads` starts no thread either.

6. **The swapped-library reading goes into evidence** (inputs#I3). /implement writes
   `chunks/2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed/evidence/swapped-library.md` from
   `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T04-02-31Z-phase/p3-measurements.md` (the five arms of P3, the debugger capture, how
   the swap was made and undone) and from the recorded outputs of this block's swap entries: the fetch with its
   checksums, the `ldd` reading under the swap, the series under the swap on the built change, and the `ldd`
   reading with no variable set. The swap is one environment variable on one command; nothing is installed.

- `pulse-app/src/xlib_threads.rs` — the one call that initialises Xlib's thread support, inert where the library
  or the symbol is not found; leaves with `Window retired`
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_xlib_threads.rs` — the three arms, the call's place in `main`, the one call site

- `xtask/src/harness_series.rs` — the own-end read, its decision, the entry's two filled members, the smoke's
  entry, the pins
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — the call as the second statement of `main`, after the render-posture step
- `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod xlib_threads;`

The chunk's own probes come first, then the targeted pins, then the builds the legs need, the swap and three
local legs, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order (`capability-drift` before the default-features
workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, the base-identity
bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure), then the local pre-push check, then the operator pass.

The three legs boot the release app on this host under a virtual display. Each moves the receivers to 14317 and
14318 through the two port variables, so the shared ports 4317 and 4318 are never bound; each unsets
`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; each writes a fresh data dir under `target/`, named at invocation. The boot verb rebuilds the
release binary itself, so the legs read the tree as it stands. They are the boot-path smoke test-plan §3 asks for
when `pulse-app/src/main.rs` changes, in its harness `boot` form.

- **The close leg** runs eight boots with the runner's Xlib swapped in. At the base it reads `self-ended` (P3: 6
  of 8, 8 of 8 and 5 of 8 in three series). The swap is the fetch entry's two libraries named through
  `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` on that one command. The `ldd` entry before it is its known positive: without it a green leg
  could be the host's own Xlib. The `ldd` entry after the legs reads the swap gone.

- **The repair leg** boots once with no display at all, so the app ends before ready by itself (P4 reading:
  `app ended: exit 101`, witness label `runtime-exit`), then runs a series of one boot in the same data dir. At
  the base the series lists no ordinal 1. That boot's log holds a panic record by design; no gate grades it.
- **The host leg** is the prior chunk's series of two on the host's own Xlib, unchanged.

- A before-ready self-end of a series boot (ordinal 2 and up) has no local leg: nothing on this host makes the app
  end before ready on demand under a live display. Step 2's fixture pin and the repair leg, which drives the same
  read on a real process, stand for it. On the runner it is read only if a self-end recurs.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched and no rendered surface
  changes. The `a11y` job's verdict is read from the operator pass's run; its regression reading compares against
  a base download that has no producer in any workflow (a11y-plan amendment `2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone`, Kept),
  so the criterion below asks for the job's own conclusion and artifacts, not a base diff.
- No Windows leg and no `agent-run.ps1` edit: nothing runs it here or in CI.

- No retry anywhere. The two re-runs of the operator pass are not retries of a red: each is fired only while every
  attempt before it read no self-end, each is one more reading of the stated three, and a self-end in any attempt
  stops the pass and is the reading.

The files a CI run keeps (`logs/boot-series.json`, `logs/harness-settled.json`, `logs/exit-witness.jsonl`,
`logs/series/boot-{ordinal}/`) are produced by that run, a step outside this block; the operator pass's read
entries carry no `artifact`.
**The operator pass, in this order.**
1. The hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the local pre-push check, then the build-branch push.
2. The CI read of the pushed tip, asserted green. It is attempt 1 and the chunk's CI verdict.

3. Three reads of that attempt by the run's id: its jobs (report-only), the `boot` job's log lines with the
   `ci-gates` frame line, and the run's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact with the series verdict, the smoke's settle
   verdict, every witness file whole and the merge commit its log carries.

4. **Each kept witness file is read whole.** A line holding anything beyond its shape stops the pass, and the
   operator is told.

5. **The stop at a self-end.** If any boot of an attempt ended by itself, the pass stops. Nothing is re-run and
   nothing is fixed on top. The report says what the job kept for that boot (its ordinal, its exit record, its
   `exit_witness` label, its witness lines whole) and that the close is not shown; P-129 is not verified.

6. When attempt 1 holds no self-end: the `boot` job alone is re-run on the same commit, and attempt 2 is read the
   same way; when attempt 2 holds none, once more for attempt 3. Every attempt is recorded with its number, its
   merge commit and its artifact id, and none replaces another.

7. A red in any other job is the standard pass's: read its log, fix on top with a further commit, read again.
   Then the count of three starts over on the new commit, since the source changed.

Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry
writes one.

body:
- (tests) The series counts a boot that ended by itself before ready: with exit record `exit 1` and witness label
  `exit-call` on a `boot-failed` cycle the boot is `ended`, the verdict reads `self-ended`, and its entry carries
  both values; the boot verb's own `signal 15 (TERM)` and `signal 9 (KILL)` are not counted as self-ends. Each arm
  is pinned in `harness_series::tests`, and the mutation check of step 2 is recorded. Proven by
  `cargo nextest run -p xtask --profile ci -E 'test(/harness_series::/)'` (per test-plan §1 Pending coverage
  triggers → `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage`).

- (tests) On a real process: after a boot with no display, the series lists ordinal 1 with `"ended": "exit 101"`
  and `"exit_witness": "runtime-exit"` and stays `all-settled` for its own boot. Proven by the repair leg, the
  entry whose `run` holds `DISPLAY=:987`; red at the base, where the series lists no ordinal 1 (per test-plan §3
  Per-chunk gate discipline → Direct-binary smoke variant).

- (arch) `logs/boot-series.json` keeps its registered shape: the six top members, the seven per-boot members, the
  closed `cycle` labels, labels of at most 48 printable-ASCII bytes, no environment value and no path, exits
  0 / 1 / 1 / 2. The existing member-set pin passes unedited (per architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI
  surfaces).

title: The cause, named from the runs and shown by a variation

data.head: ### The cause, named from the runs and shown by a variation

body:
1. **The ending call is Xlib's "no reply arrived" exit, in the runner's own Xlib build.** The three `libX11.so.6`
   frames of every `end` line (+0x41393, +0x4660f, +0x255a8) are exact return addresses in Ubuntu's
   `libx11-6 1.7.5-1ubuntu0.3`: 0x4660f follows the `call _XIOError` inside `_XReply` whose next instructions
   return 0, which is the function's exit for a request that got neither a reply nor an X error
   (`objdump -d` on the package's `libX11.so.6.4.0`, sha256 `d382a306…7d547` for the package). The runner's
   library build, which the prior chunk listed as not read, is read.

2. **Both red runs hold the same line.** `ci#38019133294` (attempt 1, tip `925be35f`, merge `ab6a1ae6ef0d`): 7 of
   8 boots self-ended. `ci#38022477393` (attempt 1, tip `95d17008`, merge `71ce5340f2ad`): 5 of 8. Twelve `end`
   lines, equal in every member but `pid` and `tid`; 28 witness lines in 16 files read whole, 0 beyond the shape.

3. **It reproduces on the dev host once the runner's Xlib is swapped in.** The same release binary under
   `cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count 8`, with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` naming the two jammy libraries: 6 of 8
   boots self-ended with the exit witness loaded, 8 of 8 with nothing preloaded, 5 of 8 with
   `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1`. The six witness lines are the runner's call chain (`_exit`, code 1, `errno`
   11, main thread, the same three Xlib offsets). With the host's own Xlib 1.8.13: 0 of 8.

4. **The variation.** Same binary, same jammy Xlib, one difference: `XInitThreads()` called first in the app
   process (a scratch preload, never in the tree). 0 of 8 self-ended, 8 settled with four windows each. Without it
   on that Xlib: 19 of 24.

5. **Why the two Xlib builds differ.** The host's libX11 1.8.13 has its thread support initialised when the
   library loads; the runner's 1.7.5 does not (`_Xglobal_lock` read at load by a ten-line program: set, not set).
   On 1.7.5 a program that uses Xlib from more than one thread has to call `XInitThreads()` before any other Xlib
   call.

6. **The app uses Xlib from two threads and never makes that call at start.** `tao 0.35.0` (the locked version)
   starts a thread at event-loop creation on X11 that opens its own display and loops on `XNextEvent`
   (`tao-0.35.0/src/platform_impl/linux/device.rs:15-32`, spawned at `event_loop.rs:263`). Its one
   `XInitThreads` call is in `x11/xdisplay.rs:48`, inside a constructor reached only through
   `platform/unix.rs:246`, not at start. `tao 0.35.3` and `0.37.1` have the same two sites, so a dependency bump
   does not change it. `grep -rn XInitThreads pulse-app/src crates xtask/src scripts`: 0 lines.

- **(a) Which side ended the connection: none did.** Under `gdb`, stopped at `_XIOError` on the main thread (the
  runner's chain), `xcb_connection_has_error` on that display's connection reads **0** and `errno` reads 11. The
  connection is healthy; the server went on serving it. Xlib raised an I/O error because its own bookkeeping held
  no reply for the request. At that instant one other thread was inside Xlib: `XNextEvent` called from the app
  binary at the offset of tao's device thread. So it is the app's own side: two threads in Xlib without Xlib's
  thread support. One capture of one ending; the variation in point 4 is what shows the cause. The step inside
  Xlib by which the reply is lost was not traced.

- **`hypothesis:` the `errno` 11 may be a stale value (inputs#I1 item 5): verified.** No connection error exists
  at the stop, so no system call failed there; 11 is left over from an earlier non-blocking read.

- **(b) Is it a property of the runner a run lands on: no.** Two runs on two runner instances both hold it (7 of 8,
  5 of 8), and so does the dev host under the runner's Xlib. It follows the library set and a race in the app's
  first second, not the machine. First boots, as the matrix's P-129 notes carry them and not re-derived here: 4
  of the twelve runs before the series ended by themselves; then run 1's did and run 2's did not (5 of 14).

- **(c) Do boots 2 to 8 run the binary boot 1 ran: no, they run a second build of the same source.** In both runs
  the series' first boot took 3 min 27 s and 3 min 36 s to reach ready, the length of the smoke's own release
  build (`Finished release … in 3m 45s` in boot 1's `build.log`), and each later cycle took at most 12 s. The five
  `pulse-app` frames of every `end` line have equal offsets in boot 1's file and the series' files. Why the runner
  relinks is not measured (no series boot keeps its `build.log`); on the dev host a shell-launched build after
  four series compiled nothing.

- **(d) GDK's message (inputs#I1 item 4): it is never written, and nothing is lost at `_exit`.** The runner's
  `gdk_x_io_error` (`gdkmain-x11.c:246`, read from Ubuntu's `libgtk-3-0 3.24.33-1ubuntu2.2`) logs at
  `G_LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG` and then calls `_exit(1)`. GLib's default writer drops debug messages unless
  `G_MESSAGES_DEBUG` names the domain, which nothing sets. The app's stdout and stderr both go to `logs/boot.log`
  (`scripts/agent-run.sh:96`), and no `boot.log` of the 16 boots holds a GDK or GLib line beside the
  accessibility-bus warning.

- **The limit "seven of eight under the instrument against four of twelve before it":** on the dev host the arm
  with nothing preloaded ended 8 of 8 and the arm with the witness 6 of 8, so the witness library does not raise
  the rate. The difference between a run's first boot and its later boots is not attributed.

- **Re-derived.** `boot-series.json` of run 1 reads `ended` 2, `other` 4; of run 2 `settled` 2, `ended` 2, `other`
  3. Each of the seven `other` boots has `cycle` `boot-failed`, five null settle members, and an `end` line in its
  own `exit-witness.jsonl`.

- **Mechanism.** `CYCLE_SCRIPT` runs `harness:settled` only when `boot` returned 0
  (`xtask/src/harness_series.rs:38-46`), so a boot that ends before ready has no `harness-settled.json`,
  `read_settle` returns `None` (`:144`), and `classify` counts it `Other` (`:261-267`).

- **What such a boot leaves on disk.** The boot verb's failure path prints how the app ended and runs its own
  `cleanup` (`scripts/agent-run.sh:139-161`). `cleanup` removes the pid file and nothing else of a data dir whose
  name does not match `*/agent-run-*` (`:229-231`, `:257-259`). So `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` (the app pid),
  `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (`exit 1`) and `logs/exit-witness.jsonl` remain in `series/boot-{ordinal}/`.

- **The readers exist and are reachable.** `harness_status::{read_pid, end_file, read_ended}` and
  `harness_witness::label(data_dir, pid, ended)` are `pub(crate)` (`harness_status.rs:204-217`,
  `harness_witness.rs:42`). `read_pid` takes any one-decimal-pid file, the spawn record included. The witness
  reader is the bounded one (64 lines of at most 4096 printable-ASCII bytes, three kinds, a `u32` pid, else
  `unreadable`); no second parser is needed.

- **A constraint on the repair.** When the app is still running at the readiness timeout, the boot verb's own
  `cleanup` ends it with `TERM` (then `KILL`), and the exit record then reads `signal 15 (TERM)` or
  `signal 9 (KILL)`. That end is the harness's, not the app's. The app re-raises the same signal and never turns
  it into an exit code (`rules/security.md`, the `app.exit` boundary), so an exit record of the form `exit N` on a
  boot that failed to reach ready is an end the app made itself.

- **The smoke's own boot has the same gap.** The workflow's smoke step runs `agent-run.sh boot || exit 1`, so a
  first boot that ends before ready writes no `harness-settled.json` and the series lists no ordinal 1 for it
  (`series_payload`, `:370-378`). Its spawn record, exit record and witness file are in the top data dir.

- **The labels fit the registered sets.** `ended` is the bounded exit record, `exit_witness` one of the six closed
  labels, `cycle` stays `boot-failed`. No member, label or kept file is added.

- `xtask/src/harness_series.rs` (1-432 read, 433-755 indexed by test name) — the cycle script, `run_boot`,
  `classify`, `boot_entry`, `series_payload`, the 16 pins.
- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` (84-233) — `run_settled`, `decide_settled`, `wait_for_settle`, `read_exit_record`.
- `xtask/src/harness_witness.rs` (1-135) — `label`, `decide`, the bounded reader.
- `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` (signatures) — the `pub(crate)` helpers.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` (20-269) — the boot verb's spawn line, its failure path, `cleanup`.

- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` (index of pins) — `:639` fixes the literal
  `run: cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count 7`.
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (278-279) — `main()` opens with `render_posture::apply_linux_default()`.
- `pulse-app/src/render_posture.rs` (signatures) — the one existing head-of-`main` Linux step.
- `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` — `libc` is a direct dependency; no X11 crate is.
- `Cargo.lock` — `tao 0.35.0`, `wry 0.55.0`; `x11-dl` and `x11` enter through tao, wry and `gdkx11`.

- The cargo registry's `tao-0.35.0`, `tao-0.35.3`, `tao-0.37.1` (`device.rs`, `event_loop.rs`, `x11/xdisplay.rs`,
  `platform/unix.rs`).
- Ubuntu's `libx11-6`, `libx11-xcb1` and `libgtk-3-0` jammy packages (symbols and disassembly).

- The two runs' kept files (16 witness files, 16 `boot.log`, 2 `boot-series.json`, the `build.log` of each smoke)
  and both `boot` job logs.
- The prior chunk's `report.md` (100-234), `evidence/local-legs.md`, `plan.md` (the three local legs' commands).

**Working entry (`working-route.md:21`):** "Boot smoke's self-end closed — every self-end counted with its label; the

(`route.py pins`: 541, 1178, 612 and 500 characters; no other freight on the line, no `BLOCKED-ON`).
**Chunk base:** `95d17008` (HEAD at take-up, equal to its upstream `origin/build/andromeda-pulse-0.4.0`). Every
diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this sha, never HEAD.

Requirement P-129 reads: "the CI boot smoke ends the same on equal source: the cause of the app ending by itself
shortly after ready on the runner is found and closed, and the job no longer reads red where nothing it builds
changed" (`matrix.py show --id P-129`, read at take-up). The chunk before this one made a run keep what names the
call that ended the app. This chunk repairs the one measured defect of that instrument, finds why the ending call
is reached, removes that cause with the smallest change, and shows equal source reading the same.

The operator's direction for this chunk (inputs#I1, the pc overseer's phase directive; inputs#I2, the invocation
word): the relay is folded as an input; a close is a removed cause shown by a variation, never a rarer symptom; the
chunk adds no retry, no soft-fail key and no filter; the instrument's record does not grow; if the cause cannot be
closed from this repository the chunk stops at P4; the plan card is printed at P5 and the chunk stops there for the
operator's `yes`.

- **Every self-end is counted with its label** (the entry; its first `CARRY:`; inputs#I1 item 6: "The series'
  undercount is this entry's first step"). This is the chunk's FIRST step, ahead of the close. The entry states the
  defect as: a boot that ends before the boot verb reads ready takes no settle verdict, so `boot-series.json` gives

    `boot-failed`, five null settle members and an `end` line in its own witness file (research.md, The series'
    undercount).
  - The repair sits in the series verb (`xtask/src/harness_series.rs`) and reads what such a boot leaves in its
    own data dir: the spawn record, the exit record and the witness file, through the readers the settle verdict
    already uses (`harness_status::{read_pid, end_file, read_ended}`, `harness_witness::label`). Neither of those
    two modules changes. `[premise-corrected: research.md "The readers exist and are reachable"; the take-up left

    harness's and is not counted as a self-end (research.md, A constraint on the repair).

  P3 and recorded in research.md with its measurements:
  - The app uses Xlib from two threads (GTK's main thread, and a device-event thread its windowing library `tao`
    starts on X11) and never initialises Xlib's thread support. The runner's Xlib (`libx11-6 1.7.5-1ubuntu0.3`)

    app's own side lost the reply.

title: Plan — 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run: "Boot smoke's self-end named from a run"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run: "Boot smoke's self-end named from a run"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T02:26:54Z
- **Chunk base:** `8936f976b129cdce00a3fc916f3846254e2dce1c`

The CI boot smoke has read red on four of twelve pull-request runs of the build branch, the last one on this
chunk's own base (`ci#38014971549`). In each the app ended by itself a fraction of a second after its webview's
first calls: an exit and not a signal, code 1, no `app.exit` record, nothing new on its output, its display and
session bus still accepting. The job says how the app ended. It does not say who ended it.

**Which plan this is (inputs#I3): it names, and the closing is the next entry.** A run can name the cause only
after the operator's pre-CI commit, and past that commit no plan revision is offered, so the change that closes the
cause cannot be planned here from a record that does not exist yet. This plan builds what makes a run name the
ending call and its caller, reads its runs, and stops at the first witnessed self-end. P-129 is not claimed.
It delivers three things:

1. **An exit witness.** A small C library, loaded into the app process alone on the harness's spawn line, records
   the call that ends the process with its caller, and says so for each way a process can end with a code: a call
   through the linker, a direct `_exit`, `main` returning, and an end it cannot see at all, which reads as its own
   named verdict and never as nothing (inputs#I3, condition 1). It keeps itself out of the webview's child
   processes (condition 2).

2. **The settle verdict says what the witness recorded**, as one closed label, and the job keeps the witness's own
   file beside the log.

3. **A series.** After the smoke the `boot` job boots seven more times, each boot on a fresh data dir, its own
   display server and empty per-user data and cache directories, each recorded with its ordinal. A boot that ends
   by itself reds the job. One run then reads eight boots instead of one.

Research measured the instrument on the dev host (research.md, "The instrument"; the phase run dir's
`p3-measurements.md`): on a known member of the silent `exit 1` class it named `_exit(1)`, called from a static
function of `libgdk-3.so.0` entered from Xlib's `_XIOError`, 2 of 2; on six green boots against six without it no
timing difference was visible. Its cost on the runner is not measured: the first run under this plan reads it on
green boots before a red one is trusted to it.
No product code changes. The window is not repaired or rewritten (inputs#I1 item 6).

1. **Write the pins first and read them red.** The in-file tests of steps 4 and 6 in the two new xtask modules,
   one per arm; the moved member pin of step 5; the workflow pins of step 8. Run the workspace suite once and keep
   the red reading in `evidence/red-before-green.md`.

2. **The library, `scripts/exit-witness.c`.** One C source with no dependency beyond the C library.
   - At load it opens the file named by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` for append, close-on-exec, and writes
     one `loaded` line (pid, process name). It registers an exit handler. It then removes `LD_PRELOAD` and
     `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` from the process environment, so no process the app starts inherits
     either. With the variable unset or the file not openable it stays inert: every interposed call passes
     through.
   - It interposes `exit`, `_exit`, `_Exit`, `quick_exit` and `abort`. At the call it writes one `end` line: pid,
     thread id, process name, the call, its code, `errno`, and up to 23 caller frames, each as module basename,
     exported symbol (empty for a static function) and offset in the module. Then the real call runs with the same
     code.
   - Its exit handler writes one `runtime-exit` line: the C runtime's own exit path ran.
   - Every line is one JSON object written by one `write`, at most 4096 bytes. A line holds no environment value,
     no argument, no path beyond a basename and nothing of the process's memory.
   - The line patterns, measured on the scratch probe (`p3-measurements.md`, "P4 control"): a call to `exit`
     through the linker leaves `loaded`, `end`, `runtime-exit`; a direct `_exit` leaves `loaded`, `end`; `main`
     returning leaves `loaded`, `runtime-exit`; a direct system call leaves `loaded` alone.

3. **The boot verb loads it onto the app, and only the app.** In `scripts/agent-run.sh`, at the spawn line (`:79`,
   the command whose `$!` the wrapper records as the app's pid): read `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB`, trimmed.
   Unset or blank: the app is spawned as today. Naming a regular file: that one command runs with `LD_PRELOAD` set
   to it and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` set to the data dir's `logs/exit-witness.jsonl`. Set and not a
   regular file: `boot: exit witness library not found` on stderr and exit 1 before anything is spawned, so a
   mistyped path cannot run a job without its witness. No other verb changes; the pid, the parent and the reaper
   stay as they are. The script stays git mode 100755. `scripts/agent-run.ps1` is not changed: a preloaded
   library has no form there, nothing runs that script here or in CI, and it leaves with "Other operating systems
   retired from the code".

4. **The witness's reader, `xtask/src/harness_witness.rs`.**
   - A bounded reader of `logs/exit-witness.jsonl`: at most 64 lines, each at most 4096 bytes of printable ASCII
     holding one JSON object whose `kind` is `loaded`, `end` or `runtime-exit`. Anything else reads as
     `unreadable`, never as a partial record.
   - A pure decision over the app's pid, the wrapper's exit record and the lines for that pid, with these arms:
     `unset` (no file) · `unreadable` · `loaded` (a `loaded` line, no `end` and no `runtime-exit` line, and the
     exit record is absent or a signal) · `exit-call` (an `end` line) · `runtime-exit` (a `runtime-exit` line and
     no `end` line) · `no-record` (a `loaded` line alone while the exit record reads `exit N`: the process ended
     by a path the library cannot see).
   - Pins: one per arm over synthetic lines, among them the control's real line from `p3-measurements.md`, and the
     reader's bounds.
   - Controls on the built library, Linux only, in the same module: the test builds `scripts/exit-witness.c` and
     four children of a few lines of C with `cc` into a temp dir, runs each child under the library and asserts
     its line pattern and the label the decision gives it: `exit(7)` through the linker, `_exit(7)`, `main`
     returning 7, a direct `exit_group` system call. A fifth control is the child boundary: a parent under the
     library starts a child that reports its environment; the file holds one `loaded` line, the parent's, and the
     child holds neither variable. Its known positive: the same parent starting the child with `LD_PRELOAD` set
     again leaves two `loaded` lines. A missing compiler fails these tests; it never skips them.

5. **The settle verdict gains one member, `exit_witness`.** In `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, `run_settled` reads
   the witness after the verdict, where it already reads the exit record and the log evidence, and
   `settled_payload` carries the label of step 4. The verdict set, the exit codes and the other seven members are
   unchanged. `settled_payload_carries_the_closed_field_set` moves to eight members in the same change.

6. **The series, `cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count N`** (`xtask/src/harness_series.rs`, declared and
   dispatched in `xtask/src/main.rs`).
   - It boots N more times, ordinals 2 to N+1, the smoke being ordinal 1. `--count` outside 1 to 16, a system
     other than Linux, an unresolved data dir or no `xvfb-run` reads `cannot-evaluate`.
   - Each boot gets its own data dir `series/boot-{ordinal}/` under the resolved data dir and its own
     `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` inside it, and runs the smoke's cycle under its own display server:
     `boot`, `harness:settled`, `status`, `cleanup`, with `cleanup` run whatever the others returned. The child's
     environment drops the package variables `cargo run` injects, as `cargo_command()` does.
   - What each boot keeps is copied file by file into the job's uploaded `logs/series/boot-{ordinal}/`: the log
     family, `boot.log`, `harness-settled.json`, `xvfb.log`, `exit-witness.jsonl`. Nothing of a boot's `run/` is
     copied.
   - A boot whose `cleanup` does not read `clean` ends the series there as `cannot-evaluate`: the next boot would
     meet its ports.
   - One JSON verdict on stdout, also written to `logs/boot-series.json`: `{verdict, boots, settled, ended, other,
     per_boot}`, each `per_boot` entry `{ordinal, cycle, verdict, ended, app_exit_record, windows_settled,
     exit_witness}`. `all-settled` exits 0; `self-ended` (a boot's settle verdict read `ended`) and
     `not-all-settled` exit 1; `cannot-evaluate` exits 2. The verdict is decided over the boots the verb ran. When
     the smoke's own `logs/harness-settled.json` is there, it is listed as ordinal 1 so one file holds every boot
     of the run.
   - The decision is a pure function pinned per arm; the member set and the kept-file list are pinned.

7. **The `boot` job, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.** Two steps are added and nothing else in the workflow moves.
   - `Build the exit witness`, after the release build and before the smoke: `cc` builds the library into the
     runner's temp dir and the step names it to the harness through `$GITHUB_ENV` as
     `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB`. A plain `run:` step.
   - `Boot series (equal source)`, after the smoke and before `ci-gates`: `cargo xtask harness:boot-series
     --count 7`, with `if: always()` so it runs when the smoke is red too. A plain `run:` step with no soft-fail
     key: a self-end in the series fails the job.
   - The smoke step's four invocations and its conjunction stay as they are; a comment may gain a sentence. A
     comment added to the workflow never uses the word the Linux-only pin refuses on every line.

8. **The workflow pins, `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`.** The `boot` job builds the library from
   `scripts/exit-witness.c` before the smoke step and exports `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB`; the series step
   sits after the smoke and before `ci-gates`, runs under `if: always()`, and holds no `continue-on-error`, no
   `retry` and no `|| true`. The four smoke pins are not touched.
9. **The local legs and the gates** of `## Test Commands`, in the fence's order.
10. **The operator pass**, as `## Test Commands` states it.
- `scripts/exit-witness.c` — the library's source
- `xtask/src/harness_witness.rs` — the witness's bounded reader, its decision, their pins and the controls on the built library
- `xtask/src/harness_series.rs` — the series verb, its decision and its pins
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — the boot verb's witness arm on the spawn line (`:79`)

- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` — `run_settled` reads the witness; `settled_payload` and its pin gain `exit_witness` (`settled_payload @ xtask/src/harness_ready.rs:347`, callers `run_settled @ :111` and the pin `@ :625`)
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the two modules and the `harness:boot-series` verb
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `boot` job's two added steps
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the pins of step 8

The chunk's own probes come first, then the library's build, its controls and three local legs, then the standard gate set in
test-plan §3 order (`capability-drift` before the default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server`
bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no
procedure), then the local pre-push check, then the operator pass.

The three legs boot the release app on this host under a virtual display. Each moves the receivers to 14317 and
14318 through the two port variables, so the shared ports 4317 and 4318 are never bound; each unsets
`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; each writes a fresh data dir under `target/`, named at invocation. The `boot` verb rebuilds the
release binary itself, so the legs read the tree as it stands. A reading taken under heavy host load says so in
the evidence.
Absences, each with its reason:
- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched.

- No boot-path smoke gate in test-plan §3's sense: none of its trigger paths is in the modify-set. The three legs
  are this chunk's own.

- No leg for the `runtime-exit` and `no-record` arms on the real app: nothing makes the app end those ways on
  demand. The compiled children of step 4 are their controls, run by the workspace suite.
- No Windows leg: nothing runs `scripts/agent-run.ps1` here or in CI.

- One targeted nextest entry, and only one: the instrument's own controls run ahead of the three legs that grade
  with it. Step 1 runs the suite as the red-before-green pair; the workspace entry runs every test on every
  re-run.

On the untouched tree the build entry and the three legs read red: the source, the member and the verb do not
exist yet. The control leg carries no exit atom, since `xvfb-run` itself returns non-zero when its display server
is already gone; its `contains` atoms decide it. Its two library-name atoms are this host's reading
(`p3-measurements.md`, the control table).

The files a CI run keeps (`logs/exit-witness.jsonl`, `logs/boot-series.json`, `logs/series/boot-{ordinal}/`) are
produced by that run, a step outside this block; the operator pass's download entries read them and carry no
`artifact`.
**The operator pass, in this order** (inputs#I3).
1. The hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the local pre-push check, then the build-branch push.

2. The CI read of the pushed tip, whole, **report-only**. It is attempt 1 and **it is the chunk's CI verdict**,
   whatever is read after it. It may end either way: a self-end in any of the eight boots reds the job, which is
   the defect staying visible.

3. Three report-only reads of that run by its id: the jobs of attempt 1; the `boot` job's log lines that carry the
   verdicts; the run's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact, downloaded under `target/`, with `boot-series.json`, the
   smoke's settle verdict and every `exit-witness.jsonl` printed.

4. **Each kept witness file is read whole.** A line holding an environment value, a path beyond a basename, a
   secret-class value or anything of a watched service's telemetry stops the pass, and the operator is told.

5. **The stop at a self-end.** If any boot of an attempt reads `ended`, the pass stops re-running and says what the
   job kept for that boot: its ordinal, its exit record, its `exit_witness` label and its witness lines whole.
   Naming the cause from them is the report's; nothing is fixed on top.

6. **When attempt 1 holds no self-end.** The instrument's green reading is recorded first (eight boots, each
   `exit_witness: loaded`, each boot's times against the earlier green runs'). Then, on the operator's word
   (inputs#I3): the `boot` job alone is re-run on the same commit, at most three times. Before each re-run the
   attempt just read is recorded with its number and its artifact is already downloaded. Every attempt is recorded
   with its number and none replaces another. The pass stops at the first attempt that holds a self-end, or after
   the third re-run.

7. **When four attempts hold no self-end.** The pass ends and the report says so as a reading: no self-end in 32
   boots, four of them first boots, under the instrument, against two red in six runs without it. It names no
   cause and does not say the instrument or the series removed it.

Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry
writes one.

body:
P-129 is not claimed by this plan (inputs#I3). Its acceptance asks for a cause named from a run and closed, then a
stated number of consecutive green runs of equal source; this plan closes nothing. One clause of it is built and
proven here without a claim: a run in which the app ends by itself says why in what the job keeps.

- (obs) A boot in which the app ends by itself keeps a machine-readable record that names the ending call and its
  caller, or the named verdict of an end the library cannot see. Proven on this host by the control leg (the entry
  whose data dir ends `-witness-display-lost`): settle verdict `ended`, `ended` `exit 1`, `app_exit_record`
  `absent`, `exit_witness` `exit-call`, and an `end` line with call `_exit` and code 1 (per obs-plan §9 Telemetry
  artifact handling; obs-plan §7 Error classes captured → Process-end cause).

- (operator, inputs#I3 condition 1) Each way a process ends with a code has a known-positive control in `cargo
  nextest run --workspace --profile ci`: a call to `exit` through the linker reads `exit-call` with an `end` and a
  `runtime-exit` line; a direct `_exit` reads `exit-call` with an `end` line and no `runtime-exit` line; `main`
  returning reads `runtime-exit`; a direct system call reads `no-record`. A self-end that leaves no `end` line is
  one of the last two labels, never an absent member.

- (operator, inputs#I3 condition 2) The library stays out of the processes the app starts. Proven by the child
  control in the same suite (one `loaded` line, the child holding neither variable, and its known positive reading
  two) and on the real app by the green leg (the entry whose data dir ends `-witness-green`): the app settles with
  its webview's child processes running and the witness file holds exactly one `loaded` line.

- (tests) The settle verdict's exit codes and verdict set are unchanged; its object holds eight members, pinned by
  equality; `harness:boot-series` prints one JSON object under the 0 / 1 / 2 contract with `cannot-evaluate` never
  passing; every decision added is a pure function with a pin per arm (per test-plan §3 `status` → Exit code
  semantics).

- (operator, inputs#I3) The series records each boot with its ordinal, its settle verdict, its exit record and its
  witness label, in the verdict and in `logs/boot-series.json`; a boot that ends by itself fails the step. Proven
  on this host by the series leg (the entry whose data dir ends `-series`).

- (arch) After the chunk `ci.yml` holds the two recorded triggers, six jobs on `ubuntu-22.04` with no matrix and
  no job edge, workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`, and a `boot` job that differs from the base by two
  added steps and nothing else; the four smoke pins pass unchanged (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns →
  CI/CD approach; architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces).

- (security) The edit adds no action reference, permission, secret reference, trigger or soft-fail key
  (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Secrets; security-plan §Bootstrap phases, `dep-security-ci-gate`).

- (security) Every file the job newly keeps is harness-written under the data dir's `logs/`, never opened by
  `pulse-app`, and named here with its content class and its classifier: `logs/exit-witness.jsonl` and its copies
  under `logs/series/` (closed-shape lines written by the library: pids, a thread id, a process name, a call, a
  code, `errno`, frames as module basename, exported symbol and offset) and `logs/boot-series.json` (closed
  labels, ordinals, counts, the bounded exit record). Classified the app's exit record and routine harness
  evidence by the operator, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10 (inputs#I3), as the operator's reading and not the
  founder's word. Each kept witness file of each attempt is read whole in the operator pass: 0 environment values,
  0 paths beyond a basename, 0 secret-class values, 0 telemetry of a watched service, or the pass stops (per
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input; security-plan §Secret Management, "What counts as secret").

- (arch) No variable this chunk adds is read by `pulse-app`'s own code: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` is read

- (a11y) The `a11y` job's steps, order and blocking status are unchanged, no artifact name is added or renamed, and

- (tests) The boot job carries no retry, no soft-fail key and no wait placed to make the self-end rarer; no CI run
  is re-run for a green, and the re-runs of the `boot` job alone that inputs#I3 allows are each recorded with

- (obs) On the runner: attempt 1's eight boots each carry an `exit_witness` label, and on every boot that settles

- Extracts with no domain coverage: design, layouts.

  end (inputs#I1 item 4).

- Naming the cause from the dev host's control — the control shows what the instrument reads; no run has shown
  what ends the app on the runner (inputs#I1 item 1).

- A system tracer installed by the job (`strace`, `gdb`) — the runner image carries none, a tracer becomes the
  app's parent or stops its threads, and its output would hold arguments and paths.

- Loading the library through the job's environment — it would enter the shell, cargo and every build process.
  It is set on the one spawn line.

- Instrumenting the webview's child processes — the record needed is of the app's own end, and children left as
  they are is one thing less changed in what is measured.

- A new product record at the exit, or a fifth field on `app.exit` — the end in question is one the product's

- A matrix value, a seventh job or a new trigger to hold several boots — each contradicts a recorded pin; a

- Uploading a boot's `run/` to keep its records — it holds the product-written `workspace-key`, a path-valued

- A second boot inside the smoke step — the four smoke pins require exactly one line per verb there.
- Fixing anything on top of a run that names the caller — closing is the next entry (inputs#I3).
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — not mirrored; stated in step 3.
- `No CI step reads nothing` is the next entry; its work is not done here, even with `ci.yml` open.

- **What the series does not reset between boots** (inputs#I3). Each later boot starts with a fresh data dir, a
  fresh display server and empty `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, so the webview's own state and the per-user
  caches that honour the cache variable start empty, as on the first boot of a fresh runner (measured on this
  host: the webview's state lands under the moved data directory and the app settles, one boot). Shared and not
  reset: the kernel's file cache, which is warm after the first boot; system-wide caches (the system font cache
  among them); everything under the runner's home that those two variables do not govern (the per-user
  configuration directory, any cache a library keeps elsewhere); leftovers under `/tmp` and `/dev/shm`; the
  session bus and whatever service the first boot left running on it. The first boot differs from the later ones
  in one more way: it runs without the two variables set. So the first boots and the later boots are two series,
  read apart.

- **What the library cannot see, by construction.** An end by a signal. A direct system call, which reads
  `no-record`. A static caller has no symbol and is named as module and offset; the exported frames around it
  carry names, and the app binary's own frames carry none, since the release profile strips symbols
  (`Cargo.toml:258-261`).

- **Readings so far, each a reading:** twelve pull-request runs of the build branch since `b3ac58a`, four red
  (`gh api …/workflows/ci.yml/runs`, re-derived at P3); under the present smoke step six readings, two red. At
  two in six, eight boots hold at least one self-end with probability about 0.96 if later boots end at the first
  boot's rate (1 − (2/3)^8); whether they do is not measured.

- **Whether the runner's C library and GTK behave as this host's do is not measured.** The four line patterns and
  the child boundary were read on this host's C library; the controls of step 4 run on the runner in the
  `lint-test` job's suite, which is where they are first read there.

- **The series adds about a minute to the `boot` job** (seven cycles of about 8 s on this host; the runner's time
  is read from attempt 1).

- **`ci-gates` does not read the series' kept logs:** it lists the log directory's own files only

- The workspace nextest and the regen after it run; no deferral is taken (two xtask tests walk the tree and the

- Sweep hazards: the Linux-only pin refuses the word for the app's windows on every line of `ci.yml`

The document does not list `strace`, `ltrace`, `gdb`, `lldb`, `bpftrace`, `perf` or `valgrind`. title: The recorded CI runs (re-read at P3)

data.head: ### The recorded CI runs (re-read at P3)

body: - **The fourth red arrived during this phase.** `ci#38014971549`, job `114103109878`, artifact `11656415762` (4510 B, expires 2026-10-24): `harness-settled.json` reads `verdict ended`, `ended "exit 1"`, `app_exit_record absent`, `windows_settled 0`, `display reachable`, `session_bus reachable`; `xvfb.log` is 0 B; `boot.log` holds the one accessibility-bus line; the log is 57 records long, `ui-bridge.ready` at 0.928 s and the last record (`triage.cue.tick`) at 1.273 s after the first. No `app.exit`, no `app.panic.fatal`, no `app.boot.window.navigation`. The commit under it changed `scripts/code-graph.py` and four files of a run dir (`git show --stat 8936f976`), nothing a job builds.

- **The four reds share one shape.** Each log holds both `ui.webgpu.adapter` records (`main` and `compact-widget`, both `no_navigator_gpu`) and ends 0 to 0.34 s after the second. Each run's one failed job is `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` (`gh api …/actions/runs/{id}/jobs`, the four reds).

- **A lead that did not hold.** On the two reds read first the webview's first record came later (0.829 s, 0.898 s) than on two greens (0.440 s, 0.565 s). Two other greens read 1.150 s and 1.390 s. It separates nothing.

- **The count, re-derived.** `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?per_page=40`, rows created from `2026-10-09T11:38:31Z` on: fourteen runs, each attempt 1. Twelve are pull-request runs on the build branch, four of them red (`b3ac58a9`, `f36a2ac3`, `cb8cc4dc`, `8936f976`); one is the hotfix branch's (green), one a push on `main` (green). Under the present smoke step (the settle verdict, from `e2931127` on) the `boot` job has six readings, two red.

- **What "display reachable" does and does not say.** The settle verdict's `display` label is a fresh connection attempt to the display's socket made after the app has ended (`xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, `unix_socket_accepts`). It shows the server was accepting. It does not show the app's own connection was sound.

- **The freight's claims hold on re-read** (scope.md, "The causal and measured claims"): 53 records with `ui-bridge.ready` at 0.835 s and the last record at 0.907 s on `ci#38010977166`; the navigation records 4.129 s to 4.696 s after `ui-bridge.ready` on four greens.

- **The runner image carries no tracer and carries a C compiler** (the image's own list, above). A tracer would be a package the job installs; a library built from a short C source needs nothing the image lacks.

- **A library loaded into the app process alone records the ending call with its caller.** A research probe of about 130 lines (kept in the session scratchpad, not in the tree) interposes `_exit`, `_Exit`, `exit`, `quick_exit` and `abort`, and at the call appends one JSON line: pid, thread id, process name, the call, its code, `errno`, and the caller frames as module basename, exported symbol and offset. It was loaded through `LD_PRELOAD` on the app's spawn line of a scratch copy of `scripts/agent-run.sh` (one line changed, line 79).

- **Read on a known member of the class (the display stopped 2 s after ready, 2 boots):** settle verdict `ended`, `exit 1`, no `app.exit`, nothing new in `boot.log`, and the probe's record: `_exit`, code 1, `errno` 11, called from `libgdk-3.so.0` +0x8ca2d (a static function, so no symbol), entered from `libX11.so.6` `_XIOError` under `_XEventsQueued` under `XPending`, under GLib's main loop and `gtk_main_iteration_do`, on the main thread, 2 of 2. One boot also recorded a second thread reaching the same handler through `XNextEvent` called from the app binary. Without the probe the same control reads only "exit 1, no record" (1 boot).

- **Its cost on green boots is not visible at this n.** Six boots with it against six without, alternating, load 2.2 to 5.9: the boot verb returned in 1.02 s to 1.09 s in both arms; the webview's first record came at 0.869 s (0.854 to 0.913) with it and 0.911 s (0.852 to 1.017) without; the four windows settled at 5.173 s in both. It wrote 0 lines on every green boot (a SIGTERM end is no exit call) and added no line to `boot.log`. **Not measured: its cost on the runner.**

- **What it cannot see, by construction.** An end by a signal. An end that returns from `main` (measured: `/usr/bin/false` under the probe leaves 0 lines; the C runtime's own exit is not an interposable call), which the product's `atexit` hook does record as `app.exit`. A direct system call that bypasses the C library's wrappers. A static caller has no symbol, so the record names it as module and offset; the exported frames around it carry names.

- **A direct-call child is a deterministic witness for a committed test.** `python3 -c "import os; os._exit(7)"` under the probe wrote one line: `"call":"_exit","code":7`, the frames under `libpython3.14.so.1.0`.

- **The webview's child processes were not instrumented and not measured.** Seven probe boots with the variable inherited wrote 0 child lines and no loader refusal line; whether those processes load an inherited library was not established either way. The record needed is of the app process's own end.

- **The corpus key does not reach such a record.** The record holds what the library formats and nothing of the process's memory, environment or arguments. On the runner the app holds no corpus key at all: every boot log read carries `corpus.open.error {error_kind: KeyringUnavailable}`, and `ci.yml` names no passphrase variable (`grep -n PASSPHRASE .github/workflows/ci.yml`, 0 lines).

title: Several boots in one run (the relay's question 3b)

data.head: ### Several boots in one run (the relay's question 3b)

body: - **The workflow's recorded shape admits it as a step, not as a job or a matrix value.** `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only` refuses a `matrix.os` token and any other runner; the trigger block is pinned; the four smoke pins read only the step named `Boot pulse-app smoke` up to the next `- name:` line (`pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs:435-449`), so a following step is not read by them. A second boot inside the smoke step itself would trip `only_line_with`, which requires exactly one line per verb.

- **Each boot needs its own data dir.** `harness:settled`, `harness:status` and `ci-gates` resolve one log family from `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`; both readers list the log directory's own files only (`xtask/src/main.rs:623-642`, `xtask/src/smoke.rs:519-536`), so a file kept one directory below `logs/` is not swept into the family `ci-gates` grades.

- **`run/` must not be uploaded with it.** The data dir's `run/` holds the product-written `workspace-key`, a path-valued file; the job uploads `logs/` alone, so what a further boot keeps is copied into `logs/` file by file.

- **Booting again changes what is measured in two named ways.** The webview keeps state under the user's data directory: one probe boot with `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` pointed at fresh directories created `com.andromeda.pulse/` there with `WebKitCache`, `CacheStorage`, `storage`, `mediakeys` and `hsts-storage.sqlite`, and settled with four windows. Without the two variables a second boot in one job finds the first boot's state. The file cache is warm for every boot after the first. Every recorded red was the first and only boot of a fresh runner.

- **Not measured: whether a later boot ends by itself at the first boot's rate.** No run has held more than one boot. On the dev host thirteen sequential boots of the unchanged sequence all settled, which says nothing about the runner.

- **What one run would read.** At two reds in six, one boot per run reads about one self-end in three runs. If later boots end at that rate, eight boots in one run hold at least one self-end with probability about 0.96; if they do not, the first boot still carries the instrument.

- `scripts/agent-run.sh:71-99` runs the app under a waiting subshell that is its direct parent, records the app's pid in `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` and its end in `run/andromeda-pulse.exit`. A library preloaded on that spawn line leaves the pid, the parent and the reaper as they are (measured: every probe boot's exit record and `cleanup: clean` read as in the plain arm).

- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` mirrors the recorder (`:170-182`). A preloaded library has no form there; the script is parsed and never run on this host and leaves with "Other operating systems retired from the code".

- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs:87-122` (`run_settled`) reads the exit record, the log evidence and the two socket labels after the verdict, prints one JSON object and writes it to `logs/harness-settled.json`. Its member set is pinned by `settled_payload_carries_the_closed_field_set` (`:624`).
- The `a11y` job does not run the `boot` verb: `agent-run` appears in `ci.yml` on lines 385, 387 and 388 only, all in the `boot` job (`grep -n agent-run .github/workflows/ci.yml`).

- The `boot` job's steps (`ci.yml:325-403`): harden-runner first, the data dir exported to `$GITHUB_ENV`, the build, the smoke step, `ci-gates` (skipped when the smoke fails), the upload under `if: always()` of `${{ env.ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR }}/logs/`.

- A sweep hazard for any new workflow comment: `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only` refuses the token `windows` on every line of `ci.yml`, comments included (`pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs:114-121`), so a step comment cannot name the app's windows by that word.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (1-22, 325-403) — the triggers and permissions, the `boot` job whole.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` (full) — the five verbs; the spawn line (`:79`), the waiting wrapper (`:78-89`), the readiness poll (`:106-118`), `cleanup`.
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` (by grep) — the mirrored recorder and `Invoke-Ready`.
- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` (1-125, 160-380, the test list) — `run_settled`, `decide_settled`, `read_exit_record`, `settled_payload`, `keep_verdict`, the socket labels.
- `xtask/src/harness_status.rs` (the function list) — `resolve_paths`, `resolve_data_dir`, `end_file`, `read_ended`, `read_pid`, `pid_alive`.
- `xtask/src/main.rs` (the verb list, 373-381, 623-642) — the three `harness:*` verbs, `cargo_command`, `collect_log_files`.
- `xtask/src/smoke.rs` (519-545) — `read_jsonl_lines`, the family reader.
- `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` (by grep) — `script-modes` reads the mode of `scripts/agent-run.sh` alone.
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` (2700-2914) — the `app.exit` record, the `atexit` hand-off, the signal listener, the stated unloggable list.
- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` (101-131, 418-562) — the Linux-only pin, the upload pin, the four smoke pins.
- `Cargo.toml` (252-261) — the release profile strips symbols (`strip = true`), so the app binary's own frames carry no name.
- `.andromeda/registries/contracts/architecture/project-directory-structure.md` (full) — the directory contract; `scripts/` is the driver's registered home in §Occupied Resources.
- The previous two chunks' records: `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed/{scope,research}.md`, `2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux/evidence/operator-pass.md` (91-190).
