title: Scope — Boot smoke's self-end named from a run

data.head: # Scope — Boot smoke's self-end named from a run

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates
**Working entry (`working-route.md:19`):** "Boot smoke's self-end named from a run — the job keeps what names who
ended the app; cause closed; equal source reads the same (P-129)", with one `CARRY:` block folded below.
**Chunk base:** `8936f976` (HEAD at take-up, equal to its upstream). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this
sha, never HEAD.

Requirement P-129 reads: "the CI boot smoke ends the same on equal source: the cause of the app ending by itself
shortly after ready on the runner is found and closed, and the job no longer reads red where nothing it builds
changed" (`matrix.py show --id P-129`, read at take-up). The `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` job has read red on four
of the twelve pull-request runs of the build branch since `b3ac58a` (re-derived at P3; three of ten when the entry
was minted). The job's own instruments say how the app ended and that its display and session bus were still
there, and they do not say who ended it. This chunk makes a run keep what names who ended the app, names the cause
from such a run, closes it, and shows equal source reading the same.

The operator's direction for this chunk (inputs#I1, the pc overseer's phase directive; inputs#I2, the invocation
word): the cause is named from what a CI run keeps, never from a local reproduction; two questions go to research
as measurements; the chunk adds no retry, no soft-fail key and no timing pad; the plan card is printed at P5 and the
chunk stops there for the operator's `yes`.

- **The boot job keeps what names who ended the app** (the entry). The freight lists what the job does not keep
  today: "any record of the call that ended it (no stack or trace at the exit), the exit statuses of the webview's
  own child processes, anything the kernel or the session logged at that instant". The chunk makes a run in which
  the app ends by itself keep a record that names the ending call and its caller.
  - **Which instrument records it** (inputs#I1 item 3a), answered at P3 by measurement (research.md "The
    instrument"): the runner image as it is carries no tracer (`strace`, `ltrace`, `gdb`, `bpftrace`, `perf` are not
    in the image's own list) and carries a C compiler. A small library loaded into the app process alone, which
    records the exit call with its caller frames, was built with that compiler's kind on the dev host and read on a
    known member of the silent `exit 1` class (the display stopped): it named `_exit(1)`, called from a static
    function of `libgdk-3.so.0` entered from Xlib's `_XIOError`, with the thread and `errno`, 2 of 2. On six green
    boots against six without it no timing difference was visible (the webview's first record at 0.869 s against
    0.911 s median, four windows settled at 5.173 s in both arms) and it wrote nothing. Its cost on the runner is
    not measured; the chunk's first run reads it on a green boot before a red one is trusted to it.
  - **Whether one run can hold several independent boots** (inputs#I1 item 3b), answered at P3 (research.md
    "Several boots in one run"): yes, inside the recorded workflow shape, as a step of the `boot` job that boots
    again on a fresh data dir under its own display server, sharing the job's one build. Booting again does change
    what is measured in two named ways: the webview keeps state under the user's data directory
    (`com.andromeda.pulse/` with `WebKitCache`, `CacheStorage`, `storage`), which a second boot finds unless it is
    given its own (measured: with `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` moved the state lands there and the app
    settles); and the file cache is warm. Every recorded red was the first and only boot of a fresh runner. So a
    series records each boot's position, and whether later boots end at the first boot's rate is read from the
    series itself, not assumed.
  - **A design that waits for a natural red waits about three runs for one reading** (inputs#I1 item 1). Verified at
    P3: under the present step the `boot` job has six readings, two red (`cb8cc4dc`, `8936f976`). The plan states
    how many readings its design needs and where they come from.

- **The cause is named from a run** (the entry's title; P-129's acceptance: "named from evidence a run produced, not
  inferred"). Never from a local reproduction (inputs#I1 item 1). Verified at P3: the previous chunk's research
  holds "0 self-ends in 51 boots", and this chunk's thirteen further local boots of the unchanged sequence all
  settled. A local boot measures an instrument's cost and shape; it does not name the cause.

- **The cause is closed** (the entry). Naming and closing may be two steps (inputs#I1 item 4: "A change that names
  the cause and a change that closes it may be two steps; if the cause cannot be closed in this chunk, say so at P5
  and claim nothing of P-129 that was not shown"). Which of the two this plan is, is P4's to state.

- Added at P4, the operator's three rulings (inputs#I3):
  - **This plan names; the closing is the next entry.** A run can name the cause only after the operator's pre-CI
    commit, and past it no plan revision is offered. The pass stops at the first witnessed self-end and says what
    the job kept; closing is planned from that record as its own entry at the wrap. P-129 is not claimed here.
    When the first run holds no self-end, the `boot` job alone may be re-run on the same commit, "at most three
    times, to collect equal-source readings - every attempt is recorded with its number, none replaces another,
    and the chunk CI verdict stays the first attempt."
  - **The kept witness file is the app's exit record, routine harness evidence**: "Operator reading (pc overseer),
    recorded as mine and not the founder word: it holds less than the app log the job already uploads." Two
    conditions: each of the three ways a process ends with a code (a call through the linker, a direct `_exit`,
    `main` returning) gets a known-positive control, "and a self-end that leaves no witness line reads as its own
    named verdict, never as nothing"; and the plan says how the library stays out of the webview's child processes
    and proves it by a control.
  - **A gating series, eight boots a run.** "The defect stays visible until it is closed. Record each boot ordinal
    with its verdict: a self-end rate that differs between the first boot and the later ones is itself a reading
    to report, not noise." What the series does not reset between boots is named in the plan.

- **Equal source reads the same** (the entry; P-129). The acceptance names "a stated number of consecutive runs of
  equal source" reading green, counted with the cause closed. A pull-request run builds the branch merged with
  `main`, so a reading is of equal source only while both tips stand. Verified at P3: the logs of the runs on
  `8936f976` and `b7101914` carry `git.commit.sha` `9df2c7b57a2e` and `4a79cbbbf22d`, neither the pushed tip.

- **The records that describe the boot job and what it keeps are corrected at the wrap, not here.** Phase amends no
  spec source.

- **Chunk base:** `279a477e9e12a1e76bae3bab3c64e42db9949a8f`. Every diff-shaped entry names this sha, never HEAD.

82 capabilities stand as claimed in two records of the 0.2 and 0.3 product. This chunk writes one current record,
`docs/capability-record.json`, that gives each of P-001…P-082 exactly one of two dispositions: **claimed** by the
engine as it will stand, naming the 0.4.0 requirement that carries it, or **retired**, naming its surface, the
route entry that removes that surface and what guards it until then. The old gate,
`cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix`, reads that file from now on: it holds all 82 ids to the form, validates

architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach).

The record is written for a second reader. Conductor derives its accepted set from it (inputs#I2, inputs#I7), and
its pin is one flat list of ids read by membership (inputs#I5, inputs#I6). So the form is stated here once:
**the accepted set is every entry whose `disposition` is the string `claimed`; an entry whose `disposition` is
`retired` says with what in `surfaces` and by which route entry in `removed_by`.** Nothing else in the file is
needed to derive the set.

No surface is removed. The window, the model, their code and their tests stand after this chunk as before it.
The classification rests on the operator's four answers at P4 (inputs#I8); four of the claimed ids are
PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word.

0. **Red first.** Before any other edit, write the per-arm pins of step 3 against a stub of the module that
   returns a pass for every input, and run them: every arm but the clean one reads red. Record the reading in
   `chunks/2026-10-10-capability-record-re-based/evidence/red-before-green.md`.

1. **Write `docs/capability-record.json`** (new). One JSON object, UTF-8, LF, two-space indent:
   - a header: `schema_version` (the number 1), `product` (`andromeda-pulse`), `version`
     (`andromeda-pulse-0.4.0`), `as_of` (`2026-10-10`), `supersedes` (the three old sources: the capability spec
     and the gate record under `docs/v0_2_0/`, and `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json`), and `legend`
     — an object stating the two disposition words, the six surface words and the three guard words, each with one
     line of meaning, so the file reads without this plan;
   - `capabilities`: 82 entries in id order, P-001 first.
   - Every entry: `id`, `title` (as the old record spells it), `disposition`, and an optional `note`.
   - A **claimed** entry adds `carried_by` (an array of 0.4.0 requirement ids, P-083…P-129; empty only on P-077,
     whose `note` says no requirement restates it), `verification_mode` and `scenarios`. Where the original
     sentence no longer holds as written it adds `changed_form`, which says so plainly and quotes the requirement
     text it is claimed in. The four PROVISIONAL ids add `provisional` (true) and a `note` naming whose word is
     owed.
   - A **retired** entry adds `surfaces` (one or more of the six words), `removed_by` (one or more route entry
     titles, spelt as `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0/working-route.md` spells them), `guard` — an object with `state`
     (`runs`, `part` or `none`), `by` (the proofs a CI job runs) and `unrun` (the automated proofs the old record
     names that no gate runs) — and, where engine-side code of the id is listed by no removing entry,
     `kept_half_owner` (the route entry that owns that code). A retired entry has no `scenarios`, no
     `verification_mode` and no `carried_by`.

     the 0.3.0 record get theirs from that record's `ref`: P-067 and P-074 a `nextest-file` with its `contains`
     anchor (both anchors were found at P3, one line each), P-075 an `external` scenario naming the Conductor round
     the 0.3.0 ledger records, P-077 a `source-evidence` scenario on `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` and a
     `manual` one. `external` and `manual` are two new scenario kinds; each needs the entry's `note`, as
     `by-construction` does.

2. **Do not touch the two old records.** `docs/v0_2_0/` and `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json` stay
   byte-identical; the scope guard holds it.

3. **Write `xtask/src/capability_record.rs`** (new): the record's reader and its pure verdict, taking the
   record's text, the route's text and the repository root, and returning the verdict with every finding. No new
   dependency: `serde_json` values, as the gate reads today. It decides, in this order:
   - **cannot-evaluate** — the record is absent, unreadable, not JSON or holds no `capabilities` array; the route
     file is absent or unreadable;
   - **findings** — the id set is not exactly P-001…P-082 once each (a missing id, a duplicate, an id outside the
     range); a `disposition` that is neither word; the `legend` not equal to the module's own three closed sets;
     on a claimed entry: `carried_by` absent, an element outside P-083…P-129, or empty with no `note`;

     does not exist; a `contains` anchor not found; an `external`, `manual` or `by-construction` scenario with no
     `note`; on a retired entry: a `scenarios`, `verification_mode` or `carried_by` key present; `surfaces` empty

     `kept_half_owner` naming such a title; `guard` absent, its `state` unknown, `runs` or `part` with an empty
     `by`, `part` or `none` with an empty `unrun`; and a record with no claimed id at all;
   - **clean** otherwise.
   A route entry's title is its line without a leading `[marker] ` stamp, up to the first ` — `.

   record so that only the arm under test differs; and one pin that reads the committed record and the committed

   caller, `main()` @ `xtask/src/main.rs:326`) reads `docs/capability-record.json` and

   `verify:capability-matrix: clean (82 ids: 36 claimed, 46 retired, 0 violation(s))`, the three counts read from
   the record, with the state word `violations` or `cannot-evaluate` in the other arms; the JSON event and the
   report twin under `target/capability-matrix/` carry the same counts. The `about` string says what the verb
   reads now. The body that walked the old file leaves; the `mod` line joins the others.

5. **Rename the CI step** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:105`: its display name stops saying "P-001..P-060 scenario
   mapping" and says it reads the capability record. The `run:` line, its place after `capability-widening-check`
   and every other line of the workflow are unchanged.

6. **Re-word the pin's message** in `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs:150-152`: the assertion
   (`content.contains("cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix")`, `:149`) is unchanged and stays green, since the
   `run:` line is; only the failure message stops naming the first sixty.
Requirement ids are the 0.4.0 ones. A quoted phrase is requirement text, copied into `changed_form`.
**Claimed (36).**

- Detection, carried by P-086 ("everything 0.3.0 detected is still detected"): P-005 (+P-096), P-006 (+P-095),
  P-007 (+P-096), P-008, P-009 (+P-091), P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013 (+P-091), P-014 (+P-098), P-015, P-016, P-017,
  P-018, P-057, P-074. `changed_form` on those whose text gives a model the last word (P-010, P-012, P-014,
  P-018): the detection stands; no model decides whether it surfaces.
- P-021, P-022 — P-086, P-112. Changed form: a cue forms the incident itself; resolution carries no model summary.

- P-001 — P-098: "'no data reached the engine' … [is one of] three different states, and a recovery is announced".
  The five named states and the connection dot are not claimed.

- P-004 — P-098 and P-091: the three states are different states; "a gap while the engine was down is not read as
  the service's silence".
- P-027, P-067 — P-109: "the service registry's liveness truth stays engine state". Nothing is rendered.

- P-036, P-044 — P-110 ("the search for similar past incidents is kept and lives where incidents live") and P-092
  ("the incidents like it from the past"). The reader is a large model through the door, not a local one.
- P-039 — P-092, P-093: the door's tools. The "Send to agent" button is not claimed.

- P-041 — P-112. P-042 — P-112 and P-105 ("incidents are formed, kept, listed and resolved the same from wherever
  the engine is started"); read and acknowledged marks are not claimed.

- P-047 — P-085, P-088. P-055, P-056 — P-108. P-075 — P-102 (the read-back half; the four timing bounds are not
  claimed). P-077 — no requirement; its `note` says so.

- **PROVISIONAL, the founder's own word owed** (inputs#I8, answer 3). Each `changed_form` opens by saying the
  original sentence no longer holds as written:
  - P-030 — P-099, P-102. Original: no OS notification by default. Changed form: "a change of state raises a
    system notification", and the engine "stayed silent through the healthy hours".
  - P-040 — P-084, P-099. Original: every capability works with no MCP configured. Changed form: "the engine
    starts, detects and reports with no model present and none configured"; "a large model reads through the door
    (P-092) and is not part of the engine". The door itself is part of the engine and is not optional.
  - P-048 — P-088, P-093, P-085. Original: no raw attribute value stored. Changed form: "everything the scrubber
    removes today is still removed before anything is stored"; "what it returns was scrubbed at ingest".
  - P-050 — P-106, P-093. Original: fully local by default. Changed form: "nothing the engine writes lands outside
    its own stores"; the door "answers only a party the node's owner has admitted".

**Retired (46).** `guard.state` in brackets: a part when at least one automated proof the old record names runs in
a CI job and at least one does not.

- With the window, removed by `Window retired`: P-002 [runs], P-003 [runs], P-023 [runs], P-024 [part],
  P-026 [none], P-028 [part], P-029 [part], P-037 [runs], P-038 [runs], P-045 [runs], P-051 [runs], P-061 [runs],
  P-062 [runs], P-063 [part], P-064 [none], P-065 [none], P-066 [none], P-068 [none], P-069 [part], P-070 [part],
  P-071 [part], P-080 [part], P-081 [part], P-082 [part]; P-025 [none], removed by `Window retired` and
  `Display-only computation retired`.
  `kept_half_owner`: P-002 and P-003 name `Display-only computation retired`; P-023 names
  `Incident is the engine's own record`.
- With the window, removed by `Window's gates retired`: P-076 [part], P-078 [part].

- With the window and the model, removed by `Window retired` and `Local model retired`: P-058 [runs]
  (`kept_half_owner` `Display-only computation retired`), P-072 [runs].

- With the model, removed by `Local model retired`: P-019 [runs], P-020 [part], P-033 [runs], P-034 [runs],
  P-053 [runs], P-054 [part], P-073 [runs]; by `Local model retired` and `Incident is the engine's own record`:
  P-031 [runs], P-035 [runs]; by `Cadence coordinator retired`: P-052 [runs], P-060 [part]; by `Digest retired`:
  P-059 [runs].

- With the model and the workspace, removed by `Local model retired` and `Workspace detection retired`:
  P-032 [runs].

- With the workspace, removed by `Workspace detection retired`: P-043 [runs]. With the window and the workspace,
  removed by `Window retired` and `Workspace detection retired`: P-079 [runs].

- With the training export, removed by `Training export retired`: P-046 [runs]. With corpus encryption, removed by
  `Corpus encryption at rest retired`: P-049 [runs].
- Guard totals: none 6, part 15, runs 25 (counted from the list above; research gives the proof behind each).
- `docs/capability-record.json` — the one current record
- `xtask/src/capability_record.rs` — the reader, the verdict and its pins
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the verb, its about string, verdict line and exits; the old walk leaves
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the step's display name only
- `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` — the pin's message only

The chunk's own probes come first, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order: `capability-drift` before the
default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step,
and the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure. The local pre-push check follows, then
the operator pass.
Absences, each with its reason:
- No boot-smoke entry: no file of the chunk is on the boot-smoke trigger list, and the chunk boots no app.

- No webview gates and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path changes. The `a11y` job is read on the CI
  run.
- No liveness probe and no live leg: the chunk drives no external process and binds no port.

- No entry runs the verb over an absent record: the verb reads a fixed in-repo path and takes no path argument or
  variable (a new input would be a boundary question). The absent-record and absent-route arms are held by the
  pins of step 3, which the workspace nextest entry runs.

- Step 0's red reading is a one-shot run at implement; the workspace nextest entry guards the arms on every
  re-run.

**The operator pass, in this order.** The hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the local pre-push entry again, the
merge-base probe, the push; then the whole pull-request run of the pushed tip is read. One read by that run's id,
as `<id>`, follows: the gate's own line in the `lint-test` job log. The last entry lists every job, report-only.
A red merge-base probe goes to the operator before any push. No run is re-run to obtain a green.

Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry
writes one.

**Marker:** `2026-10-10-capability-record-re-based` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates

claimed or retired with its surface; the old gate reads it (P-117)"
**Chunk base:** `279a477e` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this sha, never HEAD.

82 capabilities stand as claimed in two records that describe the product of 0.2 and 0.3: P-001…P-060 in
`docs/v0_2_0/pulse-capability-spec.md` with a gate over `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json`, and
P-061…P-082 in `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json`. Many of them are about the window, the local model

retired with a named surface — and makes the old gate read that record, so that it carries no retired id. The
record is also what another project reads: the external harness (Conductor) derives its accepted set from it.

  those four take is a fork, brought at P4.

- **A retired id names the route entry that removes its surface** (inputs#I1 item 3), by the entry's title. Closed

  accepted set is one flat list of ids in `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` (inputs#I5), read by list membership

- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T13:08:04Z
- **Chunk base:** `f31027a4023fd64e97bff3272d303faa628d2336` — every diff-shaped probe names it, never `HEAD`.

The engine exists today only inside the window app: one `fn main()` in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` builds its state
and spawns every one of its tasks from the Tauri setup closure. This chunk lifts that boot into one function and
adds a second program, `andromeda-pulse-engine`, that calls it with no window. The console program boots the two
loopback OTLP receivers, the ring buffer, the detectors and the corpus, is driven by a command (`run`), and keeps
the same five records of itself that the window app keeps: its log, its identity at boot, its panic record, its
heartbeat and exactly one record of how the process ended.

**It fits one chunk, and no crate's dependency on the window framework is cut.** Research measured that none of
the engine-wiring modules imports the window framework and that a binary which links the `pulse_app` library
without building the window needs none of the window's shared libraries at load (0 of 103 test binaries; the
window binary needs 6). So the console program is a second `[[bin]]` of `pulse-app`, sharing the engine code in
place. `tauri` leaves the crate's manifest at `Window retired`, with nothing for this chunk to undo.

**One engine serves both programs until Epoch 2** because both call the same boot function and neither wires an
engine part itself. Three things forbid drift: a source pin that reddens when either entry point names an engine
task or the shared boot names the window framework; one in-process test of the boot function; and two programs
run on every push (the window by the boot job and its eight boots, the console by a test in the workspace run).

**No local model in the console program** (inputs#I1 item 5, inputs#I2). It starts, loads and waits for none and
reads no model variable. At the point where 0.3.0 called the model it follows the registered variable
`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`: set, it seats the canned runner and an incident forms; unset, it seats
nothing, so cues and digests are produced and no incident forms, and its boot record says why. The unset arm's
owner is `Incident is the engine's own record` (`working-route.md:65`). The window app's own seat is not moved.

Provenance: scope.md; inputs#I1; inputs#I2; architecture §Occupied Resources and §Cross-cutting Patterns →
Module dependency direction; obs-plan §3 Tracing init, §3 Heartbeat ticks, §6, §8; test-plan §3; security-plan
§Security Anti-Patterns.

1. **Move the boot helpers into the library.** `resolve_data_dir`, `resolve_port`, `resolve_grpc_port`,
   `resolve_http_port`, `resolve_retention_seconds`, `write_pid_file`, `publish_workspace_key_for_sidecar` and
   `init_buffer` leave `pulse-app/src/main.rs` for the new `pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs`, unchanged in behaviour,
   `pub` + `#[doc(hidden)]`. Their 14 tests leave `main.rs`'s `mod tests` for
   `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_env.rs`, same names, same assertions (a test left beside them in a library
   source never runs). `resolve_mcp_sidecar_binary_path` and `emit_taurpc_bindings` stay in `main.rs`.

2. **One process-start function.** `engine_boot::init_process(data_dir)` does, in this order, what `main` does
   today at `main.rs:298-303`: the log sink and its guard, the at-exit hook, the Unix signal listener, the start
   instant, the pid file. It is called with the tokio runtime entered (the signal listener needs one).

4. **Split the heartbeat spawn.** `heartbeat::spawn` (`pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs:85`) becomes the engine's three
   ticks (`ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick`, `connection.tick`), called by `engine_boot::start`, and the window's two
   (`viz.tick`, `plugins.tick`), called by `main`. Callers: `main()` at `pulse-app/src/main.rs:1557` and
   `pulse-app/tests/unit_heartbeat_ticks.rs:25` and `:474` (research, Graph impact); the five-handle test becomes
   a three-handle and a two-handle test. The window app still emits all five.

5. **The boot record.** Target `app.boot.engine`, emitted exactly once per boot by `engine_boot::start`, fields
   `program` (`window` | `console`), `interpretation` (`model` | `deterministic` | `none`) and `reason`
   (`window_runs_model` | `deterministic_gate_set` | `deterministic_gate_unset`). WARN when `interpretation` is
   `none`, its message saying that no incident forms until the engine keeps its own incident record and naming
   the variable; INFO otherwise. Its own exact allowlist leaf in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` beside
   `app.boot.render.posture`, guarded in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_boot_engine.rs`: exact
   resolve, field-set equality both ways, the no-bare-`app` discriminator, and an emit-site capture equal to the
   leaf for each of the four program and seat combinations.

6. **The window's `main` calls the two functions.** After its first two statements and its own runtime build,
   which stay where they are, `main` calls `init_process`, then its own `window::emit_boot_spans()` and
   `render_posture::emit_posture(..)`, then selects its runner exactly as today (`main.rs:512-559`, the
   `interpretation.model.load` record included) and calls `engine_boot::start` with program `window`, the OS key
   backend, the hardware profile detector and that runner. Routers, the plugin host, `VizState`, the window
   geometry, the Tauri builder and the event-loop tail stay in `main`. The setup closure keeps only window work.

7. **The console program.** `pulse-app/src/console.rs` holds a closed command grammar and the run function;
   `pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs` is a `main` that passes its arguments to it. `pulse-app/Cargo.toml`
   gains the `[[bin]]` and `default-run = "pulse-app"`.
   - `run` — build and enter the runtime, `init_process`, then `engine_boot::start` with program `console`, the
     OS key backend, `triage::contract::UnknownHardwareProfile`, and the seat: the canned runner (at the tier
     `tier_for_profile` gives for the unknown profile) when `deterministic_mode_enabled()` is true, else none.
     Then it waits; a SIGTERM or SIGINT ends it through the existing listener, which records the end and
     re-raises the signal.
   - `version` — print one line, exit 0; no data dir is touched and no record written.
   - no command, or any other word — usage on stderr, exit 2; nothing created.
   The program applies no render posture, initialises no Xlib thread support, constructs no
   `HardwareProfileDetector` or `LlamaCliInference`, and reads no model variable.

8. **The drift pin.** `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_seam.rs` reads the sources and asserts: `main.rs` and
   `console.rs` each call `engine_boot::start(` once and `engine_boot::init_process(` once; neither they nor the
   bin file name an engine entry point from a closed list written in the test (the consumer, retention, emitter,
   cadence coordinator, lifecycle heartbeat, restart and storm detectors, the persist loops, the auto-resolution
   loop, the two receiver `serve_on` calls, the interpretation subscriber, `Corpus::open`); `engine_boot.rs`
   names neither `tauri` nor `taurpc`; `console.rs` and the bin file name no model path variable,
   `LlamaCliInference`, `HardwareProfileDetector`, `render_posture` or `xlib_threads`. Mutation check: a
   `run_retention(` call put back into `main.rs` turns it red.

9. **The boot function in process.** `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` calls `engine_boot::start` on a
   `TempDir`, with the fake key backend and two ports it picked, one test per arm:
   - both receivers accept, a span sent over gRPC advances `rows_ingested`, and that service is listed in the
     lifecycle registry (the three-observer composition is wired);
   - seat `deterministic`: a cue-bearing digest sent on the digest broadcast (the shape of `digest_with_cue()` in
     `pulse-app/tests/integration_deterministic_l4_mode.rs`) yields one incident in the registry, and the boot
     record reads `deterministic` / `deterministic_gate_set`;
   - seat none: the same digest reaches the corpus's digest archive and the registry stays empty, and the boot
     record reads `none` / `deterministic_gate_unset` at WARN;
   - program `window` with a seated runner reads `window` in the record.
   Two more arms re-execute the test binary, in the form of `pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs`
   (the child proves it ran; the parent reads the log family after the child has ended). Each child builds and
   enters a runtime, calls `engine_boot::init_process` on its own `TempDir`, and ends one way: a panic on a
   thread followed by a process exit leaves one ERROR `app.panic.fatal` and one `app.exit` of class
   `outside_event_loop`; a raised SIGTERM leaves one `app.exit` of class `signal` and the child ends by signal.
   Both show the pid file written. This is the process-start function both programs call.
   Waits are on explicit signals under a bound, never a sleep. The capture subscriber is installed process-wide.

10. **The console program run with no display.** `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` spawns
    `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_andromeda-pulse-engine")` with a cleared environment that holds only its own `TempDir`
    data dir, two ports the test picked, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` (a canary value) and, when the test
    process has one, `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`; its working directory is the `TempDir`. Arms:
    - **`run`, variable unset.** Wait until both ports accept; read the pid file equal to the child's pid; send
      spans over gRPC with a `tonic` client; wait for a `duckdb.append` record and for two `ingest.tick` and two
      `buffer.tick` records; send SIGTERM; after the child has ended, read its log family. Asserted: it ended by
      signal 15; every line parses and carries the three identity fields; the boot record reads `console` /
      `none` / `deterministic_gate_unset` at WARN; exactly one `app.exit`, the last record, class `signal`,
      signal `sigterm`, no field redacted; one `corpus.keychain.fallback`; no `app.panic.fatal`, no ERROR, no
      `interpretation.incident.created`, no `interpretation.model.*`, no `viz.tick`, no `plugins.tick`, no
      `app.boot.window.*`, `app.boot.webview.init`, `app.boot.gpu.check` or `app.boot.tray.init`; consecutive
      ticks of each target at most 45 s apart and `buffer.tick`'s `rows_ingested_delta` rendered; the passphrase
      canary and the data dir's full path occur nowhere; the child's stderr holds no log record; both ports
      refuse.
    - **`run`, variable set.** Wait for the ports; the boot record reads `console` / `deterministic` /
      `deterministic_gate_set` at INFO; send SIGINT; one `app.exit` with signal `sigint`.
    - **`version`** exits 0 with one line and leaves its data dir empty; **an unknown word** exits 2 with usage
      on stderr and leaves it empty.
    `pulse-app/tests/unit_console_commands.rs` pins the grammar in process (each word, no word, an extra word).
- `pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs` — the boot helpers, `init_process`, `start`, the boot record
- `pulse-app/src/console.rs` — the console program's command grammar and run function
- `pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs` — the console program's entry point
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_env.rs` — the 14 resolver tests moved out of `main.rs`
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_console_commands.rs` — the grammar pins
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_boot_engine.rs` — the boot record's leaf guard
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_seam.rs` — the drift pin
- `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` — the boot function in process, both seat arms
- `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` — the built console program run with no display
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — the engine boot leaves; the window shell, the routers and the bindings test stay
- `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` — the two new modules
- `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs` — the engine's ticks and the window's ticks spawn apart
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — the `app.boot.engine` leaf
- `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` — the second `[[bin]]`, `default-run`
- `pulse-app/tests/unit_heartbeat_ticks.rs` — the callers of the split spawn

The chunk's own probes and pins come first, then the window app's smoke, then the standard gate set in test-plan
§3 order (`capability-drift` before the default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings
regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure), then
the local pre-push check, then the operator pass.

**The window app's smoke** is owed because `pulse-app/src/main.rs` and `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` change
(test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate). It is the harness series of two boots on this host in its recorded form: each
boot under its own virtual display, the receivers moved to 14317 and 14318 so the shared ports 4317 and 4318 are
never bound, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset, a fresh data dir under `target/boot-smoke/` named at invocation. The same
statement then reads each boot's kept log for the new boot record with `program` `window`.

**The console program's own run** is `integration_console_engine`, a test in the workspace run. It binds two
ports it picks and never 4317 or 4318. CI's `lint-test` job and the pre-push check's `test` stage run it with no
display variable and no session bus, with no workflow edit.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched and no rendered surface
  changes. The `a11y` job's verdict is read from the operator pass's run.

- No local `cargo audit` or `cargo deny` entry: no dependency is added and the scope guard holds `Cargo.lock`
  unchanged; the `supply-chain` job reads both on the operator pass's run.

- Left for the next entries, none of it built here: the harness verbs aimed at the console program and the
  checks that grade its log (`Agent harness drives the console engine`); the door, and the end of the stdio
  sidecar (`Door inside the engine's process`); the scenario legs (`Scenario legs driven against the console
  engine`); operator-set places for stores, log and pid (`One place on a node`); a CI step and a kept console
  log (`Engine end-to-end gate reachable`); an incident from real telemetry read back (`Detection baseline
  through the console engine`).

- No panic is induced in the console program itself: it has no switch that induces one, and a test-only switch
  in a product binary is not built. The panic record and the at-exit record are witnessed through the
  process-start function it calls, in re-exec children (step 9).

- No retry anywhere. The boot job is read once; a boot that ended by itself stops the pass and goes to the
  operator.

**The operator pass, in this order.** The hygiene entry; the pre-CI commit; the local pre-push check again; the
merge-base probe; the build-branch push; the CI read of the pushed tip, asserted green, its row naming every
check read; the run's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact, with the series verdict, the smoke's settle verdict, every
kept witness file read whole and the window's boot record. A line of a witness file holding anything beyond its
shape stops the pass. A red is fixed by a further commit on top and read again.

body:
- (scope) One program, `andromeda-pulse-engine`, boots the two receivers, the buffer, the detectors and the
  corpus with no display variable and no session bus in its environment, and telemetry sent over its gRPC
  receiver lands: `integration_console_engine` passes in `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
  --no-tests=fail`, with a `duckdb.append` record read from the program's own log.

- (scope) It is driven by commands: `run` boots and stays up until signalled, `version` prints and exits 0, any
  other word exits 2 with usage and creates nothing (`unit_console_commands`, `integration_console_engine`).

- (obs) Its log is the one file sink under the data dir's `logs/`: every line of a console run parses as JSON
  with `timestamp`, `level`, `target`, `message`, `fields` and the three identity fields, and its stderr holds
  no log record (per obs-plan §3 Logging stack; obs-plan §3 Service identity).

- (obs) Each end the chunk builds leaves exactly one `app.exit` as the family's last record with its four
  fields rendered, read after the process has ended: SIGTERM and SIGINT, each still ending the process by that
  signal (per obs-plan §6 Log levels mapping, the `app.exit` entry; test-plan §3 Process-end witness form).

- (obs) The process-start function both programs call keeps the panic record: a child that calls it and panics
  leaves one ERROR `app.panic.fatal` and one `app.exit`, read after the child has ended
  (`integration_engine_boot`; per obs-plan §7 Panic hook; obs-plan §10 Always-required SLO invariant).

- (obs) A console run held past one tick interval holds two `ingest.tick` and two `buffer.tick` records at most
  45 s apart, `buffer.tick` carrying `rows_ingested_delta` unredacted, and no `viz.tick` or `plugins.tick` (per
  obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks; obs-plan §10 Standard+ invariants).

- (obs) `app.boot.engine` is emitted once per boot behind its own exact leaf, its guard asserting the field set
  by equality both ways and the no-bare-`app` discriminator (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing).

- (operator, inputs#I2) Both seat arms are pinned in `integration_engine_boot`: with the canned runner seated a
  cue-bearing digest yields one incident; with nothing seated the same digest reaches the digest archive, no
  incident forms and the boot record reads `none` / `deterministic_gate_unset`. The console program reads the
  arm from `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` in both directions (`integration_console_engine`).

- (inputs#I1 item 5) The console program reads no model variable and constructs no model runner or hardware
  probe; its run log holds no `interpretation.model.*` record (`unit_engine_boot_seam`,
  `integration_console_engine`).

- (inputs#I1 item 3) Neither entry point wires an engine part itself and the shared boot names no window
  framework: `unit_engine_boot_seam` passes, and reddens under the mutation of step 8.

- (arch) The console program holds two listening sockets, both on `127.0.0.1`, at the ports its two registered
  variables name, and both refuse after it ends (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports).

- (arch, security) Every file a console run writes lies under its data dir at a registered subpath, or is the
  registered corpus-key lock file; no full data-dir path and no passphrase value occurs in its log; with the
  store unreachable and the passphrase set it warns once on `corpus.keychain.fallback` (per architecture
  §Occupied Resources → Filesystem locations; security-plan §Secret Management → Runtime).

- (inputs#I1 item 1) The console binary needs no window library at load: the entry `f=target/debug/andromeda-pulse-engine
  && test -x "$f" && …` reads `last line 0` after its known positive reads `last line 6`.

- (inputs#I1 item 3, tests) The window app still boots on the shared engine boot: `main()` still opens with the
  render posture, then `xlib_threads::init();`, then its own runtime build (`unit_xlib_threads`); the entry
  `… cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count 2 && grep …` reads `all-settled` and `"program":"window"`; and on the
  operator pass's run the `boot` job's series reads `all-settled` with 7 settled, the smoke reads `settled`, and
  the `a11y` job is green with no step of it edited (per test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate; a11y-plan §9).

- (tests) Every entry of the fence exits per its `expect`; `git diff --quiet f31027a4023fd64e97bff3272d303faa628d2336
  -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` exits 0; the 14 moved resolver tests are listed by name in the workspace
  run (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

- (tests) The CI run on the pushed tip is green, the coverage step at ≥ 75 % line and ≥ 85 % function with the
  new code inside the measure; the run id the CI read printed is named in the report (per test-plan §9; §10).

- (P-086, advanced, not claimed) Of its acceptance this chunk shows the first half only: the engine starts as a
  console program with no display, no GPU probe and no desktop session, stays up and answers `run` and
  `version`. "Runs in the background" as a service, every kind of finding, one incident for a sustained storm
  and automatic resolution on real telemetry are not shown here.

- Spec anchors (from the extracts): architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports, Filesystem locations,
  Process / service identity, Corpus SQLite database → At-rest posture; architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns →
  Module dependency direction; architecture §Stack and Technologies → Xlib thread initialisation; obs-plan §3
  Tracing init, Logging stack, Service identity, Heartbeat ticks; obs-plan §6; obs-plan §8; obs-plan §10;
  test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline, Boot-smoke gate, Direct-binary smoke variant, Process-end witness
  form; test-plan §9; test-plan §10; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → API, Input, Logging;
  security-plan §Secret Management → Runtime; a11y-plan §9, §10.

- Research files inspected: `pulse-app/src/main.rs`, `pulse-app/src/lib.rs`, `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs`,
  `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`, `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs`, `pulse-app/src/window.rs`,
  `pulse-app/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ui-bridge/`, `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs`, five test files, `ci.yml`.

- Leaned, not asked: the console program is a second `[[bin]]` of `pulse-app` and no crate is cut, per research's
  measure (0 of 103 test binaries need a window library; no engine-wiring module imports the framework). The
  binary's name is `andromeda-pulse-engine`: architecture §Occupied Resources → Process / service identity
  reserves `pulse-app`, `andromeda-pulse` and `andromeda-pulse-mcp`. The console program keeps the app's service
  identity: obs-plan §11 bans a second hardcoded identity. Its commands are `run` and `version`, per scope.

- Asked: the model seat (inputs#I2). No option ships what the playbook's one `verdict: escalate` pattern names
  (Boundary widening): no new socket, credential, place on disk or crossing.

- Overridden extract content: the a11y extract's conditional about cutting `tauri` out of `crates/ingest`,
  `crates/triage` or `crates/ui-bridge` rests on the directive's stale crate list; no crate is cut and no router
  path, procedure, payload or event changes.

- A new workspace crate holding the engine, free of `tauri` in its manifest — rejected: it moves most of the 25
  files of `pulse-app/src` that do not name the framework for a state `Window retired` reaches by deleting
  dependencies; the console binary already loads without the window's libraries.

- A Cargo feature that makes `tauri` optional in `pulse-app` — rejected: features are additive and off by
  default (architecture §Conventions → Feature flags), and a second feature graph doubles the native build.

- A switch inside the window's `main()` instead of a second program — rejected: it would run after the render
  posture and the Xlib init, in a binary that needs the window libraries at load.

- A `stop` command — not built: the engine ends by signal, and finding it needs the pid file, whose place is
  `One place on a node`'s.

- Do not edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/agent-run.sh`, any `xtask/` source, any capability file, or
  the bindings. Do not move, rename or reorder `main()`'s first two statements or its runtime build.

- Do not add a dependency, a listening socket, an environment variable, or a file outside the registered
  locations. Do not make the console program read `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE`, `_LOGFILE`, a model path variable
  or `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_HARDWARE_PROFILE`.
- Do not add a log layer on stderr or stdout to the console program.
- Do not change `interpretation.model.load` or how the window selects its runner.

- The tokio runtime must be entered before `init_process` and `start` in both programs: the signal listener
  returns silently without one, and a spawn outside a runtime is the "no reactor running" boot panic.

- Engine tasks now start before the Tauri builder instead of inside its setup closure. The window's records keep
  their order up to the engine boot (`app.boot.tracing.init`, `app.boot.pid`, the three window boot records, the
  render posture).

- A process ended by a re-raised signal writes no coverage profile; `integration_engine_boot` is what covers
  `engine_boot::start`. Last recorded coverage: `Line: 33992/38252 = 88.9%`, `Function: 3565/4055 = 87.9%`
  (`chunks/2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing/evidence/gate-census.md:38`).

- The first tick of each target is written at boot and the next 15 s later (read in
  `target/boot-smoke/20261010T063800Z-series`: the ticks 0.375 s after the first record), so the unset arm of
  step 10 runs about 16 s; the `ci` nextest profile terminates a test at 180 s (`.config/nextest.toml`).

- A port the test picks is found by binding `127.0.0.1:0`, reading it and releasing it; `resolve_port` refuses 0
  and privileged ports.

- Not measured: what `tauri build` does with a second `[[bin]]` (the bundler may place the console binary in the
  desktop bundles). No step runs the release workflow; it leaves at `Desktop distribution retired`.

- Limits to carry into the report: the library read is of debug binaries on the dev host; the console program
  itself is ended only by SIGTERM and SIGINT here, its panic and at-exit records being witnessed one level down,
  at the function it calls; `harness:status`, `harness:ready` and `cleanup` are not aimed at the console program
  here although it writes the pid file they read.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Project Intent → Product type, §Design Philosophy and
  §Infrastructure Patterns → Deployment model and Project directory structure — a second program over the
  shared engine boot, no longer "not a CLI".

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Occupied Resources → Process / service identity (the binary
  `andromeda-pulse-engine`), Filesystem locations (the pid file and the workspace key are written by both
  programs) and Environment variables (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` is read by the console program, with
  its unset meaning there).

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §3 Tracing init (the console program's order, with no event loop), §3
  Heartbeat ticks (which ticks each program emits), §6 and §8 (`app.boot.engine`, both sites).

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Threat Model Summary (the process roster) and §Input Validation
  (a row for the console program's command words; the variable's second reader).

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §2 and §4 (the `pulse-app/tests` count, 103 → 109), §3 (the spawned
  program witness as a form), §1 Pending coverage triggers (`exit-hook-main-composition-coverage` and
  `discovery-observer-wiring-coverage` narrowed by the shared boot and its in-process test, as the wrap reads
  them).

**Chunk:** one console program boots ingest, buffer, detectors, corpus with no display, driven by commands; its log, identity, panic, heartbeat, process-end records kept
**Date:** 2026-10-10
**Commits:** `4f519c94` chore(2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point): operator pre-CI commit (the one commit since the last wrap; basis `git log --format='%h %s' f31027a4..HEAD`)

- **Files:** 15, all under `pulse-app/` (basis: `gate.py scope` — changed 15 · listed 15, base `f31027a4`).
  Modified 6: `pulse-app/Cargo.toml`, `pulse-app/src/main.rs`, `pulse-app/src/lib.rs`, `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs`,
  `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`, `pulse-app/tests/unit_heartbeat_ticks.rs`. New 9:
  `pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs`, `pulse-app/src/console.rs`, `pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs`,
  `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_env.rs`, `pulse-app/tests/unit_console_commands.rs`,
  `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_boot_engine.rs`, `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_seam.rs`,
  `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs`.
  No file of `crates/`, `xtask/`, `scripts/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `pulse-app/ui/`, `pulse-app/capabilities/`
  changed, and `Cargo.lock` is unchanged (basis: the plan's scope-guard entry, exit 0, no output, against `f31027a4`).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **A second product binary, `andromeda-pulse-engine`** — a second `[[bin]]` of the `pulse-app` package
    (`pulse-app/Cargo.toml:19-23`, path `src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs`), with `default-run = "pulse-app"`
    (`pulse-app/Cargo.toml:8`). Its `main` (`pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs:1-3`) hands its arguments to
    `pulse_app::console::main`. The product binaries are now three: `pulse-app` (the window app),
    `andromeda-pulse-engine` (the console program), `andromeda-pulse-mcp` (the stdio sidecar, unchanged).
  - **The console program's command grammar** (`pulse-app/src/console.rs`): closed, two words. `run` boots the engine
    and stays up until signalled; `version` prints one line (`andromeda-pulse-engine {version}`) and exits 0; no word,
    an unknown word, a second word or a word that is not Unicode prints
    `usage: andromeda-pulse-engine <run|version>` on stderr and exits 2, creating nothing. Public items:
    `Command` (`console.rs:19-23`), `parse` (`:25-42`), `version_line` (`:44-46`), `main` (`:48-65`), the private
    `run` (`:67-97`), consts `PROGRAM_NAME`, `USAGE`, `EXIT_USAGE` (2). No `stop` command exists.
  - **The one engine boot both programs call** (`pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs`, new, 1253 lines):
    - `init_process(data_dir)` (`engine_boot.rs:311-321`): the log sink and its guard, the at-exit hook, the Unix
      signal listener, the start instant, the pid file, in that order. Called with the tokio runtime entered.
    - `start(config, inputs) -> EngineHandles` (`engine_boot.rs:462-1253`): builds the engine state and spawns every
      engine task with `tokio::spawn` (never through the window framework): the buffer consumer and retention, the two
      receivers, the connection poller, the baseline persist loop, the cue emitter, the restart and storm detector
      ticks, the cadence coordinator, the digest assembler's cadence subscriber and persister, the lifecycle
      heartbeat, the lifecycle / storm / incident persist loops, the auto-resolution loop, the config watcher and its

body:
- **`spawn`** (`pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs`) — 3 call sites: `main()` at `pulse-app/src/main.rs:1557`, and
  `pulse-app/tests/unit_heartbeat_ticks.rs:25` (the import) and `:474`
  (`spawn_returns_five_handles_and_aborts_cleanly`). A change of its signature touches one production caller and
  one test file.

- **The nine private helpers of `main.rs`** — every reference is inside `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (9 names, 24
  sites, 1 file; `resolve_port` 9 and `resolve_retention_seconds` 8 include their tests in `mod tests`). Moving
  them into the library moves their 14 tests out of `main.rs` too: a test left beside them in a library source
  never runs and reddens the ratchet.

- **Names** — `engine` is taken as a module name by `crates/plugins/src/engine.rs` and as a field of
  `PluginsApiImpl`; `Engine`, `EngineBoot`, `console`, `start_engine` and `boot_engine` have no symbol on the rust
  plane (2 rows returned, both for `engine`).

- **The window framework is a dependency of two crates, and one of them can already drop it.** `tauri` is a
  dependency of `pulse-app` and, optionally, of `crates/ui-bridge` (`grep -n -E '^(tauri|taurpc|specta)'` over the
  workspace and member manifests: `tauri` at `pulse-app/Cargo.toml:37` and `crates/ui-bridge/Cargo.toml:29`,
  nowhere else). `crates/ingest` and `crates/triage` carry an optional `specta` behind a feature that is also
  named `taurpc-runtime`; they do not depend on `tauri`. `xtask` already builds `ui-bridge` with
  `default-features = false`.

- **18 of 43 source files of `pulse-app/src` name tauri or taurpc** (`grep -l -E 'tauri|taurpc'
  pulse-app/src/*.rs | wc -l` → 18; `ls pulse-app/src/*.rs` → 43, `xlib_threads.rs` being the one added since the
  directive's count). None of the engine-wiring modules is among them: the persistence adapters, the observers,
  `heartbeat.rs`, `digest_runtime.rs`, `inference_runtime.rs`, `corpus_retrieval.rs`, `reevaluation.rs` and
  `cadence_runner.rs` import nothing from the window framework. `observability.rs` is on the list for its strings
  alone. Three helpers the engine boot calls live in router files that also define TauRPC routers:
  `connection_router::HeartbeatBindStatus`, `config_router::settings_to_cadence_config` /
  `settings_to_lifecycle_thresholds` / `config_watch_error_category`.

- **A binary that links the `pulse_app` library without building the window needs no window library at load.**
  Measured on this host: of the 103 test binaries built from `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` (debug profile, each links the
  library, the router tests included), 0 carry a `NEEDED` entry for GTK, GDK, WebKit, libsoup or JavaScriptCore
  (`readelf -d {binary} | grep NEEDED | grep -c -i -E 'gtk|webkit|gdk|soup|javascriptcore'` over all 103). Known
  positive: `target/debug/pulse-app` and `target/release/pulse-app` each read 6. This is a reading of test
  binaries; the console binary itself is read by a gate entry once it exists.

- **The engine boot has no seam.** Every engine task is spawned from the Tauri `.setup` closure through
  `tauri::async_runtime::spawn`, on the runtime `main` builds and hands to Tauri (`main.rs:290-295`).
  `heartbeat::spawn`, the digest runtime and the inference runtime already use plain `tokio::spawn` from that same
  closure, so the closure runs with the runtime entered and the spawns do not depend on Tauri.

- **An incident is created only behind the model's output.** The chain is cue → cadence coordinator → digest
  trigger → digest assembler → `DigestBroadcast` → `spawn_l4_inference_subscriber` → `llm_runner` →
  `create_incident_from_l4_output` (`main.rs:1416-1476`). No other production path creates an incident. The one
  existing way through it with no model is the canned runner of `deterministic_inference.rs`.

- **The process-end record needs no event loop.** The signal listener records `app.exit` with class `signal` from
  a runtime task, restores the default disposition and re-raises (`observability.rs:2891-2916`); the at-exit hook
  records `outside_event_loop`. `exit_after_event_loop` is the window's tail alone. A program that runs until it
  is signalled ends through the first, and the closed label set is unchanged.

- **A second binary in the same crate is spawnable from that crate's tests.** `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_{name}")` is
  available to an integration test of the crate that declares the `[[bin]]`, and cargo builds the binary for the
  test (rules/testing.md 2026-05-13). The sidecar tests, which spawn a sibling crate's binary, need a prebuild
  step; a binary declared by `pulse-app` does not.

- **The workspace test run in CI has no display.** `lint-test` runs `cargo xtask test` outside `xvfb-run`, and the
  local pre-push check's `test` stage runs under a cleared environment with no display variable and no session
  bus. A test that spawns the console program there witnesses a boot with no display on every push, with no
  workflow edit.

- **The injector cannot feed a program on other ports.** `inject_demo` is fixed to 4317. A check that keeps off
  the shared ports sends OTLP with a `tonic` client of its own (`tonic` and `prost` are dev-dependencies of
  `pulse-app` already).

- **Coverage margin.** The last recorded coverage step read `Line: 33992/38252 = 88.9%` and `Function: 3565/4055
  = 87.9%` against 75 % and 85 % (`chunks/2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing/evidence/gate-census.md:38`).
  A process ended by a re-raised signal writes no coverage profile, so the spawned program adds no covered line;
  an in-process test of the boot function does.

- **Tests for `pulse-app` library code live in `pulse-app/tests/`**, reach internals through `pub` +
  `#[doc(hidden)]`, and are checked by name in the workspace listing (rules/testing.md 2026-05-20, 2026-08-29).

- **A new log target gets its own exact allowlist leaf, a guard under `pulse-app/tests/` asserting the field set
  by equality both ways, and a discriminator that no bare `app` key exists** (rules/observability.md; the
  `app.boot.render.posture` leaf and `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_render_posture.rs` are the
  nearest precedent).

- **A closed command-line contract rejects an unknown argument with exit 2** (`inject_demo`'s `parse`,
  `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs:210-221`; the xtask verbs' 0 · 1 · 2 exit form).

- **A cross-process claim is witnessed across a real process boundary, the log read after the child has ended,
  with the child-ran proof in the arm** (`pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs:1-10`).

- **No `sleep` for synchronisation**: wait on a record in the log family or on a TCP accept, under a bound
  (rules/testing.md, Synchronization).

- **A diff-shaped probe names the chunk base `f31027a4`, never `HEAD`**, and a scope guard's pathspec lists the
  chunk's new files beside its modified ones (rules/testing.md 2026-10-04).
- `pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs` — the one engine boot both programs call: the environment resolvers and boot helpers moved out of `main.rs`, the engine's state, its task spawns and its boot record

data.head: ## What the chunk builds (the entry's own words)

body:
- **One program boots ingest, buffer, detectors, corpus with no display.** A second way to start the same engine,
  as a console program: the two OTLP receivers, the ring buffer, the detectors and the incident corpus come up with
  no window, no webview and no display server.

- **Driven by commands.** The program is started and told what to do from a command line; it has no interface of
  its own. `[premise-corrected: read at P3 in observability.rs and the harness rules]` The entry does not state
  which commands exist at this chunk. It needs one that runs the engine; it does not need one that ends it. The
  engine ends by a signal sent to its pid: the existing signal listener records the process end and re-raises the
  same signal, the harness's `cleanup` verb already ends the app that way, and a product command that found the
  running engine would have to read the pid file, whose place is `One place on a node`'s. So this chunk's
  commands are `run` and `version`; an unknown command is refused. Token, door and node commands are later
  entries'.

- **Log, identity, panic, heartbeat, process-end records kept.** The console program writes the same five records
  of itself that the window app writes today: its log sink, its identity at boot, its panic record, its heartbeat
  and exactly one record of how the process ended. The list is closed (inputs#I1 item 4).
