title: Scope — No CI step reads nothing

data.head: # Scope — No CI step reads nothing

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates
**Working entry (`working-route.md:23`):** "No CI step reads nothing — every comparison has a producer for its baseline
or is gone; every upload finds its file or is gone (P-128)"
**Chunk base:** `6df9e95c` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this sha, never HEAD.

A CI step that compares against a baseline nobody produced, or uploads a file nobody wrote, passes while it reads
nothing. Two epochs of removals lean on these gates (the ruling that minted P-128, quoted in the ledger's notes for
`verification-matrix.json#P-128`). This chunk leaves every such step in one of two states: it reads something a
workflow produced, or it is gone. There is no third state: "kept, and neutral when nothing arrives" is the present
defect, not an option (inputs#I1 item 2).

- **Every baseline comparison a CI job makes reads a baseline some workflow produced, or the workflow no longer makes
  the comparison.** Read at take-up, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` at `6df9e95c`:
  - three `download-artifact` steps, each pull-request-only and each `continue-on-error: true`: `:162-168`
    (`criterion-${{ runner.os }}-base`, job `lint-test`), `:293-299` (`a11y-violations-base`, job `a11y`),
    `:581-587` (`coverage-linux-base`, job `coverage`). The coordinates agree with inputs#I1 item 1 (`:164`, `:295`,
    `:583` are the three `uses:` lines).
  - their consumers: `cargo xtask criterion-regression --current target/criterion --baseline
    target/criterion-baseline` (`:170-171`), `cargo xtask coverage-regression --current lcov.info --baseline
    target/lcov-baseline/lcov.info` (`:589-590`), and the regression leg inside `cargo xtask test:a11y` (`:301-302`).
    The first two run on a push as well, where no download step runs at all.
  - Verified at P3 on the newest run, `ci#38031822696` on `6df9e95c` (pull-request event, green, 7 of 7 checks): each
    of the three downloads ends `Unable to download artifact(s): Artifact not found for name: …` (`criterion-Linux-base`,
    `a11y-violations-base`, `coverage-linux-base`), and no workflow uploads a name ending `-base` (the nine upload
    names of `ci.yml`, the three of `release.yml` and the two of `update-channels.yml`, read at P3). The entry's first
    `CARRY:` stands as measured on 2026-10-09 and again today.
  - Verified at P3, what each comparison does with nothing to read:
    - criterion: `criterion-regression-check: current dir target/criterion not found; NEUTRAL (no criterion bench
      output yet)`, exit 0. It has no baseline and no current input either: no step runs a bench, the workspace holds
      no bench target, no `criterion` dependency and no `bench` verb (research.md).
    - coverage: `coverage-regression-check: baseline target/lcov-baseline/lcov.info not found; NEUTRAL (first PR / new
      branch / local dev)`, exit 0, read on `ci#38031822696` and on `ci#38026637514` attempt 1.
    - [premise-corrected: the a11y comparison DOES read a baseline. `regression-detector.mjs:9` defaults to the file
      committed at `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/baselines/a11y-violations-summary.json` (tracked; regenerated at chunk #99,
      6 informational tuples), and the job log of `ci#38031822696` reads `regression-detector: no new violations vs
      baseline (0/0)` with no `baseline not found` line.] The download step reads nothing; the comparison reads a
      baseline held in the tree, which no workflow produced. The route's carry at `working-route.md:46` ("so its
      regression comparison reads no baseline") is false in that half; a report entry carries the correction, and
      which state the comparison is left in is the operator's fork at P4.
  - Verified at P3: the three `continue-on-error` keys of `ci.yml` are these three downloads' and no other step
    carries one (`grep -n 'continue-on-error' .github/workflows/ci.yml`: `:165`, `:296`, `:584`). A key that exists
    only so an absent baseline does not red the job goes with the download it shields (inputs#I1 item 2).

- **Every upload a CI job makes finds its file, or the workflow no longer makes the upload.** Read at take-up,
  `ci.yml` at `6df9e95c`: nine `upload-artifact` steps (`grep -c 'upload-artifact@' .github/workflows/ci.yml`: 9), every
  one `if: always()` with `if-no-files-found: ignore`.
  - Verified at P3 on `ci#38031822696` (job logs and the run's artifact list; the same six names on `ci#38026637514`):
    six find a file — `logs-perf-samples-Linux` (1 file), `capability-drift-Linux` (1), `a11y-violations-Linux` (5),
    `playwright-a11y-report-Linux` (1), `logs-boot-Linux` (42), `coverage-linux` (1) — and three find none, each
    printing `No files were found with the provided path`: `logs-Linux` (`:135-142`), `nextest-Linux` (`:144-151`),
    `criterion-Linux` (`:153-160`).
  - Verified at P3: the `a11y-violations` upload's three path members each match on that run (three `logs/a11y-*`
    files, `contrast-report.json`, `regression-set.json`). The action can fail a step only when no member matches at
    all; a single missing member is not something a key can red (research.md).
  - Verified at P3, why the three are empty: no step of `lint-test` writes a log family under the job's data dir (the
    job boots no app and its tests use their own temp dirs); nothing writes a JUnit file (`.config/nextest.toml` holds

- **Which way each comparison and each empty upload falls is the operator's technical fork, brought at P4 as one
  dialog** (inputs#I1 item 3): each with what a producer would cost and what the gate is worth to the version as it

- **The two of the kind that ride other entries are settled here with the rest** (inputs#I1 item 4, the operator's
  lean "for the plan to test"): the `a11y-violations-base` download (`working-route.md:46`, first `CARRY:`) and the

  said at P4 beside it: obs-plan §11's ban on losing telemetry artifacts is written against the `logs` upload, and the
  a11y comparison's tree-held baseline is not "a baseline that a workflow produced" in P-128's words.

- **What reads `ci.yml` in the tree is kept true.** Verified at P3 (`grep -rln 'ci\.yml' crates pulse-app/src
  pulse-app/tests xtask scripts .github`): two test files read the workflow's steps,
  `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` and `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs`; `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`
  reads only its `node-version` major (`:148`, `:576-580`). The pins on the steps this chunk decides:
  `ci_workflow_invokes_coverage_regression_check` (`:218`), `ci_workflow_downloads_coverage_baseline_artifact`
  (`:228`), `ci_workflow_invokes_criterion_regression_check` (`:378`),
  `ci_workflow_downloads_criterion_baseline_artifact` (`:388`), `ci_workflow_uploads_criterion_artifact_unchanged`
  (`:406`), `ci_workflow_uploads_logs_artifact_unchanged` (`:417`), and in the second file
  `ci_workflow_uploads_a11y_violations_artifact` (`:77`) and `ci_workflow_uploads_playwright_a11y_report_artifact`
  (`:88`). Each pin follows its step: a step that goes takes its pin with it, a step that stays keeps a pin that
  reads what makes it non-empty.

- **A witness that cannot pass vacuously.** The acceptance is read "on a CI run of the tree", so the chunk's proof is
  a run on its pre-CI commit, read step by step and artifact by artifact, beside a self-lint pin in the tree.
  Verified at P3: `actions/upload-artifact` at the pinned sha takes `if-no-files-found: error` ("Fail the action with
  an error message"), so a kept upload can be made to red the step when it finds nothing; the pin reads that key.

- **The self-lint guard that reads 16 of the workflow's run steps: the plan decides whether it rides here or gets
  its own requirement line** (the entry's second `CARRY:`; inputs#I1 item 5).
  - Re-derived at P3 (the guard's own split, `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs:257-299`, run over `ci.yml` at
    `6df9e95c`): 100 step blocks, 53 of them `run:` steps; the guard reads 17 blocks, 16 `run:` steps and the
    `cargo deny` action step; 37 `run:` steps are unread, and none of those 37 carries a soft-fail key. The carry's
    16 and 53 stand. Its list of unread gates stands too: the Cyrillic lint, typecheck, staged-artifacts,
    capability-widening, capability-matrix, the mcp-server build, the Cranelift assertion, the npm supply-chain gate
    and the coverage thresholds.
  - "this is outside P-128's text, which is about comparisons and uploads" (the carry). If the guard rides here it
    is not folded into P-128's claim (inputs#I1 item 5).

- **The masters' sentences this entry's wrap corrects are listed in the plan as expected amendments, as measured**

    §9 Pipeline integration, the `xtask bench` row (`:510`); test-plan §9 Test report format (`test-plan.md:505`) with

  - the riders': obs-plan §9 Log file row (`:499`, the `logs-${{ runner.os }}` clause), §9 Pipeline integration

data.head: ## Decided at P4 (the operator's answers, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10 — inputs#I2)

body:
- **Criterion: gone whole.** The upload, the download with its soft-fail key, the comparison step, the
  `criterion-regression` verb with its two scripts, and their pins. No bench suite exists in the tree, as measured
  (inputs#I2 item 1).

- **The `logs-Linux` and `nextest-Linux` uploads: gone.** No JUnit producer is added: "an artifact nothing reads is
  the same defect as a step that reads nothing" (inputs#I2 item 1).

- **Coverage comparison: gone whole; the absolute thresholds stay** (inputs#I2 item 2). The download with its
  soft-fail key, the comparison step, the `coverage-regression` verb with its two scripts, and their pins.

- **A11y: the download and its soft-fail key go; the comparison stays, reading the baseline committed in the tree**
  (inputs#I2 item 3). The operator's reading: a baseline committed in the tree at the commit under test has a producer,
  the tree, and the comparison reads it. A pin holds that the comparison fails, and does not pass, when that file is
  absent.

- **The closing sentence reaches the five other gates, so P-128 is not claimed here** (inputs#I2 item 4). This chunk
  settles every comparison and every upload and claims nothing. At its wrap the entry that closes the sentence is
  minted first in the tail, carrying the five gates each with its measured reading, and P-128 is claimed there.
  Research is not reopened for them; what was measured is recorded.

- The six uploads that stay each fail their step when they find no file; the guard is widened in this chunk, outside
  any capability claim. Both are the plan's own decisions, shown on the P5 card.

- **P-128 is this entry's capability, advanced and not claimed.** Its acceptance: "On a CI run of the tree, every
  comparison against a baseline reads a baseline that a workflow produced, or the workflow no longer makes that
  comparison; every upload uploads a file, or the workflow no longer makes that upload. No gate stands while reading
  nothing." This chunk makes the first two clauses true; the third stands false while the five gates above stand, so
  the cap stays pooled with a dated note (inputs#I2 item 4). The note carries the operator's concretization for the
  later claim: "produced by a workflow or committed in the tree", the acceptance's wording having been narrower than
  the requirement line (inputs#I2 item 3).
- P-128 is PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word (the ledger's notes; the handoff).

- **"A CI job" is a job of a workflow that a push or a pull request of the tree triggers.** Verified at P3 (each
  file's `on:` block): `ci.yml` and `secret-scan.yml` run on `pull_request` and on a push to `main`;
  `secret-scan.yml` holds no artifact step; `release.yml` runs on a `v*` tag push and `update-channels.yml` on the
  completion of `release`. Those two hold five uploads with `if-no-files-found: ignore` and three downloads; they
  leave at `Desktop distribution retired` (`working-route.md:50`, P-114, P-127), whose card names the release
  environment and its secret names for the founder. They are outside this chunk; that reading is said at P4.

- **The `a11y` job and the `boot` job stay.** They leave at `Window's gates retired` (`working-route.md:46`, P-083).
  This chunk settles only the `a11y` job's baseline download, the state of its comparison, and the upload keys; the

  boot job's `Boot series (equal source)` step stays a gating step, and a self-end in it is a new reading, brought to
  the operator (the handoff; `working-route.md:46`, second `CARRY:`).

- **No producer that needs a new permission, a token, a new trigger or a third-party action without the founder's
  own word** (inputs#I1 item 3). The workflow's `permissions: contents: read` (`ci.yml:8-9`) stays.

- **No new requirement is minted by phase.** If the guard needs its own requirement line, the plan says so and the
  operator's requirement-add path mints it.
- No run binds 4317 or 4318 without the operator's word (the handoff's host note); the chunk's own edits need none.

`route.py pins` lists two blocks on `working-route.md:23`, both `CARRY:` (722 and 871 characters); both are folded

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing: "No gate stands while reading nothing"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T09:23:05Z
- **Chunk base:** `7419496bdf9fd23f8ed44021f08aa922caf4b76f` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped entry names it.

Four gates of the `ci` workflow pass over an empty or absent input, and three arms of a fifth cannot fail on the
input their job gives them. As measured on `ci#38038281709` and on the dev host (research.md): the coverage step
exits 0 over a report tracking nothing; its branch arm has read `0/0 = 100.0%` on every run, because the pinned
toolchain cannot write a branch count; five nextest invocations pass a run that selects no test; `cargo xtask
ci-gates` prints four NEUTRAL lines and exits 0 over an absent log, and in the boot job its heartbeat and
perf-budget arms read one tick per target and no gradable sample; `cargo xtask quarantine-tracking` prints NEUTRAL
and exits 0 when none of its search dirs exists.

The chunk leaves each in one of two states, as the operator decided at P4 (inputs#I2): it reads something that can
make it fail, or it is gone. An empty coverage report fails and the branch arm is retired; every nextest invocation
fails on an empty selection; `ci-gates` keeps the two arms that read the boot log and makes an absent log an exit
of its own; the quarantine check fails on an absent input and prints what it scanned. Two readings are not repaired
and keep an owner: the a11y upload's path members and the pre-push `ci-gates` stage (per test-plan §9 Pipeline
structure, obs-plan §10 CI gates, architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces).

With that, the closing sentence of P-128's acceptance is true on a CI run of the tree, and the capability is
claimed here (inputs#I1 item 5). The proof is the pull-request run of the chunk's pre-CI commit, read gate by
gate, beside a pin in the tree for each kept gate that is red on an empty or absent input.
**PROVISIONAL, for the founder:** retiring the 70 % branch threshold (inputs#I2 item 1), like P-128 itself.

0. **Red before green.** Write the pins of steps 1 to 4 first and run them against the untouched gates: the
   thresholds witness and the workflow pins in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, the argument-list pin
   and the quarantine pin in `xtask`'s own tests. Record each red reading in
   `evidence/red-before.md` (the failing assertion's line, a temp path written as `{tmp}`). The
   `ci-gates` unit's pins are written with the unit in step 3; their red is step 5's mutation.

1. **The coverage step** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `coverage`, step `Enforce coverage thresholds`,
   `ci.yml:506-533` at the base).
   - A report tracking 0 lines **or** 0 functions fails the step with an `::error::` line that says so. The
     "trivially passes" block (`:519-522`) is gone, and no percentage is printed as 100 over a zero total.
   - The branch arm leaves whole: the two `BRF`/`BRH` sums (`:515-516`), `branch_pct` (`:524`), the `Branch:`
     line (`:527`) and its threshold line (`:531`).
   - The job's name becomes `coverage gate (line ≥75% / function ≥85%)` (`:450`).
   - Everything else of the step and the job stays: an absent `lcov.info` still fails, the line and function
     thresholds are 75 and 85, the step is an inline `run:` step.
   - Pins, in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`: (a) a witness that cuts the step's body out of `ci.yml`
     by the step's name and runs it with `bash` in a scratch dir over constructed `lcov.info` files — an empty
     file and a file with lines but no function both exit non-zero; 90 of 100 lines with 9 of 10 functions exits
     0; 70 of 100 lines exits non-zero; 8 of 10 functions exits non-zero; no file exits non-zero. A missing `bash`
     or `awk` fails the test, never skips it. (b) The `coverage` job's block holds no branch token (`BRF`, `BRH`,
     `branch_`, `Branch:`, a branch threshold in the name).

2. **Empty selections.** Each of the five `--no-tests=pass` literals becomes `--no-tests=fail`: `ci.yml:199`
   (`mcp-test`) and the four argument lists in `xtask/src/main.rs` (`run_cargo_nextest` `:440`,
   `run_cargo_llvm_cov` `:469`, `run_perf_slo_load` `:749`, `run_perf_load_profiles` `:780`). The two `about`
   strings follow (`:78`, `:86`), and the `lint-test` step's name becomes `cargo xtask test` (`ci.yml:111`).
   - The sixth nextest step of the workflow, `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile perf-samples`
     (`ci.yml:121`), is spelled with `--no-tests=fail` too. It carries no flag today and ran 1 test; the runner's
     nextest (0.9.133) is older than the host's and its default on an empty selection was not read. This is the
     plan's own addition to the five, shown on the review card.
   - Each of the four argument lists becomes a unit the crate's tests can read. Pins: in `xtask`, every one of the
     four holds exactly one argument that starts with `--no-tests`, and it is `--no-tests=fail`; in
     `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, every `cargo nextest run` line of `ci.yml` holds
     `--no-tests=fail` and no line of it holds another `--no-tests` value. Neither pin spells the retired
     literal: a listed entry counts it in `xtask/src/main.rs`.
   - Selection form unchanged: `--workspace` narrowed by `-E` (`xtask/src/main.rs:737-738`).

3. **`ci-gates` narrowed** (`run_ci_gates`, `xtask/src/main.rs:483-571`; one caller, `main` @ `:308`).
   - A new unit, `xtask/src/ci_gates.rs`, holds the verb's verdict over the log family
     (`agent-latest.jsonl*` under the resolved log dir) and its printed lines; `run_ci_gates` hands over to it.
   - Arms: **no family member → `cannot-evaluate`, exit 2**, one line that names what is missing by a basename
     (today: four NEUTRAL lines, exit 0) · members holding zero records → FAIL, exit 1 (as today) · an
     `app.panic.fatal` record at level ERROR → FAIL, exit 1, the line naming the member's basename and the line
     number, never the record's text and never a full path (today it prints both, `:519-522`, `:536`) · otherwise
     exit 0 with exactly the two lines `ci-gates: zero-spans PASS ({n} log records across {k} file(s))` and
     `ci-gates: zero-panic PASS`, their text unchanged.
   - The heartbeat arm and the perf-budget arm leave the verb with every line they print. `invoke_heartbeat_check`,
     `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.{sh,ps1}` and `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs` are not edited: `perf:load-profiles`
     and `perf:budget` still call them (research.md, graph impact).
   - Text that names the old arms follows: the verb's `about` (`:149`), the `INACTIVE state` comment (`:486-487`,
     gone with its arm), the comment in `run_perf_slo_load` (`:734-736`), and the failure message of
     `ci_workflow_invokes_ci_gates` (`pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs:447-448`).
   - Pins, in the unit's own tests over scratch dirs: no log dir → exit 2 · a log dir with no member → exit 2 ·
     a member with zero lines → exit 1 · one non-panic record → exit 0, both PASS lines, no line holding
     `heartbeat` or `perf-budget` · a panic record at ERROR → exit 1, the line holding neither the record's
     message nor a path separator · a panic-target record below ERROR → exit 0.
   - `ci.yml`'s `cargo xtask ci-gates` step is not edited. The step runs only after the smoke and the series
     passed, so in the boot job the log exists; the new exit 2 is reached on the dev host and in the unit's tests.

4. **The quarantine check** (`xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.sh`; `lint-test`, `ci.yml:93-94`).
   - A missing search dir fails the check (exit 1, an `::error::` line naming the dir relative to the root), and so
     does a scan of zero `.rs` files. Today both read NEUTRAL, exit 0.
   - With zero `#[ignore]` it prints `quarantine-tracking-check: PASS (0 quarantine(s) across {N} file(s))`; with
     tracked ones its PASS line gains the same file count. The word NEUTRAL is gone. An untracked `#[ignore]`
     still fails as today.
   - `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.ps1` is given the same arms, mirrored and not run on this host.
   - Pin, in `xtask`'s tests, running the `.sh` with `bash` over scratch roots: no search dir → non-zero · four
     dirs and no `.rs` file → non-zero · one `.rs` file and no `#[ignore]` → exit 0, the line
     `PASS (0 quarantine(s) across 1 file(s))`, no `NEUTRAL` · an `#[ignore]` with no issue URL → exit 1 · one
     with the URL in its window → exit 0. A missing `bash` fails the test.

5. **Mutation checks, one-shot, both readings in `evidence/mutation-checks.md`.** For each kept
   gate put the BASE form of its block back (never a one-line removal), confirm the mutation is present, run its
   pin, see it red, restore: (a) the coverage step's zero-total block → the witness; (b) `--no-tests=pass` in one
   argument list and on the `mcp-test` line → the two pins; (c) the absent-log arm returning success with the
   NEUTRAL lines → the unit's exit-2 pins; (d) the quarantine script's base absent-dir arm → its pin.

6. **The local pre-push check** is run after the edits (`cargo xtask pre-push:linux`, its listed entry): six stages
   green, the `test` stage over a non-empty selection, the `ci-gates` stage over its seed record.

7. **The operator pass** (the entries keyed `operator`, in block order): hygiene, the pre-CI commit, the pre-push
   entry again, the merge-base probe, the push, the CI read, then five reads of that run by its id. From their
   recorded outputs the pass writes `evidence/operator-pass.md` and
   `evidence/gate-census.md` — every gating step of the run with the line that says what it read.
- `xtask/src/ci_gates.rs` — the `ci-gates` verdict over the log family, its printed lines, its tests

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the coverage thresholds step and its job's name; `--no-tests=fail` on three nextest
  lines; the `lint-test` test step's name. No step is added or removed

- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the four nextest argument lists as readable units; three `about` strings; `run_ci_gates`
  handing over to the new unit; two comments; the argument-list pin and the quarantine pin in its tests
- `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.sh` — the absent-input arms, the file count, no NEUTRAL
- `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.ps1` — the same, mirrored, not run on this host

- `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` — the thresholds witness, the no-branch pin, the empty-selection pin,
  the reworded `ci-gates` message

The chunk's own probes come first, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order: `capability-drift` before the
default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, and
the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure. The local pre-push check follows, then the
operator pass.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No boot-smoke entry: no file of the chunk is on the boot-smoke trigger list (test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate
  discipline), and the chunk boots no app.

- No webview gates, no headful self-verify, no `cargo xtask test:a11y`: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path changes and no
  rendered surface does. The `a11y` job is read on the CI run.
- No liveness probe and no live leg: the chunk drives no external process and binds no port.

- No targeted nextest entry: steps 0 and 5 run the pins as the red-before-green pair
  (`cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci -E 'binary(quality_gate_workflow) + package(xtask)'`); the workspace
  nextest entry runs the same tests on every re-run.

- Step 5's four mutations edit a file and restore it, so each is a one-shot run at implement; the workspace nextest
  entry guards the four properties on every re-run.

**The operator pass, in this order.** The hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the local pre-push entry again, the
merge-base probe, the push; then the whole pull-request run of the pushed tip is read. Five reads by that run's id,
as `<id>`, follow: the run's artifact names, the count of read-nothing lines across its six job logs, the coverage
step's own lines, the `ci-gates` step's own lines, and the quarantine check's line with the test selections. The
last entry lists every job, report-only. A red merge-base probe goes to the operator before any push. No run is
re-run to obtain a green. A self-end in the boot job's series step is a new reading, brought to the operator.

Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry
writes one.

body:
- (P-128, `verification-matrix.json#P-128`) On the pull-request CI run of the chunk's final pushed commit, read by
  the operator pass and named by its run id: **(a)** every comparison against a baseline reads a baseline produced
  by a workflow or committed in the tree, or the workflow no longer makes it — `ci.yml` holds no download step
  (the nextest entry's `ci_workflow_makes_no_download_without_a_producer`; the parsed-workflow entry's four changed
  steps) and the `a11y` job is green over the tree baseline; **(b)** every upload uploads a file — the artifacts
  entry reads exactly the six names; **(c)** no gate stands while reading nothing — the six-logs entry reads
  `6 0`, the coverage entry `1 1`, the boot entry `1 1 0`, the lint-test entry `1 1 3`, and the CI read is
  `verdict: green`. The gate census in `evidence/gate-census.md` names each gating step of the run with what it
  read.

- (P-128) Each gate that is kept has a committed pin that is red on an empty or absent input: a coverage report
  tracking nothing, an empty selection, an absent log family, an absent search root (`cargo nextest run
  --workspace --profile ci` returns 0 with them; `evidence/red-before.md` and `evidence/mutation-checks.md` hold
  the red reading of each).

- (P-128) Outside the sentence, each with an owner and a stated reading in the report: the a11y upload's three
  path members (5 files on `ci#38038281709`; one member missing beside a matching one never read on a runner;
  owner `Window's gates retired`) and the pre-push `ci-gates` stage, which is not a step of a CI job (it reads one
  record it wrote itself; owner `Agent harness drives the console engine`).

- (tests) The standard gate set passes on the chunk's final tree in the listed order, closed by
  `git diff --quiet 7419496bdf9fd23f8ed44021f08aa922caf4b76f -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` exit 0 (per
  test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

- (tests) The merge-base probe is listed directly before the push entry on the operator leg and reads exit 0
  before the push (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline → The merge-base probe).

- (tests) `cat .github/workflows/ci.yml xtask/src/main.rs | grep -c -e '--no-tests=pass'` reads 0, and an empty
  selection exits non-zero in each of the five invocations by its pin (per test-plan §9 Pipeline structure).

- (tests) The coverage step fails on a report tracking nothing and states no branch threshold: the witness in
  `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` passes, the branch-token entry reads 0 and the job's name reads
  `coverage gate (line ≥75% / function ≥85%)` (per test-plan §10 Coverage thresholds, as the wrap amends it).

- (arch) `ci.yml` still holds the six named jobs on `ubuntu-22.04` with no matrix and no `needs:` edge; exactly
  four steps differ from the base and none is added or removed, so the boot job's smoke, exit-witness and series
  steps are equal to their base form (the two YAML entries and the parsed-workflow entry; per architecture
  §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach).

- (arch) Every verb arm the chunk changes maps an empty or absent input to exit 1 or exit 2, never 0: the
  absent-log entry reads exit 2, the absent-root entry exit 1 (per architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI
  surfaces).

- (arch) The chunk adds no workspace crate, no variable read, no port, no TauRPC procedure and no capability, and
  `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` reports six stages green (its entry; per architecture §Occupied Resources).

- (security) `ci.yml` keeps `permissions: contents: read`, gains no job-level `permissions:` key, no token, no
  `uses:` line and no toolchain line (the added-lines entry reads 0; the parsed-workflow entry's third `True`);
  `rust-toolchain.toml` is unchanged (the scope guard) and `ci_workflow_audit_step_is_a_plain_run_step` passes
  (per security-plan §Secret Management → GitHub Environment scoping; §Dependency Security → CI integration).

- (security) The narrowed verb prints closed labels, counts, a basename and a line number: its panic line holds
  neither the record's text nor a full path, by its pin (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (obs) No step of `ci.yml` grades a perf-budget arm it cannot read: `ci-gates` grades none, and the `lint-test`
  `perf:budget --require memory,snapshot` step is unchanged and green on the run with `perf-budget: graded`
  (the lint-test entry's second count; per obs-plan §10 CI gates, the perf-budget bullet).

- (obs) A step of a job that stays on the run still fails on an `app.panic.fatal` record in the log it reads: the
  unit's panic pin, and `ci-gates: zero-panic PASS` in the boot log (the boot entry's second count; per obs-plan
  §10 Always-required SLO invariant).

- (a11y) No step of the `a11y` job changes, and its two regression-baseline pins pass unedited (the
  parsed-workflow entry; the nextest entry; per a11y-plan §3 Harness wiring & conventions → Regression baseline).

**Concretization of P-128, for the review:** the acceptance's three clauses are read on one named run; clause (a)
takes the operator's reading "produced by a workflow or committed in the tree" (the entry's fourth `CARRY:`);
clause (c), "No gate stands while reading nothing", is read as: every step of `ci.yml` whose exit decides a job
read a non-empty input on that run, and no such step or tool arm exits 0 over an empty or absent one where the
chunk kept it. The pre-push `ci-gates` stage is outside the sentence, because P-128 is about what a CI job does
(inputs#I2 item 4).

- Spec anchors the plan rests on (from the extracts): test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline (and → The merge-base
  probe), §4 Unit Test Strategy, §9 Pipeline structure, §9 and §10 Build failure conditions, §10 Coverage
  thresholds, §11 Test Anti-Patterns → CI; obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks, §9 Telemetry artifact handling and
  Pipeline integration, §10 CI gates, §10 Performance budgets, §10 Load-profile constraints, §11 → SLO and → CI;
  architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach, §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces, §Stack and
  Technologies; security-plan §Secret Management → GitHub Environment scoping, §Dependency Security → CI
  integration, §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging and → Input; a11y-plan §3 CI integration, §10 SLO Invariants.

- History the plan rests on: test-plan `2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples` (a required arm is how an
  empty input fails), `2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing` (the predecessor; the merge-base probe);
  obs-plan `2026-06-10` (the designed NEUTRAL posture this chunk amends for `ci-gates`), `2026-08-30-npm-advisory-coverage`
  (a mandate with no producer retired whole); architecture `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`
  (a check that could not fail replaced by a verdict with a `cannot-evaluate` arm).

- Research files inspected: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `xtask/src/main.rs`, `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs`,
  `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`, `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.sh`, `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.sh`,
  `.config/nextest.toml`, `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs`,
  `rust-toolchain.toml`; the six job logs and the `coverage-linux` artifact of `ci#38038281709`.
- External inputs: inputs#I1 (the operator's phase directive), inputs#I2 (the operator's four P4 answers).

- Leaned, with the artifact: the thresholds step stays inline and is pinned by a witness that runs it, per
  `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` (the last chunk's absent-baseline witness runs the real script the same
  way); the verb's two kept lines keep their text, per the masters and evidence that quote them
  (`obs-plan.md:545`, `:559`; the last chunk's `evidence/other-gates.md`).

- A nightly toolchain in the `coverage` job to produce a branch count — rejected by the operator: "a second
  unpinned toolchain is not its repair" (inputs#I2 item 1). **What a real branch count would need:** branch
  instrumentation on the toolchain the project pins. Today it is a nightly-only compiler feature (`-Z
  coverage-options=branch`, `cargo llvm-cov --branch`), so the arm returns when that feature is stable on the
  pinned channel, or when the founder admits a second channel for this job; either way with a measured first
  reading before a threshold is stated (none exists: the workspace's branch coverage was never measured).

- Removing the `cargo xtask ci-gates` step from the boot job — rejected: the job would lose the only CI read of a
  panic record over a booted app (obs-plan §11 → SLO).

- Repairing the heartbeat and perf-budget arms in place — rejected: it needs the smoke to keep the app alive past
  one 15 s tick and to produce samples, a change to a step that stays as it stands, for a job that leaves at
  `Window's gates retired`.

- A per-member assertion on the a11y upload, and removing the pre-push `ci-gates` stage — not here (inputs#I2
  item 4): each keeps an owner and a stated reading.

- Moving the thresholds into a new xtask verb — rejected here: a new registered verb for a step of about twenty
  lines; the inline step is repaired and pinned by running it.

- Do not edit: `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.{sh,ps1}`, `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs`, `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`, any
  step of the `boot`, `a11y` or `supply-chain` jobs, `release.yml`, `update-channels.yml`, `secret-scan.yml`,
  `rust-toolchain.toml`, any spec master.
- Do not rename the lines `ci-gates: zero-spans PASS (…)` and `ci-gates: zero-panic PASS`.
- No soft gate: no `continue-on-error`, no `|| true`, no retry, no `#[ignore]`.

- A change that needs a new permission, token, trigger or third-party action halts for the founder's own word
  (inputs#I1 item 7). None is planned.
- No run binds 4317 or 4318. None is planned.

- **Order.** Pins first (step 0), then the gates; `cargo fmt` once before the gate block (the per-write hook
  formats as another edition). The bindings regen is the last cargo-adjacent step; a default-features test run
  after it rewrites the tracked bindings.

- **Count check.** After the edits the workspace test count moves by exactly the number of tests added
  (`cargo nextest list --workspace --profile ci`, run under the same environment as the suite); a delta that does
  not match is a finding, not a rounding detail. 2890 tests ran in `cargo xtask test` on `ci#38038281709`.
- **The witness cuts the step by its name**, never by line numbers; it reads `ci.yml` by `str::lines()`.

- **Workflow comments** avoid the tokens `windows`, `macos`, `matrix.os`, `runner.os ==`

- **Doc comments:** no wrapped `//!` or `///` line starts with `+ `, `- ` or `* ` unless it is a list item.

- **`gate_substrings` keeps its 14 members:** every command it names is still in `ci.yml`

- **Evidence transcripts** carry `{tmp}` in place of a temp path, and are re-read by `gate.py hygiene` after any

- **`--no-tests=fail`** was read on the dev host (cargo-nextest 0.9.146: exit 4, `error: no tests to run`). The
  runner installs 0.9.133; the CI run is where the flag is read there.

- **Seen at P3, for the report:** `heartbeat-gap-check.sh` finds a tick by a compact-JSON pattern, so a record

data.head: ### (2) The same step's branch arm — `ci.yml:515-516`, `:524`, `:527`, `:531`; the job's name `:450`

body:
- **Full:** `Branch: 0/0 = 100.0% (threshold 70%)` (coverage log :5235). The uploaded report (artifact
  `coverage-linux`, id 11664724073, `lcov.info`, 1441580 bytes) holds 144 `BRF:` records and 144 `BRH:` records,
  every one `BRF:0` / `BRH:0`, and **0 `BRDA:` lines**; its `LF`/`LH`/`FNF`/`FNH` sums are 38252 / 33992 / 4055 /
  3565, the numbers the step printed (counted in python over the downloaded artifact).

- **Why the report holds no branch count:** branch instrumentation is a nightly-only compiler feature
  (`-Z coverage-options=branch`; `cargo llvm-cov --branch` "(unstable)" in `cargo llvm-cov --help` of the host's
  0.9.1, and per the fetched issue above; the runner installs 0.8.5). The project pins `channel = "1.95.0"`
  (`rust-toolchain.toml`), the runner used it, and `run_cargo_llvm_cov` passes no `--branch`
  (`xtask/src/main.rs:462-472`). On the pin the tool writes the per-file summary records with a zero total and no
  per-branch line.

- **Cost of producing a count:** a toolchain the project does not pin, in the `coverage` job (arch §Stack names
  one channel, held by the xtask test `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel`). The step that would change ran
  26 min 5 s on that run (`cargo xtask test:coverage`, 08:35:13 → 09:01:18). What the workspace's branch coverage
  reads under a nightly was **not measured**: it needs a full instrumented build on another toolchain, and the
  default-features test run under it rewrites the tracked bindings. A `nightly-2026-09-20` is installed on the dev
  host (`rustup toolchain list`), so the measurement is possible on the operator's word.

- **Nothing outside the workflow keys on the job's name:** `main` has no branch protection
  (`gh api …/branches/main/protection` → 404 "Branch not protected") and the repository has no ruleset
  (`gh api …/rulesets` → `[]`); `git grep` for the name and for a 70 % branch threshold outside the masters and
  the leaves finds only `ci.yml:450` and `:531`.

  `ci-gates: zero-panic PASS` · `heartbeat-gap-check: max gap 0ms in  (threshold 45000ms) PASS` ·
  `ci-gates: perf-budget: frame: cannot-evaluate: 0 samples, no WebGPU adapter (no_navigator_gpu)` ·
  `… memory NEUTRAL — populated 0 of 1` · `… snapshot NEUTRAL — no metric.snapshot.token_count_ms record` ·
  `ci-gates: perf-budget NEUTRAL`.

- **What that log holds:** a runner boot log of the same step, kept on the host from `ci#38026637514` attempt 3
  (`target/boot-smoke/ci-38026637514-attempt-3/`, 110 records, first 06:02:58.837, last 06:03:04.637), holds
  exactly **one** record each of `ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick`, `viz.tick`, `plugins.tick`, **one**
  `metric.buffer.memory_bytes`, no `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms`, no frame record and two `ui.webgpu.adapter`
  records. `ci#38038281709`'s own boot artifact was not opened (it also carries the exit-witness files, which are
  read whole or not at all); its `ci-gates` lines are the same shape.

- **Arm by arm, over constructed data dirs** (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR={scratch dir} cargo xtask ci-gates`):

  | input | exit | what printed |
  |---|---|---|
  | no data dir · a `logs/` dir with no log file | **0** | four `NEUTRAL` lines |
  | a log file with zero lines | 1 | `zero-spans FAIL (log files present but contain no events)` |
  | one non-tick record (the pre-push seed's shape) | **0** | `zero-spans PASS (1 …)` · `zero-panic PASS` · heartbeat `no … .tick records found (INACTIVE state — … gate trivially passes)` · `perf-budget NEUTRAL` |
  | the kept runner log | **0** | the run's lines, `PASS (110 …)` |
  | the kept runner log + one `app.panic.fatal` ERROR record | 1 | `zero-panic FAIL — app.panic.fatal at …:111` |
  | two `buffer.tick` 50 s apart | 1 | `heartbeat-gap-check: max gap 50000ms in buffer.tick exceeds 45000ms threshold` |
  | one `metric.buffer.memory_bytes` of 600000000 | 1 | `memory max 600000000 B > 512000000 B (n=1, populated 1) FAIL` |

- **Reading:** on the boot job's log the heartbeat arm has no consecutive pair to subtract (one tick per target,
  the script prints the gap as 0 and an empty target name), the memory arm holds one zero sample, the snapshot and
  frame arms hold none. None of the three can fail on a boot of this length; each can fail on an input it never
  gets there. The zero-spans and zero-panic arms read the 112 records and fail on what they are for.

- **The step is reached only behind two gating steps** that already need the log to hold records
  (`harness:settled` reads four `app.boot.window.navigation` records): an empty or absent log reddens the smoke
  first, and `ci-gates` is then skipped (test-plan §9; measured at an earlier chunk on `ci#38010977166`).

- **The same verb in `pre-push:linux`:** its sixth stage writes one seed record, `app.boot.ready`, into a fresh
  data dir and runs `cargo xtask ci-gates` over it (`xtask/src/pre_push.rs:32-34`, `:278-281`, `:519-525`). It is
  the fourth row of the table: green over a record the stage wrote itself. It is not a step of `ci.yml`.

- **Seen while probing, not a live defect:** `heartbeat-gap-check.sh` finds a tick by a compact-JSON pattern
  (`"target":"…"`). A record spelled with a space after the colon is not seen as a tick (two such ticks 50 s
  apart read `no … .tick records found … trivially passes`, exit 0). The app writes compact JSON (the kept runner
  log), so its own logs are read.

- **Where it sits:** a job that leaves at `Window's gates retired` (`working-route.md:48`). The engine-side
  owner is on the route: `Agent harness drives the console engine` (`working-route.md:31`) reads "panic,
  heartbeat-gap, process-end, budget checks grade its log (P-086)". The enforced budget gate today is
  `lint-test`'s `cargo xtask perf:budget … --require memory,snapshot`, which on this run read
  `graded 120 record(s) across 1 file(s)` · `memory max 7680000 B <= 512000000 B (n=3, populated 3) PASS` ·
  `snapshot p99 69.9 ms <= 500 ms (n=50) PASS` (lint-test log :13639-13643).

- **Measured:** no step of `lint-test` makes the check (`ci.yml:23-142`, read whole); `run_cargo_nextest`
  returns nextest's own status and reads no log (`xtask/src/main.rs:429-452`). The one check of the kind is the
  `zero-spans` arm above, which counts **log records** of any target, not spans, and runs in the `boot` job.

- **What `lint-test` does read:** the `perf:budget` step fails on an absent log family (exit 2) and on a required
  arm with no sample; on this run it graded 120 records of the producer's log. No sentence of obs-plan names that
  as a zero-record check.
- **Where it sits:** the sentence is a master's; phase amends none.

title: Scope — No gate stands while reading nothing

data.head: # Scope — No gate stands while reading nothing

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing` · version `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0` · Epoch 1 — Foundation: base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates
**Working entry (`working-route.md:25`):** "No gate stands while reading nothing — coverage branch and empty-report
arms, empty test selections, boot budget and heartbeat reads, zero-span check: each reads something or leaves (P-128)"
**Chunk base:** `7419496b` (HEAD at take-up). Every diff-shaped probe of this chunk names this sha, never HEAD.

A gate of the `ci` workflow that prints PASS or NEUTRAL over an empty or absent input passes while it reads nothing.
The last chunk settled every baseline comparison and every upload; five gates of another shape were recorded there
and not edited. This chunk leaves each of them in one of two states: it reads something that can make it fail, or
it is gone. There is no third state: a gate that prints NEUTRAL or PASS over nothing is the defect, not an option
(inputs#I1 item 2). With them settled, the closing sentence of P-128's acceptance is true and the capability is
claimed here.

- **Each of the five carried gates reads something that can make it fail, or leaves.** The entry's first `CARRY:`
  names them with how each was read; every reading below enters as a hypothesis and is MEASURED at P3 before the
  plan chooses (inputs#I1 item 1: what the gate reads on a run where its input is there, and what it does when its
  input is empty or absent; "a gate described from its text is not yet a reading"). Coordinates were re-read at
  take-up on `ci.yml` and `xtask/src/main.rs` at `7419496b`.
  - (1) "the coverage thresholds step exits 0 when lcov.info tracks 0 lines and 0 functions (read from
    the step's text; the arm did not fire on either run read)". Job `coverage`, step `Enforce coverage thresholds`,
    `ci.yml:519-522`; its message reads "Foundation epoch — gate trivially passes; activates at chunk #15 first
    tests" (`:520`). Verified at P3: the step body run over an empty report exits 0 with that line, and over no
    report exits 1; on `ci#38038281709` the arm did not fire (38252 lines, 4055 functions). The percentages also
    print `100.0` over a zero total (`:523-525`), a second pass over nothing in the same step (research.md).
  - (2) [premise-corrected: the uploaded report holds 144 `BRF:0` and 144 `BRH:0` records and no `BRDA:` line
    (artifact 11664724073 of `ci#38038281709`): a zero total, not an absent record.] The branch arm read
    `Branch: 0/0 = 100.0% (threshold 70%)` on `ci#38038281709`, as on the two runs the entry names. The same
    step, `ci.yml:515-516` (the `BRF:` / `BRH:` sums), `:524` (a total of 0 prints `100.0`), `:527`, `:531`; the
    job's name states the branch threshold (`:450`). Why the total is zero, as research found: branch
    instrumentation is a nightly-only compiler feature, the project pins `1.95.0`, the runner used the pin, and
    `cargo xtask test:coverage` asks for no branch count. "a threshold that can only be met by a toolchain the
    project does not pin is said so, with its cost" (inputs#I1 item 4): the cost is in research.md, and what the
    workspace's branch coverage would read was not measured.
  - (3) "--no-tests=pass on the mcp-test job's nextest step and inside cargo xtask test and cargo xtask
    test:coverage (read from their text; no run was read with an empty selection)". `ci.yml:199`;
    `xtask/src/main.rs:440` and `:469`, with the two verbs' `about` strings at `:78` and `:86`; the `lint-test`
    step that runs the first verb is named "cargo xtask test (no-tests=pass at Foundation epoch)" (`ci.yml:111`).
    Verified at P3: the three selections held 2928, 2890 and 2890 tests on `ci#38038281709`; on the dev host an
    empty selection exits 0 with the flag and 4 without it (cargo-nextest 0.9.146; the runner installs 0.9.133,
    its default not read).
  - (4) "cargo xtask ci-gates in the boot job read "perf-budget: memory NEUTRAL — populated 0 of 1",
    "snapshot NEUTRAL" and "heartbeat-gap-check: max gap 0ms in (threshold 45000ms) PASS" on ci#38031822696, over
    a boot that lives about five seconds". Job `boot`, step `cargo xtask ci-gates`, `ci.yml:363-364`. Verified at
    P3: the same lines on `ci#38038281709`, with a fourth the entry does not name (`frame: cannot-evaluate: 0
    samples, no WebGPU adapter (no_navigator_gpu)`); a kept runner log of the step holds one tick per target, one
    memory sample and no snapshot record, so none of the three arms can fail there; the verb's `zero-spans` and
    `zero-panic` arms read the log's 112 records and fail on what they are for; over an absent log the verb exits
    0 with four NEUTRAL lines (research.md, the table).
  - (5) "obs-plan §10's "build fails if xtask test produces zero spans" has no step in lint-test, the
    zero-span check running only inside ci-gates in the boot job". Verified at P3; `cargo xtask test` reads no
    log, and the arm in `ci-gates` counts log records, not spans.
  - "(4) and the one home of (5)'s check sit in the boot job, which leaves at Window's gates retired;
    (1), (2) and (3) sit in jobs that stay". `Window's gates retired` is `working-route.md:48`. Verified at P3.

- **The two further `--no-tests=pass` literals are measured and settled with (3).** The entry's second `CARRY:`:
  "seen and not measured at 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing: two further --no-tests=pass literals
  in xtask/src/main.rs, in run_perf_slo_load (the verb the lint-test job's perf:slo-load step runs) and
  run_perf_load_profiles (not run in CI); what either selects on a run was not read". Read at take-up:
  `xtask/src/main.rs:749` and `:780`; the `lint-test` step is `ci.yml:115-116`. Verified at P3: the first
  selected 1 test on `ci#38038281709`; the second runs in no workflow and lists 4 tests on the dev host.

- **The a11y upload's path members.** The entry's third `CARRY:`: "the a11y job's a11y-violations upload
  has three path members and its if-no-files-found: error fails the step only when none matches, so one missing
  member is invisible (all three matched on ci#38031822696, 5 files); the a11y job leaves at Window's gates
  retired". Read at take-up: `ci.yml:258-268`, three members (`:264`, `:265`, `:266`). Verified at P3: 5 files
  again on `ci#38038281709`; each member's producer is a link of the `&&` chain inside `cargo xtask test:a11y`;
  the action's own text states its no-file rule for the path input as a whole; one member missing beside a
  matching one was not read on a runner. Whether a missing member is a gate "reading nothing" in the
  acceptance's sense, and what the job loses before it leaves, is part of the P4 dialog.

- **Found at P3, not stated by the entry, and brought to the same dialog:** `cargo xtask quarantine-tracking`
  (`lint-test`) prints NEUTRAL on every run and exits 0 over a root where none of its search dirs exists; the
  sixth stage of `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` runs `ci-gates` over one record the stage wrote itself (not a step
  of `ci.yml`). Every other gating step of the workflow read something on `ci#38038281709` (research.md, the
  census).

- **Which way each falls is the operator's technical fork, brought at P4 as ONE dialog** (inputs#I1 item 2): each
  with what repairing costs, what the gate is worth to the version as it will stand, and where it sits.

- **Where a gate sits decides half of it** (inputs#I1 item 3). Gate (4), the one home of gate (5)'s check and the
  a11y upload's path members sit in jobs that leave at `Window's gates retired`. For those the plan says what the

body:
The base is the last commit that flipped a master record, `7419496b`, which is HEAD: one sha, read through
`ci.py conclusion`.

- `7419496bdf9f` (HEAD, the last wrap's commit): **green** · 7 of 7 checks · wall 1683 s (`ci#38038281709` and
  `secret-scan#38038281700`, both pull-request runs, completed/success). It is the newest run of the tree this
  chunk edits, and the one the five gates are re-read on at P3.
- No red and no `not green` was read, so nothing is dispositioned here.
- none — the entry carries no `BLOCKED-ON` (`route.py blocked`: 0 blocks on a pending, gated or markerless line).

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T20:58:24Z
- **Chunk base:** `50216d7ee49c9763d1d9304aa07d3c3f3b74c7e3`. Every diff-shaped probe names this sha, never `HEAD`.

Tests build their spans, metric points and log records by hand: 28 files, 25 span, 11 span-event, 10 number-point
and 14 log-record literals inside 170 wrapper literals, each site fixing its own stamp, service and attributes
(research, "How telemetry is built in tests today"). This chunk gives the tests one set of factories for that
data, with event time, service and attributes settable, and moves six existing test files onto it, so the set
ships with its first consumers (inputs#I1 item 1). It is test data only: no product source changes for it.

The set lives in a new dev-only workspace member, `test-support` (the operator's answer, inputs#I3). No member
may name it outside its dev-dependencies and it may depend on nothing but the types it builds; a committed test
holds both. The version setter is not built here (inputs#I3).

The entry's carry closes first: the four in-process arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` take
claimed ports. The one port claim moves into the same member, so the two twins of it are removed and all four
port-using test binaries share one definition (inputs#I1 item 3); the two unit tests that read a port they have
released take a claimed number too (scope, premise-corrected). Per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phases (item 6),
test-plan §9 Integration tests row and architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports.

1. **The member.** Create `crates/test-support` with a manifest that inherits the workspace package fields
   (`version`, `edition`, `rust-version`, `license`, `repository`), sets `publish = false`, and lists exactly one
   dependency, `ingest` by path. No `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]` or `[features]` table. Add it to
   the root `Cargo.toml` member list. `src/lib.rs` declares two public modules, `otlp` and `ports`, and says in
   its module doc that the crate is test support, taken as a dev-dependency only.

2. **The pin of the edge, red first** (inputs#I3). Add the test-only module `xtask/src/test_support_edges.rs`,
   declared in `xtask/src/main.rs` beside `license_check` and `rust_floor` under `#[cfg(test)]`, reading manifests
   as text the way `rust_floor.rs:24-46` does. It asserts: (a) in every workspace member's manifest the name
   `test-support` stands only inside the `[dev-dependencies]` table; (b) `crates/test-support/Cargo.toml` has a
   `[dependencies]` table holding exactly `ingest`, and no `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]` or
   `[features]` table; (c) the root member list holds `crates/test-support` and at least one member names it
   under `[dev-dependencies]`, so the pin cannot pass over a set nobody uses. Run it before step 3's edges exist
   and keep the red reading, then green after step 5. One-shot mutating control, both readings to
   `evidence/mutations.md`: move the `test-support` line of one member into `[dependencies]` (red on (a)), then
   add a second dependency to `test-support` (red on (b)); restore each and show the tree clean of it.

3. **The one port claim.** `crates/test-support/src/ports.rs` holds `PortClaim` and `claim_port()` with the terms
   the twins hold today, unchanged: a number from 20000 to 31999, 24317 and 24318 left out, an advisory lock on
   `target/test-ports/{number}` held for the life of the claim, the port shown bindable when claimed, the file
   never unlinked, a panic when no port can be claimed. The repository root comes from the crate's compile-time
   manifest directory; nothing is read from the environment at run time. Its own tests: a claimed number lies in
   the range and is neither harness port; two live claims differ; the lock file of a live claim cannot be locked
   again.

4. **The claiming sites move** (the carry closes here). Add `test-support` to the `[dev-dependencies]` of
   `pulse-app` and `xtask`.
   - `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`: remove `pick_port` (`:132`); `boot` (`:145`) takes two claims,
     turns each number into an `OtlpPort`, and `Booted` holds both claims for the arm's life. The four in-process
     arms (`:279`, `:319`, `:360`, `:401`) are otherwise unchanged; the two re-exec arms are not touched.
   - `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs`: remove its `PortClaim`, the two constants and `claim_port`
     (`:35-83`); its three call sites use the member's.
   - `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs`: remove its `PortClaim`, the two constants, `random_word` and `claim_port`
     (`:66-113`); `Scratch` and both binaries use the member's.
   - `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` (`receiver_probe_tells_a_listening_loopback_port_from_a_closed_one`, `:776`)
     and `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs` (`a_listener_on_a_cycle_port_is_read_as_taken_and_a_closed_one_is_not`,
     `:429`): each takes a claimed number, binds its own listener on it, reads accepting, drops the listener and
     reads refusing while the claim is still held. Only lines inside each file's test module change.

5. **The factories.** `crates/test-support/src/otlp.rs` builds, on `ingest`'s public OTLP types only:
   a span (with its span events), a metric point (a number point inside a named gauge metric) and a log record,
   and assembles them under a resource into the request and resource-level forms the tests send or hand to the
   buffer. Builder form (test-plan §3 Test data bootstrap → Mechanism): a test sets what it reasons about and the
   rest takes a default. Settable: event time as an explicit instant in nanoseconds, the service (the resource's
   `service.name`), and attributes on the span, the span event, the point and the log record; ids, names, body,
   severity and value where the first consumers set them. No version setter (inputs#I3). Properties the module's
   own tests hold:
   - no clock is read and nothing is random: two builds from the same calls are equal;
   - an unset event time is one fixed instant; an unset service is one fixed name;
   - trace ids are 16 bytes and span ids 8; spans built into one request get distinct span ids unless the test
     sets them, by position, with no process-wide counter;
   - what a test sets is read back from the built record unchanged.
   Defaults hold no word or shape a scrubber arm matches (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging); a
   canary appears only where a test sets one.

6. **The first consumers move.** Add `test-support` to `crates/buffer`'s `[dev-dependencies]`. In each file the
   local helper bodies and their call sites move onto the factories, every literal they replace is removed, and
   no assertion changes. A test that feeds a running engine states the instant itself (the retention sweep
   deletes a record older than the window, `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:178-179`); a test that seeds a store
   directly keeps its fixed instant.
   - `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`: `one_span_request` (`:205`, 2 call sites).
   - `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs`: `spans_request` (`:283`, 2 call sites).
   - `pulse-app/tests/e2e_drain_template_assignment.rs`: `make_log_record` and `make_diverse_logs_request`
     (`:52`, `:81`): 100 log records with stated bodies, stamps and service.
   - `pulse-app/tests/e2e_pii_span_masking_stored_field.rs`: the log record, the span and its span event
     (`:208-266`), canaries set through the attribute, body and service setters.
   - `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs`, test module only (from `:284`): `span_batch`, `span_batch_with_events`,
     `metrics_batch_with_credential_name`. Add one test there, named so that `default_built` is in its name: a
     batch of default-built spans with events, metric points and log records, drained by `run_consumer`, reads
     `rows_ingested` equal to the rows sent, `redactions_applied` 0 and `append_rejections` 0 on the buffer
     state. The existing credential-name test is its red side: a set canary still reads one redaction.
   - `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs`, test module only (from `:931`): the metric-point helper group
     `gauge_point`, `gauge_metric`, `labelled_metric_batch` (17 uses), the one place a test sets attributes on a
     metric point. The two lines the capability record anchors on (`P-006`, `P-048`) are not touched.

7. **What the old form leaves behind** (inputs#I1 item 5). Re-run research's scan (its patterns and exclusions as
   written in research.md) and write `evidence/census.md`: per file the four literal counts at the base and
   after, and for every file this chunk does not move the route entry that owns it (research, "Owners of the
   sites this chunk does not move"). The report carries those counts.

8. **The repeated run.** Fire the repeated-run entry of `## Test Commands` and record the count of green runs
   out of seven in `evidence/`, as a count, not an exclusion. A single failure there is the finding: it stops
   the chunk and goes to the operator, never a re-run.
9. **Gates**, in the order of `## Test Commands`.

**Halts** (inputs#I1 item 6): a new listening socket, a new place on disk, a credential, a command word of the
engine, or anything reachable from another host stops for the operator's word. If a product type turns out to
need a constructor or a field to be buildable, stop and bring it (inputs#I1 item 4).
- `crates/test-support/Cargo.toml` — the dev-only member's manifest
- `crates/test-support/src/lib.rs` — the two modules' declarations
- `crates/test-support/src/otlp.rs` — the factories, with their own tests
- `crates/test-support/src/ports.rs` — the one port claim, with its own tests
- `xtask/src/test_support_edges.rs` — the committed pin of the dev-only edge, a test-only module
- `Cargo.toml` — the member list
- `Cargo.lock` — one workspace entry, written by cargo; no registry package
- `crates/buffer/Cargo.toml`, `pulse-app/Cargo.toml`, `xtask/Cargo.toml` — one dev-dependency each
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — the test-only module's declaration
- `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` — claimed ports; its span from the factories
- `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` — claim twin removed; its spans from the factories
- `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs` — claim twin removed
- `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs` — test module only: a claimed number

- `pulse-app/tests/e2e_drain_template_assignment.rs`, `pulse-app/tests/e2e_pii_span_masking_stored_field.rs` —
  their telemetry from the factories
- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs`, `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` — test module only

The chunk's own guards and pins come first, then the repeated run, then the supply-chain reads (the lockfile
gains an entry), then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order (`capability-drift` before the default-features
workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, the base-identity
bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure), then the local pre-push check with its teardown probe, then
the operator pass.

**One-shot mutating control:** step 2's two mutations of the edge pin are run once at implement, both readings
in `evidence/mutations.md`. On every re-run the property is guarded by entries that mutate nothing: the scope
guard and the workspace nextest, which runs the pin.

**Evidence no entry produces:** `evidence/census.md` is written by step 7 and `evidence/mutations.md` by step 2,
both steps outside this block, run once at implement; the count of the repeated run is copied into `evidence/`
from that entry's own log. No entry carries an `artifact` key for them.

**The pre-push check** runs a console engine cycle of its own on 24317 and 24318 in its sixth stage (as it has
since the last chunk); the probe after it reads that the stage ended what it started.
Absences, each with its reason:

- No boot-smoke gate: no boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `engine_boot.rs`, `console.rs`,
  `observability.rs`, a capability file); the two guards below read that no product line changes.
- No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched.
- No live leg: nothing here boots a product program outside a test binary.
- No local coverage entry: the thresholds are read by the `coverage` job of the operator pass's run.

- No retry anywhere. A red repeated run, a red pre-push stage or a port found taken stops the pass and goes to
  the operator.

**The operator pass, in this order.** The hygiene entry; the pre-CI commit; the local pre-push check again; the
merge-base probe; the build-branch push; the CI read of the pushed tip, asserted green. A red is fixed by a
further commit on top and read again.

  none reads the same defaults on every build, with no clock read and no randomness: the member's tests pass in

  test(default_built)) | (package(xtask) & test(test_support_edges))'` (per test-plan §11 Universal; test-plan §7
  Self-bootstrapping requirement).

- (obs) A batch of default-built spans, points and log records taken in by the buffer reads `rows_ingested`
  equal to the rows sent, `redactions_applied` 0 and `append_rejections` 0; the `default_built` test of the same
  entry holds it (per obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage; obs-plan §10 SLO Invariants & Telemetry Budgets).

- (security) Every factory default passes the write boundary unmasked, shown by that same test; a set canary
  still reads redacted in the moved credential-name and PII tests (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns →
  Logging).

- (arch) The workspace has one added member, `crates/test-support`, named here and accepted by the operator
  (inputs#I3); no member names it outside `[dev-dependencies]` and it depends on `ingest` alone: the pin
  `test_support_edges` passes, and its two mutations each read red in `evidence/mutations.md` (per architecture
  §Occupied Resources → Cargo workspace crate names; architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Module dependency
  direction).

- (arch) No product line changes for the factories: `git diff --name-only 50216d7e… -- crates pulse-app xtask
  scripts deny.toml …` prints nothing, and the test-module-only guard
  (`git diff -U0 --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ 50216d7e… -- … | awk …`) prints nothing (per architecture
  §Conventions → Module visibility discipline; inputs#I1 item 4).

- (tests) The carry is closed: `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` hands the engine two claimed ports in
  each of its four in-process arms, and no test reads a port it has released: the entry `grep -nE
  'bind\(\("127\.0\.0\.1", 0\)\)|bind\("127\.0\.0\.1:0"\)' … | wc -l` reads 0 (per test-plan §9 Pipeline
  structure, Integration tests row; architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports).

- (tests) One definition of the port claim serves the four port-using binaries and the two unit tests: the entry
  `grep -rlE --include=*.rs 'fn claim_port|struct PortClaim|fn pick_port' crates pulse-app xtask | wc -l` reads 1
  (inputs#I1 item 3; per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline → Spawned-program witness form).

- (tests) The four port-using binaries, run together seven times by the repeated-run entry, read green seven of
  seven; the count stands in `evidence/` as a count, not an exclusion (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget).

- (tests) Six test files take their telemetry from the factories and hold none of the literals they replaced;
  `evidence/census.md` gives the four literal counts per file at the base and after, and names the owning route
  entry for every file not moved (inputs#I1 items 1 and 5; per test-plan §1 Pending coverage triggers,
  `test-data-bootstrap-factories-unimplemented`).

- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` and `cargo audit` exit 0 with no `deny.toml` change; the
  report states that `Cargo.lock` gained one workspace entry and no registry package (per security-plan
  §Dependency Security, CI integration).

- (tests) The standard gate set passes in its stated order, `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
  --no-tests=fail` included; the bindings close reads exit 0 against `50216d7e`; the local pre-push check reads
  green with its teardown probe (per test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline).

  included; the report names the run id the CI read printed (per test-plan §10 Coverage thresholds).

title: How telemetry is built in tests today (inputs#I1 item 1)

data.head: ## How telemetry is built in tests today (inputs#I1 item 1)

body:
Derivation: a line scan of every tracked `.rs` file (`git ls-files '*.rs'`) for the struct literals `Span {`,
`Event {`, `NumberDataPoint {`, `LogRecord {` and for the wrappers around them (`Export…ServiceRequest {`,
`Resource… {`, `Scope… {`, `Metric {`, `Resource {`), lines holding `->`, `fn`, `impl`, `use` or a leading `//` left
out so that a signature is not counted as a literal.

- **26 files hold a span, span-event, number-point or log-record literal:** 25 span, 11 span-event, 10 number-point
  and 14 log-record literals, inside 170 wrapper literals. Two more files (`crates/ingest/src/grpc.rs`,
  `crates/ingest/src/http.rs`) hold wrapper literals only. 28 files in all.

- **By place:** `crates/ingest` 14 files (6 under `tests/`, 5 examples, 3 unit-test modules under `src/`),
  `crates/buffer/src` 2 (`appender.rs`, `consumer.rs`), `pulse-app/tests` 11, `xtask/src` 1 (`smoke.rs`).
  **None sits in a crate that leaves in Epochs 2 and 3.**

- **Shapes:** every site that needs a request re-types the same four nested wrappers; 28 local helper functions do
  it (`make_span` ×5, `make_export_request` ×5, `make_request` ×2, `make_batch` ×2 and 14 one-offs; name sweep
  `fn (make|build|one|…)…(span|request|metric|log|record|point|batch)…(`).

- **Event time** (per file, the same scan's `SystemTime::now|now_ns()` and `1_7dd_ddd_ddd|_unix_nano: 0` columns
  over the 28 files): 16 files read the wall clock, 11 write a fixed or zero literal, 5 of them do both, and 6
  leave every stamp at its default. No site takes the instant as a parameter of a shared builder.

- **Service:** set by a hand-built `service.name` resource attribute in 19 of the 28 files; left unset
  (`resource: None`) in the ingest receiver tests and in `consumer.rs`'s span helpers.

- **Version:** no test sets a sender's `service.version` (`grep -rn '"service\.version"'`: 5 hits, all the
  product's own log identity). The product stores no version (seven span columns, `retention.rs:222`).

- **Attributes:** on span events and log records in the two PII files and `appender.rs`; on metric points in
  `appender.rs` and two dev examples only.

- **The three factories test-plan §3 names** (`MockTraceSpan`, `MockArrowBatch`, `MockMetricPoint`): 0 hits each at
  the chunk base; control `fn claim_port`: 2 hits.

title: Port picking (the carry and what the sweep found beside it)

data.head: ## Port picking (the carry and what the sweep found beside it)

body:
Sweep `\[127, 0, 0, 1\], 0\)|127\.0\.0\.1:0|"127\.0\.0\.1", 0\)|localhost:0|\(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST, 0\)` over
`crates pulse-app xtask`: 27 lines in 20 files · 1 a comment · 3 release a port they read · 23 keep the listener
they bound.

- **Release sites, 3:** `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs:133` (the carry: the number is handed to an
  engine that binds it later); `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs:777` and `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs:430` (each asserts
  that the port it just released refuses). The carry's text and the take-up's sweep named the first only.

- **Keep sites, 23 in 17 files:** a listener bound on port 0 that the test itself serves on or holds (the ingest
  receiver tests, nine `pulse-app` end-to-end and perf binaries, the census arm at
  `integration_console_engine.rs:513`). Nothing is released, so nothing can be taken in between; they lie in the
  kernel's ephemeral range, outside 20000 to 31999.

- **The claim's terms as the two twins hold them:** a number from 20000 to 31999, 24317 and 24318 left out, an
  advisory lock on `target/test-ports/{number}` held for the life of the claim, the port shown bindable when
  claimed. The range cannot yield 4317 or 4318. The directory is found from the compile-time
  `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; no environment variable is read at run time.

- **The measurement behind the carry:** the last chunk's report (`report.md:141-143`, `:267-269`) records one of
  seven hand runs failing with bind-and-release and 14 of 14 green after the claims, "a count, not an exclusion".
  Spot-checked as recorded; not re-run here.

- **`claim_port` / `pick_port`** — 5 call edges: `spawn` and one arm in
  `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` (`:125`, `:577`), `boot` in
  `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` (`:147`, `:148`), `new` in `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs` (`:253`).
  No caller outside the three files; the name sweep `claim_port|PortClaim|CLAIMED_PORTS|HARNESS_PORTS|test-ports|
  pick_port` over the tracked tree reads 26 hits in those three files and none elsewhere, so no test pins their
  text.
- **`ingest` crate edges** — used by `buffer`, `pulse-app`, `ui-bridge`, `xtask`; `ingest` uses no sibling.

- **Who reaches `ingest`'s surface from outside its `src/`** — 181 sites in `pulse-app/tests`, 110 in
  `crates/ingest/tests`, 48 in `crates/buffer/src`. The OTLP types the factories need are already public and are
  built from tests today.

- **Names** — `PortClaim` and `claim_port` exist twice (the twins); a module `telemetry` exists in `ui-bridge`; no
  symbol `test_support`, `SpanBuilder`, `MetricPointBuilder` or `LogRecordBuilder` exists.

- **A shared module inside one package** (`xtask/tests/common/mod.rs:1-9`): one file, two test binaries, no manifest
  change. It does not reach a second package.

- **No dev-only edge between workspace members exists today** (an awk over every member's `[dev-dependencies]`
  for `path =`: 0 lines).

- **The retention sweep reads the record's own stamp against the wall clock** (`crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:23-26`,
  `:178-179`): a record with a fixed past stamp is deleted by the first sweep of a running engine. A test that
  feeds a live engine states "now" itself; a test that seeds a store directly states a fixed instant.

- **A replayed span identity fails its whole batch** (obs-plan §10; `consumer.rs` holds the pin): default ids must
  differ inside one built request, and a test that wants a duplicate sets it.

- **Local helpers wrap the literals**: in every candidate file the tests call a local helper, so moving a file
  onto the factories changes helper bodies and their call sites, not what a test asserts.

- **Builder form with `rstest` composition** (test-plan §3 Test data bootstrap → Mechanism): set what the test
  states, default the rest.
- **The instant is an argument** (test-plan §4, triage crate): no factory reads a clock.

- **Library crates keep their tests in a co-located `mod tests`** (test-plan §2); `pulse-app`'s live under
  `pulse-app/tests/`.

- **A new member inherits the workspace package fields** (`license.workspace`, `rust-version.workspace`): the xtask
  pins `license_check` and `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` read every member of the root manifest.

- **`check:english-sources` and `quarantine-tracking` read `crates/` whole** (`xtask/src/source_lint.rs:25`,
  `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.sh:20`): a home under `crates/` needs no new root.
