# The five other gates — 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing

Plan step 8. Written by /implement on 2026-10-10 from `research.md` ("The newest run, read step by step") and
`scope.md` ("Read at take-up and at P3, not stated by the entry"). **No new measurement was made for this file and
none of the five was edited** (inputs#I2 item 4; the plan's Constraints). Each reading below is the one phase took,
on the run named beside it.

They are gates of the `ci` workflow that pass while reading nothing and are neither a baseline comparison nor an
artifact upload. P-128's acceptance closes "No gate stands while reading nothing"; the operator's answer is that the
sentence reaches these five, so P-128 is not claimed by this chunk. The entry that closes the sentence is minted at
this chunk's wrap and carries them.

The runs: `ci#38031822696` on `6df9e95c` (pull-request event, attempt 1, green, 7 of 7 checks) and
`ci#38026637514` attempt 1 on `4e61553b`; the workflow file is byte-identical at the two commits (research.md).

Coordinates are given twice: as phase read them at the chunk base `6df9e95c`, and where the same line stands in the
tree after this chunk's edits (found by `grep`, a locating read of the file, not a reading of any gate).

## 1. The coverage thresholds step passes when nothing is tracked

- **Where:** job `coverage`, step `Enforce coverage thresholds`. Base `ci.yml:565-568`; after this chunk
  `ci.yml:519-522`.
- **What it does:** when `lcov.info` tracks 0 lines and 0 functions the step prints `Coverage gate: 0 lines / 0
  functions tracked (…)` and exits 0.
- **Measured reading:** read from the step's text at take-up. The arm did not fire on either run: both tracked
  lines and functions (`Line: 33992/38252 = 88.9%`, `Function: 3565/4055 = 87.9%` on `ci#38031822696`, the same lines
  on `ci#38026637514` attempt 1).

## 2. The same step's branch arm passes over no branch count

- **Where:** the same step. After this chunk the line that prints it is `ci.yml:527`.
- **Measured reading:** `Branch: 0/0 = 100.0% (threshold 70%)` on `ci#38031822696` and on `ci#38026637514`
  attempt 1. The uploaded `lcov.info` carries no branch count, so the 70 % branch gate passes over nothing while the
  job's name states it (`coverage gate (line ≥75% / branch ≥70% / function ≥85%)`).

`NumberDataPoint {` or `LogRecord {`, the name not preceded by a letter, digit or underscore (so `ResourceSpans {`
is no `Span {`); lines holding `->`, `fn`, `impl`, `use` or a leading `//` are left out. The wrapper column counts
`Export…ServiceRequest {`, `Resource {`, `Resource(Spans|Metrics|Logs) {`, `Scope(Spans|Metrics|Logs) {` and
`Metric {` the same way.

**Control.** At the base the four record kinds read 25, 11, 10 and 14 in 26 files, 28 files with the two
wrapper-only ones: research's numbers, each one. The wrapper column reads 180 at the base where research states
170; research's exact wrapper pattern is not recorded and five variants of this one read 180, 180, 169, 161 and

title: evidence/mutations.md
body:
# Mutations of the edge pin — 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data

Run once at /implement, by hand, on the working tree over chunk base `50216d7e`. Subject: the xtask test module
`test_support_edges` (`xtask/src/test_support_edges.rs`), five tests. Command for every reading:
`cargo nextest run -p xtask --profile ci --no-tests=fail -E 'test(test_support_edges)'`.

## Red first (plan step 2), before any member named the set
State: `crates/test-support` in the root member list with its manifest and `src/lib.rs`; no member's
`[dev-dependencies]` named it yet.

- exit 100 · `Summary … 5 tests run: 4 passed, 1 failed, 478 skipped`
- FAIL `test_support_edges::test_support_is_a_member_that_some_member_uses`, its panic line:
  `no member names test-support under [dev-dependencies]: the pins above would pass over a set nobody uses`
- PASS the other four (`no_member_names_test_support_outside_its_dev_dependencies`,
  `test_support_depends_on_ingest_alone`, and the two that read the module's own parsing).

## Mutation 1 — a member names the set outside its dev-dependencies (red on (a))
Edit: in `xtask/Cargo.toml` the line `test-support = { path = "../crates/test-support" }` moved from
`[dev-dependencies]` to the end of `[dependencies]`. The mutated tail was read back before the run.

- exit 100 · `Summary … 5 tests run: 4 passed, 1 failed, 478 skipped`
- FAIL `test_support_edges::no_member_names_test_support_outside_its_dev_dependencies`, its panic line:
  `xtask names test-support under "[dependencies]": "test-support = { path = \"../crates/test-support\" }"`
- PASS the other four. `test_support_is_a_member_that_some_member_uses` stays green: `pulse-app` and `buffer`
  still name the set under their dev-dependencies.

Restored by the reverse edit. `sha256(xtask/Cargo.toml)` before the mutation and after the restore: `5f0f4c08…f3d375`,
equal.

## Mutation 2 — the set gains a second dependency (red on (b))
Edit: `prost.workspace = true` added under `[dependencies]` of `crates/test-support/Cargo.toml`. The mutated table was
read back before the run.

- exit 100 · `Summary … 5 tests run: 4 passed, 1 failed, 478 skipped`
- FAIL `test_support_edges::test_support_depends_on_ingest_alone`, its panic lines:
  `crates/test-support depends on the crate whose types it builds, and on nothing else` ·
  `left: ["ingest", "prost"]` · `right: ["ingest"]`
- PASS the other four.

Restored by the reverse edit. `sha256(crates/test-support/Cargo.toml)` before and after: `7241629b…d62487`, equal.

## A third reading, not asked by the plan — the default-built pin reads the defaults
Edit: the factory's default log body in `crates/test-support/src/otlp.rs` changed from `test log record` to
`test log record password=hunter2`. Command:
`cargo nextest run -p buffer --profile ci --no-tests=fail -E 'test(default_built) | test(dispatch_folds_redactions_after_a_successful_append)'`.

- exit 100 · `Summary … 2 tests run: 1 passed, 1 failed, 187 skipped`
- FAIL `consumer::tests::a_default_built_batch_of_every_kind_lands_whole_with_no_redaction`:
  `no default is masked` · `left: 3` · `right: 0` (the batch holds three default log records)
- PASS `consumer::tests::dispatch_folds_redactions_after_a_successful_append` (the set canary, one redaction).

Restored by the reverse edit. `sha256(crates/test-support/src/otlp.rs)` before and after: `28d1e29c…57e109f`, equal.

## The tree after the three restores
- `sha256(Cargo.lock)` before the first mutation and after the last restore plus one more cargo run:
  `07850078…3bc64c1`, equal (mutation 2 made cargo add `prost` to the member's lock entry; the restore took it out).
- `grep -c 'hunter2\|^prost'` over the member's `otlp.rs` and `Cargo.toml`: 0 and 0.
- The pins on the restored tree, `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --no-tests=fail -E 'package(test-support) |
  (package(buffer) & test(default_built)) | (package(xtask) & test(test_support_edges))'`: exit 0 ·
  `Summary … 20 tests run: 20 passed, 666 skipped` (14 of the member, 1 of `buffer`, 5 of xtask).

## Limits
- One run per reading. Each mutation changes one line; no mutation of (c) other than the red-first state was made.
- The pin reads manifests as text. A dependency reached through a `[target.…]` table of another member, or through a
  renamed `package = "test-support"` key under another name, names the set on its own line and is read; a manifest
  outside the root member list is not read.

body:
# The operator edit of the plan, between runs (2026-10-10)

**Whose word.** The operator, 2026-10-10, given in the implement session after its P4 report and kept verbatim as
inputs#I5: "one correction of the plan between runs, made by you as my hands and recorded as the operator edit in
evidence: entry 4 git diff takes --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ so it reads the same on any host; the plan lines
that restate the command follow. Re-fire entry 4." The course was the operator's own answer to the question on
that entry (inputs#I4). The edits below were typed by the implement agent on that word; /implement edits no plan
on its own. Edited and re-fired 2026-10-10T21:30:27Z.

Why the entry could not read its subject as written is in `evidence/test-module-guard.md`.

## The correction — entry 4 pins the two diff prefixes

`plan.md:179`, the entry's `run`, at its head:

- before: `git diff -U0 50216d7ee49c9763d1d9304aa07d3c3f3b74c7e3 -- crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs …`
- after: `git diff -U0 --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ 50216d7ee49c9763d1d9304aa07d3c3f3b74c7e3 -- crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs …`

Nothing else of the entry changed: the four paths, the awk text, `role`, `env`, `expect`, `new`, `baseline` and
`note` stand as the plan's author wrote them.

## The one line that restates the command

`plan.md:339-342`, the acceptance criterion "(arch) No product line changes for the factories":

- before: "the test-module-only guard (`git diff -U0 50216d7e… -- … | awk …`) prints nothing"
- after: "the test-module-only guard (`git diff -U0 --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ 50216d7e… -- … | awk …`)
  prints nothing"

The criterion's lines were re-wrapped so that the command stands on one line; no other word of it changed. A grep
of `plan.md` for `git diff -U0` reads these two lines and no third.

## The block after the edit

`gate.py run --plan … --dry-run`: `entries 26 · green 0 · red 0 · recorded 0 · timeout 0 · not-run 26`, the block
parses.

## Entry 4 re-fired

`gate.py run --plan … --run-dir … --marker … --entry 4`, entry line and summary line, verbatim:

```
  4 probe       green · exit 0 · 0.01s · 0 B → 4.2.log · git diff -U0 --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ 50216d7ee49c9… (447 chars)
entries 26 · green 1 · red 0 · recorded 0 · timeout 0 · not-run 25
```

Exit 0 and no output, both atoms held. The first firing's red stands in the trail beside it (`4.log`, 25 B).

## Known-positive control of the edited form, in the entry's own diff shape

Run by hand (git and awk only, the entry's awk text unchanged): the edited `git diff` with the commit one chunk
older than the base, `514fbe57`, against the work tree. That diff holds the product hunks of the last chunk in
`xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` and `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs`.

- exit 1 · 25 lines, every one opening with its file name: 21 of `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, 4 of
  `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs`.

The same count the plan's own control reads over `514fbe57..50216d7e`, now read from a diff against the work tree,
the form the entry runs.

## Limits
- Entries 1 to 3 and 5 to 22 were not re-fired: their first firing stands, the edit touched no file they read.
- The entry's `baseline` text still describes its P5 reading (an empty diff, a commit-to-commit control). It is
  left as written; this file is the record of what the entry reads after the edit.
- research.md and scope.md are unchanged.

title: evidence/test-module-guard.md
body:
# The test-module-only guard on this host — 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data

Gate entry 4 of the plan's `## Test Commands` (`git diff -U0 50216d7e… -- {four files} | awk '…'`) reads which
hunks of the four co-located-test files start above the line where each file's test module opens. Its awk takes
the file name from a header line `+++ b/{path}`.

## What this host prints
The user-level git config of this host sets `diff.mnemonicPrefix = true`
(`git config --show-origin --get diff.mnemonicPrefix` names the user config file; value `true`). Under it a diff of
a commit against the work tree prints `+++ w/{path}`, and a diff of two commits prints `+++ b/{path}`.

Header lines of the entry's own diff, as printed here:

```
+++ w/crates/buffer/src/appender.rs
+++ w/crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs
+++ w/xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs
+++ w/xtask/src/harness_ready.rs
```

So the awk never sets its file name, and every hunk of every file is read against the fall-through line 360.

## Four readings, run by hand at /implement (git and awk only, the entry's awk text unchanged)
| form | exit | output |
|---|---|---|
| the entry as written, base against the work tree | 1 | `:288` `:289` `:309` `:319` `:355` (five lines, the file name empty) |
| the same with `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` on `git diff` | 0 | none |
| the pinned form over the plan's known-positive range `514fbe57..50216d7e` | — | 25 lines |
| the entry as written over that range (commit to commit) | — | 25 lines |

The five printed lines are hunks of `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs`, whose test module opens at line 284: every one
starts inside it. They print because 288 to 355 lie below 360, not because a product line changed.

## What follows
- With the prefixes pinned the property the entry states holds: no hunk of the four files starts above its test
  module's line.
- As written, on a host with this setting, the entry is wrong in both directions for a diff against the work
  tree: it reads red on a test-module hunk below line 360 of any file, and it would read green on a product-line
  hunk between line 360 and a module line above it (`appender.rs` 931, `harness_ready.rs` 477).
- The plan's baseline for this entry was taken on the untouched tree, where the diff is empty and the header lines
  never print; its known-positive control is a commit-to-commit diff, which prints `b/`.
- The plan is not edited by /implement. This reading goes to the operator.
